summary: 2008-03-17 - Chicago White Sox @ Milwaukee Brewers (Final: Tied)
2008-03-25 - Los Angeles Dodgers @ Milwaukee Brewers (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: Big Z has looked sharp this spring and has been in control, both emotionally and pitch-count wise. Zambrano was 2-1 with a 4.26 ERA against Milwaukee last year. He is winless in three previous Opening Day assignments.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets has started more games at Wrigley Field (12) than at any other road ballpark and has had some battles against the Cubs over the years. He's making his sixth Opening Day start in the past seven years and is 3-0 in openers.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly was 1-1 with a 5.29 ERA last year against the Brewers. The lefty had trouble with his breaking pitches during Spring Training, but that could be because of the Arizona heat. He did get off to a good start last season, his first with Chicago, when he was 2-2 with a 2.18 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan is steady as she goes, looking to extend his streak of making 30-plus starts to nine seasons. Only Tom Glavine and Greg Maddux (12 seasons each) and Livan Hernandez (10 seasons) have longer active stretches than the durable Suppan, who also has worked at least 188 innings in every year since 1998.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster is back in the rotation for the first time, full-time since 2002. He spent the offseason getting in shape physically and building up endurance, and has looked sharp this spring. On the day, pitchers and catchers reported, he boldly predicted the Cubs would win the World Series. That's confidence.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Ned Yost had to choose between Bush and Carlos Villanueva for this assignment, and Bush was a somewhat surprising choice because he's 1-5 in eight career games against the Cubs and 0-2 (despite a 3.71 ERA) in four starts at Wrigley Field. That's history, argued Yost, who was impressed with Bush's Spring Training work on a slider and, to a lesser extent, a changeup.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers made a tremendous statement about their faith in the 24-year-old Villanueva with this assignment, which manager Ned Yost referred to as, "monster, mega Opening Day in Milwaukee." Villanueva was the surprise of 2007 Spring Training and won a spot in the bullpen, but this time had to battle his way into the '08 starting rotation with a 2.62 ERA in six Cactus League games.
away_pitcher_note: Although Sanchez always has wanted to start and the Giants have believed that is his destiny, he actually has performed better in relief (3-2, 4.40 ERA in 52 appearances) than as a starter (1-4, 7.27 ERA in eight games) during parts of two seasons in the Majors. Sanchez possesses electric stuff, as his 95 strikeouts in 92 innings reflect, but he frequently has struggled to repeat his delivery, which has impeded his progress.

home_pitcher_note: Parra re-established himself as a prospect last season after shoulder surgery, and now hits pay dirt. He impressed the Brewers in a brief stint last season (3.76 ERA in nine games, two starts) and would have had an opportunity to do more had he not fractured his left thumb on a bunt attempt in late August.
away_pitcher_note: Correia has never opened a Major League season in a starting rotation until now. He earned his shot by finishing 3-1 with a 2.54 ERA in eight starts at the conclusion of last season. In slightly more than three years in the Majors, Correia has made 27 starts and has allowed three earned runs or fewer in 22 of them. Correia posted a 3.84 road ERA last year, compared with 2.93 at home.

home_pitcher_note: After a marvelous outing on Opening Day (6 1/3 scoreless innings against the Cubs), Sheets makes his season debut at Miller Park, where he owns a career record of 38-37 with a 3.55 ERA in 100 starts. He is 3-2 with a 2.68 ERA against the Giants. Sheets will be among those glad to see Barry Bonds out of San Francisco's fold, since Bonds was 3-for-9 with two doubles and a home run against Sheets. Sheets will be working on an extra day of rest for the first of three times this month because Brewers manager Ned Yost elected to leave his five starters in order despite some off days.
away_pitcher_note: Zito complained of insufficient velocity on his fastball after his Opening Day start in Los Angeles, where he surrendered four runs and eight hits in five innings in a 5-0 loss to the Dodgers. Zito fared poorly against the Brewers last year, losing both of his starts to them while recording a 12.54 ERA -- his highest against any club. Ominously, each of those games was at Miller Park. Nevertheless, Zito owns a .580 career road winning percentage (58-42).

home_pitcher_note: Suppan got off to a nice start against the Cubs last week, holding Chicago to a pair of solo home runs in 6 1/3 innings of work. Now he returns home to Miller Park, where he was 9-3 last season with a 3.87 ERA (versus 3-9 with a 5.38 ERA on the road). Suppan also continued a trend of starting the season sharp; his career 4.08 ERA in April was better than any other month.
away_pitcher_note: Major League debuts don't get much better than what Cueto did in a 3-2 win over Arizona on Thursday at Great American Ball Park. The right-hander retired 21 of his 22 batters, including the first 15 in a row. In his seven-inning, 10 strikeout effort, the only hit allowed was a Justin Upton leadoff homer in the sixth inning. Cueto did not walk any batters, nor did he even reach a three-ball count at anytime vs. the D-backs. The right-hander blew hitters away with a fastball that ran inside, often at 96 mph. He also showed effective command of his hard slider and a changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Uncharacteristic control issues plagued the right-hander in Milwaukee's Thursday game at Chicago, with five walks and a hit batsman contributing greatly to a six-run allowance over 5 1/3 innings. In his career, Bush allows only one walk per 4 1/2 innings, so the outing was potentially just a blip on the radar in the blustery Wrigley Field conditions.
away_pitcher_note: In a lackluster debut for the Reds Friday vs. the Phillies, Fogg allowed six earned runs and five hits over four innings with three walks and three strikeouts. The right-hander lacked command all night and started 11 of his first 15 batters with a 1-0 count. Bad location led to a pair of home runs being hit against him. In 15 career starts vs. Milwaukee, Fogg is 6-4 with a 3.74 ERA. In 91 1/3 innings, he's allowed 12 home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Just 24 years old, Villanueva has already received plenty of kudos from manager and players alike with his unflappable nature, and he proved it in Milwaukee's home opener on Saturday. Though he allowed base hits to the last four batters he encountered, Villanueva preceded that with five shutout innings and picked up the victory.
away_pitcher_note: Although he's still looking for his first victory of the season, Harang pitched seven solid innings in his last start, on Saturday afternoon against the Phillies. Harang allowed just two runs on six hits, walked three and struck out six in a 108-pitch effort. The Phillies had the bases loaded with one out in the sixth, but Harang got the next two batters to end the inning. He is 3-1 with a 4.01 ERA in six starts at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Having pitched twice in relief last week and having not made a start in the big leagues since 2004, Figueroa has been chosen to replace disabled Pedro Martinez in the rotation -- for now. He has a 7-13 record and 5.17 ERA in 33 career starts in the big leagues. He is winless with two losses in his last four starts and hasn't won as a starter since he defeated the Brewers in August 2003.
away_pitcher_note: Parra recorded his first Major League victory after holding the Giants without a hit for five innings and finishing with two runs allowed in 5 1/3 frames. The lefty earned Milwaukee's fifth starter job out of Spring Training and looked more than capable in the first outing of 2008, hitting the radar gun as high as 97 mph in the first inning and effectively mixing his pitches. When Yovani Gallardo comes back in mid-April from a rehab assignment, the team will have a difficult decision facing it as to which starter?s spot Gallardo takes.

home_pitcher_note: Santana has pitched seven innings in each start and pitched well enough to win both. The Marlins and Braves have managed 12 base runners in 14 combined innings, and they have struck out 11 times. He has been, as advertised, yet he has split his first two decisions. He will be pitching with five-days rest. He has a 3-1 record and 3.32 ERA in against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets has not allowed a run in any of his first 15 1/3 innings, putting together back-to-back starts likely to rival any pair in his All-Star career. After 6 1/3 scoreless innings in rainy Wrigley Field on Opening Day, Sheets notched just the second shutout of his career -- and first since May 2001 -- with a dominant effort against San Francisco on Sunday. Sheets was on fire immediately, dismissing the first three batters on 11 pitches, and he needed just 109 to navigate the contest.

home_pitcher_note: Perez pitched in and out of trouble last Tuesday against the Phillies, walking three batters and hitting two. Still, his command was sharp enough to escape without any damage on the scoreboard, and he has yet to allow a run in 11 2/3 innings this season. Perez didn't face the Brewers last season, though he holds a 3-1 record and 4.32 ERA against them for his career.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan is Mr. April for Milwaukee and was on the verge of improving to 6-2 in the opening month since debuting with the team last season, only to see a win wiped away Tuesday. He worked six scoreless innings before a pair of seeing-eye singles led to a run in the seventh, and was in line for the win before Corey Patterson's two-out, two-strike home run off Eric Gagne in the ninth. Suppan has a 2.81 ERA in eight career starts against the Mets and a 2.70 ERA at Shea Stadium, numbers that don't include his eight scoreless innings in Game 6 of the 2006 NLCS for the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Things are going well for Looper thus far, which allows the Cardinals to give everyone an extra day of rest after the off-day Monday. He hit higher readings on the radar gun in his last start than he usually has managed as a starter, a very encouraging sign. If Looper can keep getting the ball low in the strike zone while also sitting in the low 90s, it will be a good year for the veteran right-hander.
away_pitcher_note: Bush has lost both of his starts, though he didn't get many breaks on Wednesday against the Reds. He's 1-3 with a 7.61 ERA in four career starts against the Cardinals, and he may need a solid outing to hold on to his spot in the starting rotation. The Brewers will have right-hander Yovani Gallardo back from the disabled list as early as this weekend, so Bush, Carlos Villanueva or Manny Parra must be bounced from the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright's last outing was a strange one, with some hard-hit balls but six strikeouts and no walks. It ended with a loss, but the total picture for the Cardinals' No. 1 starter is very good so far: 10 strikeouts, one walk, one home run and a solid groundball ratio. The Brewers are a good test for any pitcher, but he pitched solidly against them last year, going 1-1 with a 3.00 ERA in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva had no trouble at all with the top half of the Reds' potent batting order in his last start. The bottom five hitters, however, gave him trouble. He worked three full turns through the Cincinnati order and the top four hitters combined to go 0-for-11 with a walk. But the Reds' bottom five hitters combined to go 7-for-12 with four RBIs against Villanueva, with all four of the runs charged to the Brewers right-hander. He is 2-1 with a 2.70 ERA in eight career appearances against the Cards.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse finally gave up a run in his third St. Louis start, but he still pitched well enough for his second win. The Cardinals could easily be 3-0 in his games, since Lohse handed a lead to the bullpen in his debut, only to see it fade away. The right-hander has yet to allow a home run this year, which is a good way to keep winning even if your strikeout rate is low -- which his is through just three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The young lefty stayed out of trouble through three innings at Shea Stadium on Friday, but then faltered in the fourth, when New York scored three runs on four hits, a walk and a sacrifice fly. He was only at the 72-pitch mark, but was lifted for a pinch-hitter in the fifth inning when the Brewers had a runner at second base with two outs. Parra was not as sharp Friday as in his season debut, when he limited the Giants to three hits for his first Major League win. With Yovani Gallardo set to return from a rehab assignment, the team faces a difficult decision, and Parra's is one of the spots in doubt.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo has yet to pitch more than 5 2/3 innings in his first three starts this season. In a 4-3 loss to the Pirates on Saturday, the right-hander hurled five innings, with two of his three runs allowed being earned on six hits. Arroyo walked two and struck out three, but he ran his pitch count high to 102. Arroyo said he's been trying to not give into hitters who are sitting on his pitches and waiting for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets surrendered his first runs of the season in the first inning of Saturday's start in New York, but he retired 18 Mets in a row at one point and surrendered only one more run. He threw as many as 10 changeups and four or five outs came from that pitch, giving Sheets a potentially dangerous compliment to his fastball and curveball. He's 3-0 in four starts at Great American Ball Park.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto picked up his first career loss and issued his first walk, as the Reds fell to the Pirates, 9-1, on Sunday in his third big league start. The 22-year-old allowed five earned runs and five hits over six innings, with one free pass and six strikeouts. Cueto was having a decent afternoon, but a three-run sixth inning did the most damage. Cueto hung a 1-0 slider to Pirates right fielder Xavier Nady that was smoked for a two-run home run.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan surrendered six runs on eight hits through the first three innings against the Mets on Sunday, then worked around a hit during a scoreless fourth inning. It was an uncharacteristically shaky start for Suppan against a team he usually frustrates, and the righty will hope for a similar departure from history when he faces the Reds, against whom he has a 6.05 ERA in 11 career starts. He has a 7.49 ERA in six starts at Great American Ball Park.

home_pitcher_note: Not feeling well and not locating well, Harang was hit hard in a 9-5 loss to the Cubs on Tuesday at Wrigley Field. Over his six innings, the right-hander allowed five earned runs and eight hits with two walks and six strikeouts. When Harang gives up homers, they're usually solo shots, but that wasn't the case vs. Chicago. Two long balls were killers, including Mark DeRosa's two-run shot in the second inning and Derrek Lee's three-run blast in the fifth.
away_pitcher_note: This would have been Dave Bush's start, but he was bumped to make room for right-hander Yovani Gallardo's return from the disabled list. Bush has lost all three of his starts this season though he pitched better in St. Louis on Tuesday night, allowing three runs in six innings, all on two-out singles. Gallardo had his knee scoped during Spring Training and made three Minor League rehab starts to get to this point. He held the Reds to one run in 6 2/3 innings in his only start against them last season.

home_pitcher_note: It's a rematch for Villanueva of Wednesday in St. Louis, where he lasted only 4 2/3 innings and allowed five runs. Albert Pujols jumped on a 3-and-0 pitch in the first inning for a two-run double, then Villanueva locked with Rick Ankiel in a 17-pitch battle that ended in a walk. He needed 45 pitches to escape the first inning, ensuring a short night. He dropped to 2-2 against St. Louis with the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright tired a bit at the end of his last start, but nonetheless was charged with only two runs -- one earned -- in 7 2/3 innings. He's getting quick groundball outs, throwing strikes and keeping the ball in the park, and those things add up to pitching deep into games. Wainwright has gone at least seven innings in each of his three starts, which has been a valuable asset to a team that has relied heavily on its bullpen at times.

home_pitcher_note: Parra has not pitched more than four innings since his first outing of the season. In his last start Thursday in St. Louis, Parra allowed three earned runs on five hits, including a two-run fourth-inning single by Cardinals pitcher Kyle Lohse. Parra also gave up a homer, and issued a season-high five walks in Thursday's game that was won by the Brewers on Prince Fielder's two-run home run in the 10th inning.
away_pitcher_note: When you drive in as many runs as you allow, and your ERA goes up, it's probably been a pretty good season thus far. Lohse turned in another solid game, and he's showing no signs of backsliding. Lohse is throwing strikes -- five walks allowed in 24 1/3 innings. And he has yet to allow a home run in a Cardinals uniform. As long as he keeps limiting the free passes and the long balls, it's going to be a nice year.

home_pitcher_note: Bush, still looking for his first victory of the season, had his fourth start pushed back to allow for the return of Yovani Gallardo on Sunday. Bush allowed seven earned runs in 10 1/3 innings in two appearances against Philadelphia last season. He's 0-0 with a 6.23 ERA in four career appearances vs. the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Numbers-wise, Hamels' last outing was his worst this season. He surrendered five runs (four earned) on eight hits in a 6-4 loss to the New York Mets on Friday. But Hamels actually pitched well until he reached the eighth. That?s when he imploded, as the Mets scored three runs on four hits. Hamels is 1-0 lifetime against the Brewers, with a 3.60 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan pitched well for 6 2/3 innings Saturday at Cincinnati. He left with a 3-1 lead, but took a no-decision when Joey Votto tied the game with a two-run home run in the eighth off Brian Shouse. Suppan allowed two earned runs on just three hits, walked one and struck out three. It was an improvement from his previous outing at New York, in which he lasted just four innings. Suppan threw just 87 pitches Saturday, meaning he should be well-rested to make his fifth start.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer is coming off two good starts in his last three outings. He went six innings and yielded just two runs on seven hits in losing his first start this season, 4-2, on Saturday against the Mets. Moyer, who saw his ERA drop from 5.52 to 4.79 in the loss, is 8-5 with a 3.69 ERA lifetime against Milwaukee, though ht got thumped in his only start against the Brewers last season, surrendering five runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo's return to the rotation was well worth the wait, even if he didn't get a win. The 22-year-old underwent knee surgery in Spring Training, but was sharp in his season debut despite a dreary Cincinnati afternoon, holding the Reds to a run on four hits in seven innings. His return could not have come at a better time for the Brewers, who are holding their breath while ace Ben Sheets rests a sore right arm. Gallardo was especially good at Miller Park last season, going 5-2 with a 2.77 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen remains the team's most effective starter, as he comes off his third straight start that lasted at least seven innings. The 24-year-old beat the Nationals in his latest outing, giving up one run -- a homer to Austin Kearns -- in seven innings. Olsen allowed just three hits, and carried a no-hitter into the fifth before Kearns opened with the homer. For his career, Olsen is 1-1 with a 3.44 ERA in three games against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Villanueva faced the Cardinals for the second time in five days, and the second outing was certainly was an improvement over the first, when he needed 45 pitches to escape the first inning (17 of those were spent on Cardinals outfielder Rick Ankiel) and was finished after the fourth. In his most recent start, Villanueva limited the Cards to two runs on three hits in seven innings but did walk four batters, two of them with two outs in the third inning, before Troy Glaus cashed in with a two-run double. Villanueva did not allow a run in three appearances against the Marlins last season, all in relief.
away_pitcher_note: After a poor outing on Opening Day, Hendrickson has been one of the hottest starters in baseball during his past four starts. Hendrickson has won each of them, allowing only seven earned runs and 22 hits in 25 2/3 innings. He worked eight strong innings his previous time out during a 10-4 win against Pittsburgh Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Parra was down on himself after allowing three runs in five innings of a no-decision against the Cardinals on Tuesday, even though he was in line for his second Major League win before second baseman Rickie Weeks botched a double-play relay. Parra hasn't pitched past the sixth inning in any of his four starts and hasn't pitched into the sixth since his season debut. He isn't commanding any of his four pitches and said after his last outing, "I'm off. I'm very inconsistent right now. I'm in a rut. It shouldn't be that difficult."
away_pitcher_note: One out away from escaping trouble and being in line for the win, Nolasco gave up four straight hits in the sixth inning of his last start. The end result was a disappointing loss on a night when he actually pitched his best game. Nolasco allowed three runs -- all with two outs and no one on base to start with -- in a loss at Pittsburgh. Otherwise, he had a pretty strong night. Nolasco logged his first quality start of the season -- three runs in six innings. The Marlins ended up losing 3-2. The right-hander logged a season-high 90 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis had another strong start Thursday, earning a no-decision in Colorado in a game the Cubs went on to lose. For the first six innings, he neatly matched his previous outing against the Pirates, giving up one run on six hits. He added two more hits and another run in the seventh, however, yielding a solo homer to Chris Iannetta on a sinker meant to go down and away that came back over the plate. He threw 98 pitches over seven innings for his longest start of the season, striking out four while walking two.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets is slated to return to the rotation after missing his last turn with soreness in his right triceps. He exited a start against the Reds after five innings with the ailment, which he said began back on April 12 in New York. The Brewers need a healthy Sheets back in action because he's off to a great start: he leads the NL in WHIP at 0.64 and opponents are hitting only .146 against him. He allowed two hits in no runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Cubs on Opening Day and will get a boost in this game by the return of center fielder Mike Cameron from a suspension.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster matched his longest outing of the season in his last start against the Nationals. He gave up three runs -- two earned -- on four hits over seven innings but a couple walks hurt him. The right-hander also struck out five. He had some trouble in the first when he had two outs, then walked Ryan Zimmerman on four pitches and served up a homer to Nick Johnson. It was a 26-pitch first inning, and Dempster can't afford to start like that.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan does not have much to show for some solid outings this season. He's allowed two or fewer runs in four of his five starts including Thursday, when he limited the Phillies to one run over seven innings and exited a 1-1 tie that turned into a Brewers loss. Dating to last season, Suppan is 5-1 with a 3.69 ERA in his last 11 starts. His lone win this season came at the Cubs' expense, an 8-2 Brewers win at Wrigley Field on April 2 in which Suppan allowed two runs (on a pair of solo homers) on six hits in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Big Z is in a good groove right now. Zambrano beat the Nationals in his last start, striking out five over seven scoreless innings. He did walk a season-high four, but was able to escape jams. That's a good sign. Zambrano also gave the overworked bullpen a breather. He faced Milwaukee on Opening Day and did not get a decision. In that game, he held the Brewers to three hits over 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: While health questions continue to dog perennial Milwaukee Brewers ace Ben Sheets, the team appears to have another ace in the making. Gallardo made it two straight excellent starts since his return from the 15-day disabled list (knee surgery), going seven scoreless innings on Friday in Milwaukee. Gallardo has allowed just one run in 14 innings of work over two starts. The only problem -- he's gotten just one run of run support and has been saddled with two no-decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt took a no-decision in his last outing on Saturday in St. Louis, allowing three hits over six innings and leaving with the game tied at 3 after the sixth. Oswalt has held opponents to three or fewer runs in his last three starts after starting the season 0-3 with a 9.00 ERA. Oswalt faced the Brewers three times last year, taking two losses and a no-decision. He yielded a combined 12 runs over 19 2/3 innings. Lifetime versus Milwaukee, Oswalt is 11-8 with a 3.66 ERA over 23 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva recorded his second straight quality start -- and no-decision -- when he battled the Florida Marlins on Saturday. The right-hander permitted two runs on six hits in six innings and did not walk a batter -- a welcome circumstance after 11 walks in his first 23 innings of the year. While seldom overpowering, Villanueva has done his best to remove his name from consideration for a demotion to the bullpen when Ben Sheets returns to the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Backe had four good innings and one really bad inning against the Cardinals on Sunday. The right-hander allowed three hits through the first four innings but was roughed up for four runs in the fifth, including a two-run double by Ryan Ludwick and a two-run home run by Troy Glaus. In five innings, he allowed four runs on five hits, walked five and struck out four. In six starts this season, Backe has only pitched more than five innings twice and has allowed three or more runs in each of his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Parra had a so-so outing on Sunday against Florida, allowing two runs on six hits with three walks in 5 1/3 inning. Parra's inability to escape the sixth inning in any of his starts this season remains a significant factor. "That's the only important thing to me right now," Parra said. "Obviously keeping the team in the game, but if you're going deep in the game, you're probably keeping your team in the game."

home_pitcher_note: Sampson yielded five runs over 4 1/3 innings but felt he pitched better than his stat line indicated. He had one big inning in the fourth, when he yielded a leadoff walk to Orlando Hudson and later gave up a two-run double to Mark Reynolds. Of Sampson's last three outings, he was effective only once. He'll face the Brewers for the first time this season and the fourth time in his career. In 2007, he appeared twice against Milwaukee, allowing three runs over seven innings. Lifetime, Sampson is 1-0 with a 4.00 ERA over three appearances, having allowed four runs over nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets returned to action after missing a turn in the rotation with a sore triceps and was not at his best. He set a career high with seven walks in just five innings, but he also limited the Cubs to three hits and escaped with his perfect record in tact and his 10th career win over the Cubs. He also has 10 wins over the Astros to go with a 3.78 lifetime ERA in 24 starts.

home_pitcher_note: After four straight starts of lasting at least seven innings, Olsen had a rough outing on Wednesday. The lefty also suffered his first loss, giving up four runs in a season-low five innings against the Dodgers. It also was the first time in six starts the Marlins lost with Olsen on the mound. Olsen now gets to face the Brewers for the second time in three starts. On April 25 at Miller Park, he gutted out 7 1/3 innings of scoreless ball. He yielded four hits that day, and for the first time in his career he didn't log a strikeout.
away_pitcher_note: The Soup was cold at Wrigley Field. Suppan surrendered 11 runs for the first time in his career, though three were unearned, and he coughed up 11 Cubs hits without escaping the fourth inning. It was a sour end to what had been a good month for Suppan, who entered the game 1-0 with a 3.48 ERA despite a no-decision in New York on April 13 in which he was charged with six runs in four innings. Suppan missed the Marlins when they visited Miller Park last week but he's 4-3 with a 3.50 ERA against them in 11 career matchups.

home_pitcher_note: At a time the Marlins needed a starter to step up, Badenhop came through in his last start. While he wasn't involved in the decision -- so he's still searching for his first big league win -- the 25-year-old turned in his first quality start, allowing three runs in six innings against the Dodgers. His six innings and six strikeouts both were personal highs in his five MLB appearances. A sinkerball pitcher, the right-hander induced eight groundball outs to four in the air. This will be his first outing against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Bush was recalled to replace injured right-hander Yovani Gallardo, who was lost to a serious knee injury and might need surgery. Bush was demoted to Triple-A Nashville a week earlier when Ben Sheets was deemed clear of a minor arm injury, and took a no-decision in his only start for the Sounds. He allowed three runs, only one of which was earned, on three hits while striking out seven batters over six innings against Colorado Springs. Bush is 1-1 with a 5.73 ERA in two starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: A year ago, the lefty went 4-8 with the Dodgers. In his last start, a seven-inning outing against the Padres, he collected his fifth win of the young season. Hendrickson remains economical with his pitches, tossing just 81 in beating San Diego. The Marlins are 5-2 in his seven starts. And since losing to Johan Santana and the Mets on Opening Day, he hasn't given up more than three earned runs in six straight outings. This will be his second start in three appearances against the Brewers. At Miller Park on April 26, he gave up two earned runs in six innings in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva retired 12 of the first 13 Astros hitters he faced on Friday but then surrendered hits to eight of the next 10. Four of those hits were home runs, including three in a row to sluggers Miguel Tejada, Lance Berkman and Carlos Lee as a 4-0 Brewers lead slipped away. None of the those three pitches were any good, said manager Ned Yost, who has been frustrated by Villanueva's propensity for allowing quick strikes by opponents. He allowed two runs in six innings against the Marlins at Miller Park on the Brewers' last homestand and took a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Parra has not pitched more than 5 1/3 innings in any of his six starts, and that fact is starting to upset him. He lasted only four-plus frames against the Astros on Saturday, taking a 1-1 tie into the fifth inning and then allowing a five-run outburst sparked by back-to-back homers by the opposing pitcher, Brandon Backe, and slumping leadoff man Michael Bourne. Parra has great pure stuff -- a 92-94 mph fastball and three serviceable offspeed pitches -- but he has been up in the strike zone way to often, manager Ned Yost said. He has already started twice against the Cardinals, taking a pair of no-decisions while allowing six earned runs in nine total innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer lasted just five innings in his last start, on Sunday against the Cubs, which matched his shortest start of the season. The right-hander allowed two runs on three hits, struck out four and walked four. He threw 95 pitches, with 57 for strikes. In his next start, Wellemeyer will have to find a way to be more efficient with his pitches and try to get through six or seven innings to give the bullpen a break.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers and Cardinals have already played series at Miller Park and at Busch Stadium, but Sheets managed to miss both matchups. He probably didn't mind; Sheets is 5-14 in 23 career starts against the Cardinals with a 4.30 ERA. Pittsburgh is the only other National League Central rival against whom Sheets has a losing record (he's 6-8 against the Pirates). Sheets worked 6 1/3 innings against the Astros in his last start and showed no signs of the triceps injury that dogged him last month. He's one strikeout shy of Teddy Higuera's franchise record (1,081).
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro lasted only three innings and three batters Monday in Colorado, leaving the game after failing to retire a hitters in the fourth, yielding three hits and two runs -- one earned -- that inning after already allowing five hits and two runs in the first three innings.  His problems were compounded by his fourth inning at bat, when he swung and missed at a pitch that struck his right forearm as he completed his swing.  He had trouble keeping his breaking pitches down in his first Coors Field start, and he left too many pitches over the middle of the plate.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan improved over a tough outing in Chicago when he matched up against the Marlins on Tuesday, but he still was not particularly sharp, allowing three runs on eight hits in five innings and needing help from the bullpen to escape a bases-loaded, no-out jam in the sixth inning. Suppan needed to be virtually perfect because he matched up against Marlins ace Scott Olsen, who twice was one strike away from a two-hit shutout before settling for an 8 2/3-inning win. The Brewers have already played a pair of series against the Cardinals, Suppan's former team, but he did not pitch either time. He's 5-2 with a 3.32 ERA in nine career starts against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Looper pitched a gem Tuesday night in Colorado, making it to the ninth inning for the first time in his professional career. He held the Rockies two runs through eight, then let two more slip in before leaving in the ninth, finishing with 8 1/3 innings and 114 pitches. His sinker and his splitter were both on, and he made the Rox put the ball in play, walking none and striking out one, keeping the ball from the fat of the barrel. He made a couple mistakes, but until the ninth, they were isolated, allowing him to minimize the damage.

home_pitcher_note: Bush keeps getting burned by a few poorly placed pitches. That was the case again on Wednesday in Miami, when he returned to the rotation to replace an injured Yovani Gallardo and was roughed up for six runs in six innings. The Brewers were only trailing, 3-2, entering the sixth inning, but Bush surrendered a two-run home run to Jorge Cantu followed by a Dan Uggla solo shot. "He just can't get away with a mistake right now," manager Ned Yost said. Bush lost to the Cardinals in St. Louis on April 15 in his only quality start (three or fewer earned runs in six or more innings) this season.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright was on his game in Colorado, throwing seven shutout innings and earning a no decision in a game the bullpen lost in the eighth.  He avoided his curve against the Rockies, pitching off his fastball and using a four-seam changeup effectively against righties.  Wainwright excelled at limiting traffic, keeping Colorado from having multiple men reach base in all but one inning.  He relished the chance to pitch at Coors Field - after the fact, anyway - noting that it forced him to tighten his attention to mechanics, staying out front on his pitches and keeping the ball down in the zone.

home_pitcher_note: Villanueva has lost his last four decisions and has really struggled in his last two starts, allowing 13 runs and 19 hits in 10 innings of losses at Houston and at Florida. In his most recent seven innings of work, Villanueva has surrendered six home runs, including back-to-back-to-back homers to the heart of the Astros lineup, and then a pair of two-out shots against the Marlins. It's a surprisingly inconsistent start to the season for a guy who posted a 1.99 ERA in six Brewers appearances last September, five of them starts, to cement his spot in the 2008 starting rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Penny didn't get hard by the Mets on Wednesday, but he was hit often. He either fell behind in counts, or when he got ahead, couldn't put away hitters while allowing a career-high 10 runs. He didn't complete five innings. Penny threw seven shutout innings against the Brewers last year and is 3-2 lifetime, but in his only Miller Park start, he allowed five runs in seven innings and drew a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Parra still has not pitched more than 5 1/3 innings in any of his seven starts, but he probably could have passed that threshold on Friday against the Cardinals. He surrendered three early runs, then settled down over his final three innings and retired the final nine men he faced. Parra was only at 83 pitches when he was lifted for a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the fifth inning, and admitted he wanted to keep working. "When I missed, I missed down," he said. "That's something to build on."
away_pitcher_note: Lowe followed his Coors Field disaster with another rough start at home against the Astros, allowing six runs in 5 1/3 innings. Traditionally an innings-eater, Lowe hasn't gone more than 5 1/3 innings in any of his last five starts, but he's shown no signs that anything is wrong physically.

home_pitcher_note: In his previous outing, Sheets surpassed Brewers great Ted Higuera for tops on the club's career strikeout list, striking out six Cardinals to give him 1,086. He allowed three runs and nine hits with a walk over seven innings. Until Jeff Suppan picked up a win Sunday, Sheets was the only Brewers starter to win a game since Manny Parra on April 5. Sheets is among the National League's top 10 in wins and ERA, along with hits and walks per innings.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley barely survived the first two innings against the Astros, giving up five runs on six hits and two walks, but then settled down and retired the last nine batters he faced. He has faced the Brewers twice in his career, giving up three earned runs in 1 2/3 innings. He will be pitching on his regular four days' rest, as the Dodgers utilize days off to go with a four-man rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka is looking for his seventh win in eight starts this season. After a season-high eight walks on May 5 in Detroit, Matsuzaka settled down last Saturday in Minnesota and issued three over his seven innings, allowing six hits and two runs while earning his second win of the month. The right-hander will look to become the fourth Red Sox hurler this decade to start a season 7-0, joining Josh Beckett (9-0 in 2007), John Burkett (7-0, 2002) and Pedro Martinez (7-0, 2002).
away_pitcher_note: Suppan will be facing the team with which he broke into the Major Leagues in 1995 and spent parts of three seasons, going 7-9 with a 6.10 ERA in 29 outings at Fenway Park. He will hope for better results as the Brewers begin Interleague Play and is coming off one of his best starts this season, a seven-inning, one-run performance against the Cardinals at Miller Park. The win snapped Suppan's two-game losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: The knuckleballer is coming off his shortest outing since Sept. 2003, allowing seven hits and seven runs -- six earned -- in just 2 2/3 innings last Sunday night at Minnesota. Wakefield has had an up and down month, going 1-2 with a 4.58 ERA in three starts. Wakefield is looking forward to returning to Fenway Park. The right-hander is 3-1 this season with a 2.95 ERA on grass in five starts. He is 0-1 with a 7.36 ERA in three starts on turf.
away_pitcher_note: Bush put together his best start this season against the Cardinals on Monday, allowing a Rick Ankiel home run with two outs in the first inning but then blanking St. Louis through the end of the sixth. It was his first win this season and his second win in 11 starts dating to last year, when Bush tied for the team lead with 12 victories. It's been a much tougher road this year, but Bush found success in his most recent start by using the inner half of the plate, somewhat of a departure from pitching coach Mike Maddux's philosophy.

home_pitcher_note: Beckett will pitch the series finale against the Brewers, replacing Clay Buchholz, who's on the DL with a broken fingernail. Beckett struggled in his last start, allowing five runs on 11 hits in a loss to the Orioles. Beckett faced the Brewers three times when he was on the Marlins, going 0-2 with a 9.53 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva moved to the third-base side of the rubber and got much better results on Tuesday. He surrendered three Dodgers runs, two of them earned, on eight hits, but didn't walk a batter and retired nine of the final 10 he faced for his first win since the Brewers' April 4 home opener. He was only at the 82-pitch mark when manager Ned Yost opted for a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the sixth inning. "As far as I was concerned, with what has gone on for him lately, he had done his job and I wanted him out of there with a chance to win the ballgame," Yost said. "I felt like he could leave on a really, really good note and build on that."

home_pitcher_note: Despite picking up his fourth road loss of the season, Maholm was encouraged by the quality and crispness of his pitches. He did, however, allow 11 hits, a total that he has now reached twice already this season. Though don't be completely fooled by that total as four of those 11 were either infield singles or bloop hits. The good news is that Maholm's next start is at PNC Park, where the lefty is 14-9 with a 3.50 ERA in his career. This will be Maholm's first start against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: In his eighth start, Parra worked more than 5 1/3 innings for the first time this season and was in line to win for the first time since his season debut on April 5, only to see the Dodgers rally late at Miller Park. Parra should have been through the seventh inning with a 4-1 lead, but a couple of miscues behind him forced Parra to settle for 6 2/3 innings with seven hits and three runs, just one of them earned. It was a big step forward for Parra, who touched 96 mph on the stadium radar gun and worked more aggressively than in previous outings. He has never faced the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Snell continues to be mystified by his season-long struggles. The right-hander's pitches haven't been crisp. His command hasn't been sharp. And now his confidence is beginning to waver. Venting visible frustration after his last start, Snell said he is now at a loss for what the culprit is for his struggles. Snell has never faced the Brewers, but will head into the start trying to do less nibbling around the plate and get back to trusting his stuff.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets is coming off a strange start against the Dodgers in which he allowed two hits and no runs through six innings, then surrendered six runs and three home runs in the seventh. Manager Ned Yost said Sheets had no physical ailments, and Sheets admitted he didn�t know what went wrong. "I'd like to say I know what went wrong," Sheets said after suffering his first loss this season. "I'd like to be able to fix something." He called it the worst inning of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Mercifully, Gorzelanny won't be facing a club with 'Chicago' laced across the front of its uniform. Take away the left-hander's woes against the Cubs this season (three starts, 11 total innings, 21 runs), and Gorzelanny's numbers aren't so bad. His command has only sporadically matched that which he showed a year ago, however, and his fastball still clocks in about two to three mph slower than it did in 2007. The lefty needs to get his pitches down.
away_pitcher_note: Bush has had some trouble of late getting the third out. All five Red Sox runs against him in Game 2 of a doubleheader on Saturday scored with two outs, though one was unearned. Bush surrendered a two-out, two-run double to Mike Lowell on a curveball down and away in the first inning, then misplaced a fastball to Lowell in the third and saw it go for a two-out, two run home run. Thirteen of the 28 earned runs that Bush has surrendered this season have scored with two outs.

home_pitcher_note: Perez started last Friday, and a defensive miscue was his undoing against the Orioles. In the first inning, Melvin Mora hit a line drive to left over Wily Mo Pena's glove for a double on a catchable ball. Mora then scored on a single by Nick Markakis. In the third, things got worse for Perez. Brian Roberts led off and hit a fly ball near the left-field line. The ball was up in the air long enough to be caught, but it dropped in for a double. Roberts scored on a single by Mora. Markakis then hit a two-run homer. Perez, who lasted five innings and gave up six runs on 10 hits, blamed himself for the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan will be facing a former team for the third straight start, having defeated the Cardinals and lost to the Red Sox in his last two outings. In Boston, he surrendered all four of his runs in the first two innings, all with two outs, but then settled in. After throwing 54 pitches in his first two innings of work, Suppan held the Red Sox scoreless over the next four frames on 43 pitches. Brewers manager Ned Yost elected to give Suppan an extra day of rest after he warmed up for Friday's game that was rained out, then warmed up again the following afternoon.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Manny Acta usually doesn't compare his players to future Hall of Famers, but after watching Lannan pitch one of his best games in a 2-1 victory over the Orioles last Sunday, Acta called Lannan's performance Greg Maddux-esque. Lannan pitched 7 1/3 innings and gave up one run on four hits. In his first seven innings, Lannan had 10 ground-ball outs and allowed only two hits. He threw 94 pitches by that time, including 74 for strikes. The only time the Orioles had runners in scoring position during those seven innings was in the sixth, when Melvin Mora hit a two-out double.
away_pitcher_note: McClung replaces right-hander Carlos Villanueva, who was bumped to the bullpen after posting a 9.00 ERA in four May starts. Brewers manager Ned Yost figures to get about 75 pitches out of McClung, a hard-thrower who has made 37 Major League starts for the Rays, but had pitched exclusively in relief since joining the Brewers late last season.

home_pitcher_note: Redding wasn't sharp last Monday, giving up seven hits in 6 1/3 innings against the Phillies, but he managed to get his sixth win of the season. He believes that he is pitching the quality innings that he did for the Astros in 2003. The difference is that he is getting more run support.
away_pitcher_note: Parra was effective against the Pirates on Tuesday, but not efficient. He held Pittsburgh scoreless through 5 2/3 innings, with just four hits and one walk, but needed 116 pitches to do it. It was the second straight strong outing for Parra, who has surrendered one earned run in his last 11 2/3 innings over two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bergmann has been great since coming back from the Minors. He threw seven shutout innings in a 1-0 victory over the Mets, and the right-hander did it again against the Phillies. Bergmann was in trouble just once, when the Phillies loaded the bases with two outs in the seventh, but Bergmann got Shane Victorino to line out to center.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets bounced back from what he called the worst inning of his career with one of his best starts. He surrendered six Dodgers runs and three home runs in the seventh inning on May 15, then returned six days later with the 15th complete game of his career, scattering 11 hits including a solo home run in a 4-1 win at Pittsburgh. Sheets threw a season-high 123 pitches and went the distance for the second time this season, improving to 4-0 with a 2.29 ERA on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: It has been a one step forward, two steps back kind of season for Bush, who tied for the team lead with 12 wins in each of the last two seasons but has already been demoted to the Minors once this year. He took another step back on Thursday in Pittsburgh, allowing only a cheap infield single through three scoreless innings and then six earned runs and two home runs over the next two frames. Four of the runs scored with two outs, continuing a trend, and manager Ned Yost did not exactly give Bush a ringing endorsement after the game when asked if he would consider further changes to the starting rotation. Bush allowed one run in seven innings against the Braves last season in his only career start against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson bested Johan Santana in a much-anticipated duel on Thursday, allowing two runs in eight innings in the Braves' 4-2 win over the Mets. Hudson gave up seven hits, including two home runs. He shook off the back-to-back homers and struck out four. Hudson didn't allow a baserunner to reach third over the next six innings of work. He threw 100 pitches, none more important than his last, when he induced an inning-ending double play to end the Mets' threat in the eighth.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan was in complete control for the majority of his outing against the Nationals, but a defensive error triggered a four-run inning that didn't count against his ERA, but tagged him with the loss. Manager Ned Yost was effusive in his praise, calling the 89-pitch outing one of Suppan's best this season. The righty will try to build on that momentum against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: The Braves are high on Reyes and understand that his battle to find consistent control will play a big role in their bid to win a division title. The 23-year-old southpaw regressed on Friday night, when he struggled to control his fastball and was facing a five-run deficit before recording his third out of the evening. If he finds his control, the Braves believe he has the stuff to be a future front-line starter.

home_pitcher_note: McClung turned in a terrific performance in his first Major League start in two years. He used first-pitch strikes to keep his pitch count low. Despite throwing just 68 pitches, he made it through five innings and picked up the win. McClung is a viable candidate for the fifth spot in the Brewers rotation, and his start against the Braves will be closely analyzed with that in mind.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo left after the fourth inning of Saturday's start against the D-backs, but the 29-year-old reliever-turned-starter said he expects to make his next start Thursday against the Brewers. As a starter, Campillo has not allowed an earned run. In 10 innings, he has given up just six hits. Campillo has three blisters on his index and middle fingers, and said it hurts when he grips the seams.

home_pitcher_note: Parra had mixed results in his outing in Washington, but was saved by an offensive comeback and recorded a no-decision. He struggled towards the end to keep pitches away from the center of the plate, and when he served up a 91-mph fastball to Aaron Boone that turned into a home run, it was the end of his day. He remains a solid starting option, but has work to do to become as consistent as teammates Ben Sheets or Jeff Suppan.
away_pitcher_note:
Backe has been pitching well of late, with consecutive wins (at Texas and vs. Philadelphia) in his last two outings. Better command has been a factor as Backe has walked just two batters total in his last three starts. 
Backe lost at St. Louis on April 27 when he allowed four earned runs in five innings in a 5-1 loss to Kyle Lohse and the Cardinals. The right-hander is 2-2 with a 5.86 ERA in 11 career appearances vs. St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets had a solid outing against Washington, picking up a no-decision after leaving the game in a pinch-hitting situation with a total of 86 pitches. He allowed a pair of runs early before settling into a groove and pitching four scoreless innings. His fastball was sharp, hitting 96 regularly on the radar gun, and he was in command of his breaking pitches. Sheets is one of the team's best players right now, and will open the series against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Although he was considered a fill-in for the injured Wandy Rodriguez, Moehler will remain in the rotation while Chris Sampson moves to the bullpen. Moehler made a case to stay in the rotation after going 2-1 with a 3.43 ERA over four starts. He pitched five innings in his first three outings and six innings in his most recent, which translated into a win over the Phillies. In his career, Moehler is 3-6 with a 4.21 ERA over 17 appearances versus Milwaukee, including eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bush surrendered solo home runs in each of the first two innings on Tuesday against Atlanta, then found a groove. He faced one batter more than the minimum over his final 5 2/3 innings of work, and pitched seven full frames for the first time this season. His only relief appearance this season came in Houston, just after Bush was recalled from a very brief stint in the Minor Leagues. He has surrendered at least one home run in five straight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon extended his winning "streak" to two games after logging a very convincing win over the Cardinals in his last start. The right-hander held St. Louis to two runs over seven innings, yielding two solo homers. Chacon also didn't walk anyone and struck out seven. He will face the Brewers for the first time this year. Lifetime versus Milwaukee, Chacon is 1-2 with a 3.33 ERA and two saves over 12 appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan is coming off of his best performance of the season as he allowed just two hits to the Braves on Wednesday over eight scoreless innings. Suppan recorded his sixth quality start of the season and the Brewers offense woke up just in time to give him his third win. While he walked a season-high five batters, Suppan was able to avoid trouble by striking out a season-high seven and riding two key double plays by the Brewers defense. Suppan's last start against Arizona came was a loss on Aug. 22 of last season in which he gave up three runs on seven hits over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davis scuffled in his last start as he allowed six runs on nine hits over five innings to the Giants. It was quite a contrast to his previous start. In that one, his first big league outing since undergoing surgery on April 10 to remove a cancerous thyroid, Davis was outstanding against the Braves in an 11-1 Arizona win. The lefty allowed just one run on five hits over seven innings and did not show any signs of fatigue late in the game. The left-hander had been on the disabled list since he started April 8 against the Dodgers. Davis made two rehab starts for Triple-A Tucson.

home_pitcher_note: In his second start since moving from the bullpen to the rotation, McClung was charged with six runs on eight hits and six walks in just 4 2/3 innings. Two of the runs scored after McClung exited the game and two of the walks were intentional, but it was nonetheless a step back from his first start. "I know the walks were staggering, but the pitches were there, they were close," said McClung, who has a history of wildness and was traded from Tampa Bay to Milwaukee last season. "It was definitely competitive. I don't feel like I went out there and just gave it up. There are some game tapes in Tampa if you want to see totally wild."
away_pitcher_note: Johnson continues to get better with each passing start. He should have gotten a win last Thursday night after allowing just two runs in seven innings to the Giants, but the Arizona bullpen could not hold a 3-2 lead. In his start before that against the Braves, he allowed just one run over six innings, did not walk a batter and fanned 10. Johnson had won his previous three starts to give him 288 for his career. Johnson tied Roger Clemens (4,672) for second place on the all-time strikeout list in his last start. He has 210 career double-digit strikeout games, five shy of Nolan Ryan's record.

home_pitcher_note: Parra has a lot to build on coming into this start against the Diamondbacks. The lefty had one of his best performances of the season in Friday's win against Houston. Against an Astros lineup that is fourth in the league in runs scored, and especially good against left-handed pitching, Parra picked up his third win and managed to pitch six solid innings while only allowing one run on six hits. The rookie credited the work he's done between starts with catcher Jason Kendall and the coaches for his improvement.
away_pitcher_note: Owings didn't have his best stuff Friday night against the Nationals and battled through 6 1/3 innings. The big blow came when Willie Harris touched him for a three-run homer with one out in the seventh. That broke open a 3-3 game and sent the Nats on the way to the win. It was the second straight shaky start for Owings. In his previous outing, he allowed three runs over six innings to the Braves, but got the win as the Arizona offense scored nine runs. Owings struck out a career-best 10 on May 20 in Florida.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez was hit on his left knee by a line drive from Cubs shortstop Ryan Theriot in his last start but he'll take the hill Friday against the Brewers. Jimenez allowed four runs, three earned, on seven hits and three walks to take the loss against the Cubs. The right-hander's lone win this season came in his second start of the year when he defeated the Braves. This will be his fist career start against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets came tantalizingly close to his third complete game of the season Saturday, working 8 2/3 innings and allowing just one run on seven hits. An 11-pitch walk to Lance Berkman with nobody on in the ninth prompted manager Ned Yost to pull his ace after 122 pitches. The right-hander was frustrated with the decision, but he was still pleased with an outing that marked the fifth quality start by a Brewers pitcher in six outings.

home_pitcher_note: Reynolds struggled to find any rhythm in his last start and after five outings, the left-hander is still looking for his first big league win. Against the Dodgers, Reynolds allowed six runs, four earned on seven hits and three walks with one strikeout over five innings for the loss and his earliest exit this year. This will be his first career appearance against the Brewers and third start at home.
away_pitcher_note: Bush seems to have found at least a temporary answer to the struggles that have haunted him this season, delivering his second straight quality start Sunday in a Brewers victory. Bush worked seven innings and allowed four hits, with one fence-scraping home run in the first inning accounting for the only tally. The Brewers backed him with 10 runs worth of support, but Bush also helped himself by not walking anybody. He has one walk in his last three starts (19 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Francis pitched more to his 2007 form than the struggles of this year. The left-hander led the staff with 17 wins last season but had just one victory to his credit this year until his last start when he shut out the Dodgers over seven innings on four hits and two walks. He also struck out five. Francis is 2-2 in his career against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: After posting a 2.56 ERA in his five May starts, Suppan started June on a solid note, allowing three D-backs runs in seven innings of a no-decision on Monday at Miller Park. He has surrendered three runs in 15 innings of his last two starts, both Brewers wins. Suppan has had success against the Rockies; he's 5-1 against them with a 3.58 ERA in eight starts including 2-0 with a 4.34 ERA in three starts at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt's breaking stuff was better in his last start, against the Pirates on Wednesday, but it still wasn't enough to win. The right-hander, with no help from a sluggish defense, yielded four runs (three earned) over six innings in a loss. Oswalt faced the Brewers in Houston on May 2, earning his third win after yielding four runs (three earned) over six frames.
away_pitcher_note: McClung's two hits against Arizona's Randy Johnson might have been the story on June 3 had McClung not pitched so well. He allowed a run on six hits in six solid innings and might have kept pitching had the Brewers not taken their first lead of the game in the bottom of the sixth inning. McClung did not walk a batter and was only at 79 pitches, but manager Ned Yost elected to remove him from the game with a chance to win it, and two relievers preserved McClung's victory. He has not faced the Astros this season in any of his 11 relief appearances or his three starts.

home_pitcher_note: After winning two games in a row, Backe has lost his last two starts. His most recent defeat came against the Pirates, who scored four runs off the right-hander over six frames. Backe faced the Brewers at Minute Maid Park on May 3, earning the win after holding Milwaukee to two runs over 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Parra has strung together consecutive quality starts, allowing one run and four hits in each of his last two outings. He worked six innings to beat the Astros on May 30, then came back to pitch a career-high seven innings on June 4 against the D-backs. He matched a career high with eight strikeouts in his most recent start and retired the last 14 hitters he faced. "We believe that we found my key, mechanically, so if I start rushing a little bit, Mike [Maddux, the pitching coach] is able to tell me a little key word that kind of gets me back on track," Parra said.

home_pitcher_note: Brian Moehler is coming of his best outing of the season, a seven-shutout-inning, two-hit effort against the Cardinals on Friday. The Astros have won four of his six starts. The right-hander lost to the Brewers on May 31 at Miller Park after allowing four runs over five innings, including a two-run homer to Prince Fielder.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets finally conquered Coors Field in his last outing, limiting the Rockies to a run in six innings of a no-decision on Friday. He should greatly benefit from the move back to sea level after abandoning his signature curveball in the thin Denver air. Sheets took a no-decision in a start at Minute Maid Park on May 5, when he surrendered four runs in 6 1/3 innings and was in line for the win before an Eric Gagne blown save.

home_pitcher_note: When Bush gets through the first inning, he's usually OK. In his 11 first innings this season, opponents have batted .319 (15-for-47) with four doubles, five home runs and seven walks. He has surrendered more runs (11), hits and homers in the first inning than in any other frame. Bush has surrendered a first-inning homer in each of his last three starts, including two on Saturday at Coors Field, a grand slam to Brad Hawpe and a Chris Iannetta solo shot on the next pitch. Bush has surrendered a first-inning homer four times this season, but before Saturday, all of those games ended in Brewers wins. Bush is 2-1 with a 3.45 ERA in his five Miller Park starts, vs. 0-5 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey continued a recent rough patch for the Twins' starting staff, lasting just three innings and giving up eight runs in a 12-2 loss to the White Sox. The right-hander allowed 10 hits and gave up one home run. It marked the ninth time this season that Slowey has given up a long ball. Prior to this rough start, Slowey had gone 2-1 with a 2.14 ERA in his previous three outings. Next up for the pitcher is the Brewers, facing them for only the second time in his career. In his first start against Milwaukee, Slowey allowed four earned runs over his 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Relievers Carlos Villanueva and Salomon Torres preserved Suppan's second straight win on Sunday at Coors Field, each escaping one-out jams with the tying runner on third base. Suppan pitched the first 5 1/3 innings and was not necessarily efficient, but limited the Rockies to two runs, only one of them earned, on four hits. It was just his second road win in eight starts, but Suppan has been very good at Miller Park, where he is 2-0 with a 1.50 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander delivered a solid, if somewhat short outing —against the White Sox in his last start. Perkins allowed three runs on five hits over his 5 1/3 innings. Perkins hasn't pitched a full six innings in each of his last three starts. He's been getting back to pitching more inside -- something that made him effective early in his return to the Twins. Next up for Perkins will be his first career appearance vs. Milwaukee. He's 1-0 with a 2.77 ERA in two road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: McClung was fighting a stomach flu when he pitched against the Astros on Tuesday, twice running to the bathroom to get sick. You wouldn't know by the results, as the right-hander limited Houston to three hits including Lance Berkman's short-porch home run in a disappointing Brewers loss. It was McClung's second so-called "quality" start of at least six innings with three or fewer runs and his fourth start since moving to the rotation from the bullpen. He threw 85 pitches, a season-high.
away_pitcher_note: In just his second start following a month-long stint on the DL with a strained groin muscle, Baker looked much more like himself. He limited the Indians to just one run on eight hits over seven innings to deliver the Twins' first quality start in 12 games. Baker still picked up the loss when the Twins were shut out in the game. The right-hander will now head to Milwaukee, where he delivered a gem of a start in his return to the rotation last season. He pitched 8 1/3 innings, allowing two runs on six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Parra has won four straight decisions, though he wasn't at his best in Houston on Thursday. Parra surrendered a career-high 10 hits, including three solo home runs, but won on a day that included five Brewers homers. "My thought process and my mental approach was on target, I just didn't make some pitches," Parra said. "There were other times earlier in the year where I would be thinking the wrong thing and was mentally off, which is more unacceptable to me."
away_pitcher_note: McGowan dominated the Mariners in his last start. The hard-throwing right-hander tossed a complete-game, five-hitter, allowing just one run. He walked two and struck out seven. An amazing fact from the start was that McGowan was reaching 99 mph on the radar gun in the ninth inning. Also, he tossed a career-high 125 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets got sharper as he pitched deeper into Thursday's start against the Astros, a seven-inning, three-run performance for his third straight win. He whiffed seven of the final 14 hitters he faced on the way to a season-high nine strikeouts, and was the first Brewer to pitch seven full innings since June 2. He beat the Blue Jays in an Interleague start at Rogers Centre in 2005, holding them to one run in eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Facing Seattle in his last start, Marcum pitched well, despite earning a no-decision -- his third in his last three starts. The right-hander allowed just one run on seven hits over seven innings. He walked two, while striking out nine. Marcum has allowed two earned runs or fewer in 11 of his 15 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Bush was tagged for four runs (three earned) over six innings, as he gave up 10 hits, struck out three and walked one. Bush (2-7) gave up an unearned run in the first inning after the first of two errors on the night from second baseman Bill Hall, and he then gave up another three runs after the Twins snuck two bunt singles into the right side of the Brewers' infield to start a rally. The Twins collected five hits and sent eight men to the plate in that inning.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett has struggled to keep his pitch count down of late, needing 211 pitches to work through 9 1/3 innings across his past two starts. Over that span, the right-hander has yielded 10 runs on 14 hits with 12 strikeouts and eight walks. On Friday, Burnett picked up a win at home against the Cubs after giving up two runs on four hits in five innings, in which he threw 111 pitches, struck out seven and walked four. In his career against Milwaukee, Burnett is 1-1 with a 4.85 ERA in four outings.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan did everything he could to win in his last start, but once the game was out of his hands, the Brewers lost an extra-innings thriller to the Twins on Saturday night. He pitched seven solid innings and worked out of trouble when he needed to, but the 'pen cost him his fifth win of the season. Suppan allowed two runs on seven hits, striking out five and just walking one. He is now 2-0 with a 1.67 ERA in six starts at Miller Park this season.
away_pitcher_note: Liz pitched six strong innings in his last outing, but the Orioles tried to push him through the seventh and paid for their efforts. The right-hander has acquitted himself well in his first three big-league starts this season and has yet to allow more than four earned runs. Liz also hasn't been knocked out before the end of the fifth inning yet.

home_pitcher_note: McClung has turned into a pretty reliable starter for the Brewers since him move from the bullpen. In his last start, he tossed his third consecutive quality start and notched his fourth win of the year, lowering his ERA to 3.94. The big righty threw six strong innings, allowing two runs on four hits while striking out four and walking none. He's also not a bad hitter, getting his first career double Sunday against the Twins and is batting .333 on the season.
away_pitcher_note: Cabrera has had a rough month, logging an 8.47 ERA in his last three starts. The right-hander has gone five starts without a victory, but has pitched competitively for most of the season. Cabrera has managed to cut down on his walks this season and has had three outings with no free passes. Last year, he only did that twice all season.

home_pitcher_note: Parra won his fifth straight decision by blanking the Blue Jays over seven innings on Tuesday, rebounding from a shaky start. He threw 43 pitches in the first two innings but then found a groove and didn't allow a runner past second base until the seventh, when he struck out Alex Rios with a runner at third base to preserve the shutout. Since allowing a season-high six runs in a no-decision at Washington on May 25, Parra is 4-0 with a 2.49 ERA in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Olson cruised through four innings in his last start before losing command in the fifth, and he's pitched to a 1-1 record with a 6.61 ERA in June. Despite that line, the southpaw has allowed three earned runs or less in seven of his 10 starts. Olson has allowed more hits (60) than he has innings pitched (54 1/3) and has less than a 2:1 strikeout-to-walk ratio this season.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes allowed two runs -- one earned -- on five hits for the second straight start, but when he left after the seventh inning, the Braves still hadn't broken out of a 2-2 tie. The 23-year-old left-hander, who has made significant strides since the first month of the season, struck out three and walked four, one of which led to his only earned run of the night. Reyes lost against the Brewers earlier this season, on May 28, despite allowing just one run on two hits in seven innings. He also struck out a career-high nine in that game.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets didn't have his best stuff last time out, but still was able to claim a victory as his teammates provided enough run support to give the Brewers a 5-4 win. Sheets (8-1) walked four batters for the first time in nine starts, but won his fourth straight decision by limiting the Blue Jays to two runs over six innings of work. Closer Salomon Torres came in to work out of a jam and record the last five outs for the save, giving Sheets his team-high eighth win.

home_pitcher_note: Morton allowed three runs Thursday against the Rangers, but his five-plus innings of work were spoiled when reliever Jeff Ridgway gave up a three-run homer to the first batter he faced. Two of the runs were charged to Morton. The lanky 24-year-old right-hander scattered five hits before departing with no outs in the sixth after allowing two baserunners. He threw 91 pitches, striking out three and walking four. He didn't possess the same pinpoint control that he had in his big-league debut on Saturday. In that start, he impressed with a mid-90s fastball and a sharp sinker.
away_pitcher_note: Bush carried a no-hitter into the eighth inning in his last start, lasting until Lyle Overbay lifted a 1-0 pitch into left field to break up the no-hit bid. Bush (3-7) went on to allow a run in the inning, but this outing was by far his best of the season. The veteran right-hander carried a perfect game into the fifth inning, setting down the first 15 batters he faced; carried a no-hitter through seven, walking just one; and ended up with eight innings of two-hit baseball to his credit.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo was hit hard by the Mariners on Friday night, allowing four runs on eight hits in 6 1/3 innings. He took the loss, his second of the season. Campillo exited in the seventh after allowing the go-ahead run to score and two baserunners to reach base. The 29-year-old right-hander allowed four doubles, and five others reached the warning track. Campillo hasn't won since May 29, which coincidentally came against the Brewers. In that start, he allowed one run on four hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan had his shortest start in 10 years, as he didn't make it out of the second inning against the Orioles on Friday. The first three batters of the game singled, eight Orioles came to the plate and four runs scored in the inning. Suppan notched two outs in the top of the second inning, but was knocked out of the game when two more runs scored and he walked the bases loaded. The right-hander ended up with a final line of six runs on seven hits, with two walks and one strikeout in 1 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn was very effective against Arizona in his last start, going seven innings and allowing only one earned run on three hits, a 6-1 Twins victory. Blackburn mixed his fastball, curveball, slider and changeup effectively to keep the D-backs off balance. Blackburn will next have a home start against Milwaukee in the Metrodome. It will be his first career start against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: McClung has really found a home in the Brewers rotation and solidified his spot on the team since moving over from the bullpen in late May. In his last start, McClung threw 6 2/3 innings, not allowing a hit until the fifth, and gave up two runs in picking up his fifth win of the season. The big righty is now 5-3 with a 3.79 ERA on the season, but McClung is still not taking anything for granted. "I feel like I can be replaced at any time," McClung said. "That keeps me hungry."

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez had a happy reunion against Arizona on Sunday, going seven innings while only allowing one earned run on nine hits. It was the second consecutive quality start for Hernandez, who has experienced more success by relying less on his fastball and more on his slider and sinker. Hernandez's next start will come against the Brewers, whom he has not faced this year.
away_pitcher_note: Parra is coming off a performance in which he scuffled badly, but was able to battle through it and come away with a win. Parra managed to make it through five innings and allowed three runs, but the damage could have been much worse. The lefty walked six batters and gave up five hits, but the Brewers bats saved him. Four home runs -- two by Prince Fielder -- and stellar defensive play in the infield took Parra off the hook for the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey delivered his third straight quality start, pitching six scoreless innings against the Padres at PETCO Park. He scattered just four hits in the outing and did not walk a single batter while striking out a season-high seven batters. Slowey has continued to look more comfortable on the mound after a rough start to the season. He was 0-4 with a 5.49 ERA in his first four starts. Slowey will now face the Brewers for the second time this month. He picked up the victory in that contest after allowing just two runs over eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets threw his National League-leading third complete game of the season on Monday against the Braves. He allowed four hits, struck out seven and retired the last 16 batters he faced. Sheets has now won five straight decisions. He has pitched at least six innings in 10 consecutive starts, and in 13 of 15 starts this season. Sheets is 1-1 with a 2.18 ERA in three career starts against the Twins. He last pitched against Minnesota on June 18, 2004, when he allowed one run on four hits in six innings and got the win. In 20 2/3 innings against the Twins, he has allowed five runs.

home_pitcher_note: Davis has shown great command in his last three outings and it's showed up in the results -- he has allowed just four runs in 20 innings over that span. Despite those numbers, he does not have a win to show for it. In his last outing, against the Red Sox, he allowed just one run through seven innings, but reliever Chad Qualls allowed two inherited runners to score in the eighth, plus two of his own and the D-backs wound up losing the game, 5-4. Davis' best pitch is a cut fastball, though he also throws a curveball and changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Bush didn't quite have no-hit stuff Tuesday, but he was plenty effective in limiting the Braves to four hits and one run in seven innings. Bush has now allowed just two runs and six hits in his past 15 innings. Tuesday's win was his first of the season on the road (1-5). Bush is 4-0 with a 3.55 ERA in four career starts against the D-backs. He last faced them on Aug. 21, 2007, when he allowed two runs on six hits in six innings. He also struck out six in that game.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson is eager to see the calendar flip to July as he dropped all five of his starts in June. In his last outing, he pitched well against the Red Sox at Fenway Park, but Tim Wakefield was better in a 5-0 Boston win. Johnson allowed just two runs over six innings. It was a far better start than the one he had in Minnesota before that when he allowed seven runs on 11 hits while tossing his first complete game since Aug. 24, 2006. Six of the seven runs came during the third inning. Johnson is still stuck on 288 wins for his career.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan allowed four runs on nine hits in six innings Wednesday against the Braves, taking his second loss in as many starts. He has now given up 10 runs (seven earned) in his past two starts. Suppan struck out five Wednesday, but left too many pitches over the middle of the plate. Braves pitcher Jorge Campillo recorded two hits off Suppan.
