Still, it was an improvement from the 1 2/3-inning, six-run disaster against Baltimore in his previous start, which was his shortest outing since May 1998. Suppan didn't factor in the decision June 2 against the D-backs, when he allowed three runs on seven hits and struck out six in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Petit will be making his first start of the season for the D-backs. He was recalled June 28 to fill Edgar Gonzalez's roster spot. His only decision of the year came April 26 in San Diego, when Tadahito Iguchi hit a walk-off home run in the 13th inning. Petit is 0-1 with a 3.00 ERA in six innings against the Brewers in his career.
away_pitcher_note: McClung received a no-decision in his last start against Minnesota. The right-hander was touched for five runs on nine hits while going 4 2/3 innings. The outing caused his ERA to climb by nearly half a run. McClung will next start against Arizona. On June 3, McClung received his third win of the season by going six innings and allowing only one earned run against the D-Backs in a 7-1 Brewers victory.

home_pitcher_note: Webb lost his first game of the season against the Marlins, after nine victories, but got a measure of revenge in his last start. It wasn't easy as Webb lasted only six-plus innings and left with two on and no out in the seventh. But Webb showed flashes of his early-season form in the victory. He struck out eight and was particularly effective once Florida got runners in scoring position in the second, third and fourth innings. He left four of that runners stranded. What may have helped Webb as much as anything is that he received a nice jolt of run support. A five-run sixth inning put the game away for Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Parra halted Minnesota's 10-game winning streak in his last start. He went seven innings of shutout ball while allowing only two hits and recording six strikeouts in a 5-1 Brewers victory at the Metrodome. Parra's next start will complete a four-game series against Arizona. He went seven innings and only allowed one earned run while striking out eight in a 10-1 Brewers victory against the D-Backs on June 4.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets was touched for five earned runs in seven innings on Sunday against the Twins in a 5-0 loss. All five runs were surrendered with two outs. Sheets will next take the mound on the Fourth of July against the Pirates. Sheets pitched a complete game on May 21 against the Bucs, striking out six and allowing only one earned run in a 4-1 Brewers victory.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny allowed fewer than three earned runs for the first time in seven starts in his last outing, on June 29 against Tampa Bay. He has struggled with control problems this season, but he was a bit more effective tossing 111 pitches, 70 for strikes. Gorzelanny hurled six innings and was tagged for two runs on eight hits. He recorded eight strikeouts and received a no-decision against the Rays.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a pair of wins in which he surrendered two total runs on six hits in 15 innings, Bush didn't have it earlier in the week in Phoenix. Six of the nine Arizona hits off Bush went for extra bases, and he surrendered five runs, four earned, in five innings. He's been very good this season at Miller Park, going 3-2 with a 3.18 ERA in seven starts, but he lost to the Pirates in Pittsburgh in May, allowing six runs on nine hits.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm continues to be one of two steady presences in the Pirates rotation, and his last start as yet another example of that. Needing just 89 pitches to finish seven innings, Maholm allowed two runs on five hits as he notched his fifth quality start in his last six. The lefty seems to run into problems primarily when he rushes in his delivery, but he has shown in recent weeks that he can remedy the problem quick enough to keep it from getting him into too much trouble. Maholm lost to the Brewers back in May in a start where he allowed four earned runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan won his last start but is in a three-game funk in which he has allowed 12 earned runs and 15 hits in 12 2/3 innings. He surrendered five runs on nine hits in five innings at Arizona on Tuesday but got the win after the Brewers roughed up Randy Johnson. Suppan didn't pitch against the Pirates when the Brewers visited Pittsburgh last month, but he's 10-3 lifetime against the Pirates with a 3.95 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Duke's last start lasted just 77 pitches as the left-hander got into a bases-loaded jam in the sixth that his manager preferred his bullpen get out of. Though Duke's five-inning, one-run performance suggests dominance, in reality, Duke benefited from some stellar defense and some Houdini-like bullpen work to bail him out. It's not much a setback for Duke, though, who has gone at least six innings in 10 of his last 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: McClung called his last start, a no-decision at Arizona, "a dogfight." While D-backs starter Yusmeiro Petit retired all nine hitters he faced in the first three innings, McClung battled, facing 16 batters in the first three frames. He surrendered seven hits in that span and plunked two batters, but somehow limited Arizona to two runs. McClung settled in after the third and got the Brewers through 5 1/3 innings, allowing just those two runs on eight hits with one walk and six strikeouts and leaving the team in position to rally for a win. The Rockies are one of six Major League teams McClung has never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez's act plays well in Denver, but it hasn't been a hit in any other city. Now he has a gig in Milwaukee. In his last start, Jimenez held the Padres to one run in 6 1/3 innings of an 8-1 victory, and has gone 3-2 with a 2.67 ERA at Coors Field. On the road, however, he is 0-6 with a 6.96 ERA. But his gameplan against the Padres -- attack inside with his fastball for strikes, or to back hitters off the plate in the early innings -- could work anywhere if he a) has his secondary pitches working, but b) doesn't rely too much on them.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia, the reigning American League Cy Young Award winner and arguably the best pitcher available on the midseason trade market, became a Brewer on Monday when the teams formally agreed to a swap that sent four prospects to Cleveland. Sabathia is a left-hander and will join right-hander Ben Sheets atop Milwaukee's rotation in a bid to end the franchise's 26-year postseason drought.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first big league start since May 6 and pitching on short rest, Redman gave the Rockies everything they could have hoped for against the Marlins. He allowed just two runs on six hits in six innings. Both his fastball and cutter were working, which enabled him to force ground balls that resulted in three double plays. Redman was sent to Triple-A Colorado Springs after pitching ineffectively the first month of the season, but he worked with Sky Sox pitching coach Chuck Kniffin to straighten out his delivery. Redman was called up Wednesday after Jeff Francis (3-7) went on the disabled list with inflammation in his left shoulder.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Sheets didn't have his best stuff, but still came away with a win as he worked in and out of trouble all afternoon to allow just one run over 5 2/3 innings pitched.  Sheets didn't seem to have the ability to put hitters away, causing his pitch count to swell and his outing to be shortened. Still, Sheets managed to keep the game in check and became the first Brewers pitcher to reach 10 wins this season.
away_pitcher_note: Rusch makes his first start for the Rockies since May 31 at Chicago, so when he takes the mound against the Brewers, both of his starts for the club will be against his former teams. Before rejoining the Rockies on Saturday and pitching a rough inning in relief against the Marlins, Rusch went 1-2 with a 4.61 ERA at Triple-A Colorado Springs while waiting for an opening in the rotation. He got his chance when the Rockies decided to send down right-handed prospect Greg Reynolds, who went 2-6 with a 6.71 ERA in 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Bush had one of his best starts of the season, working quickly through eight solid innings. He allowed just one run on four hits, striking out a season-high seven batters and walking none. Bush was lifted for a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the eighth inning, on his way to a no-decision as he left the game with the score tied at 1 after having thrown 100 pitches. The Brewers won the game on a walk-off hit by Prince Fielder, and both manager Ned Yost and Bush were happy with the performance.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa rebounded from two straight poor outings to earn the win against Florida on Saturday. Against the Marlins, De La Rosa gave up three runs on six hits in five innings. He retired the first batter in each of the first four innings, which allowed him to allude any serious trouble. De La Rosa is 2-1 with a 4.90 ERA since returning to the starting rotation on June 14.

home_pitcher_note: With Jeff Suppan going on the disabled list and the rotation being reshuffled because of the acquisition of CC Sabathia, Parra has been pushed back from Tuesday all the way to Friday to face the Reds, who are loaded with lefty bats. He followed up a great June with six scoreless innings in his first July start and appears to be hitting his stride.
away_pitcher_note: Fogg's return from the disabled list was solid, as he pitched six innings and gave up six hits with a walk and a strikeout against the Nationals on Saturday. It was his first start since May 31 and the third time he's auditioned for the No. 5 spot in the Reds' pitching rotation. He's totally recovered from the lumbar back spasms that originally put him on the DL, and his 102 pitches against Washington marked the fifth consecutive outing -- the previous four were rehab starts -- in which he's thrown at least 100 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: McClung continued to be a sort of anti-Brewer who excels on the road and struggles at Miller Park. He battled through 4 2/3 innings against the Rockies on Monday at home, allowing three hits and five walks but limiting the damage to two runs. He has a 5.08 ERA in home games versus a 3.28 ERA on the road. The Brewers face an interesting decision after the All-Star break, and may elect to use McClung and Dave Bush as co-fifth starters, starting Bush in home games and McClung on the road. Or, either McClung or Bush could be sent outright to the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez struggled with his command and had trouble for one inning, but was solid otherwise in his last start, a victory over the Nationals on Sunday. He pitched six innings and gave up three runs on five hits with three walks and three strikeouts. His next start could be moved back a day, Reds manager Dusty Baker said, which would bring any possibility of Volquez starting in the All-Star Game into question. The win over the Nationals was Volquez's 13th quality start (out of 18) of the season. The five earned runs tied for the most he's given up this season.

home_pitcher_note: He certainly did not dominate in his Brewers debut. He just as certainly did not disappoint. Sabathia beat the Rockies on Tuesday at sold-out Miller Park after delivering six solid innings in which he allowed three runs, only two of them earned, on five hits and matched a season high with five walks. His first pitch was a 94 mph fastball and Sabathia struck out five batters in the game, including pinch-hitter Brad Hawpe to end the sixth. Sabathia got a big break earlier in that inning when Rockies outfielder Ryan Spilborghs suffered an oblique injury that appeared to prevent him from scoring the tying run.
away_pitcher_note: The Reds tabbed Triple-A Louisville's Bailey to make the start Sunday in place of Aaron Harang, who was sent home from the team's road trip with stiffness in his right forearm. A previous big league stint with Cincinnati last month didn't go well for Bailey. He was 0-3 with an 8.76 ERA in three starts that lasted a combined 12 1/3 innings. Besides giving up 16 hits, the 22-year-old walked 10 and struck out only three. In 16 starts with Louisville this season, Bailey is 4-7 with a 4.42 ERA over 93 2/3 innings. He's walked 38 and struck out 82.

home_pitcher_note: This will be only Cain's second career start against Milwaukee. He lost to the Brewers, 5-3, on Sept. 24, 2006 at Miller Park, yielding all of Milwaukee's runs in seven innings. Cain's 121 strikeouts is the ninth-most in San Francisco history before the All-Star break. But his recent effectiveness has been offset by poor run support, which is a familiar story. Cain has received only 3.7 runs per start, one of the lowest figures in the National League.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia will make his first road start for the Brewers and his second career start at AT&T Park in San Francisco. He pitched the Indians to a win there on June 10, 2005, allowing two earned runs in eight innings. He also hit a two-run double but was thrown out at third after a relay throw temporarily got away from Giants starter Brett Tomko. Sabathia was easily out, despite a headfirst slide. "It looked worse than it was," he said. "But it was bad -- a minor earthquake."

home_pitcher_note: The Giants probably couldn't have expected a first half this productive from Sanchez, who's only 25 and began the season struggling to find his consistency. Sanchez still loses his release point occasionally, but more often than not he maintains his arm slot and his stuff along with it. He has allowed three earned runs or fewer in all but three of his 19 starts. San Francisco owns a 13-6 record when Sanchez goes to the hill.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets was dominant out of the gate in his last start, but his pitch count soared and the Rockies were able to tag him for just enough runs and steal a win at Miller Park. On the day after CC Sabathia made his Brewers debut, Sheets went just as deep into his start -- six innings -- and allowed the same number of runs, but he couldn't come away with the win. The ace right-hander finished with 11 strikeouts, allowing just three runs. But the Brewers offense was only able to cut the deficit to one run before the Rockies plated more insurance runs against the Milwaukee 'pen.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum recorded a 1.99 ERA in his first 14 outings before slumping to a 4.65 ERA over his next five starts. But he recovered on July 13 against the Cubs, striking out nine while allowing one run and six hits in eight innings as the Giants triumphed, 4-2. He's the first Giants pitcher to record 11 wins before the All-Star break since Jason Schmidt in 2004. Lincecum is 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA in three career appearances against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Parra didn't have his best start of the season in his last outing before the break, coming away with the no-decision. The lefty still hasn't gotten stuck with a loss since May 3. Over his last 12 starts, Parra is 7-0 and has only allowed more than three earned runs three times over that span. Since his last loss over two months ago, his ERA has dropped more than two full runs, from 5.86 to 3.69.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro was staked to a 4-1 lead in his last start on July 13 at Pittsburgh, but wound up tossing 5 2/3 innings, allowing six runs on 10 hits. He received a no-decision. He lost a 3-2 decision to San Diego on April 20, allowing six hits and three runs in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: McClung gets the nod as the Brewers begin a rare platoon of starting pitchers. McClung will get the nod when his spot in the rotation comes up on the road, and fellow right-hander Dave Bush will take the ball at home. The Brewers are going with the numbers here; McClung is 1-1 with a 3.28 ERA in 11 games, four starts, on the road and 4-4 with a 4.95 ERA in 10 games, six starts, at home. Bush is 4-2 with a 2.49 ERA in nine starts at home and 1-6 with a 6.95 ERA in nine games, eight of them starts, on the road. With the acquisition of CC Sabathia and with Jeff Suppan likely being activated from the disabled list on Tuesday, there was not room for both McClung and Bush in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse hit his stride in May and he continues to sprint to the finish. With Adam Wainwright and Chris Carpenter on the disabled list, Lohse has provided the Cardinals with a much needed boost in their starting rotation and he has delivered. Lohse has not lost a start since May 8 and has lost only two games in his last 32 starts, dating back to July 2007. While he did not pitch his best in his last outing and was aided by some spectacular defense, Lohse pitched effective enough to last seven innings and give up two runs. Attributing his success to his confidence in his entire arsenal, Lohse has morphed into one of the better pitchers this year.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers are expecting Suppan to return to the starting rotation. The veteran right-hander was bothered by joint irritation in the elbow on his throwing arm, forcing him to the disabled list. Before going on the DL, Suppan had been struggling. He allowed 18 earned runs on 30 hits over 15 2/3 innings in his last four starts. Both Suppan and manager Ned Yost downplayed the degree of the injury, but felt that rest would be good for the righty.

home_pitcher_note: It didn't take long for the Padres to knock Looper around in his last outing on July 18. In three-plus innings of work, Looper only threw 68 pitches but managed to give up six runs on eight hits. Looper kept serving up pitches over the heart of the plate so many times that he eventually became visibly frustrated. However, Looper has been much more consistent this year than in years past. In his other three poor starts, Looper has followed with quality starts, showing a strong ability to bounce back.
away_pitcher_note: So far, so good for Sabathia, who is 3-0 in his three Brewers starts since a trade from Cleveland. He has pitched all nine innings in each of his last two starts, including a four-hitter at San Francisco to begin the second half, becoming the first Brewers pitcher to toss complete games in consecutive starts since Scott Karl in 1995. Sabathia is also living up to his reputation as a tough out; he homered against the Reds on July 13 and then doubled and scored against the Giants on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer may have found something as he went on in his last outing, and the Cardinals certainly hope so. Since he sustained an elbow injury in early June, he hasn't looked like the same pitcher who was so effective in April and May. Wellemeyer relies heavily on two pitches, his fastball and his slider, so if either one is less than its best, he's going to have a hard time.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets was lifted for a pinch-hitter in the middle of a four-run Brewers rally on Saturday, so he pitched only five innings, snapping Milwaukee's streak of seven consecutive quality starts. He surrendered four runs in the fourth inning, and while only two were earned because of an error by shortstop J.J. Hardy, it marked the first time an opponent scored more than twice in a single frame against Sheets since the Dodgers' six-run seventh inning on May 15.

home_pitcher_note: Parra is doing his best to imitate the Brewers' new co-aces. "With what CC [Sabathia] does and Ben [Sheets], it ups the ante," Parra said. "It makes you kind of want to taste the same thing they are and not have to use the bullpen." He came close on Sunday in San Francisco on the way to winning his eighth straight decision. Parra worked a career-best 7 2/3 innings, allowing only four hits through seven frames before the Giants rallied for three hits and two runs in the eighth. Both runs scored when Aaron Rowand's double popped in and out of Corey Hart's glove as Hart retreated to deep right field. Parra also set a career high with nine strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Rodriguez's first career start against Milwaukee in his fourth season in the Majors. Rodriguez comes off a very successful outing against the Cubs on Saturday, allowing just one run on nine hits against the division leaders. Rodriguez has been hit-or-miss this season but has showed a bit more effectiveness in his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: It's Bush's turn in the Brewers' fifth starter platoon. With the acquisition of CC Sabathia and Jeff Suppan being activated from the disabled list, there was not room for both Seth McClung and Bush in the rotation, so the Brewers are using them both. Bush gets the nod in home starts; he is 4-2 with a 2.49 ERA in nine starts at home and 1-6 with a 6.95 ERA in nine games, eight of them starts, on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Despite taking the loss, Backe pitched fairly well in his last appearance, a four-run outing against the Cubs. He left a few pitches up that the hard-hitting Cubs lineup took advantage of, but Astros manager Cecil Cooper was still impressed by the righty's performance. Backe lost his last start to the Brewers, giving up five runs on seven hits, including three homers, in just four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan returned from the disabled list on Tuesday and surrendered two Cardinals runs on four hits in his first inning. But he settled in after that, allowing four more hits and only one run through the seventh, leaving the Brewers in position for a comeback. Suppan was on the DL because of a tender elbow, and the "finish" returned to his pitches against the Cardinals, according to catcher Jason Kendall.
away_pitcher_note: Acquired from San Diego on Tuesday, Wolf will make his first start for the Astros in Milwaukee. Wolf was 6-10 with a 4.74 ERA in 21 starts for the Padres this season, allowing 14 home runs. The start will be Wolf's first against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers begin their biggest series of the season with their new co-ace on the mound. Sabathia pitched a three-hit shutout at St. Louis on Wednesday for his third consecutive complete game and his fourth Brewers win in as many starts since a July 7 trade from Cleveland. He faced only three, three-ball counts all night and took a no-hitter into the sixth inning. The last Brewers pitcher to go the distance in at least three consecutive starts was Cal Eldred, who worked four straight in 1994. Sabathia lost his only career start against the Cubs, allowing nine runs on eight hits in 2 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly is coming off a win against Arizona. He did it all, giving up three runs on six hits over six innings, as well as hitting a RBI single, stealing a base, throwing out a potential base stealer and helping in a rundown play. The lefty is one of three Cubs pitchers with at least 10 wins. He faced Milwaukee on April 2, and lost, 8-2.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets was happy with his last outing despite the fact he was in line for a loss until Ryan Braun hit a go-ahead homer in the ninth inning. Sheets lasted seven innings and limited the Cardinals to three runs, only two of which were earned, and four hits. He's 1-0 in two starts against the Cubs this season while allowing three earned runs in 11 1/3 innings (2.38 ERA). Cubs hitters are batting just .132 against Sheets in those games (5-for-38).
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano held the Marlins at bay last time out, striking out six and, more importantly, walking none in seven innings of two-run ball. The Cubs ace had walked six in his previous start. He has a 0.69 ERA in two outings against the Brewers this season, both no-decisions. You know Zambrano will be amped up for this start, facing an NL Central contender on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Parra was seething after his first loss since May 3 ended an eight-decision winning streak. He danced in and out of trouble against the Astros through six innings before running out of luck in the seventh, when Houston loaded the bases without hitting a ball out of the infield. Parra was replaced by reliever David Riske and all three runs scored. "I feel like I'm throwing the ball really well, six innings, seven innings and then a break here or there is the difference between what CC [Sabathia] and Ben [Sheets] are doing. They're coming out of games on a good note versus being taken out of the inning, which I can't stand," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster did not get a decision in his last start against the Marlins. He gave up one run on two hits over six innings, but he didn't get any offensive support. He also walked six, including loading the bases on three walks with two outs in the fifth before striking out Dan Uggla to escape. Dempster beat the Brewers on April 3, and again April 30, both games at Wrigley Field, where he's 10-1. He's 1-3 with a 3.42 ERA on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Bush struggled somewhat in his first appearance since July 10, a delay that came about when Bush and Seth McClung were inserted into an unusual home/road platoon. The right-hander, who has had plentiful success at Miller Park this year, allowed nine hits in five innings and surrendered four runs -- three on home runs by Carlos Lee and Hunter Pence in the fourth. Still, Milwaukee rallied for victory and now have triumphs in the last start from both platooned pitchers. Thursday's game will mark the first time one of the two pitchers has made two consecutive turns in the new system.
away_pitcher_note: It's almost impossible to believe that Harden doesn't have a win. He has struck out 10 in each of his three starts for the Cubs, and despite all those K's, he doesn't have a "W." In his last outing against Florida, he was pulled after throwing 87 pitches in five innings in an effort to keep him strong. He had thrown 112 pitches the outing before. Over 17 1/3 innings in his three Chicago starts, Harden has given up two runs.

home_pitcher_note: James, who was scratched Wednesday at Triple-A Richmond so he could make this start, has not pitched for the Braves since May 15, when he allowed five runs on six hits and walked five in four innings. After that start, he was optioned to Richmond, where he was 4-5 with a 2.48 ERA in 14 games (13 starts). The 26-year-old has not pitched for the R-Braves since last Friday, when he allowed six hits and one run in six strong innings. Control was the primary reason the Braves optioned James; he walked 16 batters in 23 innings, a span of five starts. James has issued four walks in his past 17 innings for Richmond.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan was fine for four innings Sunday, but things turned abruptly in the fifth when he was lit up by Houston for seven runs, including three on the second homer of the game from Geoff Blum. In his second start since returning from a brief stint on the disabled list, the right-hander finished with eight runs on 11 hits allowed in six innings. He has yet to recapture the form that made him an integral contributor in May and June, allowing 22 runs in 21 July innings.

home_pitcher_note: Morton allowed a career-high eight runs on seven hits and issued four walks against the Cardinals on Monday in yet another disheartening Braves loss. Morton struggled mightily with his command, leaving too many fastballs and sliders up in the zone. The 24-year-old was briefly demoted to Triple-A Richmond last Saturday, but was needed two days later to fill an open roster spot. Morton is now 1-3 with a 9.53 ERA in his past five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia didn't have his best stuff last time out, against the Cubs, and didn't get a decision as a defensive error by the Brewers allowed Chicago to tie the game. The Cubs would later break the tie and beat Milwaukee closer Salomon Torres. Sabathia missed his shot first shot at reaching 5-0 since his trade to the Brewers.  His final line was four runs -- three earned -- on nine hits over 6 2/3 innings of work.  He threw 129 pitches as the Cubs hitters made him work. After the game, Sabathia said, "I really didn't have my out pitch, my cutter. I was leaving that up and away and they were just looking for that. I tried to do the best I could."

home_pitcher_note: Campillo scattered two runs and seven hits over seven strong innings Tuesday against the Cardinals, but did not factor into the decision after the Braves' bullpen allowed six runs in the eighth and ninth innings. Campillo was staked to a 2-1 lead in the sixth before allowing a solo homer to Albert Pujols, who took advantage of a hanging breaking ball over the inside half of the plate. Campillo's schedule was a little off for this start after having his previous outing, on Sunday against the Phillies, stopped after 1 2/3 innings and a near two-hour rain delay.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets and the Brewers were stunned by the Cubs in his last outing. Sheets started back-to-back with CC Sabathia in a 1-2 punch that Milwaukee hoped would knock Chicago out of their four-game series, but instead the Brewers aces dropped two straight and dug a hole for the club. Sheets started out strong, allowing just one run in the first five innings, but gave up seven straight hits to lead off the sixth on his way to a game-changing, five-run inning. He only notched one out in the inning before being pulled and ended up taking the loss as the Cubs' Carlos Zambrano was brilliant, shutting out the Brewers for eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo gave up six earned runs and eight hits over 6 1/3 innings without a walk and three strikeouts in a 6-2 loss to the Astros Tuesday. He was done in by a two-out rally in the fifth. Despite having two strikes on three-straight batters, he couldn't close out the inning and loaded the bases. A low sinker was launched by Carlos Lee for a grand slam that blew a 2-1 game open. On April 17 vs. the Brewers, Arroyo gave up four earned runs over 5 2/3 innings for a 5-2 loss.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers were counting on Parra to be the stopper on Wednesday against the Cubs, and Parra was anything but. In his second straight loss, Parra didn't make it out of the sixth inning. He allowed five runs on eight hits, walked four and struck out five. The lefty didn't work a perfect inning all night as Chicago made him work, running his pitch count to 96 through 5 1/3 innings. He'll try to get back on track as he takes on Cincinnati on Monday. In his only other career start against the Reds, Parra was knocked around for five runs on six hits in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez pitched 6 1/3 innings and mostly appeared to shed his two-game slump with a 9-5 win over the Astros Wednesday. The right-hander encountered little trouble until a four-run seventh-inning that was extended by two errors by shortstop Jeff Keppinger. The mistakes culminated in a three-run homer by Ty Wiggington. Only one of his five runs Volquez allowed were earned on six hits with one walk and five strikeouts. Following two sub-par starts coming out of the All-Star break, Volquez watched some video and made mechanical corrections.
away_pitcher_note: Bush was pleased to return to the rotation full-time after splitting starts with Seth McClung. "I couldn't replicate the work on the sides," said Bush, who had 15 days' rest between starts after the platoon took effect in mid-July. "I was working more on mechanics and keeping my endurance up, not focusing on improving the starts. It'll be good to do a regular session for now."

home_pitcher_note: Bailey faced a Nationals team on Friday which came in losers of nine in a row. Yet, he was pounded in a 5-2 loss where he allowed five earned runs and seven hits over just two innings with one walk and three strikeouts. Of his 49 pitches, 32 were strikes, but many of those strikes were left over the heart of the plate. Bailey hasn't won a game at either Triple-A or the Majors since April 30 -- a span of 17 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Jeff Suppan pitched seven shutout innings Friday against the Braves, which was easily his most impressive outing since being reinstated from the disabled list on July 22. The 33-year-old right-hander missed only one start because of joint irritation in his pitching elbow, and said after Friday's start that the injury is becoming less of an issue with each outing. On Friday, Suppan walked the bases loaded in the fourth inning -- his only real trouble -- but induced a lazy fly out to escape the inning unscathed. He is 3-2 with a 5.33 ERA in 13 career starts against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia limited the Braves to six hits and fell two outs shy of recording his fourth complete-game victory in his past five starts. He allowed two runs in 8 1/3 innings Saturday, improving to 5-0 with a 1.88 ERA in six starts for the Brewers. He threw 109 pitches, the fifth consecutive start with at least 106 pitches thrown. Sabathia has never faced the Nationals but pitched against the Expos on June 21, 2002, when he allowed three runs on four hits in 7 1/3 innings and lost.
away_pitcher_note: Balester lasted 5 1/3 innings in his last outing, another impressive start for the young right-hander. He throw 101 pitches, 63 for strikes, and fanned five batters. He allowed just one run -- on a solo homer in the sixth. He walked two and struck out one.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets looks to snap a five-start winless streak in which he's gone 0-3 with two no-decisions. In his last outing, the righty was felled in Atlanta, dropping the decision despite allowing only two earned runs in six innings. He threw 97 pitches -- 68 for strikes -- but struck out only four while walking three, and he couldn't get past the sixth inning for the fifth time in six starts. Sheets will make his second start of the season against Washington, having taken a no-decision -- six innings, two earned runs on seven hits -- in D.C. on May 26. He is 2-3 lifetime against the Nats with a 4.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Redding improved markedly in his last performance, but a high pitch count forced him from his Monday night start against the Rockies after just five innings. He threw 112 pitches, striking out six and allowing four earned runs, in a 9-4 win, Washington's fourth in a row. He walked three in the outing.

home_pitcher_note: Parra's last start will be remembered more for what happened in the dugout than what happened on the mound. After Parra was replaced by a pinch-hitter in the seventh inning, he and Prince Fielder had words and Fielder delivered a pair of shoves that sent Parra to the bench. Both players declined to discuss specifics, but the next day Parra called the issue "done."
away_pitcher_note: Lannan registered a positively dominant performance in Colorado on Tuesday, when he struck out eight over seven innings, using his curveball to keep hitters off balance. He allowed just five hits and two runs in the outing, and 67 of his 108 pitches went for strikes. A lack of run support bested him however, as the Nationals' bullpen allowed six runs in relief and Washington lost, 8-2.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start since manager Ned Yost scrapped the home/road platoon between Bush and Seth McClung, Bush worked seven solid innings for his second road win this season. He limited the Reds to three hits and retired 17 in a row during one stretch. Bush, as much as any other Brewers pitcher, thrives on routine, and was particularly uncomfortable with the Brewers' unconventional timeshare. It's too early to call the full-time move back to the rotation a success, but it was a good start.
away_pitcher_note: Recalled from Triple-A Columbus to replace the injured Elijah Dukes on Thursday, Mock will make a spot start Monday so that Odalis Perez doesn't have to pitch on short rest after a doubleheader last Thursday. Mock has made two starts for the Nationals this season, posting an 0-2 record with a 5.27 ERA. His second start was markedly better than the first, as he lasted six innings and struck out six, allowing four runs. Mock had also pitched three scoreless innings out of the bullpen in July going into Game 2 of Thursday's doubleheader.

home_pitcher_note: Baek kept the Padres atop the Mets through 6 1/3 innings on Wednesday, allowing two runs on eight hits while striking out five. Other than a hit batsman, Baek's offspeed pitches found their spots and, on other occasions, sneakily ducked under Mets bats. The outing, which lasted 99 pitches, consisted of 65 strikes. He'll now face the Brewers, a team he hasn't faced in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan has worked seven innings to win each of his last two starts after allowing eight runs on 11 hits in a July 27 loss to the Astros at Miller Park. In the wins, he allowed four runs on 12 hits in 14 innings with three walks, none in his most recent outing in Cincinnati. Suppan retired the final nine men he faced in that game and could have escaped damage except for Jay Bruce, who hit an RBI groundout in the first inning and a two-run homer in the third. Suppan is 4-3 in his career against the Padres despite a 6.23 ERA in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Banks entered the sixth inning on Thursday but couldn't register an out, leaving the game with two runs surrendered in five innings. He was credited with a third on a sacrifice fly against reliever Cla Meredith which allowed an inherited runner to score. Banks accomplished his goal of allowing no more than three runs with Johan Santana as his rival on the mound, but it still wasn't enough to get him a win after allowing nine hits on 89 pitches. He has not faced the Brewers this season.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Sabathia (6-0 in seven starts since arriving in Milwaukee) tossed his fourth complete game -- and second shutout -- with the Brewers, allowing just five hits, while striking out nine and walking just one. The big lefty was economical, needing only 103 pitches, and he even added to the offensive output with a single in the second inning.  Still unbeaten in his seven starts with the Brewers, Sabathia has posted a 1.58 ERA since his move to the National League. His four complete games top the NL, and the southpaw is currently in the midst of a career-best nine-game winning streak, dating to June 10.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy endured a 54-minute rain delay in his last start and actually pitched better after the game against the Rockies on Aug. 8 resumed at Coors Field. Peavy, who allowed a two-run home run in the second inning before just before the rain started to fall, allowed just one run the rest of the way in taking a loss. Walks were Peavy's downfall during his six-inning stint where he allowed three runs on a season-high five walks.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Sheets was spectacular, as he set down batters in order in four of his first five innings, working his fourth complete game of the season. The righty allowed just five hits, striking out six and walking none.  Sheets matched CC Sabathia's five-hit shutout from the previous night nearly pitch-for-pitch in tying his teammate atop the National League leaderboard for complete games with his fourth of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Against the Giants, Billingsley did a high-wire act, pitching into and out of jams in five of his six innings, allowing three runs on nine hits, but stranding nine baserunners. He kept the ball in the park, and a two-run inning off him needed a bloop double to drop. He struck out six, but walked three. He's never started against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Following complete-game shutout gems from CC Sabathia and Ben Sheets in the first two games of the Brewers series against the Nationals, Parra delivered one of his best starts of the season in his last outing. The lefty allowed just six hits through seven innings, walking none and tying a career-high with nine strikeouts.  He left the game with the score tied at one run apiece and got no decision as Milwaukee took the back-and-forth game in 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe bounced back from his worst start of the season by throwing a quality start Monday against the Phillies, giving up three runs on five hits in 6 1/3 innings. Lowe's sinker worked as he induced 13 groundouts and just three flyouts besides striking out three. In his outing before that, Aug. 6 at St. Louis, he served up season highs in runs (eight) and hits (13) in 3 1/3 innings of a loss. Lowe has compiled a 1.78 ERA while going 3-2 in his last five starts at Dodger Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Bush has been sharp since manager Ned Yost abandoned his fifth starter platoon between Bush and Seth McClung. In two starts since the move, Bush has allowed two earned runs and eight hits in 13 1/3 innings for victories at Cincinnati and at home against Washington. The road win over the Reds was encouraging, but Bush is 2-6 with a 6.19 ERA in his 10 appearances away from home, nine of them starts. He lost his only career start at Dodger Stadium, in 2006, allowing four earned runs in six innings of a 10-2 Brewers loss.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw wasn't quite as sharp as his previous three starts, but he gave his team a chance to win. He allowed three runs in six innings with a career-high eight strikeouts. He served up a solo homer to Chase Utley and allowed a steal of third that turned into a run. He also struck out Ryan Howard twice.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan has been outstanding in three starts since his dismal July 27 outing against the Astros. On Tuesday, he held the Padres to two runs on four hits over eight innings, and over his three starts since he allowed eight runs in six innings against Houston, Suppan is 3-0 with a 2.05 ERA (five earned runs in 22 innings). The Brewers hope Suppan continues his trend as a second-half pitcher. In 2007, his first year with Milwaukee, Suppan posted a 5.00 ERA before the All-Star break, but lowered it to 4.12 afterward. Over the previous three years, Suppan had a 4.98 ERA before the All-Star break and a 3.09 ERA after it.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia calls his current run of success "pretty good." If this is pretty good, his new teammates would love to see what else he has in store. Sabathia has won 10 straight decisions dating to his final days with the Cleveland Indians, and is 7-0 with a 1.55 ERA in eight Brewers starts since a July 7 trade to Milwaukee. He had to work a bit against the Padres on Wednesday, but still managed to pitch seven innings while allowing only one run on nine hits. He pitched a five-hit shutout against the Nationals in his last start at Miller Park.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf had his best outing of the four he's made since his trade to Houston in his last start against the Giants. The veteran left-hander no-hit the Giants through four and cruised to the win after allowing two runs over seven innings. Wolf made his Astros debut against the Brewers in Milwaukee on July 27, when he took a no-decision after yielding four runs (three earned) over 4 1/3 innings. The Astros are 4-0 in games he's started.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets dueled Jake Peavy on Thursday in San Diego and didn't have his good curveball, but still managed to blank the Padres on only one hit through six innings. Sheets ran into trouble in the seventh, allowing four hits and three runs on the way to a tough 3-2 loss. According to MLB.com's unofficial pitch tracker, 77 of Sheets' 110 pitches were fastballs, or 70 percent. Over his final 1 2/3 innings, 24 of Sheets' 30 pitches registered as fastballs. "It was not good," Sheets said of his curve. "But, you still have to throw it. It just wasn't a good pitch today."
away_pitcher_note: Moehler wasn't as sharp in his last outing as he was the previous three, ending a streak of three starts during which he yielded two or fewer runs. Moehler allowed four runs over 5 1/3 innings but took a no-decision in an Astros win. Moehler last faced the Brewers on June 12 at home, absorbing the loss after allowing seven runs over 4 2/3 innings. Moehler is 4-2 with a 3.64 ERA over 10 road games (eight starts) this year.

home_pitcher_note: Parra's frustration is mounting, even though he has pitched well in his first full season in the Majors. But since rattling off eight straight wins, Parra has gone 1-4 in his past nine starts, including a loss at Dodger Stadium on Friday in which he matched his career and season high by allowing 10 hits. Parra was working with what he called his best pure "stuff" of the season, but he couldn't locate. "Right now, everything is finding a hole, and I'm paying for a lot of mistakes," he said. "Maybe it's the way I'm pitching right now that's making me feel this way. ... With this team being where we're at, fighting the way we are, that's not going to do it."
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struggled with location in his last outing, and the Diamondbacks took advantage, scoring four runs off the left-hander over 2 1/3 innings. Rodriguez tied a career-high with six walks and struck out four. The lefty last faced Milwaukee on June 25 at Miller Park, logging the win after yielding one run over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bush's performance may have been lost amid the drama of the Brewers' see-saw win Saturday at Dodger Stadium, but he pitched a gem. Matt Kemp doubled leading off the first inning against Bush and Andre Ethier followed with a home run for a quick 2-0 lead, but Bush then blanked the Dodgers on three more hits through the seventh. Left fielder Gabe Kapler tumbled into the stands to deny the Dodgers a home run in Bush's last inning of work, and he was briefly in line for the win when shortstop J.J. Hardy hit a two-run homer in the eighth. Instead, Bush settled for a no-decision and his seventh outing of at least seven innings in his past 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Duke was hit hard for six runs on nine hits in his last start, against the Mets. The lefty still has not won since June 9. He said he has tried a variety of things to shake up this unfortunate streak, but nothing has worked. Opponents swing freely against Duke, and he rarely gets swings and misses. He'll try to go for win No. 5 against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan has been on again, off again all season, and on Sunday in Los Angeles, he was off. He surrendered four runs on nine Dodgers hits, including a trio of home runs that left the Brewers facing deficits of 3-0 and 4-1. Matt Kemp and Manny Ramirez each hit Suppan's first offering for home runs in the first inning. Before that, Suppan had been outstanding in three starts since his dismal July 27 outing against the Astros, going 3-0 in those games with a 2.05 ERA (five earned runs in 22 innings). The Brewers hope Suppan continues his trend as a strong second-half pitcher. In 2007, his first year with Milwaukee, Suppan posted a 5.00 ERA before the All-Star break but lowered it to 4.12 afterward.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny will make his return to the Majors after spending more than a month at Triple-A Indianapolis. The lefty didn't take the demotion well at first, but he rebounded with a 3-1 record and a 2.06 ERA in seven starts as he rebuilt his arm strength. His last start before being sent down came at Milwaukee on July 4, when he gave up eight runs and 11 hits in 4 2/3 innings. Gorzelanny's promotion means that previously scheduled starter Jeff Karstens will start on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Ned Yost said the decision to keep every starter on regular turn, thus allowing for extra days of rest, played a role in the decision to let Sabathia work all nine innings on Monday against Houston. The Astros sent seven men to the plate and drove the lefty's pitch count to 130 before Lance Berkman bounded out with the bases loaded. The workhorse recorded his fifth shutout in nine starts, and he also had two hits and two huge RBIs in the win. "I guess they're going to hitch their wagon to him and ride him on off in the sunset," Astros manager Cecil Cooper said. "He was a horse tonight. Not only on the mound, but swinging the bat."
away_pitcher_note: Maholm continues to be steady and consistent. His last time out, Maholm pitched at least six innings for a 19th consecutive start. Eleven of his 20 starts have lasted at least seven innings. There's no doubt that his confidence level has soared, and he has all four of his pitches working nearly every time out. The only thing to keep an eye on is his innings total, which is already close to matching his previous career high (177 2/3), which was set last year. Maholm is 0-1 against the Brewers this year. He has allowed five earned runs and struck out 11 in 14 1/3 innings against them.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Wellemeyer didn't finish off hitters the way he wanted to, but he still picked up the win in an 11-2 victory over the Pirates. Wellemeyer needed 95 pitches to get through five innings, but he limited Pittsburgh's damage by making big pitches when he needed to. Wellemeyer has held opposing hitters to a .230 average over his past six starts, and his ERA is 2.48 over that span.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets continued a modest slump since the acquisition of CC Sabathia when he allowed five runs in six innings against Houston on Tuesday in a Brewers loss. Once the ace of the staff, Sheets worked at least seven innings in eight of his first 16 starts, but he has gone that far in just two of his past nine. He has won only once since the team brought Sabathia on board, and the team has lost five of those eight outings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright returned from a 2 1/2-month absence with a flourish on Friday, when he worked six innings against the Braves and allowed just five hits and one run. After recovering from a right middle finger sprain, Wainwright claims he is snapping off his curve as hard or harder than he has all season. Wainwright delivered 72 pitches in his last start and figures that he should be able to build on that total in his next outing.
away_pitcher_note: Parra and the Brewers beat the Astros on Wednesday for Parra's first win in a month, but he still wasn't happy. He faced one batter more than the minimum through three innings, then allowed five hits, three walks and two runs over the next two frames. He escaped with the lead when left fielder Gabe Kapler threw out a runner at the plate to end the fifth inning. Still, it was Parra's first win since July 20, when he was riding an eight-game winning streak. Entering Wednesday's win, Parra was 0-4 with a 5.70 ERA and a .295 opponents' batting average in five starts prior.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny has probably seen enough of the Brewers, but the schedule makers aren't giving him a break. His last two big league starts, both 4 2/3-inning clunkers, came at Milwaukee. An eight-run outing at Miller Park on the Fourth of July got Gorzelanny demoted to Triple-A Indianapolis for a month. He returned on Saturday, only to give up six more runs and exit before the end of the fifth once again. This time, he gets the Brewers at PNC Park, where he's 5-1 with an ERA almost five runs lower than his road mark.
away_pitcher_note: Bush is on a roll. He improved to 3-0 with a 2.30 ERA in four August starts with a win over the Pirates at Miller Park on Aug. 22 and has worked at least into the seventh inning in seven of his last eight starts. He's just 2-6 with a 5.76 ERA in 12 appearances, 11 starts, on the road this season, but has allowed three earned runs in 14 innings over his last two starts away from home. Because of two team off-days this week, Bush will be working on two extra days of rest.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm got a no-decision in his last start, when he went toe to toe with CC Sabathia and tossed six innings of two-run ball. He went six for the 20th straight start, a streak not seen in Pittsburgh in 22 years. Nearly as impressive, Ryan Braun and Prince Fielder grounded into a combined three double plays and struck one time each against the lefty. Maholm hasn't beaten the Brewers in three starts this year, but he had one of his best starts of the year at Miller Park on July 5. Even though Pittsburgh lost, 2-1, he held Milwaukee to one run in eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan apparently benefited from his brief stint on the disabled list over the All-Star break. Since missing one start because of a sore right elbow, he has pitched at least six innings in all seven of his starts and at least seven innings five times. That includes Aug. 23 against the Pirates, when Suppan allowed the leadoff man to reach base in each of the first eight innings but escaped with allowing three runs in seven-plus innings of work. He is 4-0 with a 3.09 ERA in five August starts.

home_pitcher_note: After starting the month out 2-0 with 15 scoreless innings, Karstens has dropped each of his last three starts. He has a 6.75 ERA during that span. And most telling may be this: opponents were hitting .143 against Karstens in those first two starts; they have hit .328 against him since. Location was Karstens' biggest problem in his start Monday against the Cubs, as he left most of his off-speed pitches up and over the plate. The Pirates are going to continue to watch Karstens' pitch count as they don't want to overexert him during this final month. This will be Karstens' first career appearance against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia insisted that his workload in a much-debated 130-pitch outing against the Astros on Aug. 18 had little to do with his command issues six days later against the Pirates. Sabathia surrendered only one run in six innings, but he had to work around eight hits in the shortest of his 10 starts for Milwaukee. Sabathia settled for a no-decision in an eventual 4-3, 12-inning win over Pittsburgh. "I think maybe having six days off had more to do with it than anything," Sabathia said. "But I felt I made some pitches when I needed to and I kept us in the game."

home_pitcher_note: Sheets was backed into a corner in his last start but managed to toss six scoreless innings, working his way out of more than a few jams in the early innings. He struck out twice as many batters has he walked and yielded only five hits against St. Louis. Sheets went as far as six innings all six of his August starts and will try to continue the longevity vs. the Mets, against whom he is 4-2 with a 5.10 ERA in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies were effective in either fouling off Santana's pitches or taking them over the fence, forcing the Mets ace out of the game after six innings with six strikeouts and three runs allowed in a no-decision. He threw 106 pitches, 67 for strikes, and gave up two home runs to end his scoreless innings streak at 16. Next are the Brewers, who Santana has a 3-2 career record against with 3.61 ERA in 47 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Parra's six quality innings last week in St. Louis went for naught, as the Brewers' bullpen gave up four runs in the eighth inning. He's been just as consistent as all of the Brewers' other starters this year and has made many forget that this is only his second year in the big leagues. This will be the second start of Parra's career against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: In the absence of John Maine, who hit the disabled list last week with a bone spur in his right shoulder, the Mets will turn to their top pitching prospect, Niese. Relying on his signature 12-to-6 curveball, Niese posted an 11-8 record and a 3.13 ERA between Double-A Binghamton and Triple-A New Orleans this season -- and after joining the Zephyrs, he lost only once in seven starts. Technically, Niese will be starting on short rest, having pitched on Friday night in New Orleans. But he threw only 65 pitches in that outing, meaning he should be fresh for his Major League debut.

home_pitcher_note: Bush was caught in a heated pitching duel with Pirates starter Tom Gorzelanny on Friday, but Bush was able to escape PNC Park with his ninth win of the year. The quality outing also improved his August record to 4-0. Bush continues to show signs of improvement on the road and is gaining more and more confidence from his manager, Ned Yost. Bush will attempt to keep the good vibrations going against the Mets, whom he is 1-2 with a 3.86 ERA against in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Despite walking five batters on Friday against the Marlins, Oliver Perez allowed only two runs, but he could not muster a win. The five walks weren't even the trouble -- a solo homer, an error and a sacrifice fly amounted for all the damage off Perez. But it was enough. Perez now hasn't won in three starts, marking his longest streak since early June. He'll look to right himself against the Brewers, who tagged him for six runs in 4 1/3 innings back in April.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan capped off a stellar August with a seven-inning, two-run performance against the Pirates. The right-hander finished the month 5-0 and struck out twice as many batters as he walked. Suppan said he used the movement on his fastball to his advantage and mixed in a changeup to keep hitters off balance. He'll need to do the same against the Padres, against whom he is 5-3 with a 5.66 ERA in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Estes, out since May 29 with a fractured left thumb, was activated from the disabled list on Monday. The 35-year-old will be a free agent after the season, and the Padres want to get a look at him as they move forward with an eye on 2009. Estes is 1-1 with a 3.33 ERA in five games this season, including four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia's last start will take a long time to forget. The left-hander threw a one-hit shutout to lift the Brewers to their 20th win in August. But many will remember the play that cost Sabathia and the Brewers the second no-hitter in franchise history. The official scorer called Pirates third baseman Andy LaRoche's fifth-inning dribbler back to the mound a single. The Brewers thought the play was an error by Sabathia, who was unable to throw LaRoche out at first. The victory, however, was Sabathia's 15th win of the year and ninth win as a member of the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Geer was a hit in his Major League debut, allowing two runs in five innings in notching a win. Geer got in trouble early, allowing two runs in the second inning, but finished strong. He allowed just the two runs on five hits with three walks and five strikeouts. He's likely earned himself at least one more start moving forward into September. Prior to being recalled, Geer spent the entire season with Triple-A Portland, going 8-9 with a 4.54 ERA in 28 games, including 27 starts for the Beavers. Geer is one of a handful of young pitchers the Padres are excited about and one the team wants to get a look at over the final month of the regular season.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets believes he will make his next start despite leaving on Monday after five innings with a left groin strain. The early departure was a disappointment for the Brewers on many levels, since Sheets was pitching efficiently and effectively, only to watch the bullpen blow an early lead. Sheets has never recorded 13 victories in a big league season, but this has been his healthiest season since 2004. He said the groin injury that cost him a single start in 2007 was more severe, and his removal on Monday was a precaution.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy looked very much like the NL Cy Young Award winner he was a year ago when he held Colorado to five hits over eight scoreless innings with a season-high 13 strikeouts on Sunday. Peavy relied on his fastball more than he has recently and overpowered the Rockies at times. He lowered his ERA to 2.69 but didn't earn a decision for the sixth time this season, as Trevor Hoffman blew the save opportunity in the ninth inning. Peavy doesn't like the idea of being a .500 pitcher but said that his arm feels good and strong, a good sign heading into the final weeks of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Parra was fuming after he lasted only five innings in a loss to the Mets at Miller Park. His most egregious mistake was a hanging split-fingered fastball to outfielder Carlos Beltran in a full count that was supposed to be in the dirt. Beltran hit it for a three-run home run. "In my opinion, it was another subpar performance," said Parra, who won eight straight decisions from May 20-July 20 but has one win in eight starts since. "I'm catching too much plate. Five innings is just not going to cut it." Parra did hit a couple of doubles in the game, including one that drove home two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Young was activated from the disabled list prior to his last start on Monday against the Dodgers. Understandably, Young -- who missed 18 games with a strained right forearm -- was a little rusty from a command standpoint, walking three over five innings in taking the loss. The Padres have opted to go with a six-man rotation for the time being to get a look at several young pitchers, but to also afford pitchers like Young and Jake Peavy an extra day of rest. Young has walked three or more batters in a game 10 different times this season.

home_pitcher_note: Bush was 4-0 with a 2.12 ERA in five August starts but started September with a six-run first inning against the Mets. He surrendered five hits in the frame including a grand slam to Ryan Church and a solo home run to Brian Schneider, when settled in to allow no more runs and only two hits through the end of the fifth. It was a rare poor start for Bush at Miller Park, where he's 6-4 with a 3.62 ERA (versus 3-6 with a 5.32 ERA on the road).
away_pitcher_note: Volquez pitched seven innings and gave up four earned runs and six hits with a career-high 13 strikeouts in a well-pitched performance Wednesday vs. the Pirates. But, he ended up with a no-decision during a 6-5 Reds' loss. Throwing as hard as 96 mph, the right-hander retired the side in order in five of his seven innings. All of his runs and hits came during the fourth and sixth innings when he had trouble hitting his spots. Volquez still has an outside shot to become the first Reds pitcher to win 20 games since Danny Jackson in 1988.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan consistently missed Thursday with a two-seam fastball that cut back over home plate instead of diving away from the right-handed Padres' hitters in a lifeless, 5-2 loss. It was Suppan's first loss since he surrendered eight earned runs on 11 hits on July 27 against the Astros, and came on the heels of a 5-0 August. One of Suppan's wins during the month came in Cincinnati, where he held the Reds to three runs in seven innings. He took a no-decision against the Reds in his only start against them at Miller Park (two earned runs, three hits in 6 2/3 innings on April 19).
away_pitcher_note: Rookie Ramon Ramirez will make this start in place of Josh Fogg, who came out of Thursday's game vs. the Pirates after three innings because of a strained right groin. Fogg was hurt trying to score on a sacrifice fly. Ramirez took over and threw three perfect innings of relief for a no-decision as the Reds notched an 8-6 comeback win. On Aug. 30 vs. the Giants, Ramirez gave up three earned runs and five hits with two walks and six strikeouts during a seven-inning quality start that went for a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia did his part on Friday against the Padres, but the Brewers couldn't close the deal in time for his 10th National League win. Sabathia allowed a leadoff baserunner in five of his seven innings, but he limited the Padres to one run on five hits and went 2-for-3 at the plate, including a go-ahead single. The lead got away from reliever Eric Gagne, but the Brewers rallied to improve to 11-1 in Sabathia's starts. He's the second pitcher in the past 90 seasons to win his first nine decisions after a midseason change of teams. The other is Doyle Alexander, who was traded from the Braves to the Tigers in 1987 for John Smoltz.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, on Friday, Arroyo struck out the first three Cubs he faced on 10 pitches before getting a big lead and cruising thereafter for his 14th win of the season. The 31-year-old right-hander went 6 1/3 innings and gave up just one run on four hits, striking out six, in the Reds' big win over the Cubs. A high pitch count drove Arroyo out early, as he threw a season-high 122 pitches before being chased midway through the seventh inning. The right-hander has faced the Brewers twice this season, going 1-1 with a 3.86 ERA in 11 2/3 innings. Lifetime, Arroyo is 7-4 with a 3.62 ERA in 14 appearances (11 starts) against Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer, who threw seven shutout innings in the first game of Sunday's doubleheader, has been the Phils' most consistent starting pitcher in 2008. He leads the team in wins (13) and has held opponents to three runs or fewer in 16 of his past 17 starts. The 45-year-old does will be pitching on three days rest, something he has not done in his two-plus seasons with the Phillies. Moyer earned a no-decision earlier this season against the Brewers, holding them to one run in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets shook off injury concerns and demonstrated just how important he is to the Brewers in his last start, on Saturday. Sheets threw his third shutout of the season -- after having just one in his career entering 2008 -- and recorded his career-best 13th victory in a 1-0 outdueling of Jake Peavy and the Padres. The electric performance came one start after left groin tightness caused Sheets to leave a start, and he also shook off the effects of numbness in his fingers, the result of a Peavy slider off the end of Sheets' bat. He gets a big start in the opener of a four-game set against the team's closest competitor in the National League Wild Card race, the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels arrived in New York last weekend on the heels of a 17-start stretch in which he had posted a 2.53 ERA. But he allowed the Mets three runs in the first inning and labored the rest of the way, needing 110 pitches to get through five innings. Still, it was only the third time since June 28 that Hamels has allowed four earned runs in a start. In four career starts against the Brewers, Hamels is 1-1 with a 4.76 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Parra gave up six runs in five innings on Sunday, though five of those were unearned after a pair of infield gaffes led to a big inning against the Padres. Parra would have had to seriously deal to keep up with opposing starter Chris Young, who lost a perfect game with four outs to go, but it was another in a growing series of short starts. Parra has one victory in his past six decisions and has worked beyond the sixth just once since July 20.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, Blanton earned his second win as a Phillie since his July trade from Oakland. In five innings against the Marlins, he allowed four runs, walking three and striking out one. The right-hander's control has been shaky in his first 10 starts with the Phillies. In a span of 52 2/3 innings with his new team, Blanton has walked 26. For Oakland last season, he issued only 40 in 230 innings. He has never faced Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Bush was on track for his 10th win before Salomon Torres surrendered three Reds runs on Monday. Bush, who had lost his previous start after a 4-0 August, scattered seven hits in eight innings and allowed two runs, his first eight-inning outing since July 10. He faced the Phillies on April 23 at Miller Park and allowed four runs on eight hits in six innings, but took a no-decision in a Brewers win.

home_pitcher_note: Myers, who will be pitching on three days' rest, lost to the Marlins on Wednesday, allowing four runs in 7 1/3 innings, striking out nine and walking one. He threw 117 pitches, among his higher pitch counts of 2008. He has started on three days' rest only once before in his career, on Oct. 3, 2004. He beat the Marlins that day, holding Florida to three runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan took a shutout into the fifth inning against the Reds on Wednesday, then allowed four runs in the span of two innings. The real damage came in the sixth, when he surrendered a two-run home run to Edwin Encarnacion followed by a solo shot to Jay Bruce that put the Brewers in a 4-1 hole. The Brewers have lost both of Suppan's September starts after winning five of six in August. He limited the Phillies to a run on five hits in seven innings at Miller Park on April 24, but settled for a no-decision in a 3-1 Brewers loss.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster will try for the third time to notch his 16th win. In his last start against the Cardinals, the right-hander posted his 20th quality start and fifth in his last six games. Dempster gave up three runs on seven hits, including Albert Pujols' three-run homer, over seven innings. Dempster is 1-2 this season against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers have the right man on the mound for the opener of a crucial three-game series against the division-leading Cubs. Sabathia has been stuck at 9-0 since his near no-hitter in Pittsburgh, but he pitched well in seven innings against the Reds on Wednesday. He was burned by Jerry Hairston's three-run home run, but otherwise held Cincinnati at bay while striking out eight in an eventual 4-3 Brewers win that averted a three-game Cincinnati sweep. He had to work through 6 2/3 innings against the Cubs at Miller Park on July 28, allowing four runs, three of them earned, on nine hits. It was the only one of Sabathia's 13 Brewers starts that ended in a Milwaukee loss.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis is coming off a win over the Reds Sept. 6 when he gave up two runs on five hits and five walks over 7 1/3 innings. The right-hander has been given more time between starts -- although this delay was created because of Hurricane Ike -- and has responded well. Since the All-Star break, Marquis is 4-3 with a 4.23 ERA. He was 6-5 with a 4.44 ERA in the first half. He faced the Brewers back on April 29, and took the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a 1-0 shutout of the Padres in his last start and riding a 20-inning scoreless streak, Sheets was knocked around by the Phillies for five runs on nine hits in six innings. Ryan Howard set an early tone -- and snapped the scoreless innings streak -- with a two-run home run off Sheets in the first inning, and he added an RBI double in the fourth as the Phillies built a 4-1 lead. In his most recent start against the Cubs, Sheets matched his season highs, allowing 11 hits and six runs at Miller Park on July 29 during a four-game Chicago sweep. Sheets was better at Wrigley Field, where he allowed three earned runs in 11 1/3 innings over two starts, both Brewers wins.

home_pitcher_note: Harden will be coming off a win over the Cardinals. The right-hander gave up two runs on five hits over six innings. He's now 5-1 with a 1.81 ERA since the All-Star break. If you watched the stadium radar gun speeds, his velocity was down a little against St. Louis. But Harden says that's not a problem -- and he's working on locating his pitches. He picked up a win over Milwaukee on July 31, giving up one run on six hits over seven innings and striking out nine.
away_pitcher_note: With the dismissal of manager Ned Yost, the Brewers knew that changes would occur, and new skipper Dale Sveum wasted no time in shaking things up. After allowing no fewer than five runs in any of his last three starts, Manny Parra was removed from the rotation, replaced by Bush, who moved up a day and will start Thursday�s series finale in Chicago on short rest. With the exception of one start against the Mets, Bush hasn't given up more than three runs in any of his eight August-September starts.

home_pitcher_note: This will be the second time in a row that the Brewers will get Ramirez, who was skipped in his last turn of the rotation because of a scheduled off-day. In his second career big league start on Sept. 9, the righty gave up just one earned run and one hit over six innings with four walks and four strikeouts. He did not figure in the decision in a game won by the Reds, 5-4. Ramirez survived what could have been a disastrous 35-pitch first inning that featured two walks, a balk and an error on a routine popup. Following the second inning, Ramirez faced the minimum number of hitters and retired his final 10 in a row. In two starts and one relief appearance, he has allowed just one right-handed batter to get a hit.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers badly needed a good outing from Suppan in Game 2 of a doubleheader on Sunday, and Suppan didn't deliver. The Phillies tagged him for six earned runs and eight hits in 3 2/3 innings of a 6-1 loss, and Suppan fell to 0-2 in September after going 5-0 in August.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto labored in a big way for a no-decision during Sunday's 2-1 Reds win in 10 innings at Arizona. Although he allowed only one run and four hits, the familiar issue of pitch conservation loomed large. Cueto threw 115 pitches in only five innings and allowed six walks. In two starts this season vs. the Brewers, the 22-year-old right-hander is 0-0 with a 2.70 ERA with two walks and 13 strikeouts over 13 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: With the Brewers' rotation suddenly in total disarray, the team announced Friday that Sabathia will work Saturday's game on three days' rest. The left-hander finally suffered a loss Tuesday in his 14th Brewers start, allowing four runs on nine hits in seven innings at Wrigley Field, with three of the runs and seven of the hits coming before Sabathia recorded his seventh out of the game. He had not allowed more than three earned runs in a game since July 2, when he was pitching for Cleveland at the Chicago White Sox. He's winless in his last three Brewers starts, including a Sept. 10 no-decision against the Reds at Miller Park in which Sabathia surrendered three runs on eight hits in seven innings. It's the first true start of his career on short rest, though Sabathia did throw 71 pitches on three days' rest in the final start of his rookie season in 2001, when the Indians were lining up their rotation for the postseason. Sabathia limited the Blue Jays to one run and one hit in five innings that day.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo is on a roll and just notched his career high in wins. Over his last 15 starts, he is 11-3 with a 2.88 ERA and 5-0 with a 1.45 ERA over his last six starts. During Tuesday's 7-2 win over the Cardinals, the right-hander gave up two earned runs and five hits, including two solo homers, without a walk and four strikeouts. He credits his nice run to a change in his sinker grip that has helped him keep hitters more off balance. At 187 innings, he still has a shot at getting 200 innings for the fourth straight year.
away_pitcher_note: McClung was supposed to return to the rotation two days earlier, but he was needed in emergency relief on Thursday in Chicago, so the move was postponed. One of new Brewers manager Dale Sveum's first moves was to bounce struggling left-hander Manny Parra from the rotation and replace him with McClung, who had been serving in a long-relief role. McClung is 4-4 with a 4.33 ERA in 11 starts this season, including a July 12 loss to the Reds at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Bush is the most likely choice to take the injured Ben Sheets' spot because he would be on regular rest. Bush hasn't won this month, but he hasn't pitched poorly. He has not given up more than three runs in any of his past three starts, including his last outing, at Wrigley Field on three days' rest. The right-hander held the Cubs to a pair of solo homers in five innings and would have received the win if Salomon Torres hadn't blown a four-run lead in the ninth. In his last start against Pittsburgh, Bush gave up one run in 6 2/3 innings on Aug. 29 to get his ninth win. He's 2-1 with a 3.71 ERA in four starts against the Pirates this season.
away_pitcher_note: A bad umpiring call worked against Karstens in his last start, though the right-hander can't escape the fact that he allowed 11 hits and needed 91 pitches to finish five innings. Fatigue seems to have set in with Karstens some, and for a pitcher who is not overpowering, that has been just enough to give opponents the edge. Karstens has lost each of his last six starts. One of those losses came against Milwaukee, though it was more a reflection of how good CC Sabathia was than how off Karstens may have been. Karstens allowed three runs on five hits in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia will be working on short rest for the second straight start and could pitch short again in the regular-season finale, if needed, as the Brewers get every last mile out of their second-half rental. He worked on three days' rest in his last outing, at Cincinnati, and surrendered four runs, though three scored unearned after a Prince Fielder error. Sabathia, who is coming up on free agency, isn't worried that some of his postseason suitors will be turned off by his heavy late-season workload. "I'm doing this to get in the playoffs and I really don't care what other teams say or are worried about," he said.
away_pitcher_note: For the ninth time this season, Maholm picked up a no-decision in a start in which he allowed three or fewer runs. In fact in five of those no-decisions, he's given up one or none. Maholm did issue six walks in his last start, though they were a quiet six walks. The seven innings Maholm pitched pushed him over the 200-inning mark, but put him comfortably in position not to exceed the 211-inning maximum set my management. Maholm is still looking for his first win against the Brewers this season. He is 0-2 against them and has allowed 13 runs in 25 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers are rolling the dice to some extent with Gallardo, who has not pitched in a game since he tore the ACL in his right knee on May 1 at Wrigley Field. He underwent surgery and quietly rehabbed all summer, and the Brewers believe he'll be good for about 70 pitches against the Pirates. Gallardo is a fine hitter, but did not pick up a bat until Wednesday, so it will be interesting to see how he approaches his at-bats. He can also expect the Pirates to drop a bunt or two to test his mobility. Left-hander Manny Parra and right-hander Seth McClung will be on high alert in the bullpen should Gallardo need a bailout.
away_pitcher_note: Duke's last start against the Dodgers was eerily similar to ones that preceded it. The left-hander strung together three goose eggs to begin the game, but was hit hard with a four-run inning. He would eventually be taken after five-plus innings, where he allowed 11 hits and five runs. Duke has only one victory in the second half of the 2008 season. He'll look to close the year on a good note against the Brewers, who he is 3-4 with a 5.08 ERA against in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan has not pitched since Friday in Cincinnati, when he surrendered five runs in two innings and fell to 0-3 in September with a 10.47 ERA. He insists that he's healthy, and acting manager Dale Sveum said he has no reason to suspect otherwise. But how else to explain Suppan's sudden struggles after he went 5-0 with a 3.00 ERA in August? Suppan is 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA in a pair of starts against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster threw an efficient 67 pitches over five innings in his last start against the Cardinals. He was pulled early on purpose as the Cubs prepare for the postseason. The right-hander now has totaled 200 innings for the first time since 2001. He did not issue a walk for the sixth time in his career and first since June 11. He's 4-0 against the Brewers this year.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets left his Sept. 17 start at Chicago because of that injury and revealed to reporters after the game that he had been experiencing a "cutting" sensation in his right elbow since the final week in August. He threw a bullpen session Thursday and declared himself good to go on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly picked up his career-high 16th win in his last start against the Cardinals. That game also was when the Cubs clinched the National League Central.
