The lefty is 3-0 with a 2.05 ERA in his last three starts. He's probably happier that he picked up another RBI with a successful suicide squeeze. He's driven in five runs for the second straight season.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia will make his third consecutive start on three days' rest. He is a free agent after the season, and with Ben Sheets' struggles on Saturday and Manny Parra working in the bullpen amid concerns about his workload, the Brewers are trying to get every last pitch out of Sabathia.
away_pitcher_note: Guzman will get the start in the regular season finale. The Cubs had considered Carlos Zambrano, but he wanted a side day on Sunday instead in preparation for the postseason. Guzman most likely will not be on the playoff roster. The young right-hander is coming back from elbow surgery last August, and also has had shoulder surgery. This will be his 14th career start and first since May 17, 2007.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies' leader in innings and ERA among starters (3.09) will be making his second Game 1 start after working against the Rockies to kick off the NLDS last season. A rough second inning doomed him in a 4-2 defeat, and he didn't get another chance as the Rockies won the next two games for a sweep. The Phils' lefty ace will be facing the Brewers for the sixth time in his career, and has a 4.41 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: In choosing Gallardo, Brewers manager Dale Sveum picked raw talent over experience. He could have used postseason stalwart Jeff Suppan (5-2 with a 3.00 ERA in nine career postseason starts) on regular rest or Dave Bush on three days' rest. Instead, Sveum went with Gallardo, the Brewers' most promising young pitcher, but also a 22-year-old less than five months removed from a major right knee injury. He had surgery to repair a torn ACL in May and was back in Milwaukee's rotation on Sept. 25 for a start against the Pirates. He threw 67 pitches in four innings and allowed one run on three hits, including a Steve Pearce solo home run. He looked extremely good on the mound but in his only at-bat, Gallardo never took the bat off his shoulder. It was sign that the Brewers did not want him on the basepaths with a surgically repaired knee.

home_pitcher_note: Myers' second-half resurgence gave the Phillies an acquisition as valuable as CC Sabathia or Rich Harden. The righty posted a 1.80 ERA in 11 starts -- and dominated. There is some concern regarding his final two outings of the season, in which he allowed 14 earned runs and 19 hits in 8 1/3 innings. He has a 1.77 ERA in eight career appearances against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Make it four straight starts on three days' rest for Sabathia, who continues to cement his status as the greatest midseason pickup in Major League history. Sabathia carried the Brewers to their first postseason bid in 26 years on Sunday in Milwaukee, allowing an unearned run on four hits in a complete-game, 122-pitch win over the Cubs. Less than an hour later, after a Mets loss, the Brewers won the Wild Card. The Brewers squeezed every ounce of energy out of their prized rental. Sabathia threw 334 pitches the last nine days of the regular season, starting three straight times on three days' rest.

home_pitcher_note: Bush went 7-3 over his final 18 regular-season appearances with a 3.23 ERA and was charged with three or fewer earned runs in 13 of those 17 starts. But Bush, who was 4-0 in August with a 2.12 ERA, was not immune to the Brewers' September swoon. He was winless in five September starts with a 4.97 ERA before working three scoreless frames in Milwaukee's next-to-last game of the year. That September streak included a loss in Game 1 of a Sept. 14 doubleheader in Philadelphia. Bush was charged with three runs on five hits in that game, a 7-3 Brewers loss.
away_pitcher_note: No one will be more prepared for the big game than Jamie Moyer, who pitched the division-clinching game for Philadelphia for the second straight season. Moyer won 16 games, tying Phil Niekro for the most wins by a pitcher beyond  his 45th birthday, and recorded the most wins since winning 21 in 2003. The lefty has a 2.43 ERA in five career postseason starts.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan was bumped all the way to Game 4 after struggling to an 0-3 record and a 8.44 ERA in five September starts. But this is precisely the kind of situation Brewers officials envisioned for Suppan when they gave him a four-year, $42 million contract on Christmas Eve 2006. In fact, when general manager Doug Melvin gathered his baseball staff at a Scottsdale, Ariz., restaurant that October to begin planning for the postseason, a television carried Game 7 of the 2006 National League Championship Series, Suppan?s signature performance. He worked seven strong innings against the Mets that night to help send the Cardinals to the World Series. He is 5-2 in his nine career playoff starts with a 3.00 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton will be making his first career postseason start. He worked two innings in relief against Detroit in 2006. The right-hander was acquired in July for three Minor Leaguers and has gone 4-0 with a 4.20 ERA in 13 starts for Philadelphia. He has allowed three or fewer earned runs in eight of those outings. He will be working on eight days' rest.

home_pitcher_note: He'll have to overachieve to exceed last season's accomplishments. As all Giants fans know, Lincecum won the National League Cy Young Award, electrifying the baseball world with his charismatic combination of style (a big leaguer resembling a member of a teenage garage band) and substance (a 5-foot-11, 170-pound pixie throwing with the force of a behemoth).
away_pitcher_note: The 34-year-old Suppan has been here before. He started three consecutive season openers for the Royals from 2000-2002 but was 0-1 in those games, allowing 20 hits including nine home runs in 16 innings. His most recent Brewers start was not much better. After Dave Bush pitched the Brewers to a Game 3 win in the NLDS to stave off elimination, Suppan, who has the reputation of being a postseason stalwart, took the mound for Game 4 and surrendered a first-pitch homer to Philadelphia Jimmy Rollins that was one of three home runs off Suppan in three innings. It capped a tough finish to the season for the veteran, who went 5-0 with a 3.00 ERA in August and then 0-3 with an 8.44 ERA in September. His troubles, Suppan concedes now, date back to an elbow injury in May that briefly landed him on the disabled list over the All-Star break. Suppan gets the nod here over the offseason favorite to start Opening Day, 23-year-old Yovani Gallardo. Manager Ken Macha wanted a veteran for the assignment.

home_pitcher_note: The "Big Unit" will make his regular season Giants debut after spending eight of his previous 10 years with the Arizona Diamondbacks. Johnson, who's entering his 22nd season, needs five victories to reach 300 for his career. He hopes to maintain the momentum he established in the second half of 2008, when his 2.41 ERA ranked fifth among National League pitchers. Johnson struggled against the Brewers last year, losing both of his starts against them while recording a 9.00 ERA. But he's 18-9 with a 3.70 ERA lifetime against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: He just turned 23 at the end of February, but Gallardo pitches much older than that and could grow into the Brewers' newest ace with a healthy 2009 season. He missed much of '08 after a serious knee injury that required surgery, though he did return in time to start Game 1 of the National League Division Series against the Phillies. It was Milwaukee's first postseason game since 1982, and that Gallardo was interim manager Dale Sveum's choice spoke volumes about the organization's trust in the young pitcher. He has faced the Giants twice in his career and has allowed eight runs in 9 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: It's easy to forget that Cain is still only 24, 3 1/2 months younger than Tim Lincecum, yet has already started 104 games. Cain has steadily increased his workload in his three full big league seasons, from 190 2/3 innings in 2006 to an even 200 in 2007 to 217 2/3 last year. He has established a reputation for unluckiness, having received the second-lowest run support in the Majors in each of the last two seasons. No wonder his record in that span is 15-30.
away_pitcher_note: Parra is a Northern California native who has pitched extremely well against the Giants in his brief career. He is 2-0 with a 2.95 ERA in five appearances that span 18 1/3 innings. The 26-year-old is looking to bounce back from a somewhat disappointing finish to last season, when he was bounced from the starting rotation in September due to a slide probably related to fatigue. He was 8-2 with a 3.78 ERA in 19 games before the All-Star break and 2-7 with a 4.87 ERA after. The Brewers hope the first-half Parra shows up for the full 2009 season.

home_pitcher_note: Looper has been on a fast track to this start -- Milwaukee's home opener -- leaving him a bit behind the rest of the starters in terms of arm strength. He was set back by about two weeks, beginning Feb. 28, when he strained a muscle at the back of his left rib cage. He didn't make his first Cactus League appearance until March 26, and in his two official games surrendered seven earned runs on 14 hits in six innings. He made his finale tuneup in Minor League camp. The Brewers signed Looper to a one-year deal to deepen a starting rotation that lost CC Sabathia and Ben Sheets to free agency, and he'll be counted on as an innings-eater, but he needs to find the sink on his fastball in order to be effective. In his final official exhibition game against the Padres, he faced 22 hitters and induced only five ground balls.
away_pitcher_note: Harden moved to Arizona this offseason so he could rehab with the Cubs staff, and the extra effort appears to have paid off. The only thing that has slowed him was some bad chicken salad. A bout with food poisoning resulted in Harden losing seven pounds and missing one spring start. The Cubs have been careful with him, making sure he has plenty of time to strengthen his shoulder. Last year marked the first time he faced the Brewers, and he was 1-0 with a 1.50 ERA in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bush starts the season as Milwaukee No. 5 starter, but he better than that, going 33-31 in his three-year Brewers career, with a 4.57 ERA and at least 185 innings each season. His strength is his ability to limit baserunners. Bush has finished in the National League top five in WHIP (walks plus hits per innings pitched) in two of the past three seasons, finishing  fifth last year at 1.14, behind league leader Cole Hamels (1.08) of the Phillies, Ricky Nolasco of the Marlins, Dan Haren of the D-Backs and Derek Lowe of the Dodgers. The rest of the top 10 reads like an All-Star team: Johan Santana, Ben Sheets, Tim Lincecum, Roy Oswalt, Jake Peavy. ou can score runs if you don get guys on base," Brewers manager Ken Macha said.  very impressed with him. I saw him pitch when he was in Toronto, and he knows what he doing out there. He got a lot of 'equipmentto get you out a lot of different ways." Bush has really struggled against the Cubs, going 1-7 in his career, despite a respectable 4.84 ERA. But he is excellent at Miller Park: 28-20 with a 3.82 ERA in 71 appearances vs. 15-26 with a 5.18 ERA on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano can take a deep breath. He finally won on Opening Day, beating the Astros 4-2 in his fifth season-opening assignment. Big Z gave up one run over six-plus innings and struck out six. He was 1-0 with a 0.43 ERA in three starts against the Brewers last year. The last time Zambrano pitched at Miller Park was Sept. 14 and he threw a no-hitter. That game was against the Astros, also, who were relocated because of Hurricane Ike. The last time he faced the Brewers on their home turf was last July 29, when he threw eight shutout innings, giving up five runs and striking out nine.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan wouldn't see it this way because of his start-to-start focus, but Brewers fans would like to see him bounce back from a lousy finish to 2008 and it didn't happen on Opening Day. Suppan, who had a fabulous August but went 0-3 with an 8.44 ERA in September and then lost Game 4 of the National League Division Series, was hit for six runs over four innings against the Giants on Tuesday in a 10-6 Milwaukee loss. He dropped to 0-2 in his four Opening Day starts with an 8.55 ERA and, including Aaron Rowand's blast Tuesday, he has surrendered 10 home runs in those games. Suppan started three straight season openers for the Royals from 2000-2002. He is 6-6 with a 3.60 ERA in his career against the Cubs, including 1-1 last season, when he surrendered 11 runs in 15 innings against Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster did not get a decision in his first start Tuesday in Houston. The right-hander did notch a quality start, giving up two runs on six hits over six innings but the Astros won in extra innings. Dempster struck out five and walked three. He was 4-0 with a 2.40 ERA in five starts against the Brewers last year. His defense definitely helped as Alfonso Soriano robbed Michael Bourn of extra bases with a running catch and also threw out Hunter Pence, who was trying to advance on a long single.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo was good on the mound in his 2009 debut -- 6 2/3 innings, six hits, two runs against the Giants on Wednesday -- and even better at the plate. Gallardo turned on a Randy Johnson pitch in the fifth inning for a two-out, two-strike, three-run home run that gave the Brewers a 4-1 lead. It was his third career homer and it propelled him to his first win since Sept. 17, 2007. He missed most of 2008 with knee injuries but did face the Reds, allowing one run and four hits in seven innings in his season debut. The Brewers lost that game in extra innings and went on to play extras in three of his four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez lacked command and pitch economy as he used 107 pitches in just 4 1/3 innings for a 9-7 loss to the Mets on Wednesday. He allowed five earned runs and six hits with four walks and four strikeouts. Lacking a put-away pitch hurt Volquez a couple of times. A two-out walk came before Carlos Delgado's first-inning two-run homer. There was a 32-pitch fourth after two outs when he gave up a double and two walks.  In three starts vs. the Brewers last season, Volquez was 1-1 with a 5.09 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Parra looked superb through the first three innings of his first start of the season and looked just as dreadful the rest of the way of what turned out to be an ominous performance. He gave up all five of his runs in his final 1 1-3 innings of work and allowed seven of the final 10 hitters he faced to reach base. The Brewers have lost the last nine games, dating to last year, in which he's appeared and Parra lost for the seventh time in his past eight decisions. If past numbers are any indication, he could be in for another tough day against the Reds, whom gave scored 16 runs on 17 hits in 16 1-3 career innings against him. There's some good news though: he's a much better pitcher at home.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo overcame a bumpy beginning and earned an 8-6 win over the Mets on Thursday. He gave up five earned runs and eight hits over six innings, with two walks and four strikeouts. Only a few days before the start, he received a cortisone shot to lessen the pain from carpal tunnel in his right arm. Arroyo reported no issues the day after the start and is expected to be fine. Last season in four starts vs. the Brewers, he was 1-2 with a 3.65 ERA and is 7-5 with a 3.59 ERA in 16 career games against Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Looper limited the Cubs to a run in five innings for a solid Brewers debut, but wasn't exactly jumping up and down about it. "I definitely wouldn't say that I pitched my best," said Looper, who missed the first half of Spring Training with a rib cage injury. "I knew early on that I didn't have my command like I normally do. But I had a really good changeup, and I was just trying to keep the ball down and let the guys make plays." He issued four walks in the game, but mitigated them with four strikeouts and one key double play, initiated on a slick defensive play by second baseman Rickie Weeks. The Brewers won the game in the ninth inning but Looper remained winless at Miller Park, 0-4 now in 19 career appearances including four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Owings got bumped back after a rainout on Friday forced manager Dusty Baker to alter his rotation. The right-hander earned the fifth starter's spot with a strong Spring Training in which he was 3-1 with a 1.52 ERA, 10 walks and 24 strikeouts in six starts over 23 2/3 innings. A .319 lifetime hitter with five homers, Owings will also be a threat from the ninth spot in the Reds' order. Last season, Owings was 6-9 with a 5.93 ERA in 22 games for the Diamondbacks after starting 2008 with a 4-0 record and 2.42 ERA. A sore shoulder ended Owings' season as a pitcher before his trade to the Reds in exchange for Adam Dunn. He was still used as a pinch-hitter. Lifetime vs. the Brewers, he is 0-2 with a 8.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Needing some measure of length from their fifth starter after none of the previous four had survived the middle innings, the Mets received precisely that from Hernandez. Against a Marlins team that had averaged nearly eight runs per game heading into Saturday's game, Hernandez pitched 6 2/3 innings, allowing two runs -- one on a bloop, the other on the bullpen's inherited runner. For his career against the Brewers, Hernandez is 7-6 with a 3.77 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Bush settled for no decision in his first start of the season on Saturday, when he surrendered three earned runs on six hits in 6 1/3 effective innings against the Cubs. Bush walked two and struck out five, and might have been out of trouble with only two runs on his record if not for a close call at first base by umpire Angel Hernandez that went against Milwaukee. Bush has traditionally struggled away from home; he was 28-20 with a 3.82 ERA in home games and 15-26 with a 5.18 ERA away from home entering this season, a trend he will look to reverse. He has pitched twice in New York, but both outings were against the Yankees during Bush's Blue Jays days. He is 2-1 despite a 6.75 ERA in three career starts against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Despite striking out 13 batters and allowing just three hits, Santana took his first loss of the season in last Sunday's game against the Marlins. Sound familiar? This one wasn't the fault of the bullpen, but of some shaky defense in left field and an offense that could not muster a single run. Santana, now 1-1 with one earned run and 20 strikeouts in two starts, will look to change his luck against the Brewers. Against the Brewers last year, he recorded a loss and a no-decision -- and 17 strikeouts -- in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Milwaukee's ace in the making imploded in the third inning of his most recent start against the Reds after his teammates built him a comfortable 5-1 lead. Gallardo retired the first two hitters he faced, but the next six reached safely on two hits, three walks and a hit batsmen. The hit batsman was Jay Bruce with the bases loaded, and Edwin Encarnacion launched Gallardo's next pitch for a go-ahead grand slam. Gallardo has never faced the Mets. He'll be pitching on regular rest here, despite the Brewers' off-day since his last start, because manager Ken Macha flipped Gallardo and Jeff Suppan in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Given the Brewers' righty-heavy lineup, the right-handed Figueroa was the logical choice to start in place of Mike Pelfrey, who was diagnosed with right forearm tendinitis on Tuesday. A fill-in starter for the Mets last season, Figueroa last pitched for Triple-A Buffalo on Thursday but was pulled after only two innings. In two games in the Minors this year, Figueroa has a 3.00 ERA over nine innings. He was 3-3 with a 4.57 ERA in 16 Major League games last season.
away_pitcher_note: The good news was that Suppan surrendered only two hits in his most recent outing against the Cubs. The bad news was that he issued six walks, including four in the fourth inning and three with the bases loaded, and he didn't make it through that frame. In two starts this season, Suppan has started only nine of the 20 hitters he's faced with Strike 1, and pitching coach Bill Castro planned to work with the veteran between starts on "throwing" his pitches with conviction instead of "aiming" them. "It's mental more than anything else," Castro said. In his last eight starts dating to last season and including the playoffs, Suppan is winless with a 10.13 ERA and has surrendered 12 home runs. He will be pitching on two extra days' rest here, a move that allowed Suppan three between-starts throwing sessions instead of his usual two.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer has allowed four runs in each of his first two starts this season, but picked up the win a week ago Monday in a 9-8 victory over the Nationals at Nationals Park. It was a tough day to pitch for Moyer, who grew in Souderton, Pa. It was tough because Hall of Fame broadcaster and Philadelphia icon Harry Kalas died just hours before the game. Moyer grew up listening to him. But perhaps under better conditions, Moyer will return to 2008 form against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Parra allowed three runs on only three hits in six innings of his last start against the Reds, but his pitch count reached 66 by the end of the third inning and two of the three runners who scored reached on walks. He was more efficient beginning with a five-pitch fourth inning, throwing 18 pitches in the fifth inning and 14 in the sixth thanks to an Edwin Encarnacion double play. With Parra at the 103-pitch mark after that frame, the Brewers were forced to dip back into the bullpen. Still, it was an improvement for Parra, who lasted only 4 1/3 innings in his season debut because of walks. "I just felt like I had to get through a minimum of six innings for the bullpen and for the team," Parra said. His changeup remains a developing pitch; he surrendered a go-ahead homer to Jerry Hairston on one, but also used it to induce Encarnacion's double play. Commanding that pitch is the key to Parra's success.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton is still searching for his first victory of 2009. After a rocky season debut against the Braves on April 8, the right-hander improved on Thursday against the Nationals, giving up eight hits and three earned runs while striking out five and walking one in six innings. The big blow was a three-run homer to Adam Dunn in the first inning. In two starts, Blanton has surrendered 17 hits and 10 earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Looper impressed Brewers manager Ken Macha by pounding the strike zone in his first Brewers win, a victory over the Reds on April 15 at Miller Park. Looper limited the damage to three runs on six hits in six innings, and he struck out five batters versus one walk. It was much better than his Brewers debut in the home opener, a no-decision against the Cubs in which Looper walked four batters in five innings. He's 2-6 with a 5.53 ERA in 60 career appearances against the Phillies, but he started only two of those games. In the starts, he's 0-2 with a more respectable 4.15 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels took a step forward Friday in an 8-7 loss to San Diego at Citizens Bank Park, despite allowing eight hits, five runs, one walk and three home runs in six innings. He took a step forward because he increased the velocity on his fastball about five miles per hour, from 85-86 mph in his season debut April 10 in Colorado to about 89-90 mph. That gives him better separation from his changeup. The next step for Hamels is improving the location of his pitches. Once he does that, Hamels believes he will round back into form as the ace of the staff the Phillies need him to be.
away_pitcher_note: Bush has faced the Phillies three times at Citizens Bank Park, where he has no record and a 4.86 ERA in 17 1/3 innings. And in six outings against the Phillies in his career, the right-hander is 0-0 with 5.88 ERA in 33 2/3 innings. Bush is coming off an outing against the Mets in New York in which he started very poorly and finished with reason to be encouraged. He took the mound with a 6.14 ERA. He gave up hits to the first three Mets he faced and was down, 3-0, after facing all nine men in the batting order before ending the long inning. Then Bush pitched five scoreless innings of three-hit ball while his team overcame the 3-0 deficit to take a 4-3 lead. But Milwaukee's bullpen couldn't hold the lead and Bush got no decision.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino "opened some eyes," as Cecil Cooper said, after his last outing, during which he held the Reds scoreless over a six-inning, 97-pitch performance. That was Paulino's first big league start of the season after having two impressive outings for Triple-A Round Rock. Paulino has faced the Brewers twice in his career, allowing 10 runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo had much to be happy about in his last start. Even though he took a no-decision in a game the Brewers lost, 1-0, to the Mets in New York, the starter matched two-time Cy Young Award winner Johan Santana pitch for pitch. Gallardo worked six shutout innings, striking out seven and walking two. Even better, he didn't have his breaking ball in the early innings and recorded outs with his fastball until he found the touch on his breaking ball. Gallardo is 2-0 against the Astros during his young career and threw a season-high eight shutout innings in a 6-0 win against Houston in his only start at Minute Maid Park, which came on Sept. 7, 2007. Gallardo was born in Mexico, but he moved to Texas at and early age.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Hampton pitched well enough to win but took a no-decision when the bullpen blew a lead against the Reds. Hampton yielded three runs in 6 1/3 innings, walking one and striking out five. The left-hander did not face the Brewers in 2008, but he has appeared in 11 games against Milwaukee in his career, going 4-2 with a 2.87 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan struggled mightily in his first two starts of 2009, but he pitched a gem to help the Brewers salvage a win in their series against the Mets. New York scored in the first inning against Suppan on two hits, a walk and a wild pitch, but he settled in after that, yielding just three hits over the next four innings and surviving a pair of two-out hits in the sixth. Houston presents a challenge; Suppan is 2-7 with a 5.34 ERA in his career against the Astros, including 1-2 with a 6.26 ERA at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz wasn't efficient in his last outing versus the Dodgers, but it was enough to earn his first win of the season. Ortiz threw 116 pitches over five frames, allowing three runs on three hits while walking five. Ortiz has made nine starts against the Brewers, going 4-3 with a 5.23 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Parra continued a poor start to the season by allowing five runs and 10 baserunners -- seven hits, three walks -- in four innings of work against the Phillies on Tuesday and dropped to 0-3. He's allowed at least three runs in all three of his starts and has issued nine walks in 14 1/3 innings this season. Parra has a 5.47 ERA in five career starts against the Astros but has a 3-2 record in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Looper has emerged as an early-season stopper for the Brewers. They had lost three of four games before he took the mound Wednesday in Philadelphia and delivered six shutout innings for his second Brewers win. They key, especially considering Looper did not strike out a single batter, was that he issued only two walks, and both were partly by design. They both went to Phillies slugger Ryan Howard, who grounded into a double play in his first at-bat but entered the night 4-for-5 against looper with four home runs. Looper has walked only three batters in his last two starts, both wins. He has a 3.02 ERA in 29 career appearances against the Pirates, five of them starts.
away_pitcher_note: After a shaky first outing, Karstens rebounded to allow just one run in six innings on Tuesday against the Marlins. He was much more efficient with his pitch count, needing only 87 pitches to go that deep. Karstens isn't going to overpower anyone, which makes it that much more critical that he gets first-pitch strikes and is efficient. It should benefit Karstens, too, that he is now pitching on a normal four-to-five days of rest after having a 17-day layoff prior to his first outing.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start at Philadelphia, Bush was five outs shy of the first Brewers no-hitter in 22 years when Matt Stairs clanked a solo home run off the right-field foul pole. It marked the second time in 10 months and the third time in Bush's career that he took a no-hitter into the eighth inning of a game, and he's not an altogether surprising candidate to end Milwaukee's no-hitter drought, even if he's not exactly a household name outside of Milwaukee. Bush has ranked among the National League's five best pitchers in terms of limiting baserunners (as measured by WHIP; walks plus hits per inning pitched) in two of the last three seasons, including 2008, during which he worked seven no-hit innings against the Blue Jays in June. He's had mixed results in 11 career matchups against the Pirates (10 were starts), going 3-4 with a 4.67 ERA. Two of those wins came last season, when Bush posted a 3.98 ERA against Pittsburgh in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm stumbled a bit in his last outing, allowing four runs on eight hits in six innings. He still managed to get the win and has now pitched at least six innings in 24 of his last 25 starts, dating back to 2008. He continues to be the Pirates' most reliable arm, and when he's sharp, his efficiency is remarkable. He's a groundball pitcher and will mix all of his pitches to both sides of the plate. The fact that he is consistently around the strike zone also keeps him from going into deep counts too frequently.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo gave up a two-run homer to Houston's Carlos Lee and not much else in his last start Friday night in Houston. Gallardo pitched the first complete game of his career, surrendering five hits, four of them singles. He had not pitched more than 6 2/3 innings in any of his three previous starts this season. He struck out four, walked none and threw 106 pitches. After shutting out the Mets for six innings April 18, the game against the Astros represented Gallardo's second strong start in a row.
away_pitcher_note: Snell snapped a streak of 13 scoreless innings in his last outing, one in which he labored through five innings. Reminiscent of a number of 2008 starts in which he fought with his command, Snell walked five and gave up six hits (five for extra bases) in five innings. Snell's pitch count in the first few innings is usually a telling sign of how the rest of the outing is going to go for him. If it gets high early, Snell has a tough time rebounding. He is 4-1 with a 3.60 ERA in six career appearances (five starts) against the Brewers. He is 109 at Miller Park, but has allowed six earned runs in eight innings there.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan lasted six innings in his last outing on Saturday at Houston, and did not figure in the decision. He allowed only four hits, but two of those were home runs by Carlos Lee and Michael Bourn. One of the four runs the Astros scored was unearned and Suppan left for a pinch-hitter with the game tied at 4. Seeking his second win in a row, he struck out four, walked three and threw 98 pitches. Suppan has a 3-3 record and 4.43 ERA for his career in eight games against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer cruised through the first four innings of his last start against the Giants, but ran into a buzzsaw in the fifth. The right-hander allowed four runs in the inning and ended up on the short end of a 5-3 decision. Scherzer is still looking for his first Major League win after 19 big league games, 10 of which have been starts. Scherzer began the year on the disabled list after receiving a cortisone shot in his right shoulder in January. He has yet to pitch past the fifth inning this year in large part because his pitch count tends to rise early in his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Parra pitched five innings in his last outing, Sunday at Houston, before being lifted for a pinch-hitter with the Brewers trailing by one. He gave up five hits and three runs, but only one of them was earned. He struck out four, walked three and threw 97 pitches. Parra felt he had better command of his fastball against the Astros, and manager Ken Macha was pleased to see him throw more changeups. Parra has allowed only one earned run in two games, a total of 13 innings, in his career against Arizona. That gives him an 0.69 ERA vs. the Diamondbacks.
away_pitcher_note: Garland has pitched well in three of his four starts this season. In his last outing against the Giants, he allowed just one run through the first seven innings. The Giants were able to break through against him in the eighth with the big blow being a three-run homer by Pablo Sandoval, which came after Garland had passed the 100-pitch mark. His one rough outing came against the Cardinals when he allowed seven runs in just 3 2/3 innings. He has victories against the Dodgers and Rockies to his credit.

home_pitcher_note: Looper worked without his good fastball on Monday against the Pirates and he made it work, using a higher than usual number of changeups and cutters to match a career high with seven strikeouts in five respectable innings. He was charged with two earned runs, which wasn't bad considering the first four Pirates hitters reached safely in the first inning, and he was in line for his third consecutive win before reliever Carlos Villanueva surrendered a tying, two-run double in the eighth. He has a 4.08 ERA against the Diamondbacks, but only two of his 28 appearances against Arizona have been starts. Both were in 2007, and both were no-decisions after Looper surrendered a total of nine earned runs in 9 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Haren could easily be 5-0 right now instead of 2-3. In his first three starts of the year -- all losses -- the right-hander received one total run of support. In his last start against the Cubs, Haren was on top of his game. He allowed a leadoff homer to Alfonso Soriano, but only gave up two more hits the rest of the way as he tossed the seventh complete game of his career. Haren helped himself out offensively in the fourth inning when he chopped a two-run double down the left-field line. His 0-3 start was the first time a pitcher had started the year losing his first three games while having an ERA under 2.00 since Juan Cruz did it for the Cubs in 2002. Overall, he has walked just five and fanned 36 in his 35 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Five days after carrying a no-hitter into the eighth inning in Philadelphia, Bush surrendered his first hit to the third batter he faced on Tuesday. It was one of six Pirates hits off Bush, who lasted just five innings and surrendered five runs, four of them earned. Four of the runs scored on two-run doubles by Wisconsin natives -- the first by Eric Hinske in the third inning and the other by Jason Jaramillo in the fifth after Bush brushed the jerseys of Pirates hitters with consecutive pitches. He'll aim for better command against the Diamondbacks. Bush is 4-1 with a 4.15 ERA in five previous starts against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Petit has taken Brandon Webb's place in the rotation while the right-hander is on the disabled list with shoulder stiffness. The right-hander struggled in his last start against the Cubs on Tuesday. After working two scoreless innings, he gave up a three-run homer to Alfonso Soriano. That seemed to open the floodgates as one inning later the Cubs chased him from the game with a four-run rally. In two starts prior to that, Petit allowed five earned runs in 10 innings. Unfortunately the bullpen struggled both times. Petit has filled the spot-starter/long-relief role for the D-backs the past two seasons. Though he doesn't possess overpowering stuff, he has a good feel for pitching and generally has good command.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm will have another shot at the Brewers after suffering his shortest outing of the season in a no-decision in Milwaukee on Tuesday. The left-hander lasted just 5 1/3 innings and worked in and out of jams the entire night. Maholm gave up seven hits and allowed five earned runs while stranding the bases loaded on two occasions. The Bucs ace benefited from his defense, which turned two double plays in each of the first two innings. Maholm struggled with his location and rarely topped 90 mph with his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo is on a roll. He pitched seven brilliant innings against the Pirates on Wednesday and hit a solo home run for a 1-0 win, and has allowed only two runs in 22 innings over his last three starts. Wednesday's win was filled with hitting milestones: Gallardo became the first pitcher to win a 1-0 game on his own home run since the Dodgers' Odalis Perez in 2002, and with his fourth career home run he set a Brewers record for a pitcher. Both of his home runs this season have won games, including a three-run shot off Randy Johnson on April 8 for a 4-2 Brewers win. But he did throw 116 pitches against the Pirates after working a complete-game in Houston in his previous start, which caused at least mild concern for manager Ken Macha. Since Gallardo missed most of last season with a serious knee injury, the Brewers are worried about wearing him out early this year.

home_pitcher_note: Snell was the tough-luck loser in his last start, allowing just five hits and one run in seven strong innings in a 1-0 setback at Milwaukee on Wednesday. The right-hander appeared to get stronger as the game went on and tallied a Major League season-high 131 pitches. Snell gave up a solo home run to Brewers starter Yovani Gallardo for the game's only run. Working with a fastball in the 87-93 mph range in the early innings, Snell dialed it up to 95 mph late in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan says the only thing that's changed since his ugly outing against the Cubs on April 12 is the result. But those results speak for themselves; in his last three starts he's limited opponents to six runs in 18 1/3 innings for a 2.95 ERA, much better than the 11 runs he allowed in his first 7 2/3 innings and two starts. The Brewers gave Suppan an extra day of rest between those segments, allowing him to throw one extra side session that seems to have made a difference. He didn't face the Pirates when they visited Milwaukee last week but he's 12-3 against them in his career with a 4.20 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo stymied the Pirates for eight scoreless innings and a 4-0 Reds win on Friday night while giving up four hits, three walks and striking out four. He relied heavily on his fastball and established it early, but used his breaking stuff as the out pitch. A pair of double plays on the ground also helped him stay out of serious trouble. Arroyo has worked exclusively with backup catcher Ryan Hanigan to this point and it's been especially to the right-hander's liking.
away_pitcher_note: Parra remained winless in his fifth start Friday against the D-backs, but at least he didn't suffer the loss. The lefty, who had lost each of his first four starts, shut out Arizona hitters on just 63 pitches through the first five innings before running into trouble in a 30-pitch sixth. He was burned by a pair of two-out walks, including a pass to Conor Jackson that forced in the first run of the game. It was intriguing that Parra walked Jackson on a full-count changeup, a pitch that manager Ken Macha has urged -- strongly -- that Parra use more often. Parra missed the Pirates when they came through Milwaukee, but he did beat them last season, allowing four hits and no runs in 5 2/3 innings on May 20.

home_pitcher_note: Owings paid dearly for a rough top of the first inning where the Pirates jumped him for four runs in an 8-6 loss on Saturday at PNC Park. The right-hander pitched 5 2/3 innings and allowed five earned runs and nine hits with two walks, a hit batter and no strikeouts. His first start of the season came vs. the Brewers on April 15 at Miller Park. Owings was a 9-3 loser when he gave up four earned runs and five hits over five-plus innings with two walks, two strikeouts and two home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Looper suffered his first Brewers loss despite working a season-best seven innings against the D-backs on Saturday. He took a no-hitter into the fifth inning and didn't walk a batter all night, but ended up allowing a season-high four runs and matching a season high with six hits. Still, Looper has been the Brewers' most reliable starter this season. He beat the Reds on April 15 at Miller Park when he allowed three runs on six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Bush breezed through six innings against Arizona on Sunday, allowing back-to-back singles leading off the fourth but nothing else. But he imploded in the seventh inning, when Mark Reynolds and Justin Upton connected for back-to-back home runs to open the frame and No. 8 hitter Miguel Montero connected three batters later for a two-out, two-strike shot that tied the game and cost Bush a shot at his second win. Bush took a no-decision in his April 11 start against the Cubs, when he allowed three runs on six hits in 6 1/3 innings of an eventual 6-5 Brewers loss. He's just 1-7 against the Cubs in his career.
away_pitcher_note: This would have been Carlos Zambrano's spot in the rotation but he was placed on the 15-day disabled list on Monday with a Grade 2 strained hamstring. Wells was expected to be called up from Triple-A Iowa for the game. The right-hander has appeared in four big league games before, but has not made a start. Included in his starts for Iowa was a stellar effort April 22 when he gave up one hit over seven scoreless innings, striking out four. He walked two.

home_pitcher_note: He wasn't as dominant as his previous three starts (2-0, two earned runs in 23 innings), but Gallardo was still very good against the Pirates on a chilly Monday night in Pittsburgh. He scattered a season-high seven hits in seven innings and limited the damage to three runs, and his ERA over the last four starts is still an impressive 1.50. He missed the Cubs when they came through Milwaukee in early April, and he has yet to record a decision against them in two career starts (five runs in 12 innings for a 3.75 ERA). The last time Gallardo faced the Cubs was last May, when he suffered a serious right knee injury that cost him most of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster had his longest outing of the year in his last start, going seven innings against the Giants. The right-hander struck out seven and walked two while giving up two runs on five hits. It was his first win in two starts at home -- he was 14-3 last year at Wrigley Field. Somehow, he keeps getting assigned road games. He beat the Brewers on April 12 at Miller Park, holding them to four runs on six hits over six innings and striking out six.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan did just enough on a miserable night in Pittsburgh to continue his hot streak. He surrendered three runs on five hits and three walks in 5 2/3 innings while working only one clean inning -- the fifth -- and throwing 108 pitches. He had not thrown that many since a 110-pitch win over the Cardinals last May 11, before Suppan developed the elbow discomfort that hampered him from June to the end of the season. He's on a roll of late. Since he surrendered 11 runs in 7 2/3 innings over his first two starts, including a nightmarish outing against the Cubs on April 13 in which he issued three bases-loaded walks, Suppan has gone 2-0 with a 3.38 ERA in four games.
away_pitcher_note: Marshall needs to wine and dine his teammates a little bit. The Cubs have scored six runs in the lefty's last three starts. He took the loss in his last game, a 6-2 decision to the Giants. Marshall served up a three-run homer to Bengie Molina in the first and then settled down and scattered four hits over the next six innings. He finished with one walk, one strikeout and threw 95 pitches over seven-plus innings. The arm strength is there, and Marshall is making the most of being on a regular schedule. Now, he just needs some offensive support.

home_pitcher_note: Despite the ugly record, Parra is coming off his three best performances of the season. Although he took a no-decision on May 1 after allowing three hits and a run in six innings against Arizona, Parra finally earned a victory last Wednesday against the Reds. Though he needed 119 pitches to get his team into the seventh inning, he gave up eight hits and two runs in six innings. It wasn't his strongest line of the season, but he's sure to enter the contest against the Marlins with some much-needed confidence.
away_pitcher_note: The Marlins called up Koronka from Triple-A New Orleans on Sunday, sending down outfielder Cameron Maybin to make room. Koronka, a former Chicago Cub and Texas Ranger, has thrown back-to-back scoreless five-inning starts for New Orleans. The left-hander is taking Anibal Sanchez's spot in the rotation for the time being. On May 7, Sanchez exited after 4 2/3 innings with right shoulder discomfort and will be on the disabled list for two months. Koronka hasn't pitched in the Majors since 2007 and has never faced Milwaukee. The Brewers are hitting .262 as a team against left-handers this season.

home_pitcher_note: Looper looked flummoxed and frustrated in his last outing, a 6-5 defeat at Cincinnati. He was 2-0 with a 2.45 ERA through four starts, but he has struggled in the month of May. Against the Reds, he couldn't locate his pitches and finished the contest allowing eight hits and five runs in 3 1/3 innings. Afterward, he bemoaned the fact he didn't give his team a chance to win.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco earned his first win since pitching Opening Day for the Marlins, and earned his first quality start of the season. He held the Rockies to three runs on eight hits and a walk while striking out five. Nolasco maintained his dominance over the Rockies' lineup, giving him a 3-0 record against them with 26 strikeouts against just two walks. Nolasco gave up runs on a solo homer in the second and a pair of run-scoring doubles in the third, but he found his rhythm and shut down Colorado the rest of the way.

home_pitcher_note: Bush turned in his fifth quality start in his last six outings, holding the Cubs to two runs on four hits in seven good innings on Friday night, but he exited in a 2-1 hole and was spared a tough-luck loss when Ryan Braun hit a go-ahead homer in the eighth. Bush's record is not indicative of the way he has pitched; the team has won each of his last four starts but he's 1-0 in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Not even Coors Field could tame the fast-rising Marlins ace last time out. The right-hander took a shutout through seven innings in Saturday's 3-1 win against the Rockies, giving up one run in eight frames. He struck out five and walked none, bringing his absurd strikeout-to-walk ratio to 43 to six on the season. But Milwaukee does have hope. Before the trip to Denver, Johnson's previous two road starts were pedestrian. He gave up three runs in six innings to the Mets on April 29 and six runs in six innings to the Nationals on April 18. Johnson has never faced the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse pitched well for five innings Friday night but was doomed by a five-run sixth at Cincinnati. The big blow was delivered by Reds pitcher Aaron Harang, who snapped an 0-for-13 skid with a two-run bases-loaded single. Lohse finished with seven earned runs allowed on nine hits in six innings. He walked three and struck out four. Overall, Lohse has not fared as well on the road as a Cardinal as he has at Busch Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo either struggled with his command or with home-plate umpire Jerry Crawford's postage stamp-sized strike zone on Saturday against the Cubs, but he limited the damage to two runs in five workmanlike innings and nearly didn't allow a run at all. Gallardo's pitch count hit 60 before he recorded the final out of the third inning, and he crossed the 100-pitch barrier in the fifth, but the righty was one out away from a scoreless outing when Micah Hoffpauir belted a two-run home run with two outs in the fifth. Gallardo has faced the Cardinals twice without much success; he allowed four runs in five innings of a no-decision at Busch Stadium and seven runs in 5 2/3 innings of his only outing against the Cards at Miller Park, a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright did not have a strong outing against the Reds on Sunday, going six innings and allowing four runs on seven hits. Still, he was in line to get the win until the Cardinals' bullpen lost the lead in the ninth inning. Wainwrighht did have speed and control, though, walking only one and saying that he felt strong in the fifth and sixth innings. The best news is that Wainwright feels that he knows what went wrong. "It's not a question of arm strength or stuff -- the ball just isn't sinking the way it normally does, and I'm throwing fly balls," Wainwright said. "It's just a matter of arm slot -- so now that we recognize the problem, I should be able to correct it."
away_pitcher_note: Suppan will face his former teammates for the sixth time since leaving via free agency following the 2006 season. In five previous starts as a member of the Brewers against the Cardinals, Suppan is 4-0 with a 1.93 ERA -- having allowed eight earned runs in 37 1/3 innings -- and he's 6-2 with a 3.18 ERA in 11 career appearances against St. Louis. Suppan is coming off his first loss since April 12, a 4-2 decision against the Cubs at Miller Park in which he surrendered all four runs, only three earned, in the fourth inning. Alfonso Soriano hit a two-run home run to tie the game, and that has been a problem for Suppan; he has allowed at least one homer in six of his seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has been a puzzle this year, but one thing has been pretty much constant: He gets in trouble early. The first two innings have been a minefield for the right-hander, and he needs to navigate them more successfully. When he can do that, he can often fashion a pretty good game. But too many times, he's dug himself too deep a hole to be able to dig out.
away_pitcher_note: After losing his first four decisions, Parra suddenly has suddenly won two starts in a row. He beat the Marlins in Milwaukee on Tuesday despite a rocky first two innings, in which he hit one batter, walked another and surrendered three two-out, run-scoring singles. He settled down after that, allowing only one more hit through the end of the sixth and recording six of his final nine outs via strikeout. Parra finished with eight whiffs, matching his season high, and put together a "quality start" (defined as six or more innings with three or fewer earned runs) for the third consecutive outing. He's pitched against the Cardinals six times in his career, including five starts, and has pitched well, to the tune of a 3.77 ERA, but he has yet to record a decision against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse finally had a game where no physical ailments plagued him. So instead, a massive rainstorm washed out what was looking like a nice start after just two innings. The Cubs aren't the best matchup for him, but he tends to pitch well at home, and the rainout left the Cardinals scrambling to sort out how their rotation will work out. Lohse will pitch on two days' rest, treating the Friday night game essentially as a bullpen session.
away_pitcher_note: This was originally an off-day, but a rainout Friday night that was re-scheduled for Monday prompted manager Ken Macha to shuffle the deck. He could have used Yovani Gallardo, but instead bumped up Braden Looper to start against his former team. He'll be on regular rest coming off a "salvage" start against the Marlins last week. The first four Marlins hitters went single, homer, double, single for a 3-0 lead before Looper had his first out, but he settled down after that and allowed only two more runs through the sixth to snap a personal two-game losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton was the beneficiary of the Astros' 24-hit, 15-run drubbing of the Rockies in his last outing, during which he contributed two hits and allowed five runs over six innings. Hampton walked two and struck out three in the landslide win at Coors Field. Hampton returns to Minute Maid Park to face the Brewers, whom he last faced at home on April 25. He allowed four runs over six innings in that game, which the Astros lost in extra innings. Hampton is 0-1 with a 5.09 ERA over three home starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Bush was originally slated to start Game 2 of this three-game series in Houston, but was bumped up a day after the Brewers' rainout in St. Louis. He will nonetheless be pitching on regular rest. Bush has been good for seven innings in each of his last three outings, matching his season high with seven strikeouts in two of those games, and he has put together a quality start in six of his seven starts this season. He missed the Astros when the Brewers went through Houston last month, but he's 5-1 against them in his career with a 3.50 ERA. All of that success has come in Milwaukee, though; Bush is 0-1 at Minute Maid Park with a 4.31 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struck out a career-high 11 batters in his last outing at Coors Field to record his team-leading fourth win of the year. Rodriguez has won three of his last four starts and hasn't allowed more than three runs in any of his eight outings this year. Rodriguez will face Milwaukee for the first time this year. In 2008, he was 1-1 with a 2.38 ERA over two games. In his career, he's 3-5 with a 4.55 ERA over 12 games.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo threw only 30 pitches in St. Louis on Friday before the game was rained out and the statistics -- Gallardo had surrendered a two-run home run to up-and-coming Cardinals outfielder Colby Rasmus -- were washed away. Instead of slotting him into the makeup game in St. Louis on Monday, Brewers manager Ken Macha opted to keep Gallardo in his regular spot in the rotation. "You know what? If you just look at the short term, you probably say that's a tough thing to do," Macha said. "But I think long-term, it will be good for him. He's got some innings right now, and he's also had some stressful innings." Gallardo is 3-0 with a 1.80 ERA over his last five starts, including his first career complete game at Houston on April 24.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt turned in another quality outing in his last start vs. the Cubs, but took a no-decision in an eventual Houston loss. Oswalt yielded three runs over six innings, but the Astros didn't score until he was already out of the game. The Astros have scored one or no runs six times this year when Oswalt is on the mound. Oswalt has not faced the Brewers yet this year. In 2008, he was 2-0 with a 2.77 ERA in two starts vs. Milwaukee. Lifetime, he's 13-8 with a 3.59 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan was stupendous against his former club on Saturday, holding the Cardinals scoreless on six hits in seven of his best innings this season. It marked the first time this year that Suppan took a shutout into the fifth inning, but he has been a consistent innings-eater for Milwaukee, working at least six frames in five of his last six outings while posting a 2.77 ERA. He took a no-decision in Houston on April 25, when Suppan allowed four runs, three of them earned, on four hits in six innings. He struck out a season-high six batters in that game.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey delivered a gem of a performance against the Yankees his last time out, holding the club to just two runs on seven hits over 7 2/3 innings. Five of those hits came after the start of the seventh inning as Slowey had to work his way out of a few jams. The right-hander did not issue a walk in the start and struck out a season-high eight batters. Slowey next will face the Brewers, a team he's pitched well against. In three career starts vs. Milwaukee, Slowey is 2-0 with a 2.42.
away_pitcher_note: Parra will happily strike out to end the first inning every time. Parra batted before he pitched on Sunday in St. Louis, when the Brewers batted around to spot him a 4-0 lead. Parra made it hold, allowing two runs on five hits in six innings to win his third straight start after losing his first four. He wasn't happy with walking four Cardinals batters, and he's walked four in three of his last four starts. Still, he's 3-0 with a 2.25 ERA this month and has worked six innings in each of those games. He won his only start against the Twins last season with seven shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Swarzak will be making his first Major League start Saturday after being promoted from Triple-A Rochester on Wednesday to fill in for injured starter Glen Perkins. Swarzak was 3-4 with a 2.25 ERA allowing 40 hits with 11 walks and 32 strikeouts in seven starts for the Red Wings this season. He will likely make just one more start before Perkins returns from the 15-day disabled list. If the Twins like what they see, Swarzak might be in line for a relief role, manager Ron Gardenhire said Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Facing his former team in St. Louis on Monday, Looper bounced back nicely from a pair of starts in which he surrendered five runs in each. Looper worked six innings and surrendered three runs, only one of which was earned, because of a pair of Brewers errors. Looper is 2-1 with a 3.52 ERA in his three road starts this season. He has made three appearances at the Metrodome but all three were in relief before he moved into the Cardinals rotation three years ago. He surrendered two runs on six hits in 3 2/3 innings in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Baker continued to struggle Tuesday against the White Sox. The right-hander couldn't get the ball down in the zone with favorable counts and too often fell behind Chicago hitters. He lasted just five innings, walking four and surrendering four runs to pick up his fifth loss of the season. Baker has allowed at least four runs in six of his seven starts this season. In four career starts against Milwaukee, he is 2-2 with a 5.62 ERA. Baker is 5-2 with a 4.61 ERA lifetime in seven Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bush has been a quality-start machine this season, pitching at least six innings while allowing three or fewer earned runs in seven of his eight outings. Last year, he ranked second on the staff to Ben Sheets with 16 such starts. Bush doesn't particularly buy the notion that three runs in six innings is a quality start, but he does talk often about the importance of keeping his team in the game, and that's just what he's done, particularly in May. In his four starts this month, all "quality," he's 2-0 with a 3.00 ERA. Bush didn't pitch against the Cardinals during the team's swing through St. Louis, so this will be his first chance to improve on his career 2-4 record and 6.06 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Because of a rainout in St. Louis, Gallardo threw only 30 pitches in the 10 days prior to his most recent start, and it showed. He struggled to corral his fastball through a five-plus inning stint in Houston and surrendered six earned runs, the most he'd allowed since an awful start against the Reds back on April 13. In his five starts after the Cincinnati outing Gallardo was 3-0 with a 1.80 ERA and a complete game, but he came back to Earth against the Astros and surrendered seven hits including Miguel Tejada's home run, plus a pair of walks. He actually pitched 1 1/3 innings against the Cardinals on May 15 and surrendered a two-run homer to Colby Rasmus, but those stats were washed away by the rain so this is his official season debut against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter once again amazed with his ability to be sharp upon returning from injury. Now he'll try to make it two healthy starts in a row. There's no question about his effectiveness if he can avoid injury. Held to a pitch count of somewhere around 70-80 in his first game back from an oblique strain (he was removed after 67), chances are he'll have a longer leash next time out. Somewhere in the neighborhood of 80-90 pitches is a good guess, and when Carpenter is going well, he can make that many pitches cover plenty of innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan limited the damage on a shaky night in Houston on Thursday but was burned by a couple of home runs. Hunter Pence's two-run shot in the second inning and Miguel Tejada's solo shot in the fourth accounted for all the damage against Suppan, who matched Dave Bush in allowing a team-high nine homers this season. Still, Suppan has been steady, holding opponents to three or fewer runs in each of his last seven starts, including a gem in St. Louis on May 16 in which Suppan surrendered six hits but no runs in a 1-0 win. He pitched for the Cardinals from 2004-06, and in six starts against them since he signed a four-year, $42 million deal with the Brewers, Suppan is 5-0 with a 1.66 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: It took the Cardinals' Opening Day starter a while to find his groove, but he has assuredly found it with back-to-back outstanding starts. He has adjusted his arm slot, refined his command and maintained his excellent stuff. Moreover, he is back to relying on his fastball. There are few better starters in the National League than a healthy, rolling Wainwright, and the Cardinals are reaping the benefits right now.

home_pitcher_note: Parra appeared to have turned the corner after a difficult April in which he was 0-4 with a 6.52 ERA in four starts. Entering Friday's game against the Twins, Parra was 3-0 with a 3.00 ERA in four May starts and 3-1 with a 2.79 ERA in five starts since April 26. Parra's May resurgence hit a major snag on Friday, when he allowed nine runs -- eight earned -- on eight hits and three walks in 3 1/3 innings. The left-hander will look to right the ship immediately on Wednesday against the Cardinals. Parra has been successful against the Cardinals in his career, going 1-0 with a 3.63 ERA in six starts and one relief appearance over 34 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has shown signs of progress a couple of times already this year, and he did so again his last time out. The key is not to take two steps back after a step forward. Wellemeyer insists that as much as anything, he needs to get out of his own head and stop thinking so much about his delivery. He also needs to have all of his pitches available to throw for strikes from the start of a game. When he's able to mix in his slider and changeup along with his fastball, Wellemeyer is much more effective.

home_pitcher_note: Looper's first Interleague start of the season was not a success. The right-hander did not have his best stuff, but he was able to complete six innings while getting touched for nine hits and five runs -- four earned -- in a 6-2 loss to the Twins on Saturday. Looper walked one and struck out one, and he also surrendered solo home runs to Joe Crede and Joe Mauer. Next up is a matchup against a familiar National League Central foe. Looper will kick off a three-game series on Friday against Cincinnati. He is 5-3 with a 3.86 ERA in 38 appearances -- eight starts -- over 81 2/3 career innings against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: In a 4-3 Reds win in 11 innings, Cueto received a no-decision after he pitched seven innings and allowed three runs -- two earned -- and six hits with three walks, two hit batters and seven strikeouts. He was effective at getting ahead and threw first-pitch strikes to 22 of his 29 batters. It was the seventh consecutive start in which the right-hander worked at least seven innings, but he's winless in his last two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Bush was solid through six innings but took the loss on Sunday against the Twins. He ended up going 6 2/3 innings and allowing four earned runs on five hits and four walks while striking out four in a 6-3 defeat. Bush gave up a pair of solo home runs in the contest. His earned runs were slightly inflated when two runners he left on in the seventh eventually scored off Milwaukee's relief corps. Next up is Cincinnati, a team Bush was struggled with in his career. In 10 career starts, Bush is 2-3 with a 6.54 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Harang got a five-inning outing for a win the hard way over the Astros on Monday. The right-hander had worked 4 2/3 innings before a two-hour, three-minute rain delay interrupted the game. Harang, who was at 81 pitches, kept loose by throwing indoors and was able to get that final out by throwing 12 pitches to two batters after play resumed. His line was three earned runs on 10 hits with one walk and four strikeouts. Harang reported no soreness the next day after his unusual outing, but it will be interesting to see if there are any effects in his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo bounced back from a poor start in Houston to deliver eight stellar innings against the Cardinals on Memorial Day. He took a no-hitter into the sixth, when Brendan Ryan led off with an infield single, and allowed only one more hit while throwing a career-high 126 pitches. His only start against the Reds this season was his worst of the year. Gallardo surrendered only three hits but walked four batters and gave up seven runs in five innings. Edwin Encarnacion did much of the damage with a grand slam.
away_pitcher_note: During the Reds' 6-4 win over the Astros on Tuesday, Owings gave up three earned runs and six hits over a five-inning no-decision where he threw 99 pitches. At one point, he also took a Carlos Lee line drive off of his hip but was able to continue in the game. In two starts this season vs. the Brewers, Owings is 1-1 with a 6.55 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Considering how he started off in his last start, Miller rebounded rather nicely. At Philadelphia, he allowed three runs in the first inning (one earned) and faced eight batters. In all, he threw 30 pitches in the inning. While it looked as if he may not go deep into the game, he still managed a quality start. Miller allowed four runs (two earned) over six innings, logging 104 pitches. He did walk four and struck out four. This will be the left-hander's first time facing the Brewers. He has made five starts on the season, and seven overall appearances. Miller is stressing attacking the zone more.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan lasted just 3 2/3 innings Tuesday against St. Louis, giving up five runs on seven hits, three of which were home runs. Nick Stavinoha hit his first career home run off Suppan in the second inning, while St. Louis starter Adam Wainwright went deep in the fourth inning. Colby Rasmus also homered in the three-run fourth inning for the Cardinals, who knocked Suppan out of the game after just 57 pitches. Suppan is 4-4 with a lifetime ERA of 3.63 against Florida. home_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Sanchez will make his first big league start since he suffered a right shoulder injury on May 7 against the Braves. Sanchez proceeded to throw 22 more pitches in the bullpen after the game to bring his total to 75. The four-year veteran has been strong against the Brewers in his career, going 2-0 with a 2.84 ERA in three starts. Recently demoted right-hander Ricky Nolasco allowed one run over seven innings for Triple-A New Orleans on June 1. While the outing was encouraging, the timing eliminated him from possibly returning to the Majors for this start. Right-hander Burke Badenhop, who was another possible starter, will be available out of the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Parra suffered his second consecutive loss Wednesday against St. Louis, giving up three runs on seven hits in 6 2/3 innings in a 3-2 Milwaukee loss. He also finished with six strikeouts but walked six while throwing 108 pitches. Parra avoided the big innings that plagued him in his previous start against Minnesota, giving up just one run in the first, third and sixth innings, but failed to get any run support. Parra has had little success against Cincinnati in his career, holding a career record of 0-1 with an 8.27 ERA against the Reds in three games.

home_pitcher_note: Granted, it's only two starts, but if they are any indication, the Marlins have made a major addition. One of five Florida first-round picks in 2005, West has tremendous potential. The question was whether he would be ready for the big leagues at age 22. Thus far, he's up to the task. In his last outing, West gave up one run on four hits over seven innings. It was his longest outing in either the big leagues or Minor Leagues this season. At Double-A Jacksonville, he only went as long as six innings. In 12 MLB innings, he's allowed three runs.
away_pitcher_note: Looper broke an eight-game losing streak for Brewers starting pitchers in his last start, giving up two runs on two hits in seven innings in the Brewers 3-2 win over Cincinnati on Friday. After giving up a game-tying two-run homer to Cincinnati's Ramon Hernandez with two outs remaining in the top of the fourth, Looper retired 10 of the last 11 batters he faced. Looper, who played for the Marlins from 1999-2003, is 5-2 all-time against his former team with a 4.31 ERA. In his last start against Florida, Looper allowed five runs on eight hits in six innings, earning the win in the Brewers 8-6 win on May 13.

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins are 8-3 in Johnson's 11 starts. But one of those loses came the last time the 6-foot-7 right-hander faced the Brewers. On May 14 at Milwaukee, Johnson worked a season-low four innings in a no-decision. He felt some fatigue in his right shoulder, but since then has rebounded nicely. Johnson has had nine quality starts. The right-hander comes off a victory against the Mets at Citi Field in which he gave up two runs in seven innings, walking two and striking out five.
away_pitcher_note:
Bush gave up two first-inning homers Saturday against Cincinnati, and was removed from the game after four innings in which he allowed five runs on seven hits. He also walked three. Bush will close out a four-game series against the Marlins, who he has a career record of
2-2 against with a 5.62 ERA. Bush earned the win in his last start against Florida, a 5-3 Milwaukee win on May 14. The right-hander gave up three runs (two earned) on seven hits while striking out seven in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander received the run support he had been seeking all season but struggled in the 88-pitch outing against the Diamondbacks in his last time out. Against Arizona, Jurrjens was charged with eight hits and five runs in five innings pitched. He had pitched at least six innings in his four previous starts and seven of his last eight before the outing in Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo struck out the side in the first inning and finished with nine strikeouts in Sunday's 5-2 win over Cincinnati. The 23-year-old started stellar, retiring eight of the first nine batters via strikeout, but struggled with his command and was pulled after 5 1/3 innings. He allowed seven hits and two runs -- one earned -- while walking two. Gallardo made his only career start against the Braves in September 2007, when he received a no-decision after allowing two runs on three hits over seven innings while striking out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez had a strong outing last Saturday against the D-backs, even though he didn't get the win at Chase Field in his first start there in four years. The right-hander allowed two runs (one earned) on seven hits, walked one and struck out seven in 6 1/3 innings. Vazquez pitched the 2005 season for the D-backs and was traded to the White Sox the following offseason. After three years in Chicago, Vazquez was traded to the Braves this past offseason. His last start at Chase Field was on Sept. 25, 2005, and his last win came five days earlier. Vazquez had allowed five earned runs or more in three of his past six outings and allowed two earned runs or fewer in the other three starts that encompass that span.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan had to battle in his start at Florida on Monday, throwing 51 pitches in the first two innings and 68 pitches through the third. But he limited the damage to two Marlins runs in five innings despite allowing 10 Florida baserunners (seven hits, three walks) by stranding a runner in scoring position in the second, third and fifth innings. Suppan left with a 4-2 lead, but his short night further taxed an overworked bullpen that lost the lead before recording the first Marlins out in the sixth. Suppan is 2-5 with a 4.65 ERA in seven career starts against the Braves but was excellent against Atlanta last season, going 2-1 with a 1.71 ERA in three starts, including a win at Turner Field last Aug. 1 in which he twirled seven shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Tommy Hanson will make his highly-anticipated Major League debut on Saturday when the Braves take on the Brewers at Turner Field. The MVP of the Arizona Fall League and the No. 24 prospect in MLB.com's 2009 pre-season Top 50 Prospects list, Hanson is widely regarded as one of the best young pitching prospects in the game. The 6-6 right-hander has dominated at Triple-A Gwinnett this season, posting a 1.49 ERA while striking out 90 batters in 66 1/3 innings. Hanson will start in place of his roommate and friend Kris Medlen, who will move to the Braves' bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers desperately needed Parra to pitch deep into his start at Florida on Tuesday to spare a battered bullpen, and he didn't do it. Not only did he set dubious career highs in allowing 10 runs and 11 hits, Parra only made it through the fourth. His ERA has jumped from 4.82 to 6.75 over his last three starts, all losses. The Brewers are one of only three teams in baseball to use just five starting pitchers this season (the Giants and Pirates are the others) and the Brewers appear committed to allowing Parra to work out his kinks in the big leagues.

home_pitcher_note: Looper will get an extra day of rest before this start, and he could use the time to cool off. Looper was upset with himself on Wednesday after he entered the fifth inning with a 9-1 lead and could not get out of it, allowing four Marlins runs before exiting with the bases loaded and the potential tying run stepping to the plate. Seth McClung preserved the lead, but Looper, who had allowed only one hit before that inning, was stuck with one of the most frustrating no-decisions of his career. "I don't know what happened," he said. "It's still such a big blur to me." He owns a 5.28 ERA in 19 games against the Rockies, but only two of those appearances were starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel matched his career high for innings in a smooth, seven-inning, four-hit performance against the Astros. He gave up two runs in the Rockies' 10-3 victory. Hammel simply kept his fastball and slider down, something he has done on the road, where he is 2-1 with a 1.86 ERA this season.

home_pitcher_note: Bush began Thursday's start in pain, when a ball off the bat of Florida's Hanley Ramirez came back to the mound and hit him in the pitching elbow in the top of the first inning. Bush has faced the Rockies three times in his career, with a career record of 2-1 and an ERA of 2.50.
