home_pitcher_note: After meeting with the Brewers' head physician on Friday evening, Dave Bush declared himself fit to make his Monday start against the Cardinals as scheduled. The outing was in doubt after Bush surrendered eight runs in St. Louis on Wednesday -- his third start off the disabled list -- and complained of lingering soreness in his right triceps. "I should be good," Bush said late Friday night. "The doctor said this is all part of the process of [recovering from] a torn muscle. It's usually a multi-month kind of thing, and ... it doesn't do any good to stop throwing because [the scar tissue] has to break up at some point." Bush threw a bullpen session at about 75 percent of full effort on Friday afternoon. "Before the year is over, I want him to feel good about himself," manager Ken Macha said.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter is coming off of two relatively ordinary outings in a row. Then again, that just shows you what a standard he's set, since in those two games he has allowed five runs in 12 innings. Carpenter hasn't lost a decision since June, and the Cardinals are 10-2 in his past 12 starts. He's a legitimate NL Cy Young contender, and he'll try to strengthen his case in a holiday matinee on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Parra pitched his best game in six weeks on Thursday in St. Louis, when he surrendered two runs on three hits in the first inning but then allowed only three more hits into the seventh. A trio of relievers helped finish that inning, leaving Parra in line for his seventh win in nine decisions since his demotion to Triple-A. It's a somewhat deceiving streak, since the lefty has a 5.40 ERA in those 11 starts. He's 2-1 with a 2.42 ERA in four starts against the Cardinals this season.
away_pitcher_note: Smoltz felt he was two pitches away from an excellent outing against the Brewers on Thursday. He'll get a chance to make up for those two pitches just five days later. This will be his toughest assignment yet since his return to the National League, not only facing the potent Brewers but doing so at their home park. His strikeout and walk rates have been outstanding, and if he keeps those up, he should be just fine.

home_pitcher_note: In his third start off the disabled list, Suppan finished with a strange line: He worked 5 2/3 innings against the Giants, allowed two hits and no earned runs with four walks, three strikeouts and a nearly even balls-to-strikes ratio. Of Suppan's 102 pitches, only 52 found the strike zone. "Tonight, I felt like I had a lot of movement but my location wasn't necessarily my strong suit," Suppan said. "But I had movement, so I was trying to pitch with movement. You have to throw with what you've got." The good news was that, at least on the mound, he felt no effects from the rib-cage strain that sidelined him for nearly a month. At the plate, though, Suppan has yet to take the bat off his shoulder since returning from the DL.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright became baseball's first 17-game winner in his last start, but it was far from his finest moment during his Cy Young-caliber season. The right-hander yielded six runs in the fifth inning of his start against the Pirates, but got picked up by his offense. Prior to that hiccup, he'd been about as solid as any starter in the big leagues, with 13 straight starts in which he allowed two or fewer earned runs. This will be his fourth start against the Brewers. He's gone 2-1 with a 0.77 ERA, having allowed just two earned runs over 23 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Davis pitched pretty well in his last outing, but came away with a loss nonetheless. The lefty allowed three runs on seven hits over six innings as the D-backs fell, 4-1, to the Rockies. Davis has gone 0-2 in his last five starts with a 4.70 ERA. His last win came on Aug. 10 against the Mets, part of a three-game winning streak. Davis will be facing his former team for the first time this year. In four career starts against Milwaukee, Davis is 1-1 with a 5.49 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This is Yovani Gallardo's spot to pitch, but the Brewers are concerned about their budding ace's workload so they are essentially skipping his spot in the rotation. An off-day during the week allows the team to use Looper here on regular rest, and he's coming off a fine outing against the Giants at Miller Park in which he allowed only one run and matched a season high with seven innings. Looper got some help after he surrendered successive singles leading off the sixth inning when San Francisco's Aaron Rowand grounded into a 5-4-3 triple play, the first turned by the Brewers in 10 years. He's 7-3 away from Miller Park this season despite a 5.03 ERA, a half-run worse than his ERA at home.

home_pitcher_note: Mulvey is taking the place of Yusmeiro Petit in the rotation, likely for the rest of the season. The club wants to get a look at the right-hander acquired in the deal that sent Jon Rauch to the Twins. Mulvey is no stranger to being traded. A second-round pick by the Mets in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, he was dealt to the Twins as part of the Johan Santana deal. Mulvey, who was 5-8 with a 3.93 ERA in 24 starts for Triple-A Rochester this year, has appeared in two games in relief for the D-backs since joining the team on Sept. 1. He made his big league debut on July 20 with the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Bush's availability was briefly in doubt before his start against the Cardinals on Monday, but he delivered seven strong innings in a tough-luck loss to Chris Carpenter. Bush was cleared to pitch after receiving assurances from head physician William Raasch that the discomfort in his right triceps was a normal part of healing. Bush spent about two months on the disabled list with microtears of the muscle, the result of a line drive off his arm in early June. In his first two starts back, Bush has surrendered 13 runs in eight innings, but he limited St. Louis to two runs on seven hits with no walks and three strikeouts. A few more outings like that one would give Bush something positive to think about over the winter.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer was hurt by the long ball in his last start. The right-hander allowed four runs over seven innings to the Dodgers, with three of the runs coming via homers. Manny Ramirez and James Loney hit back-to-back homers to open the second inning and Ronnie Belliard hit one with one out in the fourth. In his previous start, Scherzer tied his career high for his longest outing when he lasted 7 2/3 innings against the Dodgers in Dodger Stadium. Scherzer only allowed one run in that game as he picked up his second win in as many starts.
away_pitcher_note: This was scheduled to be Manny Parra's turn in the rotation, but he exited his last start after only one inning, complaining of neck spasms.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster picked up the win in his last start, against the Pirates, but was helped by a seven-run first inning. That will make any starting pitcher relax. Dempster wasn't sharp and admitted that after the game, and scattered eight hits over 6 1/3 innings. He's 5-3 with a 4.59 ERA at Wrigley, and will be shooting for his 10th win, which would be his fourth season in double-digit wins and second in a row. He's 2-1 against the Brewers this season, last facing them July 2 and picking up a win in a 9-5 Cubs victory.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan didn't have good command in his most recent start against the Cardinals, and it cost him in a three-run fifth inning in which St. Louis hit for the cycle. The big blow was a two-run homer to Albert Pujols, who got ahead in the count, 2-and-0, before hammering a misplaced fastball. "I just tried to move it around and locate the best I could," Suppan said. He has been much more effective this season on the road, going 4-2 with a 3.80 ERA in 12 starts. At Miller Park, Suppan is 2-7 with a 6.39 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano picked up his first win since July 22 in his last start vs. the Pirates. Big Z gave up two runs on five hits over six innings and struck out eight. But how long will he go against the Brewers? Zambrano wasn't happy when Lou Piniella pulled him in the sixth, and the Cubs manager said next time, he'll let the right-hander go the distance, even if it means he throws 200 pitches. Will he or won't he? Piniella did say he wants Zambrano to win three, four more games in the final stretch. He's got about four starts left in the regular season.
away_pitcher_note: Worried about the 23-year-old's workload after he spent most of last season on the disabled list, the Brewers skipped Gallardo's last start. That means Gallardo should be fresh for his return to Wrigley Field, site of the devastating knee injury on May 1 of last season that cost Gallardo all but four regular-season starts. Gallardo said he understood the decision by Brewers officials to limit his starts the rest of the way. "I don't want to be shut down. I want to finish out the year strong," Gallardo said. "We're trying to find ways to make that happen. It's somewhat of [a compromise]. I feel like everything is coming out nice and easy. You have to deal with it, I guess. It's in the best interests for me. I know they're looking out."

home_pitcher_note: Harden has pitched well this season and has a 2.39 ERA since the All-Star break. Yet the Cubs have him on a strict pitch count and rarely allow him to throw much more than 100 in order to keep him healthy. When you combine that with a lot of strikeouts and walks, you get some short outings, like the one Harden had in his last start, Friday against the Reds. In that game, he walked five and although he gave up just one run, he left after four innings after throwing 103 pitches. Of Harden's 25 starts, 10 have lasted fewer than six innings, including each of the past three.
away_pitcher_note: Looper has a 3.52 ERA over his past five starts, including a Friday win at Arizona that was quite lucrative for the right-hander. By simply making his 30th start this season, Looper maxed out the performance bonuses in his 2009 contract (meaning an additional $750,000 on top of his $4.75 million salary) and increased the price of his mutual option for 2010. The base salary for that option increased $500,000 to $6.5 million, and the buyout, should the Brewers decline, increased $250,000 to $1 million. Even at a slightly higher price, the Brewers probably want Looper back next season because he's tied for the team lead in wins (pending Yovani Gallardo's start in Chicago on Tuesday) and second among Brewers starters with a .278 batting average against.

home_pitcher_note: Wells has gone at least six innings in 19 of his 23 starts but matched his shortest outing of the season in his last start, on Saturday against the Reds. The National League Rookie of the Year contender pitches to contact with his sinker, which makes him reliant on his infield defense, and that defense let him down. Three errors led to two unearned runs in the second inning, and Wells was knocked out after surrendering five runs in 3 2/3 frames. Wells has not faced the Brewers since his Major League debut back on May 8, when he pitched five scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bush is trying to author a happy ending to an injury-marred season, and his past two starts have him on the way to doing just that. Bush pitched seven innings in each of those outings -- vs. the Cardinals on Sept. 7 and then at Arizona on Saturday -- and allowed three earned runs on 12 hits. Compare that to his previous two starts, in which Bush, fresh off two months on the disabled list with a triceps injury, was tagged for 13 runs and 15 hits in eight total innings. He has thrown 97 pitches in each of his past two outings, further allaying fears that his triceps was still giving him trouble. Bush is 1-7 in his career against the Cubs despite a respectable 4.62 ERA in 13 starts and one relief appearance. He has no decisions and a 3.38 ERA in two starts against the Cubs this season.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson will make a second consecutive start in place of fellow lefty Manny Parra, who remains sidelined with a stiff neck. Parra underwent an MRI scan on Wednesday that yielded no further information, but it's clear that Narveson will be needed for at least one more turn through the rotation. Narveson pitched three good innings in Arizona last weekend but was out of the game before recording an out in the fourth. Narveson made both of his career appearances against the Astros in 2006, for the Cardinals, including a Sept. 22 start in which he allowed two runs on two hits in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris will start on six days of rest, having not pitched since giving up six hits and one run and striking out seven batters Sept. 11 against Pittsburgh. He's received decisions in all eight of his starts this year, going 3-0 with a 3.00 ERA to start his career before losing his next three starts (0-3, 13.11 ERA). He's 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA in his last two starts, beating the Phillies and Pirates. This will be his second career appearance against the Brewers. He beat them Aug. 7, giving up three hits and two runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan surrendered only three Cubs hits in seven innings Monday, but one of them was a Derrek Lee homer. Suppan allowed that lone run, but was on the wrong end of a 2-0 loss to Ryan Dempster that was highlighted by some spectacular Cubs defense. It continued a trend for Suppan, who has been very tough this season on the road but had struggled at Miller Park, where he's 2-7 with a 6.26 ERA in 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler is coming off a quality start against the Pirates, allowing seven hits and two runs in six innings. He is 0-1 in his past four starts and has lost five of his past six decisions. His only win in that span came Aug. 22, when he beat Arizona in Houston. He's 4-9 with a 4.75 ERA in 21 games (12 starts) in his career against the Brewers, including 1-3 with a 4.08 ERA in 10 games (four starts) at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Ken Macha said he would give Gallardo one last start before shutting the talented young right-hander down for the rest of the season. He'll be on the hill with a pitch count, though Macha declined to say what the magic number would be. It hasn't been a disappointing season for Gallardo, per se, but the right-hander will aim to lower his pitch counts and limit his walks in 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Paulino has three losses in his last three starts, but the Astros did not score a run while he was on the mound in any of those games. In those three starts, he's allowed five earned runs in 17 innings and struck out 20. Paulino hasn't won since holding Detroit to one run and three hits in seven innings June 27. He's 0-2 with a 9.69 ERA in his career against the Brewers, including 0-1 with a 6.00 ERA this year.

home_pitcher_note: Looper struggled to get through the fifth inning at Wrigley Field on Wednesday but managed to win his 13th game, a new career high after notching 12 wins in each of the previous two seasons as a starter. He had to work through some discomfort, the result of a batting practice line drive that struck him square in the back the previous afternoon and caused his back to tighten in the middle innings of his outing against the Cubs. He knew he was chasing a personal milestone. "I knew that going in," Looper said. "I had 12 [wins] every year, and to get the 13th is nice."
away_pitcher_note: The Cubs have decided to skip Rich Harden and insert Gorzelanny into the rotation. Harden was roughed up by the Brewers in his last start, giving up five runs on five hits and three walks over three innings. This will be Gorzelanny's fifth start with the Cubs. He's 2-1 with a 4.74 ERA in nine appearances since joining Chicago on July 30. In his four previous starts with the Cubs, the lefty is 2-1 with a 4.82 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Bush pitched 5 2/3 innings to beat the Cubs on Thursday, then hustled home to welcome a new member to the family. Bush's wife, Carrie, was to be induced into labor on Friday morning. "He had a lot on his mind with the baby coming, and that's something we had been talking a lot about over the last couple of days," Brewers pitching coach Chris Bosio said. "He gave us a chance to win it, and that's what we're looking for. The offense and the bullpen came through." Jody Gerut provided most of the offense with a grand slam, and four relievers worked the final 3 1/3 innings for a 7-4 win. It was a rare win for Bush, who is just 2-7 against the Cubs despite a respectable 4.73 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Wells was upset with himself after giving up five earned runs in four innings in his last start, Thursday against the Brewers. The rookie walked a season-high five, for a total of eight in his past 7 2/3 innings. That's not a recipe for success for Wells, who issued two or fewer free passes in 19 of his first 22 starts. But Wells said manager Lou Piniella "hit a nerve," when they talked in the dugout after Wells' outing. Piniella told his pitcher to go back to doing what he has for most of this season: challenging hitters in the strike zone and getting ahead in the count, rather than nibbling at the corners of the plate. Wells said he will fix the problem before his next start.

home_pitcher_note: With Manny Parra's ailing neck still an issue, Narveson is likely to make a third straight start instead, and he certainly did nothing to dissuade his use on Friday. Narveson threw five innings and allowed just one run, the lengthiest outing of his big league career. He has allowed just five earned runs since rejoining the team from Triple-A Nashville on Aug. 21, posting a 2.11 ERA over nine appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija will sub for Ted Lilly, who is being given a few extra days because of tendinitis in his left shoulder. This will be Samardzija's second big league start. He made his first start Aug. 12 against Philadelphia, giving up seven runs on eight hits over 3 1/3 innings while striking out four. The right-hander, who was the Cubs' fifth-round pick in 2006, has split time this season between the big league team and Triple-A Iowa. For the season, he's 1-2 with a 7.89 ERA in 19 games with the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan has worked seven quality innings in each of his last two starts, including a win over the Astros on Saturday in which he set a season high with seven strikeouts. It was Suppan's third win at Miller Park in 14 home starts; he's 3-7 with a 5.92 ERA at home and 4-3 with a 3.56 ERA in 13 starts on the road. Suppan missed the Phillies when the Brewers went through Philadelphia in April, but he's 3-6 against them in his career with a 6.13 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Happ left Friday's game after just three innings for precautionary reasons. He had missed his previous two starts because of a strained right intercostal muscle, and when he appeared to favor it on a play in the third inning, Phillies manager Charlie Manuel decided to take him out of the game. Happ said he was fine. He said he felt no pain or discomfort, but because the Phillies already were without left-handers Scott Eyre, J.C. Romero and Jack Taschner in the bullpen, Manuel wants to make sure Happ is healthy in case he needs him in the bullpen in the postseason.

home_pitcher_note: This is Yovani Gallardo's slot and the Brewers will give it to Parra, who has not started since developing a stiff neck and exiting a Sept. 8 start against the Cardinals. Parra declared himself "100 percent healthy" after throwing a series of bullpen sessions this week and will have two starts to author a positive finish to his disappointing season. He has the highest ERA of any Major League pitcher with at least 80 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lee pitched just four innings Sunday against the Braves at Turner Field, but only because of a 1 hour, 51 minute rain delay. He had allowed five hits and one run to that point. Lee wanted to run back out there, but the Phillies told him it wasn't worth the risk. It made sense. While it would have been nice to have Lee pitch a few more innings, they want to make sure he is healthy for the postseason. He is 7-2 with a 2.65 ERA since he joined the Phillies on July 29.

home_pitcher_note: Looper surrendered two more home runs against the Cubs on Monday to set a dubious club record. He's surrendered 37 homers this season, most in the Majors and one more than former Brewers lefty Wayne Franklin allowed in 2003. He pitched six scoreless innings in his start against the Phillies on April 22, one of only six starts (of 32) this season in which Looper hasn't allowed at least one home run. He's surrendered one in 11 of his last 12 starts, but remains tied for the team lead in wins.
away_pitcher_note: Pedro Martinez was scratched from his start on Saturday with a stiff neck in the hopes that he'll be ready to go in more meaningful games later on. Replacing him is Kyle Kendrick, who finished 9-7 with a 3.34 ERA as a starter on the Triple-A level before joining the Phillies this month after rosters expanded. Kendrick is 2-0 in two appearances (one start) since returning to the Majors, with a stellar 1.59 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Five days after he beat the Cubs at Wrigley Field, Bush surrendered more earned runs -- five -- than he recorded outs -- four -- in a loss at Miller Park. Bush lasted only 1 1/3 innings in his shortest start of the season and lost for the first time in three starts. He'll face the Phillies for the first time since April 23, when Bush took a no-hitter into the eighth inning only to lose it on a Matt Stairs home run. He still won that day, allowing one run on two hits in a season-high 7 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton allowed just two hits and two walks and struck out nine in seven scoreless innings in a 9-3 victory over the Marlins in Game 1 of a doubleheader Tuesday at Land Shark Stadium. Combined with six shutout innings the previous Thursday against the Nationals at Citizens Bank Park, Blanton (11-7) has now thrown 13 consecutive scoreless innings. Blanton threw a career-high 18 consecutive scoreless innings Aug. 16-31, 2005, when he pitched for Oakland. Blanton is 9-4 with a 2.78 ERA in 21 starts since May 21 in Cincinnati, where he allowed five runs in five innings. His ERA ranks 10th in the Majors and seventh in the National League in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Whether it's pitch selection, mechanics or plain old execution, Marquis is struggling these days. He has a 6.49 ERA in his last six starts, during which the Rockies are 1-5, and has given up five earned runs in four of those. Before his last start, when he gave up six runs (five earned) in 4 2/3 innings against the Padres, manager Jim Tracy said Marquis was over analyzing, anticipating adjustments by hitters. The manager wants him to get back to the sinker that was responsible for his success through three-quarters of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Whomever starts this game will also get the Brewers' season finale, and an off-day could allow manager Ken Macha to shuffle the rotation to make Jeff Suppan the choice. But Narveson may have pitched his way into that honor with 5 2/3 outstanding innings against the Cubs on Wednesday, allowing only three hits, including a solo homer to opposing starter Jeff Samardzija. Narveson is trying to make his case for a job next season, and the Brewers may want to take the opportunity to see him as much as possible.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel saw another strong start go for naught Thursday, as he lasted 6 1/3 innings and yielded two runs on six hits, striking out six while walking none. The Rockies bullpen let in the tying run in the seventh and eventually lost the game when the go-ahead runs scored in the eighth. It was Hammel's fifth no-decision in his last seven starts, and his fifth quality outing in the span. He's gone at least six innings in his last five starts, and in 10 of his last 11 starts, he's allowed three runs or less, earning his stripes as one of the club's most dependable starters in the second half of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan has been much better on the road this season (4-3, 3.56 ERA in 13 starts) than at Miller Park, and he's 3-0 with a 3.75 ERA in four career starts at Coors Field. He had another poor start at home on Thursday, when he surrendered seven earned runs and a season-high 12 hits in a loss to the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Any fears that five weeks off because of a shoulder injury would make Cook ineffective proved unwarranted. Cook held the Cardinals scoreless on four hits in five innings (76 pitches) Friday night. He also forced 12 groundball outs. It was one of those games when Cook could stay with his sinker almost exclusively. He'll be asked to throw more pitches, and it will be a test if he has to adjust. But the Rockies are counting on Cook in the season's final days and, they hope, in the playoffs.
away_pitcher_note: Parra missed three starts with a stiff neck but looked no worse for the wear on Friday, when he worked seven innings and limited the Phillies to two runs, one of them unearned and the other earned only because of a scoring change. Ryan Howard's two-run single was originally ruled an error on Brewers first baseman Prince Fielder and one RBI, but it was later switched to a base hit. Parra matched his season high with eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright will be going on an extra day of rest, and he can use it. He threw 130 pitches in the Cardinals' division-clinching win on Saturday in Colorado, and had to work hard for most of them. However, he may also have cemented a Cy Young Award with the performance. He'll be going for win No. 20, but it's unlikely that the Cardinals will push him in his last start before the playoffs.
away_pitcher_note: Looper surrendered two more home runs in his most recent start and has served up 39 this season, most in the Majors and a Brewers record. He has allowed at least one homer in 12 of his past 13 starts. He's allowed one in each of his two starts against St. Louis this season but is 1-0 in those games with a 3.75 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: It's the last chance for Lohse to show his stuff before the playoffs. There are no guarantees for him, as John Smoltz has pitched well and he has yet to really find his form. Lohse has felt good for two starts in a row, though, and that's encouraging. Things would seem to work better if Lohse can secure a rotation spot, because Smoltz has experience as a late-inning reliever while Lohse has pitched very little out of the bullpen in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva is likely to make a spot start in place of Dave Bush, who decided to shut it down for the year because of arm fatigue. Earlier this season, the Brewers hoped Villanueva could bolster a rotation beset by injuries to Bush and others, but he went 0-3 with a 6.38 ERA and was bounced back to the bullpen. Villanueva has been better of late, posting a 2.31 ERA over his last 15 appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro gets one more chance to go into October on a positive note. He's been less effective in September than earlier in the year, and his last time out he got rocked. Pineiro needs to keep the ball in the park, and he didn't do that well his last time out. He's been much better at home than on the road, which would actually be the one upside if the Cardinals begin the playoffs on the road: Pineiro would pitch Game 3 at Busch Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan will work on short rest to reach the 30-start milestone for the 11th consecutive season. Among active pitchers, only Livan Hernandez (12 seasons) has a longer streak. Trouble is, Suppan has surrendered 15 earned runs and 22 hits in 10 1/3 innings over his past two starts. He'll probably pitch only a couple of innings before the Brewers turn to former Cardinal Chris Narveson.

summary: 2010-03-21 - Chicago White Sox @ Milwaukee Brewers (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: Bush, the Brewers' No. 4 starter, will be making his final start of Spring Training. Bush has allowed 10 runs -- nine earned -- in 18 2/3 innings this spring.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello, who won 19 games during his rookie season in 2009, has allowed six runs -- three earned -- over 18 innings this Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: Last year, Brewers manager Ken Macha held his young right-hander for Game 2 of the regular season. This time, Macha figures that the 24-year-old Gallardo is ready for the bright lights of Opening Day. He was the obvious choice after going 13-12 with a 3.73 ERA and 204 strikeouts in 30 starts last season before the Brewers shut him down. It was the fifth 200-plus strikeout season in club history, and Gallardo ranked third in the National League with a .219 opponents' batting average.  The Brewers would love to see Gallardo get off to another hot start; he was the team's pitcher of the month last April after beginning the season 3-1 with a 2.86 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Last season, as Jimenez's arsenal of power pitches and competitive spirit grew, manager Jim Tracy recognized him as a potential staff ace. Jimenez struck out 158 against 85 walks last year. His task this year will be to increase his efficiency and go beyond the 218 innings he tallied last year. Jimenez's experience against the Brewers is scant -- 1-0, 2.77 ERA in two starts. His one start at Miller Park was stellar, however. He went seven scoreless innings, gave up three hits, struck out seven and walked five for the win in the Rockies' 4-3 victory on July 7, 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf's Brewers debut will come against a team he's handled well in his career. He was 1-1 with a 2.96 ERA against Colorado last season for the Dodgers and, in 14 career starts, Wolf is 5-3 with a 4.02 ERA against Colorado. The Brewers signed Wolf during baseball's Winter Meetings to a three-year contract and hope he'll provide a left-handed foil to right-handed ace Yovani Gallardo atop the starting rotation. Gallardo led the Brewers last season with 17 quality starts (six or more innings with three or fewer earned runs). Wolf put together 24 such starts, tying Cliff Lee for the most of any left-hander in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: This start originally belonged to Jeff Francis, but the Rockies transferred the left-hander to the 15-day disabled list on Saturday morning due to shoulder soreness, making room for Smith in the rotation. Smith, who had been lined up for a spot in the Rockies' bullpen, pitched admirably during Cactus League play, striking out 18 batters and walking six over 18 innings in which he surrendered just three runs.

home_pitcher_note: Davis returns to Milwaukee after a three-year stint with the Arizona Diamondbacks. He resuscitated his career with the Brewers from 2003-06, and Milwaukee GM Doug Melvin was interested in a reunion because of Davis' durability. He's topped 200 innings in four of the past six seasons and made at least 33 starts in five of those six. The exception was 2008, when Davis underwent treatment for thyroid cancer. He is 19-14 with a 3.37 ERA in 58 career starts at Miller Park and has limited opponents to a .229 average there.
away_pitcher_note: When Cook and the Brewers last saw one another, it was a happy occasion. Cook pitched eight innings and held the Brewers to four hits and one run in eight innings of a 9-2 victory at Coors Field last Oct. 1, as the Rockies clinched a playoff berth. Cook went through a brief crisis when he lost the release point on his sinking fastball, but one afternoon on a Minor League field he regained his form and all was fine in Rockies Nation. Cook is 6-2 with a 3.02 ERA in 10 career games (nine starts) against the Brewers, and 2-1 with a 3.00 ERA in five starts at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Bush entered Spring Training in something of a tenuous situation because of his $4.215 million salary, which wasn't guaranteed until Opening Day. But he pitched his way into the Brewers' mix, going 1-1 with a 4.34 ERA in four Cactus League appearances. That ERA is a bit deceiving because Bush surrendered six earned runs in his final Arizona start; before that he had allowed only one run in each of his three outings. When Bush is hitting his spots he is extremely effective; he took a no-hitter into the eighth inning in each of the past two seasons. His 2009 season was marred by an elbow injury -- the result of a line drive off Hanley Ramirez's bat in Florida that caused Bush trouble throughout the summer. He says he's 100 percent healthy this year.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse will be looking to put a frustrating and at times painful 2009 season in the rear-view mirror as quickly as possible. His performance didn't live up to what he managed in an outstanding 2008, and he was beset by one malady after another. Lohse dealt with a string of injuries and even a nasty stomach illness in one start. He's stayed healthy this spring, though, and looks poised to put together a better season in '10. He may not repeat his '08 success, but he should be better than he was last year, and that would be a good start for the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers briefly considered bringing a fifth starter into the mix here, but instead will go back to Gallardo on regular rest. He was the team's pick to pitch Opening Day against the Rockies after winning the team's pitcher of the year honor in 2009, and he should be on a longer leash this season with a full Major League season under his belt. Gallardo has struggled against the Cardinals in his career, going 0-2 with a 5.70 ERA in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia entered camp as the longest shot of three candidates to make the Cardinals' rotation, but he pitched so well that the club simply didn't have any choice. The lefty was the clear winner of the competition with Kyle McClellan, who will go to the Cardinals bullpen, and Rich Hill, who will go to Triple-A Memphis. He has good stuff, developing but already decent command and a solid mound presence. He's also still pretty inexperienced as a professional pitcher and is less than two years removed from Tommy John surgery. That means the club will handle him gently, with hopes of keeping him healthy by limiting his innings and pitches.

home_pitcher_note: The prime-time assignment goes to Wolf, who could have his hands full with Cardinals hitters like former Brewer Felipe Lopez (7-for-21, .333 lifetime against Wolf), Albert Pujols (5-for-16, .313) and Matt Holliday (5-for-16, four extra-base hits). Wolf surrendered nine hits in his Brewers debut but won after allowing four runs in 6 2/3 innings thanks to an offense that scored seven times. He may spend some time between starts working on some ideas against left-handed hitters; Wolf is traditionally tough on them but gave up six hits to lefties on Tuesday night.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter had one frustrating inning in Monday's win over the Reds but otherwise looked a lot like the guy who steamrolled the National League Central in 2009. Of all the things Carpenter accomplished in '09, one of the most impressive was his dominance within his own division. In 15 starts within the Central, Carpenter went 11-0 with a 1.58 ERA. He's already off to a good start in that regard this year, so you can expect to see him pitching an awful lot in division games in 2010. He was especially brilliant in two starts at Miller Park last year, allowing no runs, three hits and two walks over 17 innings -- with 20 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster gets the call to start the home opener. The right-hander should have a win after pitching six solid innings against the Braves on Wednesday. He struck out nine and gave up one run on three hits. But a high pitch count -- he threw 95 in six innings -- forced his exit. Last year, Dempster was 7-4 with a 3.97 ERA in 14 home starts compared to 4-5 with a 3.38 ERA in 17 road games. He faced the Brewers four times in '09 and had the upper hand, posting a 3-1 record and 3.67 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Davis endured an awful first inning against the Rockies on Wednesday, throwing half of his 40 pitches out of the strike zone, including two in the dirt that eluded catcher George Kottaras. But he limited the damage to three runs and then settled in nicely, throwing 29 of his final 48 pitches for strikes while the Brewers rallied for a 5-4 win. Davis happily settled for a no-decision, and so did his manager. "He got out there into the fifth [inning] and it wasn't completely ugly," Ken Macha said. "It could have been a blowout there in the first inning." Davis is 9-6 with a 3.20 ERA in 16 career starts against the Cubs including 3-2 with a 1.93 ERA in six starts at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Wells didn't get his first win last year until his eighth start. This season, the sophomore picked up his first "W" and the team's first win in his first start. Wells threw six scoreless innings against the Braves, giving up six hits and striking out one. He was helped by three double plays. If he keeps the ball on the ground, he'll do fine. Against the Brewers last year, Wells was 1-1 in three starts with a 3.60 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: A rare blown save by Trevor Hoffman cost Bush a win in his season debut, but the good news for Bush and the Brewers is that the right-hander appears back on track after a 2009 season marred by injury. He worked 5 2/3 innings against the Cardinals and was a strike away from getting through the sixth inning with only one run on the board when Matt Holliday connected for a two-run homer. It would prove Bush's final pitch, but he was looking at the bright side. "It's been about 10 months since I've been out on the mound and felt like I didn't have anything to hold back on," said Bush, who wasn't the same last season after a Hanley Ramirez line drive struck him near the elbow. He's just 2-8 with a 5.13 ERA in 16 career appearances against the Cubs, 15 of them starts.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano redeemed himself after a disastrous Opening Day start. The right-hander struck out nine over seven innings against the Reds on Saturday for his first win. It was a much improved outing after lasting just 1 1/3 innings back on the season opener. This will be Big Z's first start at home, where he was 2-5 with a 5.03 ERA last season compared to 7-2 with a 2.73 ERA on the road. In his career, Zambrano is 46-39 at Wrigley compared to 59-30 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan gets the nod as the Brewers' fifth starter over left-handers Chris Narveson and Manny Parra despite a decidedly subpar spring in which he allowed 14 runs and 21 hits in 16 1/3 innings while dealing with a neck injury. That ailment -- cervical disc pain -- landed Suppan on the 15-day disabled list to start the year but he made a rehab start at Class A Wisconsin on Friday and appears set to debut against the Cubs. Suppan has a very respectable 3.63 ERA in 23 career starts against Chicago, including a 3.77 ERA in 12 starts at Wrigley Field. He's in the final season of a four-year contract.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan has struggled so far this season. After getting hit hard in his Opening Day start against the Phillies, Lannan allowed three runs in a five-inning start against the Mets to secure his first win. The Brewers likely aren't Lannan's choice for which team to face when his club needs a quality outing. The lefty has struggled against Milwaukee in his career, going 0-1 with a 7.10 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo's first start after signing a five-year, $30.1 million contract didn't go as planned. He surrendered six Cardinals runs on five hits including Yadier Molina's second-inning, three-run homer, and Gallardo remains winless through his first two starts of the season. It continued Gallardo's career struggles against St. Louis, but he's had much better luck against the Nationals, going 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA in two starts and one relief stint. Gallardo has struck out 21 Nationals batters in his brief career versus only four walks.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez limited the Mets to five hits and allowed only two runners to reach scoring position on Sunday. He threw just 88 pitches, but acknowledged that he didn't have anything left after the seventh inning. It's amazing that Hernandez, who didn't have much of a Spring Training, went as far as he did in the game. He pitched in only two Grapefruit League games, because he was trying to get into pitching shape after signing a Minor League contract with the club in late February. Hernandez didn't go more than five innings in a Spring Training game. When the regular season started, Hernandez was left behind in order for the team to carry eight relievers. Washington didn't need a fifth starter until this past Sunday. Hernandez spent most of his down time in Miami, where he lives, but had bullpen sessions and pitched in an intrasquad game in the team's complex in Viera, Fla.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf has pitched into the seventh inning in both of his Brewers starts but was denied his second win on Sunday when Trevor Hoffman blew a save. For the second straight outing Wolf surrendered four runs, but this time only two of them were earned, the result of an error charged to shortstop Alcides Escobar. Wolf is 9-4 with a 4.43 ERA in 20 career starts against Washington's franchise, tying his second-best win total against any team. He has 12 wins against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis made his second start for Washington Monday, and as he did in his first one, he struggled. He lasted 4 1/3 innings and gave up seven runs (six earned) on seven hits. Marquis got off to a great start, throwing no-hit ball through three innings. He even helped himself with the bat, hitting a two-run double in the top of the fourth to give Washington a 4-0 lead. But things started to unravel as he gave up seven runs in two innings. Marquis' worst inning was the fifth, when Philadelphia batted around and scored five runs. Chase Utley highlighted the scoring with a two-run homer.
away_pitcher_note: Free-agent pick-up Doug Davis was supposed to be Mr. Reliable in the middle of the Brewers' starting rotation. So far he's been anything but. Five days after he lasted only four innings in his season debut against the Rockies, Davis was touched for six runs and seven hits in just 3 1/3 innings against the Cubs on Monday. Most of the damage came in the third inning, when Davis surrendered a three-run homer to Xavier Nady and a two-run homer to Jeff Baker, both with two outs. Twenty-two of Davis' 34 outings last season qualified as "quality starts" of at least six innings with three or fewer earned runs. He hasn't met that threshold in either of his starts so far.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has not gotten off to the start he had envisioned. He was able to log six innings in his most recent start, but the six runs he allowed off three home runs cost Morton the chance to take a step forward. Pinpointing one problem with the right-hander is a bit hard. He has been hurt when behind in the count, so first-pitch strikes are definitely a must. His execution must also improve. Morton is going to rely heavily on a fastball-curveball mix, but too often those pitches are drifting back over the plate. Morton is 0-2 with a 2.77 ERA in two previous starts against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Dave Bush's turn would come up next when the Brewers open a three-game series at PNC Park on Tuesday, though manager Ken Macha won't announce his rotation for the series until Saturday. Bush is still searching for his first win of 2010, though he's coming off a no-decision in a decent enough outing at Chicago on Wednesday. He'll need to repeat his performance against the Cubs -- seven hits and no walks in six innings -- and he needs to remain around the plate. Against Chicago, Bush threw 56 of 77 pitches for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Zach Duke should be sitting on three wins right now if not for a poor night from the Pirates' bullpen after his last start. Duke threw 90 pitches in his last outing before being pulled after allowing a leadoff walk in the eighth. That runner eventually scored, as did another two, which took Duke out of line for the win. Regardless of his record, though, the Pirates have to like what they're seeing from the lefty so far. His sinker has been devastating, and Duke has had a nice changeup to go along with it. He's been pretty efficient and, to this point, the only reliable starter the Pirates have. In 13 career starts against the Brewers, Duke is 3-5 with a 5.38 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo may be the Brewers' staff ace, but he's still searching for consistency, not to mention his first 2010 victory. The right-hander thought he took a positive step forward in his last outing, on Friday, when he allowed two runs on six hits and four walks in six innings against Washington. For Gallardo to succeed, the Brewers need the strikeout artist who 204 hitters in 184 2/3 innings last year, not the guy who's given up a home run in each of his three outings and walked eight hitters in 15 innings. Gallardo, however, believes he's on the verge of becoming his old self. To do that, he'll have to avoid big innings, keep the ball inside PNC Park and attack the Pirates hitters.

home_pitcher_note: McCutchen is guaranteed at least one more start with Ross Ohlendorf on the mend from back spasms. However, McCutchen is going to soon have to start proving that he belongs in the rotation to stay. He has combined for just 7 1/3 innings in his first two starts of the year, with 12 runs scoring against him. Granted, the results were much improved his last time out -- four innings, three earned runs, four hits, three walks -- but they aren't good enough for what the Pirates need from a fifth starter in their rotation. Surprisingly, control and efficiency have been issues for McCutchen, who has always been known to be a strike thrower. This will be McCutchen's first career appearance against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: There's not a lot of mystery when it comes to what Wolf needs to do to be successful. When the veteran southpaw commands his fastball, pounding the strike zone and challenging and getting ahead opposing hitters, he gives his team a chance to win. When he doesn't, Wolf falls behind hitters, goes deeper than he wants to into counts and gives the advantage to the hitter. Fastball command was the issue in Wolf's last start, on Saturday in Washington, where he lasted only five innings, throwing 100 pitches. There's significant pressure on Wolf to start justifying Milwaukee's investment of $29.75 million for a three-year free-agent contract this past offseason, but there's also ample time for Wolf to turn his first season with the Brewers around.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers bumped Suppan's start a few days in order to split their two left-handers in the rotation, and the result is that the veteran right-hander will make his second start of the season after seven days' rest. Suppan started the year on the disabled list with a neck injury and was only so-so against the Cubs on a wind-blown afternoon at Wrigley Field on April 15, allowing four runs on six hits in five innings. Suppan surrendered home runs to Derrek Lee and Marlon Byrd that probably would have cleared the fence even without a stiff breeze blowing straight out, and he'll have to keep the Cubs in the ballpark to have success in the rematch. Suppan was 3-8 with a 6.39 ERA at Miller Park last year.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster should be 3-0. In his two starts in which he did not get a decision, he has given up two earned runs over 13 2/3 innings. In his lone win, which was against Milwaukee, he wasn't as sharp, serving up five runs over 6 1/3 innings. The good news about his last outing against the Astros on Sunday was he bounced back fine after throwing 114 pitches vs. the Brewers on April 12. Ryan Braun homered off Dempster in the last meeting at Wrigley Field and is 6-for-26 lifetime off the right-hander.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers aren't about to bail on Davis after three starts, but it's time for the left-hander to start pitching to his track record. Davis has been steady as she goes since resurrecting his career in Milwaukee in 2003, but his first three starts of the reunion tour have been forgettable. He has yet to pitch past the fifth inning and couldn't hold a 10-0, first-inning lead in Washington on Sunday. Davis was lifted with two outs in the fifth inning and the Brewers had to hold off a Nationals charge for an 11-7 win. Davis will continue to get the ball "for right now," manager Ken Macha said on Tuesday, hardly a ringing endorsement.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly returns to the Cubs rotation after passing all the tests in his rehab. He's coming back from arthroscopic surgery on his left shoulder. He made his last Minor League start Monday in Peoria. In that game, Lilly threw threw 88 pitches over seven innings and picked up the win. He struck out nine and gave up one run on three hits and one walk. Of his total pitches, 63 were strikes. The lefty also singled and was thrown out trying to steal. The shoulder actually has been the least of his problems as he was slowed this spring by the flu and then early in April by back problems.

home_pitcher_note: Bush delivered seven shutout innings against the Pirates on Tuesday just when the team needed a quality outing. He allowed only three hits -- two of them to Andrew McCutchen and the other an infield single to pinch-hitter John Raynor, who was promptly erased on a double play. Bush notched his first win of the season but could easily be 3-0; he exited with the lead on April 9 against the Cardinals and April 14 against the Cubs, only to see the game slip away each time by a reliever.
away_pitcher_note: This would've been Carlos Zambrano's turn in the rotation but he's now in the bullpen. Wells stays on schedule. In his last start Monday against the Mets, Wells gave up one run on six hits over six innings but did not get the win as the bullpen imploded. He faced the Brewers on April 14 at Wrigley Field and struck out the side to start the game, then got into trouble in the fifth. He finished giving up 10 hits, four runs, and striking out seven over 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: It's a rematch of Wednesday at PNC Park, where Gallardo was not his sharpest but nonetheless pitched five scoreless innings in the fourth double-digit strikeout game of his career. The first inning was a harbinger of Gallardo's night, when he needed 26 pitches to get through five batters despite the fact that none of them put a ball in play. Gallardo walked two of them and struck out the other three. In all, he notched 10 strikeouts and earned his first win this season. He improved to 4-2 against the Pirates with a 2.66 ERA in nine games, including eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Duke will get another shot at the Brewers, who knocked him around in his last start. Duke's first three outings of the year were strong, but he worked behind in the count too often in his last start and that hurt him. Duke served up three homers and walked four while allowing six earned runs in five innings. His usual bread-and-butter sinker was also not so sharp. The Pirates are pretty confident this was just a hiccup for Duke, who has been the staff's most reliable pitcher since the start of 2009. Still, he hasn't beaten the Brewers since 2006 and has a career 5.73 ERA against Milwaukee (14 starts).

home_pitcher_note: Last time out, Wolf benefited from the Brewers' historic offensive performance, as they put up 20 runs against the Pirates at PNC Park. Lost in all the offense for Milwaukee was the fact that Wolf had his best outing as a Brewer. The lefty pitched six strong innings, scattering six hits, and did not allow a run. For good measure, Wolf added a pair of hits and scored twice in three at-bats. Thanks in part to Wolf's strong performance, the Brewers notched the first 20-0 result in Major League Baseball since 1900 and the largest margin of victory in a shutout in club history.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' need for a spot starter leads them back to Triple-A, where this time the club will pluck Karstens. Though Karstens started the 2009 season in the Pirates' rotation, the organization had him lined up to be a reliever this season. All the fluctuation in the big-league rotation, though, forced Karstens into Indianapolis' rotation recently. He has made five appearances (one start) so far this season. In 16 innings, the right-hander has allowed 13 earned runs on 21 hits. He's walked two and struck out five.

home_pitcher_note: After two poor outings by veteran right-hander Jeff Suppan to begin the season, Narveson will be given his shot at the fifth-starter role on Wednesday against the Pirates. Narveson gets the opportunity based on his performance last September and in Spring Training this year, Brewers manager Ken Macha said. In five Cactus League games, Narveson pitched 13 scoreless innings, allowing 10 hits. Last season, Narveson went 2-0 with a 3.83 ERA in 21 games (four starts) with Milwaukee, including a 1-0 record with a 3.38 ERA as a starter. He was named Brewers Pitcher of the Month for September/October last season after finishing the season 1-0 with a 2.73 ERA in 29 2/3 innings over his final nine appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm hasn't necessarily added to the Pirates' starting pitching woes, but he hasn't been dominant to this point either. Maholm gave the Pirates a much-needed seven-inning start on Friday, though he took the lost by giving up four earned runs on seven hits. Maholm has lasted at least six innings in three of his four starts this year, which is particularly significant given the burden the bullpen has carried so far this year. The Pirates will continue to rely on the lefty to pitch deep and keep any deficits manageable. Maholm is 3-5 with a 4.58 ERA in 14 career starts against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: LeBlanc has proven to be an apt fill-in for injured righty Chris Young, who's on the disabled list with a strained right shoulder. On Saturday, LeBlanc tossed six scoreless innings against the Reds, who chased his fastball, slider and curveball in addition to his plus pitch, the changeup, all afternoon. In doing so, the left-hander lowered his ERA to 0.82 and earned himself another start. LeBlanc walked two, allowed three hits and struck out three. He was efficient and did the one thing needed of all pitchers at Great American Ball Park: Keep the ball down. "[LeBlanc] was throwing the ball on both sides of the plate and changing speeds," Reds third baseman Scott Rolen said. "I'm sure that's what he set out to do, and he did a good job. He gets the ball and throws it."
away_pitcher_note: It took him four starts, but Davis finally posted his first quality start since returning to the Brewers for the 2010 season. Unfortunately for Davis, he was outdueled by Cubs lefty Ted Lilly, who did not allow a run in six innings for the win on Saturday. Davis will look to build on his much-improved performance as the Brewers head west to square off with the Padres, a team Davis is quite familiar with after spending the past three seasons with the Arizona Diamondbacks. In 18 career appearances (17 starts) against the Padres, Davis is 10-3 with a 2.92 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Richard is the only pitcher in the Padres' starting rotation without a victory this season. It looked like he might have a shot at a win in his last start against the Reds on Sunday, even though his command betrayed him at times. "A couple of pitches were close," said Richard, who walked four in 5 1/3 innings. "I got too deep into counts, [that's] where I really got hurt." Richard allowed one hit over the first three innings but allowed back-to-back RBI singles in the bottom of the fourth inning. Both occurred with two outs, something Richard was kicking himself over after the game. "You get two quick outs, you've got to attack that third hitter," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Entering his start against the Cubs on Sunday, Bush had the lowest ERA of any Brewers starter at 2.41. That all changed on Sunday, however, as Bush allowed nine runs -- seven earned -- on 10 hits, including four home runs. With that outing of just 3 2/3 innings, Bush's ERA jumped more than two full runs to 4.84. Bush has struggled in two starts at home this season, allowing 12 runs -- 10 earned -- on 14 hits in 9 1/3 innings. He has allowed just two runs on 10 hits in 13 innings on the road this season, though, and will look to continue his road success in San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: Latos may find himself pitching to retain his rotation spot here, with Chris Young nearing a return from the disabled list. Latos left plenty of questions about himself in his last outing against the Marlins. He lasted just 2 2/3 innings and gave up seven runs on seven hits and three walks. Most prominent in manager Bud Black's mind is whether Latos can string together good pitches. Black saw some good signs in Latos in the ashes of that defeat, but said the right-hander would often follow a good pitch with a not-so-good one. Notable was a first-inning home run served to Hanley Ramirez on a pitch supposed to be low and outside. Latos also allowed a two-out, two-run single to the opposing pitcher in the second inning of that game. Then in the third inning, everything fell apart. A one-out walk ignited a four-run inning and Latos was done for the night. Through it all, at least Latos maintained his composure, which he saw as an improvement from last season. Most agree the 22-year-old has plenty of potential, but he'll need to be sharper against the solid-hitting Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo has benefited from consecutive starts opposite the Pirates and left-hander Zach Duke. While Duke surrendered 14 earned runs in those games on 16 hits and eight walks in nine innings, Gallardo held the Pirates to no earned runs over 11 innings with eight hits and 14 strikeouts. Gallardo's ERA dropped from 5.50 to 3.41 in that span. He lost his only career start against the Padres and has never pitched at spacious PETCO Park.

home_pitcher_note: Garland had yet another great outing, this time against the Marlins on Tuesday, giving up just one run on three hits and three walks while striking out 10 in six innings. After a 30-pitch first inning, Garland was dominant in the second, third, fourth and fifth innings, when he struck out a total of eight batters and didn't allow a ball to be hit out of the infield. In the sixth, the 30-year-old got out of a jam to keep his team in the game. With nobody out, runners on the corners and a 2-0 lead, Garland got Hanley Ramirez to bounce into a double play that scored a run but killed a rally. Then, on his 105th pitch, he struck out Jorge Cantu -- the only man who got a hit off him in the first five innings -- to tie his career-high for punchouts. Garland has given up just two runs in his past two starts -- a span of 13 innings. He is 1-0 with a 2.65 ERA in four games (two starts) against the Brewers in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf is coming off a gem against the Pirates in which he worked eight innings, the most by a Brewers starter this season, and allowed only two runs while scattering 10 hits. Wolf was in line for the win before Trevor Hoffman suffered a blown save in the ninth inning, but it was another positive outing for the Brewers' most significant free agent pickup. In his last two starts, Wolf has surrendered only two runs in 14 innings, and he's also been very good at the plate. With two more hits Tuesday, Wolf is 6-for-13 this season.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw walked the first two batters in his last start, they both scored on a misplay by center fielder Matt Kemp, and that was all it took to saddle the left-hander with a loss. Almost overlooked was the fact that he pitched the Dodgers into the seventh inning, allowed no other runs and only two other hits. He's still a little erratic and walks too many batters, but he's the Dodgers starter most capable of dominating an opponent. Nothing wrong with a 3.07 ERA. He's allowed Colorado only two runs in 16 innings at Dodger Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson allowed three runs and two home runs in five innings in his first start of the season against the Pirates. He struck out five and walked two and got a no decision. He has taken Jeff Suppan's place in the rotation. In his first stint with the Brewers last season, he struggled with an 8.44 ERA in nine relief outings before being sent to Nashville. He was switched to a starting assignment in Nashville and later returned to the Brewers, going 1-0 with a 3.38 ERA in four starts in September.

home_pitcher_note: If two starts is a trend, Billingsley is back on track. After two shaky starts, he's rebounded with two quality starts against Washington and Pittsburgh while trimming his ERA from 7.07 to 4.85. He's done it by returning to the basics, throwing fewer cutters and relying on fastballs and curves. He said his goal is to simplify his approach. The Dodgers can't argue with the results. His only start last year against the Brewers was in Miller Park, and it wasn't pretty: five earned runs and four walks in a five-inning no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Davis took the loss on Thursday in San Diego, but suffered an unusual fate, as all eight of the hits he allowed were singles.  He gave up six runs (five earned) over four innings, and the Padres proceeded to hit only singles throughout the course of the game as the Brewers fell, 9-0.  Davis fared better in his previous start, allowing only two runs over 6 1/3 innings, but has been knocked out of each of his other five starts prior to the fifth inning.  He is 5-4 for his career against the Dodgers, with a 3.51 ERA in 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Eight days after his Major League debut, Ely gets another shot at being the fifth starter. Against the Mets, he made it through six innings, which is more than some of his more experienced teammates have done this year. He showed enough poise to rebound from two shaky innings early, but he looked the part of a rookie in those shaky innings and cost himself three runs with a poor defensive decision on a comebacker. He also allowed four extra-base hits, perhaps an indicator that he doesn't have the velocity to get away with mistake pitches. He came into that start with only three games above Double-A.
away_pitcher_note: Bush pitched well enough against the Padres on Friday (three runs on six hits in seven innings), especially considering that he had been shelled in his previous outing against the Cubs to the tune of nine runs on 10 hits, including a career-high four homers, in 3 2/3 innings. But he didn't get any support at all from an offense that ran its scoreless streak to 22 innings in a 3-0 loss. Nevertheless, Bush will try to build on the positives from that outing when he faces the Dodgers for the fourth time in his career. He owns a 3.98 ERA in his three previous starts against them, including a 4.15 ERA in two starts at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson would just as soon forget his last start. The right-hander was battered by the Rockies in Coors Field as he allowed 10 runs on 11 hits over 2 1/3 innings. It was the most runs he had allowed in a start in his career. Jackson said that regardless of whether he made good pitches or bad ones, whenever the Rockies made contact they seemed to be able to get hits. Jackson was not overly sharp in his start prior to that, when he allowed three first-inning runs against the Cardinals at Chase Field. He was able to get through eight innings in that game, however. Jackson was acquired by Arizona in a three-team trade during the Winter Meetings that sent Max Scherzer and Daniel Schlereth to the Tigers. The D-backs are his third team in three years. He pitched for Tampa Bay in 2008 before being dealt to the Tigers prior to last season. Jackson throws a fastball, curve, slider and change.
away_pitcher_note: Against the Padres, Gallardo pitched seven strong innings and struck out a season-high 11 batters while giving up one run on six hits and walking two. He also hit a solo home run, snapping a stretch of 24 innings without a Brewers run. Gallardo has homered and struck out at least 10 batters twice in his career, making him just the eighth pitcher to accomplish that feat on multiple occasions since 1960. The others are Steve Carlton (five times), Don Drysdale (four times), Bob Gibson (three times), Earl Wilson (three times), Ferguson Jenkins (twice), Tom Seaver (twice) and Kerry Wood (twice).

home_pitcher_note: Valdez made his Major League debut last Monday against the Astros in Houston. He pitched his way into and out of trouble in the game's first two innings before settling down and allowing one run over five innings. The right-hander replaced Kris Benson, who was forced to leave his last start with discomfort in his shoulder/pectoral muscle area. Valdez was 1-1 with a 3.80 ERA in four starts for Reno this year with 25 strikeouts and five walks in 23 2/3 innings. He  was named the organization's Minor League Pitcher of the Year in 2008, when he had 13 wins between Class A Visalia and Double-A Mobile. Last season was a struggle for him at Reno as he went 7-6 with a 4.78 ERA in 19 games (18 starts). Valdez has a good sinker and changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf had his shortest outing of the season in his last start, an 8-0 loss to the Padres on Sunday, and he still kept the Brewers close. Despite allowing two home runs, he limited the damage to four runs in five innings. Wolf is  2-2 with a 3.86 ERA this season and 8-3 with a 4.38 ERA in 16 career starts against the D-backs. He's done particularly well in his starts at Chase Field, with a 6-1 record in seven outings.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy was once again magnificent in his last start against the Astros in Houston. The right-hander did not allow a run over 6 2/3 innings to earn a 1-0 win. His start before that against the Cubs was outstanding, though you might not be able to tell that from the box score. The right-hander cruised through seven innings, allowing just one run. With a worn-out bullpen, he was left in for the eighth and Kosuke Fukudome hit a grand slam. Still, Kennedy got through eight innings, which helped save an exhausted pen. He appeared in just one game for the Yankees and four in Triple-A in 2009 after missing most of the year following surgery to remove an aneurysm near his right shoulder. The right-hander came in the same three-team trade that netted the D-backs Edwin Jackson.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson was staked to a 9-0 lead in the second inning of his last start, an 11-6 win over the Dodgers. Narveson has been effective in both of his starts since taking the struggling Jeff Suppan's spot, allowing just nine hits and six walks in 11 innings total. Narveson is dominating left-handers, holding them to a .156 batting average but right-handers are batting .404 against him.

home_pitcher_note: It took him six starts and nearly a month, but Doug Davis finally notched the first win of his second tour of duty with the Brewers. He held the Dodgers to three runs in 5 1/3 innings on Wednesday, and the Brewers scored some late insurance runs for an 11-3 win that was closer than the final score indicated. Davis continues to be plagued by some bad luck; opponents are batting .452 against Davis on balls in play this season. The Major League average is in the neighborhood of .300.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson has spent the early portion of this season learning that opposing hitters are taking an aggressive approach against him early in the count. After allowing three earned runs in the first two innings against the Nationals on Wednesday night, the 23-year-old right-hander displayed better command and surrendered just one more run in the six-inning effort. Hanson allowed three two-run homers in his Major League debut against the Brewers last year. He went 0-1 with a 5.54 ERA in two starts against them last year.

home_pitcher_note: Bush was one out away from a tough-luck loss in Los Angeles on Thursday before his Brewers teammates bailed him out. He lasted only five innings, but allowed only one earned run, and that without the benefit of a hit. Bush walked the leadoff hitter for the second straight game, then issued another walk before Dodgers first baseman James Loney cashed in with a sacrifice fly. Two unearned runs scored in the second inning before Bush cruised through three more innings. He has been very good in his career against the Braves, going 1-0 with a 1.71 ERA in three starts, with 14 strikeouts in those games versus two walks in 21 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has allowed two earned runs or fewer in five of his first six starts and limited opponents to a .226 batting average. The veteran right-hander's seven-inning effort against the Nationals on Thursday was marred by a pair of solo home runs. By pitching into the seventh inning in each of his past three outings he has provided further indication that he has recovered from the Tommy John surgical procedure that sidelined him most of last year. Hudson is 2-1 with a 2.90 ERA in four career starts at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: If it's a sunny afternoon and the shadows are in play at Miller Park for this game, Gallardo could be very tough. He has reached double-digit strikeouts in three of his last four starts -- the first Brewers pitcher ever to do so -- and has won all four of those outings, most recently a 3-2 win in Arizona on Friday in which Gallardo struck out 10 batters in five innings. The Braves, of course, were the Brewers' opponent on a sunny day in May 2004, when Ben Sheets used a glare-aided curveball to notch 18 strikeouts, a franchise record.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe certainly looked distressed after allowing the Phillies seven runs and 11 hits in five innings on Friday. The veteran right-hander entered this season with the hope that his offseason adjustments would allow him to avoid the frustration he experienced during the latter portion of the 2009 season. But his stats through the first seven starts of this year look very similar to the ones he posted during his last nine outings last year. Opponents have compiled a .293 batting average and .371 on-base percentage against him. He is 3-1 with a 3.25 ERA in seven career starts against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: The former Phillie notched his third win on Saturday with six solid innings and another huge night by the Brewers' offense, which has scored a whopping 44 runs in Wolf's three wins and no runs in his two losses. Wolf has aided that offense; with seven hits in seven starts he's already four hits shy of his output in 33 starts for the Dodgers last season. Wolf had his best offensive seasons with the Phillies, including a 14-hit season in 2003 with 11 RBIs. Wolf is trying to keep his hitting success a secret this season. "I like to lay in the weeds," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer had been scheduled to pitch Wednesday in Colorado, but a rainout pushed everybody in the Phillies' rotation back a day. That means Moyer will open the three-game series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Friday night at Miller Park. Moyer is coming off a shutout against the Braves, which made him the oldest pitcher in baseball history to throw a shutout at 47 years, 170 days.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson has stabilized the fifth slot in Milwaukee's starting rotation since he replaced veteran right-hander Jeff Suppan on April 24. In three starts, Narveson is 2-0 with a 3.78 ERA including a win at Arizona last weekend in which he allowed only one run in 5 2/3 innings and contributed an RBI single. Narveson has never faced the Phillies in his brief Major League career.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton is making just his third start this season after spending most of the year on the disabled list with a strained left oblique. He is 0-2 with a 4.97 ERA in his first two starts, but the Phillies had chances to win both games. He pitched better than his line indicated on May 3 against St. Louis with the bullpen allowing a couple of his runners to score in a 6-3 loss. The Phillies then lost Saturday to Atlanta, 4-1. If Blanton can get a little more comfortable, and the offense can give him a little more support, he should be fine.

home_pitcher_note: Doug Davis was scheduled to make this start, but he was scratched hours before first pitch due to unspecified medical reasons. In his place will be Bush, who was in line to start on Monday in Cincinnati but will make Sunday's start on regular rest. Bush enters the start having allowed three or fewer runs in six of his seven outings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels did not follow up his masterful performance against St. Louis last week -- one run in eight innings -- with another. He allowed three runs in five innings Sunday against the Braves, struggling to get out of the fifth inning with just three runs scoring. The key for Hamels is to put together a few quality starts in a row. He will try to start that streak up again Saturday against the Milwaukee Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Cueto pitched a one-hitter for his first Major League complete game, allowing only a third-inning single, as the Reds beat the Pirates, 9-0, on Tuesday. Cueto has struggled with pitch efficiency his whole career, yet he required only 102 pitches. Cueto's fastball touched 96 mph. It was the first time this season that Cueto lasted more than six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo delivered his fifth quality start of the season last time out on Wednesday against the Braves, but left with the game tied at 2. He allowed just two runs on five hits through six inning while striking out six and walking three, but settled for his second no-decision of the season as the Brewers went on to lose, 9-2. On the season, Gallardo is 4-2 with a 3.06 ERA, leading all Brewers starters. Only right-handed reliever Todd Coffey has a better ERA on the Brewers staff. Against the Reds on Monday, Gallardo will look for his third win of the month and team-leading fifth overall.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey is coming off of the best outing of his season, and his career, on Wednesday when he tossed a four-hit shutout for a 5-0 win over the Pirates. It was the first complete game of Bailey's career. He needed only 90 pitches and did not walk a batter while striking out six. "Bailey's fastball was working," Reds manager Dusty Baker said. "His location was going good and we turned a couple big double plays, and we got some early offense from Phillips and Votto and that's all Bailey needed."
away_pitcher_note: With Doug Davis on the disabled list with inflammation in the tissue around his heart, the decision was made to move Parra from the bullpen and back into the starting rotation, where he won 11 games for the Brewers last season. Parra, who competed for a starting role in Spring Training, is 0-2 with a 3.98 ERA in 15 relief appearances. He made 27 starts for the Brewers last year, going 11-11 with a 6.93 ERA. Brewers manager Ken Macha said he closely studied Parra's statistics for his past 10 games and said he had improved drastically in most categories. Macha had considered Jeff Suppan, Chris Capuano and Minor League options before deciding to start Parra on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Burres had a 13 scoreless innings streak snapped his last time out and labored through his four-inning start. The left-hander scattered seven hits and allowed six runs (five earned) in what was his fourth start with Pittsburgh. To this point, only two of those starts have extended past the fourth inning. Burres' spot in the rotation is by no means secure. The club is likely to give him at least one more chance to prove that he belongs in the rotation, but the leash probably won't be much longer. Burres' only previous appearance against the Brewers came in relief. He allowed two runs on three hits in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf minced no words after his last start, a loss to the Phillies in which he surrendered six runs in five innings. "It's kind of embarrassing the way I pitched," Wolf said. "I couldn't execute anything. I was behind everybody. ... There's no excuses other than I was terrible today." He's allowed at least one home run in each of his past four starts and has had trouble with left-handed hitters. Last year with the Dodgers, he limited left-handed batters to a .159 average and surrendered only four extra-base hits in 185 plate appearances. This year, left-handers are batting .302 against Wolf, with 10 extra-base hits in 60 plate appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm wasn't sensational, but he got the job done his last time out. Despite allowing a number of deep fly-ball outs, the left-hander worked his way through six innings, limiting the Cubs to two runs on eight hits. He struck out four and didn't walk a batter. Maholm's season has been very much up and down, though he's still managed to pitch at least six innings in six of his eight starts. Maholm allowed four runs on seven hits in seven innings against the Brewers back on April 28. He is 3-5 with a 4.63 ERA in 15 career starts against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers considered giving Narveson an extra day's rest after he threw 130 pitches in Saturday's loss to the Phillies, the most pitches for any Major League pitcher this season. Narveson was given extra treatment and conditioning before being cleared to make his scheduled start on Thursday. Narveson had allowed only two runs on Saturday, but was already nearing 110 pitches when he went out for the sixth inning and surrendered a two-run homer to Shane Victorino. When he struck Chase Utley with pitch No. 130, Macha was forced to tap the bullpen. Before Saturday, Narveson had topped 100 pitches once in eight big league starts.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn thrives on location in order to be successful, which is evidenced by his 13 strikeouts over 46 2/3 innings this season. Fortunately, Blackburn has been able to curb the home run trend that plagued him earlier in the season, allowing no home runs over his past 20 innings. He also has issued more than two walks in a game only once this season -- April 6 against the Angels. In his last start vs. the Yankees, Blackburn went seven strong allowing only three earned runs for his third consecutive quality start. The right-hander is 0-1 with a 6.36 ERA in two starts against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Bush was bumped up a day for his last start when lefty Doug Davis suddenly went on the disabled list with swelling around his heart. Bush did reasonably well on short notice, delivering a quality start, but a trio of RBI doubles by the Phillies, including one by opposing pitcher Cole Hamels, were enough to finish a Philadelphia sweep. This will be a tough assignment for Bush, who is 1-5 in six career starts against the Twins despite a respectable 4.38 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: A trend has developed for Slowey so far this season and it's been his inability to pitch deep into outings. The right-hander had an eight-inning gem against the Indians on April 20 at Target Field, but it's the only one of his eight starts in which he's pitched beyond 5 2/3 innings. Even though Slowey only lasted five innings against the Blue Jays during his last turn in the rotation, he picked up the win and improved to 5-3 on the season with an ERA of 4.70. Slowey allowed three runs on eight hits with no walks to Toronto. His only major blemish was a two-run home run to American League Player of the Week Jose Bautista in the second inning. Next up for Slowey will be a start against the Brewers, a team he's 3-0 against with a 2.43 ERA in four career starts.
