away_pitcher_note: Against the Reds earlier in the week, Gallardo battled command issues all night and issued a career-high six walks while throwing 120 pitches in six innings, just 66 for strikes. But he limited the damage to one run and six hits. "Certainly not your typical Yovani game," Brewers manager Ken Macha said. "A few too many walks. But you can't complain, just one run."

home_pitcher_note: Pavano has been solid in six of his eight starts this season, but when things go wrong for the starter they really go wrong. Such was the case in his last time out against the Blue Jays, when Pavano lasted just four innings while giving up six runs on 10 hits and throwing just 70 pitches. Pavano gave up runs in four consecutive innings to start the game, including two home runs, and saw his ERA inflate to 4.11 on the season. Although Pavano has delivered clunkers in two starts this year, he's pitched at least six innings and allowed two runs or fewer in each of his other six outings. The Twins hope he can find that form when he faces the Brewers. He's 2-2 with a 4.69 ERA in 11 career appearances (nine starts) vs. Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Scheduled Milwaukee starter Manny Parra was called into duty late Saturday when the Brewers went 12 innings in their 8-7 loss to the Twins at Target Field, leaving him perhaps available for duty, but not ready to start. Estrada will make his first Brewers start in Parra's place, despite throwing 21 pitches in relief Saturday while recording only one out. "I'm going to try to go as far as I can," Estrada said. "Right now, I feel good enough to pitch [Sunday]. I'll be ready." Estrada, claimed off waivers from the Nationals over the winter, made his only career start last season for Washington and allowed five runs and three hits in 2 1/3 innings of a loss to the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf was humming along through six innings on Wednesday in Pittsburgh, but he hit a wall in the seventh, allowing three runs on the way to his fourth loss in his last five starts. He was charged with six earned runs on 10 hits in 6 1/3 innings, five days after allowing six runs on seven hits in five innings against the Phillies in an outing he termed, "embarrassing." Wolf was similarly blunt after his loss to the Pirates. "I'm concerned about the fact that I stink," Wolf said. "I'm not going to candy-coat it." He had to ask how many batters he walked. The answer was five, one shy of the career-high he matched three starts earlier against the Padres. "That's horrible," Wolf said.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros won a game in which Paulino started for the first time this year when they beat Colorado Wednesday in Houston, but the big right-hander is still searching for his first win of the season. He had lost six consecutive starts before holding the Rockies to six hits, two runs and five walks in six innings.  He's worked at least five innings seven times in eight starts. Paulino is 0-3 with an 8.53 ERA in four career games against the Brewers, including three starts. He was 0-2 in two starts against them last year, allowing 18 hits in 12 innings. He's pitched two games previously at Miller Park (one start) and is 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson overcame a rough first inning in his last outing Thursday to pick up the win and help the Brewers snap a nine-game skid with a 4-3 win at Pittsburgh. After surrendering three runs on four hits in a 34-pitch opening frame, the southpaw settled down to allow just three hits over his next five innings and finish with 112 pitches, 71 of which went for strikes. Narveson has started two games and made three career appearances against the Astros, with 11 strikeouts in 11 total innings and a 2.45 ERA. It will be just the second home start of the season for the 28-year-old, who threw a Major League-high 130 pitches in his last start at Miller Park, a 10-6 loss to the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt will be making his first start since the Astros acknowledged his agent had asked owner Drayton McLane to trade him to a contender. Oswalt has began the season with nine consecutive quality starts, making him the first Astros pitcher to do so since Roger Clemens in 2005. He has a chance to become the first Houston pitcher since Bob Knepper in 1988 to have 10 consecutive quality starts to begin the season. Oswalt has been the victim of poor run support. The Astros are averaging 2.07 runs per game in Oswalt's starts, and they have scored four runs in 39 innings in his six losses. Oswalt is 13-8 with a 3.75 ERA in 27 career starts against the Brewers, including 5-6 with a 5.36 ERA in 14 starts at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Things couldn't have been much worse for Bush in his last start. After delivering quality starts in each of his previous two appearances, the Brewers right-hander lasted just one-third of an inning against the Twins, surrendering seven runs on six hits while walking two. It was Bush's shortest outing of his career and according to Bush, "the worst outing I've ever had at any level." He'll look to turn things around at Miller Park against the Astros, a team Bush has had more wins against than any other team in his career. In 13 appearances -- 11 starts -- Bush is 6-1 with a 3.46 ERA against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Myers beat the Tampa Bay Rays in his previous start Friday, allowing six hits and one run and striking out seven batters in seven innings. He's pitched at least six innings in all nine of his starts this year, combining with Roy Oswalt to become the first Astros teammates to achieve that feat since Mike Hampton and the late Jose Lima in 1998. Myers has pitched well against the Brewers in his career, going 4-1 with a 1.77 ERA in eight games (four starts). His previous start against them came in 2008 for Philadelphia, and he threw a two-hit complete game.  He's 1-1 with a 2.84 ERA in two games (one start) at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough first inning in which he allowed four runs after recording just two outs, Gallardo did not allow a run while surrendering just two hits over his last five innings at Target Field. For the third straight start, however, Gallardo settled for a no-decision, as the Brewers offense was quiet until the ninth in the club's 12-inning loss to the Twins. The outing also broke a streak of five straight quality starts for Gallardo. He'll look to get back on track Friday against the New York Mets, as he hopes to record his first win since May 7th in Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Santana continues to pitch deep into games for the Mets. The lefty went 7 2/3 innings in a 6-4 win against the Yankees on Sunday, marking the fourth consecutive start he has gone at least seven innings. He has also allowed only three earned runs in his last three outings combined. All of Santana's wins have come at home this season, and he will be looking to register his first road win in Milwaukee. In four starts away from Citi Field, his road ERA (4.38) is more than a full run higher than his home ERA (3.19).

home_pitcher_note: Though he hasn't started a game since his first start of the season on May 18 in Cincinnati, Parra picked up his first win of the season in the series finale against the Twins as the Brewers avoided the sweep. Parra also picked up a loss the night before, as he was called on to pitch in the 11th inning with the Brewers out of other options. He was scratched from his scheduled start the next day as a result but came on to pitch the fourth and the fifth, in which he did not allow a run, yielding three hits while striking out two and walking a pair.
away_pitcher_note: With the Mets needing a spot start before Jonathon Niese or John Maine is healthy enough to return to the rotation, manager Jerry Manuel said that Nieve, who made seven starts for the Mets last season, is the leading candidate to get the nod Saturday against the Brewers. Nieve has made 18 starts in his career with the Mets and Astros, going 5-6 with 4.11 ERA. Nieve worked a hitless ninth inning in Wednesday's night game to keep him sharp for his start.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf wasn't happy in his two starts before Tuesday's win over the Astros, calling his May 14 loss to the Phillies "embarrassing," and saying after his May 19 outing in Pittsburgh, "I'm concerned that I stink." His performance against the struggling Astros, though, left him smiling. Wolf allowed no runs on four hits in seven strong innings for his first win at Miller Park since his April 6 Brewers debut. He snapped a streak of 20 straight games that a Brewers starter pitched fewer than seven innings, since Yovani Gallardo went seven in a 2-1 win at San Diego on May 1. "We need to do that more," Wolf said.
away_pitcher_note: Dickey worked his way through two bases-loaded jams in the first three innings and a line drive to his left elbow to earn the victory in his last start against the Phillies. The knuckleballer blanked Philadelphia in six innings Tuesday before eventually coming out of the game when his left elbow started swelling. Dickey has been cleared to play medically and is expected to get the start Sunday in Milwaukee. He attributes his recent success to trusting his knuckleball more as he has felt more comfortable throwing it from behind in the count. This has allowed his fastball to become more of a weapon, surprising hitters who are getting approximately 80 percent knuckleballs.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson logged a season-high 107 pitches in his previous start, a no-decision against the Braves. The veteran left-hander exited with a 2-1 lead after six innings, allowing an unearned run. He struck out five. His previous season-high pitch count was 105, turned in twice before.
away_pitcher_note: Last time out, Narveson simply didn't have good command of his pitches. Not one of them. His counterpart on the night, Astros ace Roy Oswalt, was dominant. Together, those two things gave Narveson his second loss of the season. Narveson allowed four runs over four innings on eight hits while striking out just two batters. In his last three starts, Narveson has a 1-2 record after winning each of his first two. Both losses have come at home, while all of Narveson's wins have been on the road. As the Brewers travel to Florida for a four-game set, Narveson will make his first career start against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Rain cut short Nolasco's last outing. The right-hander was taking the mound for the fifth before play was halted against the Braves. So his line was four innings, and he was tagged for three runs on eight hits. He threw 64 pitches, and was tagged with a loss. Nolasco has dropped two straight starts, allowing 11 runs in 9 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: While not great by any means, Bush's last start, against the Astros, was a drastic improvement from his previous outing against the Twins, in which Bush lasted just one-third of an inning and gave up seven runs on six hits at Target Field. After waiting a long six days to pitch again, Bush lasted five innings while giving up two unearned runs on four hits. Bush did not factor in the decision, but kept the Brewers close enough to pull out the come-from-behind win over the Astros for their first home series win since taking two of three from the Rockies to open the season. In five career starts against the Marlins, the Brewers right-hander is 2-3 with a 5.70 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Bottom line is Volstad has dropped four straight decisions. The untold line is the 23-year-old has been deserving of a better fate. Volstad comes off a tough defeat at the hands of the Phillies, giving up three runs in 6 1/3 innings. He entered the seventh inning in a 2-2 game, and exited with two runners on. One of them scored. In his four-game losing streak, he has given up 12 earned runs in 23 1/3 innings. In all four games, he kept his team right in it.
away_pitcher_note: Tossing his first career shutout, Gallardo pitched as well as he has all season and as well as manager Ken Macha has ever seen in his last outing. Gallardo scattered eight hits over his nine innings and did not walk a batter until the second-to-last one he faced. It was the Brewers' first shutout since 2008 and the club's first complete game since April '09. In his career, Gallardo has faced the Marlins just once. He tossed seven scoreless innings, giving up just six hits while walking two and striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: History happened when Johnson last took the mound, but fate wasn't on his side. Johnson was impressive in seven innings against the Phillies. He allowed one unearned run. However, he had the misfortune of pitching the same day Roy Halladay tossed the 20th perfect game in MLB history. Johnson had a string of 20 straight scoreless innings snapped with an unearned run. He hasn't allowed an earned run in 25 straight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Capuano will be making his first Major League appearance since Sept. 28, 2007, after more than two years spent rehabbing a left elbow injury that required Tommy John surgery, the second of his career. Capuano replaces fellow lefty Manny Parra in Milwaukee's rotation and has a chance to put to rest a nasty streak. Since a May 17, 2007 win over the Nationals, in which Capuano worked eight scoreless innings, the Brewers are 0-22 when Capuano has pitched. He is 0-12 with a 6.08 ERA in that span, which includes 18 starts and four relief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has yet to throw fewer then six innings in a start this season and is averaging just over seven frames per game. Good news for a stretched bullpen that could use the day off and a strong start from Wainwright to reset itself. With Wainwright striking out almost one batter per inning, there should be plenty of swings and misses for Milwaukee batters, currently in the bottom ten of the Majors for K's.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf has been struggling with his command all season, and now he's struggling to get on the same page with his catcher. Rookie Jonathan Lucroy has had a difficult time picking up Wolf's complicated set of signs with runners on base, leading to a series of mound visits during the pair's two games together. Manager Ken Macha would prefer to save his slightly more experienced catcher, George Kottaras, for his less-experienced pitchers, so Wolf and Lucroy will probably stay together for at least one more turn. More concerning is Wolf's uncharacteristically high walk count; he issued 2.4 free passes per nine innings for the Dodgers last season and has walked 4.5 batters per nine innings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Missing Kyle Lohse and Brad Penny from the rotation, the Cardinals need another starter to step up and help carry the load after Chris Carpenter, Adam Wainwright and Jaime Garcia. With rookie P.J. Walters scuffling to the tune of seven earned runs on Tuesday night, the burden falls on Ottavino to help spare the bullpen from covering five innings at a time. Walking six batters in his only start of the season, Ottavino must nail down his location against a tough Brewers offense.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson was humming along through five scoreless innings against the Marlins on Memorial Day, with eight strikeouts and only two singles against him. But things unraveled in a hurry for the lefty, who surrendered a game-tying three-run home run to Cody Ross amid a seven-run Florida rally, with five of those runs charged to Narveson. In the Cardinals, Narveson will be facing the team that drafted him (in 2000) and first brought him to the big leagues (in 2006). He's already made seven appearances against them for the Brewers, including two starts, and has a 2.25 ERA in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia's remarkable start to the season came with one major caveat: how would he handle facing a team that has seen his stuff before? Garcia passed the first part of the challenge, limiting Cincinnati hitters in his second go-round with the Reds despite lacking his "A" game. Ranking No. 2 in the Majors in runs scored, Milwaukee's righty-dominated lineup will prove a sizeable test for Garcia's ability to adjust to hitters who are already making adjustments to him.
away_pitcher_note: Parra gets the nod over a surprised Dave Bush, who expressed some confusion after being informed this week that his turn was being skipped. The Brewers would like a look at Parra and it makes some sense to feature him against the Cardinals, who as of Thursday were batting .243 with a .674 OPS against left-handed pitchers and .272 with a .782 OPS against righties. Bush is 2-6 with a 6.45 ERA in nine career starts against St. Louis including 0-3 with a 10.57 ERA at Busch Stadium. Compare that to Parra, who is 2-1 with a 2.97 ERA in 12 games, including 10 starts, against the Cardinals and is 2-0 with a 2.86 ERA in five starts at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo is the only Brewers starter on a roll, going 6-0 with a 1.86 ERA in his past 10 starts after going 0-2 with a 6.75 ERA in his first two. In his last outing against the Marlins, he allowed one earned run and four hits in seven strong innings and hit a game-tying two-run home run to help the Brewers to a win. "I've been feeling good the whole year," Gallardo said. "The first few starts, I struggled a little bit with a lot of walks and command overall. That's something I still have to work on -- work on it every bullpen [session] and apply it to the following start."
away_pitcher_note: Lilly has fared slightly better on the road, posting a 3.08 ERA in four starts compared to a 4.15 ERA in four at Wrigley Field. In his last start on June 1 against the Pirates, he gave up three runs on six hits over 7 2/3 innings and lost, 3-2. Lilly was cruising and then served up a game-winning home run to Neil Walker in the eighth. The Cubs decided to push him back and miss the makeup game vs. the Pirates because Lilly is 0-2 in three starts against them.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers gave Wolf a choice: Start Wednesday on regular rest, or take an extra day, something all Brewers starters have been doing when the team encounters a day off. Wolf opted against the extra rest, thinking he would be more sharp on a set schedule, so he'll pitch Game 2 of a series between the Brewers and Cubs. Wolf's command has not been good of late; he averaged 1.7 walks per start last season but has walked at least four batters in three of his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Miller Park is one of Zambrano's favorite venues. The right-hander threw his no-hitter there in September 2008. This will be his second start since returning to the rotation. In his first, Big Z gave up three runs on six hits over 4 1/3 innings and took the loss against the Astros. He threw 84 pitches and the stadium radar gun showed his fastball was at 90-91 mph.

home_pitcher_note: Bush was bumped from the rotation so lefty Manny Parra could start Sunday against the Cardinals and he found himself in a surprising relief spot. Bush got the call to relieve Parra with one out, the bases loaded and the Brewers clinging to a 3-2 lead in the sixth inning. He struck out pinch-hitter Skip Schumaker in a 12-pitch marathon, helping avoid a big Cardinals blow-up in a game the Brewers eventually won, 4-3, in 10 innings. Now he's headed back to the starting rotation. "I was going to throw a bullpen session after the game anyway, probably 20-30 pitches," Bush said. "So [the relief work] ended up being just about the same thing with warming up and that long at-bat."
away_pitcher_note: Dempster finally got some run support in his last start against the Astros as the Cubs scored eight runs. He struck out seven for the eighth time in 12 starts and notched his eighth quality start, giving up three runs on six hits over 6 1/3 innings. Dempster did give up two home runs, and now has served up 12 in 12 games. On the plus side, they were solo shots and he avoided any big innings.

home_pitcher_note: If you take away his first inning on Saturday in St. Louis, Narveson pitched pretty well. But the Cardinals' four-run rally, which included a two-run home run by Albert Pujols on an 0-and-2 pitch, hurt, and the Brewers lost the game in 11 innings, 5-4. Narveson has surrendered at least four earned runs in four of his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Rays, Harden took his second loss of the season, giving up four runs on five hits in five innings. The Rangers offense gave Harden four runs but failed to get a win, as Harden fell to 41-1 in his career when receiving at least four runs of support. Opponents hitting in the No. 9 hole are hitting .476 (10-for-21) against Harden this season. In five career starts against the Brewers, Harden is 1-2 with a 4.70 ERA. However, two of those starts came at Miller Park, where Harden is 1-0 with a 1.30 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Parra made some strikeout history in his last start against the Cardinals but needed a bailout from the bullpen. First, the good: Parra became the 50th pitcher in Major League history to strike out four batters in an inning after Cards catcher Yadier Molina reached base on a wild pitch in the fourth. Parra also struck out the side in the third inning, making him the first pitcher since 2003 to whiff seven batters in the span of two innings. The bad: After Albert Pujols led off the sixth inning with a homer, Parra recorded an out but then walked three straight batters. He needed relief help to escape with the lead.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Mariners, Feldman gave up four runs on nine hits with four strikeouts in 5 2/3 innings. Feldman has now surrendered four home runs over his last three starts. In his last seven outings, Feldman has a 2-4 record with a 6.45 ERA. This will be his first career start against the Brewers. In seven starts in Interleague Play, Feldman is 1-4 with a 5.71 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo settled for a no-decision against the Cubs on Tuesday after a valiant effort. He worked seven shutout innings, allowing four Cubs hits with two walks and seven strikeouts, and has now allowed two or fewer earned runs in 11 consecutive starts. Since beginning the season 0-2 with a 6.75 ERA in his first two starts, Gallardo is 6-0 with a 1.67 ERA in his last 11.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis pitched seven innings while giving up one run on four hits with five strikeouts in a 7-1 win over the Mariners on Tuesday. It was his third quality start in his past four outings and game him seven for the season, tying him for the team lead with C.J. Wilson. Opponents are batting .154 off him with runners in scoring position. Lewis is 1-4 with a 3.95 ERA in seven starts on the road. This will be his first career start against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Having shut down the Athletics for the second time this season, Saunders now turns his attention to the puzzle that is Angel Stadium. Facing the Brewers for the first time in his career, he'll try to get well at home, where he's an unsightly 1-5 in seven starts with a 6.34 ERA. That one win was a May 14 shutout of the A's, who scored in the ninth inning on Wednesday night to avoid getting blanked again by Saunders, who yielded seven hits and one walk while striking out two men. Eleven of his outs came on ground balls as Saunders won his fourth decision in the past five.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf lasted just 4 2/3 innings in his last outing, when he surrendered eight runs on nine hits -- five of which were home runs -- and two walks. The lefty had one clean inning, the third, and also drove in a pair of runs with a double in the bottom of the fourth. As the Brewers head west to take on the Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim, Wolf will look for his first win since May 25, when he tossed seven scoreless innings while giving up just four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Santana, the most durable of the Angels' starters this season, lasted a season-low five innings in a loss at Oakland on Thursday. He yielded five runs, four earned, on seven hits and two walks, striking out three men. His command was nothing close to what it had been while he was winning five consecutive decisions coming into the start. Facing the Brewers for the first time, Santana has done most of his best work this season on the road. He's 4-3, 3.04 in eight road tests.
away_pitcher_note: After being bumped from his previously scheduled start, Bush gave the Brewers just enough in his last outing to keep them in the ballgame late. Bush went six innings, giving up four runs on six hits while walking three and striking out five. Next up for the Brewers right-hander is a club he's had moderate success against in just two starts but hasn't faced since he was with the Blue Jays in 2004-05. In his last start against the Angels, though, Bush went 8 1/3 innings, giving up just one run on five hits while walking two -- both intentional -- and striking out four batters. Bush, who has lost his last five decisions, is looking for his first win since April 20 at Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro went the distance for the third time this season and 14th time in his career in turning away the Dodgers on one run, a solo homer by James Loney, at Dodger Stadium on Friday night. Pineiro allowed only five hits and one walk, striking out seven. He found a groove after frustrating the Dodgers in the first inning when they left Rafael Furcal stranded after his leadoff triple. Pineiro is 3-0 in six career starts against the Brewers with a 3.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: After finally getting through the first inning cleanly -- striking out the side, in fact -- Narveson had his best outing of the season on Friday against the Rangers, allowing just two runs on six hits in seven strong innings, which marked a career-high. In 2 1/3 innings against Colorado during the season-opening series at Miller Park, Narveson allowed one run on five hits while walking one batter. In his only career start against the Rockies, Narveson went five innings allowing three runs on five hits on Sept. 29, 2009 at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel was excellent for the third straight time in his outing on Saturday against the Blue Jays, striking out six batters in eight innings and allowing just three hits for a 1-0 win. In his last two starts, he's pitched shutout ball in 15 1/3 innings of work. Hammel has not allowed more than two runs in an appearance since May 21 and is 4-1 in six starts since returning from the disabled list on May 15.
away_pitcher_note: According to manager Ken Macha, the Brewers "pitched well enough to win" on Saturday night against the Rangers, and among those pitching was Parra. The lefty tossed six strong innings, giving up three runs, which earned him his first quality start of the season. Parra took the loss, however, despite striking out eight batters, which would have been a career high if he hadn't just recorded 10 strikeouts in his previous start in St. Louis. After giving up five runs in 11 1/3 innings over his previous two starts, Parra seems to be coming around for the Brewers and establishing himself as a legitimate option within the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Francis threw his fourth straight quality start on Sunday against the Blue Jays to help the Rockies complete a three-game sweep. It was his second win of the season, as he allowed two earned runs in seven complete innings. In five career starts against the Brewers, Francis is 2-3 with a 7.76 ERA
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo struck out 10 batters against his hometown Rangers last weekend, but his string of quality starts ended at three. He allowed four runs on six hits and four walks in six innings and saw his ERA bump up a bit to a still-respectable 2.66. He has a 2.01 ERA in his last 12 starts. Gallardo matched up against Ubaldo Jimenez and the Rockies on Opening Day and took the loss after allowing four runs, three earned, on seven hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Here's a statement that, even with the humidor making Coors Field play bigger than ever, it's hard to imagine saying: Cook returns to the safety of Coors Field. He is 2-0 with a 2.62 ERA there, as opposed to 0-4, 7.38 on the road. Why? Maybe that question could be tackled before his following start, which will be at Anaheim. For now, why not enjoy his work at Coors?
away_pitcher_note: Wolf had a long chat with pitching coach Rick Peterson in the days leading up to his last start and it apparently paid off. Wolf, who tied his troubles to mindset rather than mechanics, tossed seven strong innings and didn't allow any Angels hits outside of a trio of consecutive hits in a two-run second inning. Wolf composed himself and retired Erick Aybar to end the threat and went on to finish an outing that helped ease the pain of a loss to the Cubs five days earlier in which he surrendered five home runs. Wolf beat the Rockies on April 6 in his Brewers debut but wasn't thrilled with the outing after allowing four runs on nine hits.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson has surrendered at least four earned runs in four of his past five starts, including a poor outing against the Angels on Wednesday in which he allowed four runs and a pair of homers in his first pass through the batting order. But presented with the premise that Narveson was struggling, manager Ken Macha dug deeper into the numbers. Narveson's win over the Rangers on June 11 was a good one. In his previous start, June 5 against the Cardinals, he surrendered four runs in the first inning but followed with five shutout innings after that. On May 31 against the Marlins, Macha wanted to pull Narveson after five innings in the South Florida sunshine on Memorial Day, but he was short in the bullpen because of Todd Coffey's thumb injury. The Marlins scored seven times in the sixth inning to erase a 4-0 Brewers lead, and five of the runs were charged to Narveson. So you have to go back to May 26 to find a truly poor outing. "He's been all right," Macha said. "He has to avoid the homers and the big innings."
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing against the Rockies, Baker put up one of the best performances of his career. He tallied a career-best 12 strikeouts, marking only the second time in his career with 10 or more strikeouts. The first time came in a 2009 game against Cleveland. Baker didn't give up a run through the seven innings he pitched and allowed only two hits and one walk in that outing.

home_pitcher_note: Parra limited the Rockies to two runs in six innings on Friday, and didn't walk a batter for only the fourth time in 63 career starts. The last time he made a walk-free start was Aug. 27, 2008. It continued a string of solid performances for the left-hander, who has allowed three or fewer runs in all five of his starts since a move from the Brewers bullpen. He has 23 strikeouts in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: In a great pitching matchup against Colorado's Ubaldo Jimenez, Liriano struggled in the first inning of what could have been a duel. He gave up three runs on four hits in that inning as well as hit two batters and give up a walk. He had only hit one batter prior to that start. However, he settled down after that and gave up only one more hit and two walks in the last six innings of his outing. He had six strikeouts. He has 93 total strikeouts in his 13 starts and has walked 24 batters this season.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo notched nine strikeouts and limited the Rockies to one run on four hits in six innings on Saturday, but his seventh win slipped away from reliever Carlos Villanueva along with a 4-1 lead. Gallardo has 19 strikeouts in his last two starts, but no wins to show for them. Before his loss to the Rangers on June 13, he had won six straight decisions, but took a no-decision against the Twins on May 22 after allowing four runs on six hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Like Nick Blackburn, Slowey has been going through a tough stretch in his last two outings. Against the Phillies, Slowey allowed seven runs on seven hits in just 1 2/3 innings. Over his past two starts, Slowey has given up 12 earned runs in 6 1/3 innings, raising his ERA from 3.45 to 4.58 over that stretch. Pitching deep into contests has been an issue for Slowey this season -- he's been unable to complete six innings in 10 of his 14 starts this year. Slowey will try to see if he can last later into a ballgame when he faces the Mets at Citi Field on Friday. It will mark his first career start against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Bush will have gone nine days without a start when he takes the mound against the Mariners. Manager Ken Macha shuffled the rotation at a time the Mariners were batting just .235 against right-handed pitchers and billed the move as a bonus for Bush. But the pitcher, who pitched 7 1/3 scoreless innings in Anaheim on June 15, had a different view, saying, "I'd rather stay on a regular schedule. I feel like the way I threw the ball last time, I earned the right to go back out there."
away_pitcher_note: Hyphen got the outing he'd been looking for all year against the Reds on Sunday, earning his first win and throwing six shutout innings. Rowland-Smith hasn't had the kind of season he'd hoped for and is likely the odd starter out when Erik Bedard returns from the disabled list, but a few more good performances could at least make that decision tougher for manager Don Wakamatsu.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf has bounced back nicely since surrendering a career-high five home runs in a June 9 loss to the Cubs at Miller Park. On the Brewers' recent road trip, he tossed a pair of quality starts, combining to limit the Angels and Rockies to three runs on six hits in 14 innings. Wolf only allowed one run in seven innings in Colorado, and it came when Rox right fielder Brad Hawpe hit just enough of a slider to send it the opposite way to the left-field seats. Wolf has faced the Mariners only twice in his career and lost both games.
away_pitcher_note: Fister is scheduled to make his first start after going on the disabled list with shoulder fatigue on June 1. His biggest value (despite his 2.45 ERA) has been his ability to get deep into games, but that likely won't be the case Saturday. He'll be on a pitch count of about 85, which could keep him shy of his average of just under seven innings per start.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson got the nod for his last start when right-hander Dave Bush was pushed back due to poor career numbers against the Twins, including a career-worst outing at Target Field earlier this season in which Bush was unable to get out of the first inning. Through six batters, Narveson was doing his best Bush impression. The rest of the way, he got 15 outs while facing just 16 batters. First-inning struggles have been common for Narveson, whose first-inning ERA jumped to 12.27 for the season after allowing three in the first on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas has taken tips from Seattle ace Cliff Lee to improve his approach on the mound, and it's clearly paying off. He notched his fifth quality start in a row with seven shutout innings against the Cubs on Tuesday, dropping his ERA to 2.66. He's walked a total of three batters in his last four starts while striking out 20, and he hasn't taken a loss since May 4.

home_pitcher_note: Despite four wild pitches, Parra effectively limited the Twins offense in his last start, giving up just two runs in 5 2/3 innings pitched, as the Brewers took the 5-3 victory over the Twins. Parra tied a club record with four wild pitches in a game, set by Ed Sprague on May 14, 1975, against the Rangers. But as catcher Jonathan Lucroy was quick to point out, Parra only allowed two runners to score following a wild pitch -- first baseman Justin Morneau and third baseman Michael Cuddyer in the fourth -- and stranded runners in scoring position in the second, fourth and sixth innings after he made those wild pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Norris will make his first start since May 23 for the Astros. He has been on the disabled list with bicep tendinitis and completed his final rehab start with Triple-A Round Rock on Tuesday. Norris had a 3.06 ERA with the Express over three starts. He will look for his first win since May 13.

home_pitcher_note: Through 5 1/3 innings on Thursday, Yovani Gallardo was perfect. After nine innings, the Brewers' ace had turned in the best pitching performance of his career. Over his past six starts, Gallardo has allowed six earned runs on 29 hits in 44 innings for a 1.23 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Myers became the first Astros pitcher to throw six or more innings in each of his first 15 starts of a season. Against the Giants he threw seven innings and gave up three runs, only one of which was earned. He also helped his cause with two hits and an RBI.

home_pitcher_note: For Bush, who was pitching on nine days' rest instead of his usual four, the key last time out was overcoming some early struggles that could be attributed to the long layoff. Once he had the lead, Bush faced just 10 batters over the final three innings of his outing.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez earned his first win since June 2 against the Giants. He pitched six innings and gave up two runs, none of which were earned. Rodriguez also gave up just two hits and had one walk in the Astros' 7-5 win. He has not faced the Brewers this season.

home_pitcher_note: Hawksworth wowed the Redbirds with an outstanding start on Saturday in a game that was considered more a "bullpen start" than a proper start by Hawksworth. He was good enough to pitch himself into another start, and this time the expectations will be higher.
away_pitcher_note: Last time out, the Brewers looked to veteran lefty Randy Wolf to help guide them to a sixth consecutive win. Unfortunately for Wolf and the Brewers, the lefty fell victim to the home run ball, giving up two, including the eventual game-winner in the 5-4 loss to Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off his rockiest start of the year, Garcia will be looking to regain his command. Last time out, he simply couldn't locate, and he didn't get a single swing-and-miss. If he gets ahead in counts against Milwaukee, the swings-and-misses should follow.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson simulated the first two batters he would face in the bullpen before his last start to shake the struggles that accounted for a 12.27 first-frame ERA this season. He responded by going out and turning in a career-best performance for his seventh win of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter's command may not be quite as pinpoint as it was a year ago. His velocity is down a tick from a year ago. But he simply doesn't lose. Over the last 12 months, a span of 34 starts, Carpenter is 21-2 with a 2.41 ERA. The Cardinals are 26-8 in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Parra said he hoped to go seven innings and give the team a chance to win every time out, but he came up short of a quality start again in his last start, by one inning and one run. He took a no-decision, however, as the bullpen had its worst performance in nearly a month.

home_pitcher_note: As expected, Wainwright's Toronto slipup was a one-time deal. He remains one of the best and most consistent pitchers in baseball, not to mention dominant at home. Even against a familiar foe, his stuff, command and home-field advantage should add up to another fine game.
away_pitcher_note: After a shutout five days earlier, Gallardo did not have his best stuff last time out, allowing four runs on seven hits over six innings with two walks and five strikeouts. It was just the fourth time in 17 starts in 2010 that Gallardo has given up four or more earned runs.

Sanchez saw his personal three-game winning streak snap in his last start against the Dodgers, when he allowed five runs -- four earned -- in five innings. Sanchez is 0-1 with a 8.31 ERA in eight career appearances (four starts) against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf was in control Thursday against the Cardinals, giving up just one walk and scattering four hits over 6 1/3 innings. His command was excellent, as he threw a first-pitch strike to the first 11 batters he faced while mixing in his curveball effectively.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has worked seven innings in each of his two starts since being recalled from Triple-A. Both times, the rookie has fallen prey to the long ball during the early innings before settling down.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson stumbled out of the gates in St. Louis, giving up four hits and two runs in the first to put his club immediately behind the eight-ball, a familiar theme for Narveson. The lefty has allowed 17 runs and 32 baserunners in opening frames in just 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum has lost his last two starts after winning three in a row. However, he managed to maintain his velocity in his most recent outing at Colorado, and he did so in 87-degree heat -- the sort of weather that often has drained his energy.

home_pitcher_note: Spotted an eight-run lead after four innings and an 11-run lead after the fifth, Parra was unable to take advantage, laboring through 5 2/3 innings and giving up five earned runs. He threw deep into most counts, ringing up a pitch count of 116 in less than six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Zito has lost his last two decisions over a span of four starts. That stretch actually began with a strong outing -- a complete game in a setback on June 18. The Giants gave Zito a lead last Saturday with their stunning seven-run outburst, but Zito couldn't hold it.

home_pitcher_note: On the disabled list since May 16 due to inflammation of the lining around his heart, Davis is finally making his return. The veteran left-hander made three rehab starts. In his last one, he pitched seven innings, and allowed just one run on six hits.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates' ace suffered his second awful outing in his last three starts, getting chased in the fourth inning Saturday against the Phillies after giving up seven earned runs on 10 hits. Maholm has given up at least four earned runs in three of his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bush has put together four consecutive quality starts, including a no-decision against the Giants this week in which he allowed only one run on five hits in six innings. One of his best outings of the year came against the Pirates on April 20, when he tossed seven scoreless.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens has pitched six innings in each of his past two starts, though his last outing was not one his sharpest. He allowed more than four runs for only the second time in 10 starts this year. Fourteen of the 31 runs Karstens has allowed starting have come off homers.

home_pitcher_note: A Craig Counsell error cost Wolf a chance to win his last start against the Giants, but he had his best curveball of the year. A follow-up effort in the final game before the break could give the Brewers' big offseason pickup something to build upon in the second half.
away_pitcher_note: Lincoln never settled in comfortably his last time out, and an inability to establish his fastball command compromised his ability to be successful with his secondary pitches. Lincoln is at his best when he's aggressive and using both sides of the plate effectively.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has pitched well since returning from a two-month stint on the disabled list with a left hamstring injury. In two starts, he's allowed four runs on just eight hits over 11 combined innings, but he has shown some command issues with five walks.
away_pitcher_note: Since getting roughed up for seven runs in just one-third of an inning in Minnesota on May 21, Bush has gone 3-1 with a 3.37 ERA, with six quality starts. Bush's performance lately has been as good as it has been since suffering a triceps injury in June 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson has allowed two earned runs and recorded 14 strikeouts in the 12 1/3 frames he has completed in July. It's safe to say he has distanced himself from what was an inconsistent and sometimes miserable June. He threw eight scoreless innings vs. Milwaukee on May 1.
away_pitcher_note: Home runs and walks hurt Wolf once again against the Pirates, as the Brewers lefty gave up a pair of solo homers and walked three batters over six innings along with four runs on seven hits and five strikeouts. A late Brewers rally allowed Wolf to escape with a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson ended the season's first half with seven scoreless innings against the Mets. In his only other start vs. the Brewers this year, he allowed one run in six innings. He has allowed two runs or fewer in 14 of 18 starts and posted a 2.05 ERA in his past 14 outings.
away_pitcher_note: First-inning struggles continued for Narveson against the Giants as he surrendered three home runs before throwing his 12th pitch. Narveson, who has given up 21 first-inning runs this season, was charged with 10 runs -- nine earned -- on nine hits in 3 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe turned his season around on May 12, when he limited the Brewers to two runs in six innings.  In the 12 starts he's made dating back to that outing, he has gone 5-5 with a 3.45 ERA.  He has posted a 3.03 ERA in his past six starts and been victimized by run support.
away_pitcher_note: Last time out, lefty Manny Parra surrendered six runs (four earned) on 10 hits over five innings with two walks while recording five strikeouts. Parra has pitched well, but struggled to go deep into games this season, having pitched no more than six innings in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens will rematch with Milwaukee, who tagged him for a loss in his last outing. Back-to-back Brewers homers hurt the cause, but the real surprise was a career-high six walks for a pitcher with just 16 walks headed in.
away_pitcher_note: Capuano, who won 18 games for the Brewers in 2005, gets a spot start in place of Doug Davis, who had to go back on the DL. Coming back from Tommy John surgery, Capuano was called up from the Minors to start at Florida on June 3 and has made seven relief appearances since.

home_pitcher_note: Lincoln allowed two home runs against Milwaukee on July 11 in his last start, but kept his team in the game and left in line for a win that never came. His moment of truth came when he walked Ryan Braun and Prince Fielder to lead off the sixth, but kept runs off the board.
away_pitcher_note: Bush has six straight quality starts, but the Brewers are just 3-3 in those games because of a lack of offensive support. Bush lost, 2-1, in Atlanta on Thursday, with both of the Braves runs coming on homers. He has allowed 13 home runs this season.

home_pitcher_note: Duke's first start off the DL was a successful one, given that he showed some of the better command he's had in months. He was limited to just 78 pitches in the outing because of the month-long layoff, but Duke should be free to go as deep as he can from here on out.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf is 5-4 on the road, winning his last three decisions. Only seven of the 21 homers he's allowed have come on the road. This will be Wolf's fifth start against the Pirates. He's 1-1 at Pittsburgh and has two no-decisions at home.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf's last start was entirely forgettable as he lasted a career-low 1 1/3 innings. Other than an easy 15-pitch first, there were few positives. Ohlendorf's lost his fastball command, had suspect control and struggled to find a good tempo in the 46-pitch effort.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo, an All-Star pick, is coming off the DL after straining his left oblique against the Cardinals on July 4 and leaving in the third inning. He is 2-0 against the Pirates this season and struck out 10 over five scoreless innings at Pittsburgh on April 21.

home_pitcher_note: At the urging of manager Ken Macha, Narveson went to his off-speed stuff early and often against the Braves. The result was a nice bounce-back outing in his first start of the second half.
away_pitcher_note: Despite having one of his best outings of the season, Stammen took the loss Sunday as the Nationals fell to the Marlins, 1-0. The right-hander gave up only one run on six hits in six innings. Gabby Sanchez's RBI double in the fifth inning proved to be the difference.

home_pitcher_note: The struggling Parra will retain his spot in the rotation for now, but pitching coach Rick Peterson and manager Ken Macha could call some pitches from the bench. Parra has a 9.86 ERA and a .385 opponents' batting average in his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Martin will look to bounce back after a poor showing last Monday against the Reds. In the Nationals' 7-2 loss, he allowed six runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings. In two career starts against the Brewers, Martin is 0-2 with a 6.39 ERA.  He is 1-2 in his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bush was touched for 10 runs in the first inning on Tuesday, though only two of them were earned because of three Brewers errors. The outing conjured memories of Bush's May 21 in Minnesota, where he allowed seven runs while recording only one out.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler makes his season debut against the Brewers. He underwent surgery to repair a labral tear in his right hip last February. Detwiler is a combined 2-2 with a 2.27 ERA for Class-A Potomac and Double-A Harrisburg in eight rehab starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf is coming off a loss to the Bucs in which he set dubious career highs in runs allowed (12) and hits (13). Under normal circumstances, Wolf would have been long gone before the Pirates reached double digits, but he offered to stay in to help preserve a depleted 'pen.
away_pitcher_note: After winning five of six starts, Arroyo ran into trouble Wednesday opposite Washington's Stephen Strasburg, giving up seven runs in 5 2/3 innings. It was the third time this season Arroyo had given up seven or more runs in a game.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo returned from the disabled list on Thursday and looked extremely sharp in his first start since July 4. He's coming back from a left oblique injury, an ailment that often lingers, but managed to spend only two days more than the minimum on the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez's second start of the season wasn't nearly as successful as his 2010 debut. He got off to a bad start and had control problems almost immediately. As a result, Volquez's pitch count rose and he lasted just 2 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After struggling through the second, Narveson gave up runs in the third and fourth innings before retiring the final nine batters he faced in the fourth, fifth and sixth on Friday against the Nationals, giving the Brewers a chance for the comeback victory.
away_pitcher_note: The winless Wood felt like he had to grind through his start on Friday at Houston, as he allowed four runs and nine hits over six innings. He had allowed 12 hits over his first four big league starts.

home_pitcher_note: Happ was acquired by the Astros on Thursday in the deal that sent ace Roy Oswalt to the Phillies. The left-hander was limited to three starts this season due to injury.
away_pitcher_note: With Jonathan Lucroy back behind the plate in place of George Kottaras on Saturday, Parra had his best start of the season, allowing just two runs on four hits and three walks over six innings for his third quality start of the season and first since June 18 in Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had another quality start last Sunday against the Reds, giving up no runs in a win. He's gone 5-1 with a 2.30 ERA over his past six starts after starting the season 3-10 with a 6.09 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a rough outing against the Pirates, in which he surrendered 10 first-inning runs, Bush tossed six-plus strong innings Sunday against the Nationals, giving up just two earned runs on six hits. Bush recorded seven strikeouts vs. zero walks.

home_pitcher_note: Wright said he improved from his first career start to his second on Monday against the Cubs. He gave up four runs over his first three innings, but settled down to toss two scoreless frames before he exited.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf recovered from one of the worst starts of his career -- a 12-run stinker at Pittsburgh on July 21 -- with a gem against the Reds thanks in part to good curveball command. He pitched seven shutout innings against Houston on May 25.

home_pitcher_note: Wells did not pitch poorly in his last start vs. the Astros, but did fall behind hitters and also walked a season-high five over 5 2/3 innings. He needs to get re-focused.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers timed Gallardo's return from the DL so he would appear in this series, but he's coming off a bad start against the Reds in which he allowed five earned runs in 2 2/3 innings, matching the shortest start of his career.

home_pitcher_note: This would have been Ted Lilly's spot, but instead the Cubs will call up Diamond from Triple-A Iowa. He was 5-4 with a 3.16 ERA in 21 starts for the Minor League team. This will be his Major League debut.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson took a 2-0 lead into the sixth inning of his last start but didn't retire any of the three batters he faced in a Reds rally that denied the left-hander his ninth win. The Brewers are 8-9 in his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster walked five in four-plus innings in his last start, his shortest outing of the season. He started well, then admitted he lost his "aggressiveness."
away_pitcher_note: Parra has met the definition of quality start -- six or more innings, three or fewer earned runs -- in only one of his past six outings. He is 0-1 with a 5.84 ERA in two starts and two relief appearances against Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: Bush's roller-coaster ride continued in Houston last week when he allowed two runs in the first inning, three more in the second and allowed six runs on 10 hits in all during a five-inning stint. The 10 hits matched his season high.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez improved to 6-1 in his last seven starts by throwing eight scoreless innings vs. the Brewers. He had nine strikeouts to just one walk. Rodriguez hasn't allowed a run in his last 14 innings and will go for his 10th win of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Though he could have been pushed back to Tuesday with the off-day this week, Wolf is expected to make his start Saturday, just five days after taking a sharp line drive by Hunter Pence off his left wrist. Wolf said Wednesday he was, "Ready to go."
away_pitcher_note: Myers stretched his streak of throwing six or more innings to 22 starts Monday vs. the Cardinals. He didn't factor in the decision in a 9-4 win. Myers gave up two earned runs on just three hits against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo matched his career high with 12 strikeouts in his last start and might have worked more than his six innings and 95 pitches had the Brewers not owned a 13-1 lead. He's 6-2 with a 2.72 ERA in eight career starts against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Wright is coming off his best start to date in win over the Brewers, giving up just two runs over a season-high seven innings. Wright has improved each start since being converted from a long reliever and is hoping for similar results.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson has been so-so on the mound this season but he's been excellent at the plate, including his start at Wrigley Field on Tuesday in which Narveson's RBI single loomed large in a 4-3 win. He's batting .313 on the year with four RBIs.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy has not been sharp in his last three starts, going 1-2 with a 7.02 ERA over that span. In his last start against the Nationals, Kennedy allowed four runs on eight hits in just four innings as the club continues to try to limit his innings.

home_pitcher_note: Through five innings on Wednesday, he outdueled Ryan Dempster, but a big sixth inning did Parra in as he gave up five runs in the frame and six overall in the Brewers' 15-3 loss. Parra is 1-0 with a 0.86 ERA in three career starts against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Enright has pitched very well since being called up from Triple-A Reno. In six starts, he has yet to allow more than three runs in a game or last less than five innings. Last time out he beat the Nats, allowing two runs on six hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bush missed the Brewers' series in Arizona earlier this season, but he's 5-1 lifetime against the D-backs with a 3.65 ERA in seven starts. He has 6.5 strikeouts for every walk against Arizona hitters, by far his best ratio against National League teams.

Blackburn, who entered with a 2.35 ERA over 10 previous starts, allowed eight runs (seven
