away_pitcher_note: Halladay was not his usual dominant self in his last start, allowing three runs (two earned) on nine hits over six innings. The ace right-hander took a no-decision against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf won his rematch with Jake Westbrook and the Cardinals by allowing only one run and four hits in eight innings. He has won six of his last seven decisions after losing the four before.
away_pitcher_note: Lee is making a serious run at the NL Cy Young Award. He is coming off his sixth shutout, a game in which he recorded his 200th season strikeout for the first time in his career. He last allowed a run in the second inning of his Aug. 17 start.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo is finished with the Cardinals for 2011, and good riddance. He had allowed 11 earned runs in eight starts before allowing 11 more in back-to-back losses to St. Louis in the span of six days.
away_pitcher_note: Worley continued to make his case for NL Rookie of the Year honors, allowing two earned runs over six innings against the Braves on Tuesday. The Phils have won the past 14 games he has started, one shy of the club mark set in 1972 by Steve Carlton.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke was outdueled by Chris Carpenter last week in St. Louis, marking only the seventh time in 24 games that the Brewers lost a Greinke start. He has a 2.96 ERA in 12 home starts vs. 5.04 in 12 starts on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers has struggled as he tries to audition for a spot in next season's rotation. He surrendered six runs on eight hits and five walks over 5 1/3 innings in a loss to the D-backs on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum is the rare Brewer who does better on the road than at Miller Park, where his ERA is nearly two runs higher (4.15). The Brewers have lost three of Marcum's four Miller Park starts since the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood hit his third career home run against the D-backs on Wednesday, but he also took the loss after surrendering four runs on 10 hits over 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Rockies on Saturday, Arroyo departed without recording an out in the second inning. He gave up three home runs, putting his season total at a franchise record-tying 40 homers surrendered.
away_pitcher_note: The curveball is key to Wolf's success, and he never felt comfortable with it in his last start against the Phillies, despite allowing only two runs in seven innings. He's 10-4 with a 3.40 ERA in 22 starts against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start in the big leagues since early July, Volquez made it through five innings and allowed two runs, four hits and four walks. He is trying to finish the 2011 season on a high note as he tries to build some sort of momentum for 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo owns a 5.76 ERA in 10 career starts against the Reds and has allowed eight earned runs on 17 hits in 11 innings over two starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Maloney, who was stepping in for the injured Johnny Cueto, got moved up a day to start for the injured Dontrelle Willis. His only action since his Sept. 1 recall was in relief on Sept. 10. He went two innings, allowing two runs (one earned).
away_pitcher_note: Brewers ace Zack Greinke lasted just five innings on Tuesday, but fanned nine Rockies hitters on five hits and two walks while holding Colorado to just one earned run in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Coleman had an abbreviated outing in his last start. He was pulled after giving up six runs over 3 2/3 innings against the Reds. He's winless in his last six starts and has a 6.82 ERA in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson was skipped in the rotation due to two off-days this past week. He pitched two scoreless innings in relief on Wednesday. His last start was Sept. 8, when he allowed six earned runs in 5 2/3 innings against Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Wells is 5-0 in his last nine starts, but did not get a decision in his last outing against the Reds. He failed to finish the fifth inning, and blamed himself for "nibbling" too much pitch-wise. He's 0-1 in two starts vs. the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Brewers right-hander Shaun Marcum dropped a decision to the Rockies on Wednesday after being tagged for six runs (five earned) on eight hits and one walk. He struck out four over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Garza is 4-2 with a 2.54 ERA in his last nine starts after a no decision in his last outing against the Astros. He likely has two more starts this season. "I want to finish strong, finish healthy and finish on a good note," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf pitched seven strong innings on Friday for his 13th victory, allowing three earned runs and seven hits while striking out seven with no walks. He threw 101 pitches, 71 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo is getting hot at a good time. He matched his career high with 12 strikeouts in a Sept. 11 win over the Phillies and set a new mark with 13 strikeouts against the Reds last weekend.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad had one of his finest performances in a while. The right-hander still hasn't won since July 10, but he allowed one run in seven innings in a no-decision in Washington. He lost to the Brewers on June 4, giving up three runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke has a 1.93 ERA over his last five starts and has been excellent at Miller Park, where he is 10-0 with a 2.89 ERA. The Brewers have won all 13 of his Miller Park starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season, the 23-year-old right-hander received a no-decision after allowing one run on six hits in six innings against the Phillies in Game 2 of a doubleheader. Sanabia takes over Brad Hand's spot in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson has worked on irregular rest all month because of ill-timed off-days, and it showed in his last start against the Cubs. His changeup, usually sharp, was erratic, and Narveson needed 75 pitches for only four innings.
away_pitcher_note: In consecutive starts against Atlanta, Nolasco has cruised until four-run seventh innings. He received a no-decision in his previous outing after going 6 2/3 innings and allowing five runs  (four earned). He has a 6.00 ERA in one start vs. Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Bouncing back from poor starts in his previous two outings, Marcum tossed eight solid innings in Chicago, allowing just one run on five hits in the Brewers' 5-1 victory. He'll be looking for his career-high 14th win of the season against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Morton is on track to finish strong and with no workload limit. He threw 106 pitches his last time out and snapped a six-game winless streak. Morton has already thrown more innings than ever before at the Major League level.

home_pitcher_note: In a road loss, Wolf was knocked around for six runs on 10 hits in his last start. Wolf had been 2-0 with a 2.45 ERA in his previous three September starts. He won his only previous start against the Pirates this year, going 6 2/3 scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf has one last chance to impress before the Pirates decide whether to tender him a contract. To this point, his argument has not been strong. Ohlendorf has lasted just two innings in two of his previous three starts.

home_pitcher_note: With the No. 2 seed in the NL and home field in the NLDS still up in the air, the Brewers will call upon Greinke to deliver in his 15th home start of the year. Greinke is unbeaten at Miller Park this year and the Brewers are 14-0 in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Locke gets one more chance at picking up his first Major League win before having to wait another year. He has made three big league starts and has finished five innings just once. Locke will be limited to about 75-80 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo will start his second Game 1 in three years, but the circumstances are vastly different. He was one start removed from knee surgery in 2008 when he took the mound in Philadelphia and gutted through four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy, a 21-game winner and a major part of the D-backs' success, is expected to take the ball in Game 1 in what will be his postseason debut. He went at least seven innings 20 times in 33 starts this season and allowed one run or fewer in 16.

home_pitcher_note: After coming through with a win on the final day of the regular season, Greinke will make his second consecutive start on three days' rest and likely will not go much deeper than the sixth. Greinke will be making his first career postseason start.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson will start Saturday's Game 2, something that had been assumed all along. The right-hander, who was 16-12 with a 3.49 ERA this season, was roughed up at Miller Park on July 4 as he allowed six runs (five earned) on eight hits in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter was promoted from Triple-A Reno on April 15 and stabilized the back of the rotation. His funky, over-the-top delivery was picked up throwing tomahawks in the woods as a kid. He did not allow a run in 14 innings vs. Brewers this year.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum was touched up for seven runs on 10 hits over 4 2/3 innings in his last start on Sept. 26 against the Pirates. He has excelled on the road this season, posting an 8-3 record with a 2.21 ERA. He will be making his first career postseason start.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders suffered a bruised left hand when he was jammed with a batting-practice pitch prior to the season finale. The left-hander faced the Brewers on July 20 at Chase Field and did not get a decision after allowing two runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf does not garner nearly the buzz of the Brewers' top three starters, but he led the team in innings this season. He also has postseason seasoning -- two starts for the Dodgers in 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo was stellar over eight innings in Game 1, allowing only four hits and matching Don Sutton's franchise postseason record with nine strikeouts. Six of Gallardo's whiffs came on called third strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy would like to redeem himself after an uncharacteristically poor outing in Game 1 in Milwaukee. He allowed four runs in Arizona's 4-1 loss. The big blow of the game was a two-run homer by Prince Fielder in the seventh inning.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke was poised to enter Game 5 of the NLDS in the 11th inning, but the game never got that far. That's a big bonus for the Brewers, who won all 16 of his Miller Park starts, including NLDS Game 2.
away_pitcher_note: The road is not Garcia's friend, and Milwaukee has sometimes been a tough matchup for him. But on a good day, the young left-hander can be absolutely dominant, and the Cardinals are hoping to see that Garcia on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Allowing a grand slam in Game 3 of the NLDS vs. Arizona was one of many frustrating moments for Marcum, who has posted a 7.76 ERA and allowed a .331 opponents' average in his past five starts. He has a 4.95 ERA in three starts vs. St. Louis in 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson never seems fazed by anything, a trait that should help him in the NLCS. He was hit hard in his first start against Milwaukee as a Cardinal, but bounced back with two more good games against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a defining game, Carpenter will take the ball in the first Cardinals home game of the series. His ERA was .80 better at home than on the road, and he allowed just five homers at Busch Stadium all year.
away_pitcher_note: He didn't earn the victory, but Gallardo held the D-backs to one run over six innings in a must-win Game 5 of the NLDS, helping the Brewers win a postseason series for the first time since 1982.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse will be pitching on extended rest -- 11 days -- but that hasn't been a problem for him this year. In fact, at times it's seemed to benefit him. Despite a 1-2 record, he was very effective against Milwaukee in 2011.
away_pitcher_note: After he gave up seven runs in Game 4 of the NLDS against the D-backs, the Brewers are hoping for a better performance from Wolf against the Cardinals. Wolf was 3-2 against St. Louis this season, giving up 19 runs on 32 hits over five starts.

home_pitcher_note: The going hasn't been very good for Garcia so far this month, but he's always got a better shot at home than on the road. He'll be looking to avoid the big inning, a problem that has plagued him repeatedly.
away_pitcher_note: He still hasn't lost in the postseason, but Greinke was far from dominant in the Brewers' 9-6 victory in Game 1 of the NLCS. He will need to be more effective to win on the road. In three career Busch Stadium starts, Greinke is 1-1 with a 2.35 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Though Yovani Gallardo on short rest is an option, Brewers manager Ron Roenicke has insisted that he will go with Shaun Marcum in Game 6. Marcum  has allowed 12 runs in 8 2/3 innings over two postseason starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers have seen quite a bit of Jackson, but for the most part haven't figured him out. If the NLCS goes to six, they'll get one more shot as he looks to make it 12 times out of 15 as a Cardinal that he's allowed fewer than three runs.

summary: 2012-03-04 - San Francisco Giants @ Milwaukee Brewers (Final: Tied)

venue_name: Salt River Fields at Talking Stick

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo will be the fourth Brewers pitcher to start three Opening Days, and is halfway to Ben Sheets' club-record six openers. The Cards have given Gallardo trouble; he's 1-7 with a 5.66 ERA in 11 regular season starts.
away_pitcher_note: Perhaps Garcia is poised for another big step forward as he prepares for his third full season as a big league starter. The sole lefty in the rotation, Garcia had an up-and-down spring, but he did so last year, too, and started the season strong.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke added a cutter this spring and was sensational before a stinker against the White Sox on Monday. He expressed "zero" concern that the outing would affect his season, and is poised for a big one as a free agent-to-be.
away_pitcher_note: After Tommy John surgery cancelled his 2011 season, Wainwright showed this spring that he is fully healthy. St. Louis will monitor his innings closely but that will be of little consequence early. Wainwright won 20 games in his last full season.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf is Mr. Steady for the Brewers, with 13 wins, 33-34 starts and more than 210 innings each of the past two seasons. He'll draw on a gem against the Cardinals in last year's NLCS, a win in which Wolf worked seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: After weeks of preparing to pitch in the bullpen, Lynn's role changed in mid-March when Chris Carpenter went down. Lynn adjusted to the move seamlessly, and he should have no issues with the workload given that he started in the Minors.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired from the Marlins for Carlos Zambrano, Volstad is coming off a rough season. He did set a career high with 117 strikeouts. He has worked a lot with former Cubs pitcher Rick Sutcliffe this spring not just on mechanics but on attacking hitters.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum's spring was abbreviated by some early shoulder stiffness, and probably won't top the 90-pitch mark to start the season. But he had a similar '11 spring and was Milwaukee's best pitcher in April and May.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm was slowed this spring by the flu, which is why he was dropped into the No. 5 spot. But his goal is to pitch 200 innings, which few fifth starters can do. He does like pitching at Wrigley Field, where he has a career 6-2 record.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson is a late bloomer who has established himself with 28 Brewers starts in each of the past two seasons. He drew a good matchup; Narveson is 6-1 with a 3.55 ERA in 13 career appearances against the Cubs, six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster was in line for the win on Opening Day, but the bullpen blew it. He struck out 10 in the opener against the Nationals, giving up two hits over 7 2/3 innings. He is 15-5 in his career against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo said he "stunk" in his season debut, a loss to the Cardinals in which he surrendered four home runs and did not pitch through the fourth inning. Gallardo is 4-1 with a 2.93 ERA in 10 career starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Garza had another tough-luck outing in his first start of the season, leaving with a lead only to see it disappear late at Wrigley on Saturday. In three career starts vs. the Brewers, he's 2-1 with a 4.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke gets his first opportunity to turn around last year's home-road splits. He was 11-0 with a 3.13 ERA in his debut season at Miller Park, versus 5-6 with a 4.70 ERA everywhere else.

home_pitcher_note: There is still some skepticism surrounding Jurrjens as he prepares for the home opener. He struggled through Spring Training and his velocity was still down as he lasted just 4 1/3 innings against the Mets on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Turner Field is a relatively pitcher-friendly park, but has given Wolf trouble to the tune of a 5.01 ERA in his 16 starts and two relief appearances there. Overall against Atlanta, he's 5-12 with a 5.28 ERA in 28 games.

home_pitcher_note: Minor impressed during the exhibition season and also before surrendering three consecutive two-out hits in the fifth inning of Sunday's season debut against the Mets. He posted a 3.10 ERA in seven home starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: Job No. 1 for Marcum: Keep the Braves in the yard. He's surrendered a homer in eight straight starts, including last year's postseason, and has allowed a first-inning homer in three straight games dating to last year's NLCS.

home_pitcher_note: Beachy struggled with his secondary pitches and was doomed by defensive miscues during Monday's season debut against the Astros. The right-hander also battled his command while walking three in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson has allowed only two runs in 12 career innings against the Braves. Keep an eye on leadoff man Michael Bourn, who's 4-for-8 with a walk in his previous nine plate appearances against Narveson.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo was so shaky on Opening Day, the Brewers studied video to see if he was tipping pitches. They didn't find anything, and Gallardo allayed fears with seven superb innings against the Cubs on Wednesday in a 2-1 win.
away_pitcher_note: Dominant through his first two starts, the right-hander has combined to give up only one run on eight hits against the Padres and Pirates. With pinpoint control in both starts, Billingsley has walked only one and struck out 15 in 14 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Could this be an audition for the free-agent-to-be? Extension talks with the Brewers have been tabled, and the Dodgers figure to be big spenders next winter. Greinke was knocked around by the Cubs in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Capuano got his first win Thursday vs. the Pirates, giving up two runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings. The lefty walked none and struck out seven. In two career starts against the Brewers, he's 1-0 with a 4.63 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf had no feel for his pitches while giving up eight runs in 4 1/3 innings against the Braves on Friday. The left-hander gave up two home runs during a six-run fifth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Harang dazzled in his last start vs. the Padres. He struck out nine straight to set a new Dodgers record, previously held by Johnny Podres. He also tied a career high with 13 strikeouts, in 6 1/3-inning no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Showing that his shoulder was healthy, Marcum threw 105 pitches in a hard-luck 2-1 loss to the Braves on Saturday in Atlanta. He allowed just three hits and had six strikeouts to two walks over seven innings in his second straight quality start.
away_pitcher_note: After a walk-filled meltdown in a home-opening loss to the Giants, Chacin corrected some delivery flaws in his last start. He held the D-backs to one run and four hits in four innings, but a rain delay ended his start.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada moves from the bullpen to pitch in place of injured lefty Chris Narveson. Estrada made seven Brewers starts last season with a 3.70 ERA in those games. He should be good for about 75 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz was consistently behind in counts in his debut, allowing five runs in 4 1/3 innings. He couldn't establish three pitches for strikes, avoiding his changeup as the D-backs laid off his curveball.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo fixed a rhythm issue and has turned in two encouraging starts since a clunker against the Cardinals on Opening Day. In his last two outings, he's allowed only three runs and 12 hits in 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie took the mound suffering from a sore throat -- strep was going around the clubhouse -- and gave up six runs and nine hits in seven innings of a 7-1 loss to the Padres at Coors Field. He settled down after being hit hard early.

home_pitcher_note: The streak goes on the line again. The Brewers have won all 19 of Greinke's starts at Miller Park, including two games in last year's postseason. Greinke is 13-0 in those games, including 12-0 in regular-season starts.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell has delivered with two quality starts in three outings this year and has allowed 14 hits in 17 2/3 innings. He's looking for his first win since holding the Rockies to no runs in seven innings on April 7 in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf's loss against the Dodgers on Thursday counted as progress. Six days after allowing eight runs in 4 1/3 innings in Atlanta, he limited the damage to four runs in a season-high six innings at home.
away_pitcher_note: Norris had quality starts in his first two outings, but didn't have any wins to show for them. He got plenty of run support and picked up his first win of the season Thursday in Washington, giving up four runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum is 2-0 with a 1.80 ERA in three starts against Houston, all of them last season, including a pair of scoreless seven-inning outings.
away_pitcher_note: Happ is the only Astros starter to have given his club a quality start in his first three outings of the season. He's pitched six innings three times, allowing three earned runs twice and two earned once to start 2-0.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook was a hard-luck loser his last time out despite continuing his strong season start. He reached a season-high 113 pitches and recorded only two outfield outs. The latter is a sign that his sinker was effective. That is his key to success.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers altered their pitching plans so Gallardo will work on regular rest in the series opener. He's is 1-8 with a 6.17 ERA in 12 regular-season starts against the Cards, including an Opening Day loss.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has thrown at least seven innings in three of his four starts and would have four wins if not for a blown save. He's walked only two, highlighting how well his command has been. Lohse has also not pitched from behind all year.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Estrada's second start for left-hander Chris Narveson, who is out for the year with a shoulder injury. Estrada struck out nine and limited the Rockies to one run Saturday in his first start in Narveson's spot.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia pitched 7 2/3 impressive innings against the Cubs but didn't factor in the decision in a walk-off win for Chicago. The lefty is 4-2 with a 3.24 ERA in nine games (eight starts) in his career against Milwaukee, including a win this year.
away_pitcher_note: The road has been tough on Greinke. He allowed eight runs in 3 2/3 innings at Wrigley Field earlier this month and has a career road ERA of 4.29.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Bud Black said Wieland, 22, has looked more comfortable in each start. He allowed two runs in six innings against the Nationals in his third major-league start Wednesday. He gave up no runs in the first inning for the first time this season.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf was inconsistent in his first four starts but fared much better against the Astros last Tuesday. The southpaw allowed two earned runs on four hits, struck out four and walked four over six innings and earned his first victory of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Edinson Volquez had his best start of the season on Thursday against the Nationals, striking out seven and allowing a run and three hits in seven innings. He also issued just one walk, a season low.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum lasted five innings in his last start, Wednesday vs. Houston, and gave up four runs (three earned) on eight hits in five innings. He struck out seven and walked four. He's allowed 16 hits in his last 11 innings over two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan will make his first Major League start since Oct. 4, 2010, when he gets the start against one of his former teams, the Brewers. Suppan, 37, missed most of Spring Training with a triceps injury. He's made two starts for Triple-A Tucson.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo struggled against the Cardinals, allowing eight earned runs on eight hits in two innings. The Brewers ace was coming of a three-start stretch in which he allowed four earned runs over 21 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Though Lincecum lacked dominant stuff against San Diego in his last outing, none of the hits he allowed was thunderous. He surrendered two infield singles, the second of which was initially ruled an error, and a bunt hit.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers have opted to skip No. 5 starter Marco Estrada's turn in the rotation, so Greinke will work on regular rest. He will be pitching on unfamiliar ground at AT&T Park, where he has never pitched.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has limited opponents to two runs or less in his last nine starts at AT&T Park. Last Sunday, he and backup catcher Hector Sanchez, also 22, combined to form what was believed to be one of the youngest batteries in Giants franchise history.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf is off to a sluggish start, but at least he knows the problem: being too fine with his fastball. He will try to grip it and rip it against the Giants, against whom he owns a 2.85 career ERA in 20 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cain's scoreless-innings streak at AT&T Park ended at 21 innings last Tuesday when the Miami Marlins pushed across a fourth-inning run against him. Before that, he hadn't allowed a run at home since last Sept. 13 against San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum worked seven scoreless innings against the Padres in Tuesday, which manager Ron Roenicke said should "really get him locked in." Marcum has met the definition of quality start in four of five outings.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada starts for the first time since April 28, meaning that he'll go nine days between starts instead of the usual four. This will be his third game in place of injured lefty Chris Narveson, who is out for the season.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo has pitched well of late but has also been bothered by a sore lower back. He said it did not affect him during Tuesday's outing vs. the Cubs, but it could be something to watch out for in future outings.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo looks to snap a four-start winless streak. He did not exactly pitch poorly against the Padres in his last outing, allowing three runs in six innings, but before that was torched by the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey pitched well vs. the Cubs in a no-decision, with three solo homers accounting for all his runs allowed. Two of the home runs, he felt, came on mistake pitches. The three homers tied a career high.

home_pitcher_note: The streak goes on the line again. The Brewers are 18-0 when Greinke starts at Miller Park in the regular season (he's 13-0 in those games) and 20-0 if you include last year's postseason.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto turned in another dazzling outing against the Pirates on May 4, allowing just one run on seven hits in a complete game victory. Cueto needed just 110 pitches to complete the masterful performance.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf missed the Cubs when the teams played last month, so this is his first chance to improve on a 6-11 career record against Chicago. He has a respectable 4.22 ERA in those 23 starts, including two shutouts.
away_pitcher_note: Garza is slated to return to the rotation after being skipped because of the flu. In his last game April 29 against the Phillies, he gave up one hit over seven scoreless innings, striking out 10. Hopefully, he can duplicate that.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum has met the definition of "quality start" -- six or more innings, three earned runs or fewer -- in five of his six outings, and allowed three earned runs in five innings in the other game.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad was given a couple extra days rest after his last start, a loss to the Dodgers in which he gave up five runs on four hits over five innings. He's had one inning when he struggles. He's looking for his first win since July 10.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada was done in by one poor inning on Monday, when he allowed five consecutive hits and five runs to open the fourth. In his six other innings of work, he limited the Reds to three hits and no runs.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija is on a roll. He's given up two earned runs over 21 1/3 innings in his past three starts, picking up the win in his last outing vs. the Braves. In that stretch, he's struck out 23 and walked six. That's a good ratio.

home_pitcher_note: Batista struggled early in his first start as a member of the Mets' rotation, giving up four runs over his first two innings. But he settled down to last into the sixth, and the Mets are committed to giving Batista a long look as a starting pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo has a 22.24 ERA in two starts against the Cardinals and a 2.45 ERA in his other five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Gee has struggled to keep his pitch count down in recent outings, needing 103 pitches to throw 5 2/3 innings last time out against the Phillies. Next up for Gee is a Brewers team that he has not seen since his final start of the 2010 season.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke was upset when a quality outing got away in San Francisco on May 4, continuing his trouble in road games. He is 1-1 with a 7.20 ERA in three away starts this season and 30-46 with a 4.27 ERA in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Norris struck out eight in six innings of work in a 1-0 win at Pittsburgh. Norris escaped a bases loaded jam in the sixth inning to record his third win of the year. Norris has allowed just three runs over 18 2/3 innings in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: With everything that happened after he left the game, Wolf's strong start got a bit lost in the shuffle on Friday night. Despite walking three batters, Wolf delivered his best outing of the season, with six scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Happ allowed five runs on six hits over six innings in a 5-2 loss at Pittsburgh. Happ settled down after a rough first frame and retired 13-of 15 batters but struggled in the fifth and allowed two runners to open the sixth to end his day prematurely.
away_pitcher_note: Retiring 16 of the last 18 hitters he faced, Marcum tossed seven innings in his last start, allowing one run on three hits, along with two walks and six strikeouts. He lowered his ERA to 3.07, best among Brewers starters.

home_pitcher_note: The righty limited the Cubs to two runs in six innings on Sunday and avoided a blow-up inning, but allowed two home runs for the third straight start. "That's what's killing me right now," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Diamond stretched his consecutive scoreless streak to 14 innings this season by holding the Blue Jays without a run over seven innings on Sunday. He allowed just five hits and didn't walk a batter while striking out four.

away_pitcher_note: Pavano has been bothered by a strain in the front of his right shoulder, but he still battled against the Indians on Monday. He showed better velocity, but allowed four runs on six hits over six innings.
