away_pitcher_note: Estrada became the first Brewers starter to work past the sixth inning when he delivered seven innings of two-run ball to spoil the Cubs' home opener. He's not known as a hitter, but he has RBIs in each of his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta threw 6 2/3 solid innings but received a no-decision in a 6-3 loss to Chicago on Tuesday. He gave up six hits, struck out five and walked two in a 94-pitch effort. It was his first quality start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Zito's excellence has hit historic levels. He's the first Giants pitcher to throw seven shutout innings in each of his first two starts to a season since Al Worthington, who broke into the Majors with a pair of complete-game shutouts in July 1953.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse threw seven strong innings vs. St. Louis on Friday, but picked up the loss. It marked his second quality start with little support. He allowed one run over six in a loss to Arizona on April 5. The Crew has scored one run in Lohse's 13 frames.
away_pitcher_note: Despite Vogelsong's inflated ERA, he flashed the form that made him a 2011 National League All-Star and Team USA's No. 2 starter in the World Baseball Classic by retiring the final 10 Cubs he faced in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo gave up five earned runs in 5 1/3 innings vs. lifetime nemesis St. Louis in an 8-0 loss Saturday. He's 1-11 vs. the Cards in his career, including the playoffs. Gallardo allowed just one run through the first five before hitting a wall.
away_pitcher_note: Cain allowed two home runs in his last start, marking the first time this year that he yielded multiple homers. That never happened in 2011, when he surrendered just nine homers all season. He was the victim of five multi-homer games last year.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada turned in his second successive quality start in Sunday's 4-3, 10-inning win at St. Louis. He allowed seven hits and three runs over six innings. He has 21 strikeouts and two walks in three starts so far this season.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija is looking for his first win since Opening Day. He ranks among the NL leaders in strikeouts with 27. He wasn't sharp in his last start against the Giants, who collected seven hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers need a fifth starter for the first time since April 6 and their choice was Burgos, the team's reigning Minor League Pitcher of the ear. He will make his Major League debut.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson is looking for his first win with the Cubs after three starts. In his last outing against the Giants, he gave up five runs over 5 1/3 innings. Jackson has yet to post a quality start. So far, left-handers are batting .333 against him.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers gave Peralta a 9-3 lead in the third inning Tuesday, and he wasn't able to pitch through the fifth. His ratio of eight walks to 10 strikeouts is an issue the team will try to iron out.
away_pitcher_note: The Cubs took advantage of Monday's off-day to give Feldman an extra day. He's had some tightness in his back. His pitch count knocked him out of his last game, as he threw 92 pitches over 4 1/3 innings vs. the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis became the first Padres starter to record an out in the seventh inning, as he allowed one run over 7 2/3 innings in a win over the Dodgers. He walked one and struck out five in a 107-pitch effort.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse is 3-for-3 in the quality-start department but is still seeking his first Brewers victory. At least the team won his last start, a significant game in that Lohse extended past 100 pitches for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Richard returns to the rotation on Tuesday after having his start on Saturday scratched due to flu-like symptoms. Richard last pitched on April 14 when he tossed six scoreless innings against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo earned his first win by pitching six innings and hitting a two-run home run against the Giants, his first step in moving past a drunk-driving arrest. He said he will feel extra pressure to perform all season.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez got a no-decision his last time out against the Giants as he allowed two runs in six innings. He walked three and struck out three. It was the second time in four starts this season that he completed six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada has delivered three consecutive quality starts since allowing four runs to the Rockies in his season debut. Friday's outing against the Cubs marked the first time Estrada has walked more than one batter.

home_pitcher_note: With Chad Billingsley out for the year, more is needed from Josh Beckett. He's still winless after his most recent start, which was marred by two more homers. He's already allowed six and needs to keep the ball off the middle of the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Following a very impressive Major League debut on Saturday, Burgos gets the ball again in Los Angeles on Friday. The 25-year-old Burgos allowed five hits and one run in five very sharp innings of work against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Magill makes his Major League debut, replacing the injured Stephen Fife. Magill has posted a 2.84 ERA with 23 strikeouts over 19 innings in four starts for in Triple-A this season.
away_pitcher_note: In four starts this season, Peralta has pitched well in two and struggled in two. His last time out, the right-hander picked up his first win of the season, going 6 2/3 innings and allowing just two runs to the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw has struggled with his curve the last three starts and beat himself up in comments after his last start in New York, not sounding like a confident staff ace. He hasn't lost velocity, but three two-out walks in an inning is a red flag.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander exited his last start early because of a dislocated pinkie. It cost him what would have been his fourth-straight quality start, but he did stick around long enough to earn his first win with the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo threw only 58 of 108 pitches for strikes in his last start, and Brewers manager Ron Roenicke described his top starter as "out of whack." Gallardo still pitched into the seventh inning for his second straight win.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is coming off a no-decision last time out vs. the Phils. The left-hander allowed nine hits and three runs, including a pair of homers, in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada has authored four consecutive quality starts, including a loss to the Padres in which he allowed only one earned run in 6 1/3 innings. "It was probably the best I've felt all year," Estrada said.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald has been extra stingy over his last two outings, allowing just seven hits and four runs in 11 innings. The right-hander has struggled in his career vs. the Brewers, though, posting a 6.98 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Burgos was briefly in line for his second win in as many big league starts, but it was snatched away in the seventh inning on Friday in Los Angeles. He still managed to deliver his second quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Gomez emerges from the bullpen to make his first start of the season, but hardly his first in the Majors: He made 38 starts for the Indians over the last three seasons, posting a 5.32 ERA while averaging 5 1/3 innings per outing.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta appears to be building some confidence. He hit 96 mph with his second pitch against the Dodgers and 97 mph three pitches after that, and balanced that heat by throwing a higher-than-usual percentage of changeups.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook will be going for career win No. 100 for the third time after the bullpen blew a lead in his last start. The Cards have lost three of his four starts even though he has allowed an earned run in only one of them.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has been great, but unlucky. The Brewers are 2-3 in his starts while scoring a total of one run in the losses, including 2-0 duels with the Dodgers' Clayton Kershaw on Sunday and the Cards' Shelby Miller on April 12.
away_pitcher_note: Miller's smooth April endured a laborious end on Sunday, when he needed 113 pitches to cover 5 2/3 innings. Fastball command continues to be key for Miller, who is still learning how best to incorporate his offspeed pitches.

home_pitcher_note: After a laborious first two frames last time out, Gallardo settled down and completed seven innings while giving up only one earned run and retiring the final 13 batters he faced. He is 1-10 with a 6.84 ERA in 15 starts vs. the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright had a dominant April, averaging 7.4 innings per start and posting a 43:3 strikeout-to-walk ratio. He has been every bit the ace the Cardinals hoped, and he continues to experiment with throwing more high fastballs.

home_pitcher_note: With the roof open and the baseballs flying Tuesday on the first warm night at Miller Park, Estrada picked a bad night to elevate some pitches against the Pirates. He surrendered three home runs, matching a dubious career high.
away_pitcher_note: Using the Reds' aggressiveness in his favor, Garcia was efficient (92 pitches) in an eight-inning win on Tuesday. He recorded 18 of his 24 outs via the ground ball, an indication of superb movement on his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta was singled to death Thursday, when the Cardinals used seven singles to score six runs in the third inning to beat the Brewers, 6-5. Before that, Peralta's previous two outings were quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Grimm was the AL Rookie of the Month for April, going 2-0 with a 1.59 ERA in three starts. He lost his last start vs. the White Sox when he allowed three runs in 6 2/3 innings. Opponents are 3-for-25 off him with runners in scoring position.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse did not have his best stuff against the Cardinals on Friday, but he's due some help from his new teammates. The Brewers are 2-4 in the veteran's starts, and have scored a total of two runs in the four losses.
away_pitcher_note: Holland threw eight scoreless innings in a 7-0 win over the Red Sox on Friday in Arlington. Holland is 1-1 with a 4.12 ERA in three starts on the road. He has never pitched against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: In a no-decision vs. the Cubs on Saturday, Cingrani didn't locate well, especially with his secondary pitches. He gave up a pair of two-run home runs to Alfonso Soriano on a fastball and a changeup -- neither were located where he wanted.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo had not allowed a home run since Opening Day, but he surrendered two in Saturday's no-decision against the Cardinals. Jon Jay's came after Gallardo deflected a would-be double-play ball that could have ended an inning.

home_pitcher_note: Feeling sick before Sunday's outing, Latos earned the win over the Cubs but did not have a quality start for the first time this season. Two blooped hits led to three runs in the fifth and ended a 21-inning scoreless streak, which tied a career high.
away_pitcher_note: Burgos returns to the mound for his fourth career start after a pair of off-days over a four-day span led the Brewers to skip his last turn through the rotation. He has limited the opposition to three runs or fewer and pitched at least five frames.

home_pitcher_note: Not surprising is that Ryan Braun leads current Brewers hitters with four career home runs vs. Arroyo. On the other hand, Rickie Weeks struggles against him with a .170 average and 16 strikeouts in 47 at-bats.
away_pitcher_note: Three of Peralta's last four starts have met the definition of "quality," including Tuesday's win over the potent Rangers. "This should be a great outing for him to get locked in like he can," manager Ron Roenicke said.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates have scored merely four runs in the four starts by Burnett that didn't result in a victory. His ERA in those games (23 innings) is 3.13. Right-handed hitters are batting .141 with 39 strikeouts in 92 at-bats against him this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers bumped Estrada by two days to allow for an extra bullpen session between starts. He has allowed 13 earned runs and four home runs over his past two starts, and felt "lost" while walking five Cardinals on May 5.

home_pitcher_note: Though Locke has allowed four runs in his two most recent starts (11 innings), he came away with no-decisions in both. Opponents have attempted one stolen base -- it was unsuccessful -- with him on the mound this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse has not been quite as sharp in his past two starts, but could still be winning games if the Brewers provided him with run support. They are 2-5 when he pitches and have scored a total of three runs in the five losses.

home_pitcher_note: That Rodriguez won his most recent start almost goes without saying. He beat the Mets, and he owns them. He walked none and struck out two in six innings, but needed 92 pitches to do so. He'd been winless with two losses in three previous starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo minced no words in discussing his lousy command against the Reds after throwing 100 pitches in four innings. He said it was a matter of mechanics and dismissed the fact he did not exceed 91 mph.

home_pitcher_note: Supported by an uncharacteristic run output, Liriano made his 2013 and NL debuts against the Mets and appeared to be in midseason form -- nine strikeouts, two walks, six hits and one run in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching for the first time in 10 days, Burgos allowed 12 runs (10 earned) in three ugly innings in Cincinnati. It was only the third time in Brewers history a starter allowed 10 or more earned runs in three or fewer innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jaime Garcia - Garcia gave up a season-high five earned runs in an 8-2 loss to Colorado on Sunday. He surrendered eight hits in six innings and struck out seven. He is 0-3 with a 10.53 ERA against the Rockies, his highest total against any opponent.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta notched his fourth "quality start" on Sunday against the Reds due to his own error, allowing three earned runs in six frames. It was his fourth such outing in five tries. The exception was against the Cards on May 2.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn walked four of the first 10 batters he faced in his last start before settling in and retiring 16 of the final 18 of his outing. It positioned Lynn for the win, making him the second NL starter to reach six wins this year.
away_pitcher_note: Working on seven days' rest, Estrada held the Pirates to one run and three hits over seven innings to earn his third win on Monday. Estrada had his start pushed back after struggling in his previous two outings, but he was sharp on long rest.

home_pitcher_note: Gast, who is filling in for Jake Westbrook, earned his first big league win in his debut on Tuesday. He pitched five scoreless innings before allowing four runs in the sixth. His changeup was especially effective in the start.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse tossed 5 2/3 innings and allowed two runs on five hits in a 4-3, 12-inning loss to the Pirates on Tuesday. He struggled with control and issued five walks. Lohse didn't get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo allowed just three hits and two runs over six innings Wednesday, but two of his four walks came back to bite him in a loss to the Pirates. The right-hander struck out five on the night. Overall it was a nice showing amid an up-and-down year.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a 132-pitch marathon, Kershaw was given an extra day of rest before making his start against Milwaukee. Kershaw struck out 11 with one walk in 8 2/3 scoreless innings against Washington his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Burgos has been effective in each of his two starts at Miller Park, holding opponents to a .205 average with seven strikeouts and only one walk. He left both games (vs. the Cubs on April 20 and the Bucs on May 1) in line for the win.
away_pitcher_note: The only problem with Greinke's first start back after undergoing collarbone surgery was that he ran out of gas after allowing one run in 5 1/3 innings. Greinke threw his regular bullpen session Saturday and seems fine physically.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta has struggled so far at Miller Park, where he owns a 4.57 ERA in eight games -- seven of them starts, including a 6.49 ERA in five starts at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Ryu, who was spent after throwing 100 pitches in five innings in Atlanta his last time out, will look to improve on a 4.50 road ERA. Away from Dodger Stadium, Ryu has walked 13 in 30 innings, including five against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada earned one of the Brewers' two wins on their 10-game road trip with a three-hit, seven-inning gem against the Pirates, allowing one run. But his last time out he was hit hard against the Cardinals, giving up four runs in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett leads the NL in strikeouts and hasn't surrendered more than three runs in a start this season. He has gone seven innings in each of his past four starts, as well. He lost his last start vs. the Brewers on May 13.

home_pitcher_note: Kyle Lohse was originally supposed to take the mound, but will miss a start due to right elbow irritation. Fiers lost his only start on April 6, allowing nine hits and six runs in five innings against the Diamondbacks.
away_pitcher_note: Locke has continued his steady 2013 behind A.J. Burnett in the Pirates' rotation after going 1-3 with a 6.30 ERA in six starts in September and October last season. He tossed seven shutout innings in a 1-0 win over the Astros on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo is 3-4 with a 4.50 ERA on the season but threw a quality start his last time out against the Dodgers. Gallardo tossed six innings, allowing eight hits and three runs while striking out seven and walking one.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has been a model of consistency in a strong Pirates rotation this month. He has thrown at least six innings in his four starts in May, going 3-1 with a 2.88 ERA. He has struck out 19 and walked two in those starts, as well.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta is 1-4 with an 8.27 ERA in five May starts and has allowed 10 earned runs and 18 hits in his past two starts, spanning just 6 2/3 innings. This will be his first career outing against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Correia, who has been the club's most consistent starter this year, was hit hard by the Braves in his worst outing of the year on Monday. The righty gave up five runs on eight hits and a walk without a strikeout over a season-low four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Figaro will leave the Brewers' bullpen to make a spot start, replacing injured righty Hiram Burgos. Figaro was a starter in Japan the past two seasons and made four Major League starts for the Tigers in 2009-10.
away_pitcher_note: Diamond left with a lead but was stuck with a no-decision after allowing three runs on nine hits and a walk over 5 2/3 innings against the Tigers on Thursday. It marked the third straight start the left-hander didn't go at least six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Deduno, who was recalled from Triple-A before his start against the Tigers on Friday, struggled in his season debut, giving up six runs on nine hits and three walks over 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada provided a positive start to a stretch of 20 games in 20 days when he worked seven strong innings against the Pirates on Friday. He owns a 3.09 ERA in five starts away from Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Walters impressed in his season debut, tossing a quality start against the Tigers on Saturday. The right-hander gave up two runs on eight hits and a walk to pick up the win and the help the Twins end a 10-game losing streak.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse, who began his career with the Twins and pitched parts of six seasons for that team, is returning to Milwaukee's rotation after missing a start with what he called a "cranky" elbow. He's never pitched against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels' nightmarish season continued Sunday with a loss in Washington. He dominated through six innings before everything fell apart in the seventh. He hopes to rebound against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo struck out seven but lasted only four innings in his last start Sunday against Pittsburgh. After beginning the year 3-1 he has lost his last four starts. Last season, he faced the Phillies once, fanning nine over seven innings in a 6-2 win.

home_pitcher_note: Cloyd allowed nine hits, six runs, one walk and two home runs and struck out two in just 2 1/3 innings Monday in a loss to the Red Sox at Fenway Park. It was tied for the second-shortest start by a Phillies starter this season.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta dropped his last four decisions after starting the season 3-2. Last time out, he walked five and gave up five hits in five innings against the Twins, a step up after getting knocked out in the second inning by the Dodgers on May 22.

home_pitcher_note: Lee is 4-0 with a 1.15 ERA in his past five starts after shutting down the Red Sox on Tuesday, when he allowed four hits, one run and struck out eight in eight innings. He earned his sixth win after winning six last season.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers pitched three innings out of the bullpen in Tuesday's 14-inning loss to Minnesota, but manager Ron Roenicke said it would not affect Fiers' availability. He will make his third start to go with eight bullpen appearances this year.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada has worked seven innings in three of his last four starts since taking two extra days to recover from an eight-run outing against the Cardinals on May 5. He has been trying to emulate Kyle Lohse's crisp pace.
away_pitcher_note: Milone started strong against the Giants last time out but unraveled in the sixth frame, when he allowed three of his four runs without recording an out. He's struggled, however, in even-numbered starts with a 1-3 record and 6.46 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse returned to the rotation against the Twins after missing a start with pain in his elbow and allowed a season-high six runs and a career-high four home runs. He insisted that his arm was not the problem; location was.
away_pitcher_note: A.J. Griffin cruised through five innings of one-hit ball against the Giants before faltering in the sixth. The right-hander was charged with the loss after getting spanked by San Francisco for four runs in the inning.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Ron Roenicke and catcher Jonathan Lucroy were both encouraged by Gallardo's victory over the Phillies, though he surrendered a trio of home runs. They cited better life on a fastball that has lagged so far this year.
away_pitcher_note: Colon tossed a five-hit shutout against the White Sox on Friday, walking none and fanning three while using 106 pitches. The right-handed veteran has issued just four walks in 70 1/3 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta is coming off a gem. When he threw his first pitch of the seventh inning on Saturday, Peralta became the first Brewers starter not named Marco Estrada to pitch past the sixth since Kyle Lohse 23 games earlier, on May 8.
away_pitcher_note: Cloyd bounced back after a bad start in Boston with a quality start Saturday in a loss to the Brewers. He allowed eight hits, two earned runs, one walk and struck out three in seven innings at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Figaro will make his second Brewers start, this time as a replacement for demoted righty Mike Fiers. Figaro was burned by home runs in his first start -- three of them in five innings of a 5-2 loss to the Twins on May 28.
away_pitcher_note: Lee is on a roll again. In his last six starts, he's 5-0 with a 1.54 ERA. It's a streak that's reminiscent of 2011, when he was named the National League's Pitcher of the Month for both June (5-0, 0.21) and August (5-0, 0.45).

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny will come out of the bullpen and make a spot start in place of Marco Estrada, who is on the disabled list. Manager Ron Roenicke said the club isn't expecting the lefty to go more than four innings, but it depends on his pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed six hits, two runs, one walk and struck out five in a complete-game win over Miami on Monday at Citizens Bank Park. He retired the final 15 batters he faced to pick up the fourth complete game of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse seems to be past the elbow issue that forced him to miss a turn in the rotation last month, but now there is worry about his lower half after he tweaked his left hamstring running the bases on Tuesday against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Pettibone bounced back nicely after struggling against the Red Sox on May 30. He allowed just one earned run in six innings in a 7-3 victory over the Marlins on Tuesday. The Phillies are 7-2 in Pettibone's starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco has been snakebitten. In his last three starts, he is 0-1 with a 2.66 ERA. Nolasco pitched well enough to win at Philadelphia in his last outing. He allowed one hit entering the seventh, but took a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: The box score did not show it, but Gallardo is coming off his best outing of the season. He'd allowed a run and three hits in six strong innings before a walk, a dribbler and a jam shot led to a five-run A's rally and a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Both of Turner's starts have been extremely encouraging since he was called up from Triple-A New Orleans. After winning his first game, Turner had a no-decision at Philadelphia. He has allowed one run in 13 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Two starts ago, Peralta limited the Phillies to two runs in seven encouraging innings, but came back to allow five runs in five innings of a rematch five days later. The question is which Wily will show up in Miami?

home_pitcher_note: Initially, Slowey was set to start on Tuesday, but he was pushed back a day for good reason. Slowey threw seven innings of relief and collected the win in the 20-inning win over the Mets. Slowey is given an extra day.
away_pitcher_note: The longball has dogged Figaro in his two starts; three in a May 28 no-decision against the Twins and another in Friday's no-decision against the Phillies. Stuff-wise, it does not get much better than Figaro's high-90s heat.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo has gone at least five innings in each of his starts this season and has lost just once (on May 29) since a three-game losing streak from April 25-May 6.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse is coming off his best outing as a Brewer. The right-hander held the Phillies to one run on four hits over a season-best eight innings. Lohse will look to repeat his success against the Reds, whom he has held to a 3.34 ERA in 11 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey was fantastic in an eight-inning start against the Cubs on Monday, when the Reds' tired bullpen needed it most. It was the third time this year he threw at least eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo turned in his best outing of the season, shutting out the Marlins over a season-high eight innings. The right-hander held Miami to just four hits and fanned four, including his 1,000th career strikeout.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto, coming off the DL for the second time this season, admitted it might be hard to keep his strained right shoulder off his mind in his first start since May 31. However, he said he feels good, and he doesn't think he'll be limited at all.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta struggled early in the game, giving up three runs on five consecutive hits in the second. But the right-hander regained command to toss four scoreless innings before he was pinch-hit for in the seventh.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles is quietly becoming one of the AL's best young pitchers, posting quality starts in four of his past five outings. The righty dominated Seattle his last time out, striking out 10 and allowing no runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a seven-inning outing in Miami in which he retired 17 consecutive hitters at one point, this is a big outing for Figaro, because starters Chris Narveson and Marco Estrada are nearing return from the disabled list.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard has settled in as a mainstay of the Astros' rotation, allowing two earned runs or fewer in six of his last seven outings. With the Pirates last year, Bedard was roughed up twice by the Brewers, giving up three homers and 11 runs.
away_pitcher_note: After a tough May in which he fought a sore elbow, Lohse is cruising in June to the tune of a 2.25 ERA and .219 opponents' average in his first three starts of the month.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell hasn't been a model of consistency this year, but he has lowered his ERA by nearly a run during his last four outings. However, Minute Maid Park hasn't been too kind to the righty this season.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo has not surrendered a run in 14 innings over his last two starts and is 13-3 with a 2.87 ERA in 13 career starts against the Astros. He has a 2.66 ERA in seven career starts at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta has not fared well at Miller Park so far in his young career, going 3-5 with a 5.60 ERA in his first 11 games, including 10 starts. This season, he is 2-5 with a 7.34 ERA in eight starts at home.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran commanded his four-seam fastball and escaped a pair of bases-loaded jams to turn in six scoreless innings Sunday in Atlanta. He tied a season high with three walks in his first meeting with the Mets this year.

home_pitcher_note: Hand will make his first Major League start on Saturday against the Braves. The right-hander, who was called up from Triple-A Nashville on May 26, has made eight relief appearances this season in a long relief role and has a 3.38 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson is 1-6 with a 6.07 ERA in his eight road starts this season and is winless in his past eight starts, with a 4.47 ERA over that span. He is 3-2 at Miller Park for his career, but his last win there came on May 11, 2010.

home_pitcher_note: Figaro cited fatigue for his command issues in Houston last time out, but he must be sharp this time. With other pitchers due off the disabled list, it is a critical start for Figaro if he wants to remain in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: After surrendering four home runs during his first 10 starts, Maholm has surrendered one in each of his past five starts. He has limited opponents to two earned runs or fewer in three of his past four starts.

home_pitcher_note: He still is getting almost no run support, but Lohse is doing his part with four consecutive quality starts. "I'm not going to be selfish about it," Lohse said. "I want this team to get going in the right direction."
away_pitcher_note: Jackson's only mistake in his last start was a 1-2 pitch to Yadier Molina, who hit a two-run homer in a victory for St. Louis. Jackson's last three outings have been better, and he says it's because he was too "robotic" earlier and overanalyzing.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers and Cubs played a pair of series in April, and Gallardo managed to miss both of them. He'd rather pitch; in 14 career starts against the Cubs, he is 7-2 with a 2.95 ERA and 105 strikeouts in only 88 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman may want to check the schedule and avoid NL Central teams. In his last start, he walked four and gave up six hits over 5 1/3 innings against the Cardinals. He now has a 6.65 ERA and 0-4 record against the NL Central.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta put together his best start of the year against the Braves on Friday in Milwaukee. The right-hander held Atlanta to two hits in seven scoreless innings, improving to 5-8 on the year. It was just his second game going a full seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garza has given up one run over his past 15 innings in two starts. In his previous outing against the Astros, he set season highs in innings pitched (eight) and strikeouts (eight). He has not faced the Brewers this season.

home_pitcher_note: Cole's first three starts were remarkably similar, as he has gone either 6 1/3 or 5 2/3 innings while allowing an average of six hits. Cole is aware of needing to throw more offspeed stuff to get the most out of that 100-mph fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Hellweg will make his Major League debut, receiving the call after Alfredo Figaro landed on the DL. He will become the 10th Brewer to start a game this year. He was 7-4 with a 2.82 ERA in 14 starts for Triple-A Nashville.

home_pitcher_note: Five quality starts out of his first nine testify to the impressive comeback by the veteran lefty, who is still recording more than a strikeout an inning (61 in 54 2/3) while dramatically reducing his walks. He has received a decision in every start.
away_pitcher_note: Hand made his first big league start against the Braves on Saturday and held them scoreless on two hits over 4 2/3 innings. Hand has spent most of his time as a long reliever since his May promotion from Triple-A Nashville.

home_pitcher_note: Morton makes his fourth start on the road back from Tommy John surgery. He matched his career high of five walks the last time out -- when he also had his trademark sinker, with only one ball hit in the air to the outfield in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse is working on five straight quality starts. He has faced the Pirates plenty in his career and is 9-2 with a 3.41 ERA against them. That's the highest winning percentage (.818) against any opponent in his 13-year career.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann became the second MLB starter to reach 11 wins this season after another smooth outing against the D-backs. He gave up two runs on three hits over seven innings with four strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo had worked 22 consecutive scoreless innings, spanning four starts, before the Cubs hung two runs on him in the second inning of Wednesday's loss. He has a 3.33 ERA in eight road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg pitched seven innings in his last outing, giving up six hits and two runs while striking out four. He gave up multiple earned runs for the first time in his past seven starts, which dates back to May 4.
away_pitcher_note: Burned by two third-inning errors in his last start, Peralta lost for the third time in his past three decisions. "When we get an error, I've got to be able to pick up my teammate and execute a pitch," Peralta said.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Mets, Detwiler battled, lasting five innings, allowing three runs (two earned) on six hits and striking out four batters. Detwiler is looking to win his first game since May 10.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse's bid for a sixth quality start in June was denied by Mother Nature, who delivered a rainstorm of more than two hours on Sunday in Pittsburgh. Because he only worked 1 2/3 innings, he is coming back three days later.

home_pitcher_note: In his MLB debut, Jordan, the 17th-ranked prospect in Washington's system by MLB.com, lasted 4 1/3 innings, allowed three runs (one earned) on five hits and struck out one batter against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Hand is Exhibit A for the benefits of filling the strike zone. Because he has thrown 86 of 116 pitches for strikes in his two spot starts, he has been able to deliver 9 2/3 effective innings, allowing only two earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: The first pitch of Hellweg's Major League career was 87 mph, a sign of nerves for a pitcher who usually pumps 96-98 mph heat. Brewers manager Ron Roenicke has encouraged Hellweg to be more aggressive this time.
away_pitcher_note: Zack Wheeler struggled in his home debut in his last outing, giving up five runs on six hits to the Nationals. His fastball command and ability to put away hitters has been inconsistent through three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo has not done much for his trade value lately. After three consecutive starts between June 10-20 without allowing an earned run, he has allowed 11 in seven innings over his last two outings.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum labored in his last outing, vs. Arizona, giving up three runs on six hits in six innings. He's pitched some solid games this year but hasn't been able to string any together.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny will make his second start in place of Wily Peralta, who was pushed back to Tuesday with a left hamstring injury. In his only other start on June 8, the lefty tossed four innings allowing five hits and one run vs. the Phils.
away_pitcher_note: Hefner delivered another strong outing, and this time, his teammates didn't fail him. He allowed one run over seven innings to lower his ERA to 3.54 and win his third game of the year. In his past 13 starts, he has a 2.93 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse's one-run, eight-inning gem in Washington on Wednesday was his sixth straight quality start, if you're kind enough to wipe away his rain-shortened outing in Pittsburgh three days earlier. He has not lost since May 30.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey faced one over the minimum Tuesday, delivering his second no-hitter in the last 10 months. On Sunday, he'll look to become just the second pitcher to throw back-to-back no-nos, with former Red Johnny Vander Meer being the first.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta was originally scheduled to start Sunday against the Mets, but was pushed back to Tuesday because of a strained left hamstring he exited his last start with. He tossed 5 1/3 scoreless innings against the Nationals before leaving early.
away_pitcher_note: Cingrani has given up nine home runs this season, all of which have come against right-handed batters. He made just one major mistake in his last start, leaving a fastball up in the zone for a two-run homer.

home_pitcher_note: Hellweg will get a third start despite two rough ones to start his career. In his debut on June 28, the righty allowed seven runs (five earned) in 1 2/3 innings, and on Friday, he gave up another seven runs (three earned) in just 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The 100th game of Leake's career on Friday against Seattle was less than memorable, as he was behind, 2-0, just four pitches into the game. He had a combined 1.31 ERA over his previous nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Miley earned his first win in more than a month his last time out, tossing eight strong frames vs. the Rockies, allowing one run on five hits.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo will face the team that has reportedly shown interest in trading for him. The righty has batted away any talk about distractions, but he has allowed 17 runs (15 earned) in his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin finally won his 10th game of the season Sunday by tossing eight strong frames vs. the Rockies. He joined Randy Johnson, Curt Schilling and Brandon Webb as the only pitchers in club history to reach double digit wins before the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander has been terrific in his two spot starts this season, holding the Phillies and Mets to a combined one earned run in 10 innings, with no walks and 11 strikeouts. He struck out eight Mets on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado did not pitch poorly last time out, but he was not as sharp as he has been. he allowed just three runs over six innings, but did allow 11 hits to the Dodgers in a 6-1 loss.
away_pitcher_note: The righty pitched to contact on Monday against the Reds, when he scattered nine hits and a walk in 6 2/3 innings but limited the damage to three runs without a single strikeout. He hasn't lost since May 30.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy once again struggled in his last start, a 6-1 loss to the Dodgers. He was able to get ahead of hitters, but struggled to put them away. Command has been a big issue for Kennedy this year.
away_pitcher_note: With his mom in the stands for the first time in his professional career, Peralta pitched a three-hit shutout against the Reds on Tuesday for the Brewers' first complete game in two and a half years. He threw 113 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse lost after allowing five runs on four hits -- including three home runs -- and one walk with five strikeouts in 6 1/3 innings against the Diamondbacks  in his last start before the break.
away_pitcher_note: Turner comes off another strong outing, giving up only two runs on four hits in seven innings in a win against the Braves. He now has six quality starts in eight tries, five of which have lasted at least seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo finished the first half with a quality start against the D-backs, allowing three earned runs on four hits in six innings for a no-decision. The righty has pitched well below expectations thus far and sports a 7-8 record and 4.83 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Eovaldi earned his second win and notched his fifth quality start in five tries in his most recent start, a win against the Nationals on July 12. Eovaldi held the Nats hitless after giving up three runs in the first.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta has allowed just one earned run in his last 21 1/3 innings and threw the Brewers first complete game in 2 1/2 years two starts ago against the Reds. The young right-hander is 4-3 with a 2.86 ERA since June 1.
away_pitcher_note: Alvarez earned his first quality start in his most recent outing, giving up two runs on nine hits in a season-high 6 2/3 innings. He is searching for his first win since Sept. 13, 2012, with the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny lost his last two starts despite not allowing an earned run against the Mets and D-backs. The left-hander has allowed one earned run in three starts (16 IP) this season to earn a spot in the rotation to start the second half.
away_pitcher_note: Cashner will be making his first start of the second half and his 16th of the season. He earned a loss in his last outing, allowing three runs - two earned - on eight hits and two walks against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Hand went back-and-forth from the bullpen to the starting rotation at the end of June and into July and will make his fourth start of the season for the Brewers. In three starts he has thrown 14 2/3 innings and allowed five earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Ross began the season as a starter, but an injury to his non-throwing shoulder landed him on the DL and eventually in the bullpen, as it prevented him from batting. He is 0-1 with a 3.86 ERA in three starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse's 2-0 win over the Marlins was his team-best 12th quality start, and marked the sixth time this season that he pitched at least six innings and issued zero walks. He's won five of his last six decisions.
away_pitcher_note: O'Sullivan will make his third appearance, and second start, when he gets the nod against the Brewers. He's replacing an injured Jason Marquis in the rotation. He allowed three runs in two innings in a relief role July 19.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo was inconsistent in the first half of the season, but started the second half strong with 6 1/3 scoreless innings against the Marlins. The right-hander is 4-2 with a 4.17 ERA in seven career starts against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez pitched a perfect first three innings before running into trouble, as his pitch count rose to 107 after five. He gave up three runs on four hits and a walk, but the Padres hung on to secure his seventh win.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood labored early but held the Cubs to two runs and seven hits in six innings of a 4-3 victory on Sunday at Coors Field. The home run he gave up to Anthony Rizzo was just the third he has yielded in 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old Peralta has dazzled over his last four starts, posting a 0.31 ERA (one earned run allowed) in 29 1/3 innings. The Brewers have won all four of those games, and manager Ron Roenicke seems to think his young pitcher is settling in.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh, with solid Triple-A numbers pitching in high altitude in both Las Vegas and Colorado Springs, moves into the rotation to replace Drew Pomeranz, who was ineffective before suffering left shoulder soreness.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny will make his fifth start for the Brewers against a team he has a career 8.64 ERA against in four starts and six relief appearances. He had allowed one earned run in his first three starts but gave up five in 5 2/3 innings in his last one.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin was hit on the inner thigh by a line drive in his last start, a loss to the Marlins, but still managed to give up just three runs in seven innings. He pitched well enough to win, but didn't because of his team's offensive slump.
away_pitcher_note: Hand's last start was cut short when he was hit by a 97 mph fastball on his right hand. X-rays were negative and there was only some swelling and soreness to work through for the righty. This will be his fifth start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija threw a season-high 118 pitches and walked five over 5 2/3 innings in his last outing vs. the D-backs, which resulted in the early exit. He may prefer to pitch on the road. He has a 1.93 ERA in 37 1/3 innings in his last five road games.
away_pitcher_note: A win over the Padres evened Lohse's win-loss record for the first time since late April, and he registered his team-leading 13th quality start. He lowered his ERA to 3.37, and over his last 11 starts, he is 6-1 with a 2.49 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Villanueva will face his former team for the second time this year. He may be happier at Wrigley Field, where he's posted a 3.72 ERA in 14 games (seven starts) vs. a 4.83 ERA on the road. As a starter, Villanueva is 1-6 with a 4.52 ERA in 12 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo struggled mightily his last time out -- surrendering six earned runs on eight hits in 3 1/3 innings against the Padres -- but he has good numbers against the Cubs for his career. In 15 career starts vs. Chicago, he is 7-3 with a 3.12 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta, acquired from the Orioles in the Scott Feldman deal July 2, will make his Cubs debut in the second game of the doubleheader. He tuned up Thursday for Triple-A Iowa, giving up one run on four hits in 6 2/3 innings and striking out eight.
away_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old entered the season as MLB.com's top Brewers prospect, but for the second straight season, he has slipped into organizational no-man's land. Is he a starter? A middle reliever? A closer in the making?

home_pitcher_note: Jackson is on a good roll. He's won three of his last five games and posted a 2.51 ERA in that stretch. The difference? Better fastball command, balls are being hit at people, and he's throwing with more conviction.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta's sensational July ended with a dud in Denver. He was 2-0 with a sparkling 0.31 ERA in his first four starts for the month, before allowing eight runs (five earned) on seven hits in 3 2/3 innings against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny's victory last week in Denver was his first as a starting pitcher since May 7, 2011 for the Nationals against the Marlins. Saturday marked his 15th start since that date.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has been unusually inefficient in his two starts since the All-Star break. In his last start against the Mets, he allowed five earned runs, walked three batters and needed 118 pitches to work through 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: A reliever who was thrust into starting duty for the injury-plagued Brewers, Hand's six-inning outing in Colorado on Sunday was his longest since 2009, when he was a starter in Double-A.
away_pitcher_note: Haren was superb in his last outing, allowing just three hits and one run over seven innings against the Mets on Saturday. In four starts since his stint on the disabled list, he has a 3.13 ERA with 18 hits allowed, six walks and 26 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Since the end of May, Lohse is 6-1 with a 2.29 ERA in 12 starts."He's done what we hoped he would do," manager Ron Roenicke said. "He's done his job. We haven't supported him, which is too bad."
away_pitcher_note: It took six tries, but Jordan finally picked up his first Major League win in a 14-1 victory over the Mets on Sunday. He allowed just one run on five hits over six innings with a career-high seven strikeouts, including four by slider.

home_pitcher_note: Gaudin has been tough on hitters when it counts most. Opponents are batting .163 off him (8-for-49) with runners in scoring position. Though Gaudin owns a 26-29 career record as a starter, his teams are 46-38 when he starts.
away_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old right-hander will fill-in for Yovani Gallardo, who is on the DL with a hamstring strain. Gallardo was hurt in Game 1 of a doubleheader Tuesday before Thornburg delivered six scoreless innings in Game 2.

home_pitcher_note: Without the four outings in which he allowed seven runs or more, Cain's ERA would be 2.76. Bugged by the long ball earlier this season, Cain has allowed just three home runs in his last 13 starts. Cain's 4-4 with a 5.26 ERA this season at home.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta posted a 0.31 ERA in his first four July starts (one earned run, 29 1/3 innings) and a 8.31 ERA in his final two (eight earned runs, 8 2/3 innings). The Giants touched him for five earned runs on April 16.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner's nine-game streak of pitching at least seven innings and allowing three runs or fewer is tied for the second-longest in the Major Leagues since 1996. Arizona's Randy Johnson pitched 14 such games in 1999.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada has seven weeks to save his season, beginning with his return from a two-month stay on the DL. He is fighting for a job after pitching to a 5.32 ERA in his first 12 games, then missing time with a hamstring strain.

home_pitcher_note: The Giants have scored one run or were shut out 10 times in Lincecum's 22 starts. He's winless in his last two outings despite recording a 1.93 ERA in that span. The Giants have lost 12 of his last 14 starts after winning six of his first eight.
away_pitcher_note: Hand has helped relieve the pain of an ailing Brewers' pitching staff since shifting from the bullpen to the rotation. In six starts this season, Hand has allowed 13 earned runs in 31 2/3 innings (3.69 ERA), but he is yet to earn his first win.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders worked his way in and out of trouble for six innings on Sunday in Baltimore and was rewarded with his 10th win. It's the fourth double-digit win season of Saunders' career. He's 0-1 with a 5.68 ERA in two career starts against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse owns a 1.13 ERA in his last four starts, all Brewers victories, and allowed only one home run in those games after serving up three to the D-backs on July 13 in a frustrating finish to the first half.

home_pitcher_note: The All-Star allowed just two runs on four hits in 7 1/3 innings in his last game, but took a tough loss vs. Toronto. Iwakuma, who has never faced the Brewers, is 3-1 with a 1.91 ERA (29 strikeouts and nine walks) in his past five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny will be working on three extra days' rest after taking a line drive off his pitching elbow in his last start. Gorzelanny said he could have pitched as scheduled Wednesday night, but the Brewers opted for caution.

home_pitcher_note: The American League ERA leader lost for the first time in his last 13 starts in a five-inning outing Tuesday when he gave up six runs (three earned) and nine hits in five innings against Toronto. This will be his first career start against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: After two duds to finish an otherwise sensational July, Peralta's 6 1/3 solid innings in San Francisco on Tuesday represented a welcome bounce-back. "I think I needed an outing like that," he said.

home_pitcher_note: Ogando has made four starts since coming off the disabled list and is 1-1 with a 4.34 ERA. He has yet to pitch more than five innings and is 2-0 with a 2.76 ERA in just three starts at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada enjoyed a successful return to the mound after two months on the disabled list, allowing only one hit and no runs in San Francisco. He retired the final 14 batters he faced, six of them on strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Garza is 2-1 with a 3.38 ERA in four starts since being acquired from the Cubs on July 22. He has allowed four runs in each of his last two starts and is 4-1 with a 2.66 ERA in seven career starts against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old has pitched six innings in each of his two starts without allowing an earned run, though the Giants made him work Monday. Thornburg needed 81 pitches through his first four innings before getting through six.

home_pitcher_note: Since the beginning of June, Lohse owns a 2.49 ERA and a .226 opponents' batting average in his last 86 2/3 innings. The Brewers have scored at least five times in each of his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Over seven innings, Cingrani gave up two unearned runs on two errors in the first inning on Saturday in a loss to the Padres. It forced him to throw 32 pitches in the frame and he was done with 92 pitches in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers signed Gorzelanny as a reliever, but are now looking at him as a starter for 2014. In his first seven Brewers starts, the lefty owns a 2.57 ERA. Overall, he has held opponents to a .199 average.
away_pitcher_note: Though Leake pitched a season-high 8 1/3 innings July 10 at Miller Park, he admitted it wasn't one of his better outings. Besides walking four, he was in a few jams early and made pitches to escape. Later, he did retire a stretch of 13 in a row.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers timed Gallardo's return from the disabled list so he will miss his arch-enemy Cardinals (1-10, 6.78 ERA) and make two straight starts against the Reds, against whom Gallardo is a more respectable 6-6 with a 4.53 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Latos had one of his best outings of the season with eight scoreless innings vs. the Cubs on Monday, when he threw just 94 pitches. He and Devin Mesoraco were in sync as Latos said he did not have to shake off his catcher one time all night.

home_pitcher_note: If this is what Peralta looks like when he can locate his slider and changeup, then the Brewers have a good young pitcher on their hands. With those offspeed offerings working, he has a 2.10 ERA in his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey earned a win and a no-decision in his first two August starts despite nine earned runs on 15 hits in 11 2/3 innings combined. He has not fared well in two starts vs. Milwaukee this year, giving up 10 earned runs on 18 hits in 12 2/3 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada has surrendered only one run and five hits in 11 innings since returning from a two-month stint on the disabled list for hamstring and back issues. He is pitching to reclaim a spot in next season's starting rotation.
away_pitcher_note: One week after an injury-shortened, two-pitch start, Miller returned to the mound. The righty served up two homers in the second inning of a 5-1 loss to the Bucs and gave up three earned runs on eight hits, which matched a season high.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse will make his fourth start against the team that let him go last winter, having lost to the Cardinals once in April and twice in May. He leads the Brewers with 16 quality starts, including five in his last six outings.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn had a string of four consecutive quality starts snapped on Thursday when he allowed four earned runs in 5 1/3 innings. With six strikeouts, Lynn surpassed the 150-K mark for the second straight season.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny is coming off his poorest start since joining the Brewers' rotation, a 4 2/3-inning, six-hit, three-walk dud against the Reds. He needed 37 pitches for the first inning alone.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook has a 10.13 ERA and .333 opponents' batting average over his last four outings, but the Cardinals are keeping him in the rotation for at least one more turn. The Cards are winless in Westbrook's last four appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey struggled against the Brewers in his first two outings against them this year, but he threw eight innings of one-run ball vs. Milwaukee on Sunday. He walked one and struck out eight, while throwing 119 pitches, 82 for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo will make his second straight start against Cincinnati. The last marked his return from two and a half weeks on the disabled list for a left hamstring strain, and saw Gallardo work 6 1/3 scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo didn't feel his best physically on Monday but still held the D-backs to three runs in six innings en route to a 5-3 win. Despite giving up 12 hits the last time he saw the Brewers on June 14, Arroyo allowed just two earned in 7 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Reds have seen the good and bad of Peralta this season. He blanked them in a three-hit shutout on July 9, the Brewers' first complete game in more than two years, then surrendered seven runs on eight singles on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Taking the place of the injured Tony Cingrani, Reynolds will make his second start of the season for the Reds. He last pitched for Triple-A Louisville on Tuesday, delivering a one-run, five-hit complete game.
away_pitcher_note: The Reds and Brewers will have played 15 games this season before Estrada gets his first look at Cincinnati. He has decent career numbers against them, including a 3.50 ERA and 22 strikeouts versus two walks.

home_pitcher_note: Locke had his shortest start of the season (four innings) last time out, also his sixth straight winless start. Control has become a big issue, with 14 walks and 12 strikeouts in last 17 innings. Has gone 1-3 in his last eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse is proving that when healthy, he is outstanding. His victory over the Cardinals on Tuesday was the 13th quality start in his last 16 outings, all since the beginning of June. In May, Lohse was bothered by a sore elbow.

home_pitcher_note: A series of solid, consistent starts has raised Morton's stock to dependable No. 3 starter status. He's averaged seven innings and two runs allowed in his last four outings and has not allowed a home run in his last 38 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny made it through just 3 2/3 innings against the Cardinals his last time out, giving up seven runs on 10 hits and a walk. He's surrendered 12 total runs in two outings since tossing seven innings of shutout ball vs. the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Cole continues as a real homebody, making his 10th of 14 starts in PNC Park. Despite six losses in eight decisions since beginning his career 4-0, he has been impressively consistent, allowing either two or three runs in 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: In each of his two starts since coming off the disabled list, Gallardo has gone at least six innings. He's given up a total of two earned runs, both of which came on Friday against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta has been better on the road this season (3.94 ERA in 14 starts) than at Miller Park (5.17 ERA in 13 starts), though two of his last three outings at home have been excellent, including a July 9 shutout of the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver had one of his best outings of an injury-riddled season on Sunday, pitching eight innings of one-run ball against the Mariners while giving up three hits -- one a solo homer -- and walking none with eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: In his first four starts since a two-month stay on the disabled list, Estrada is 2-0 with a 1.88 ERA and a .169 opponents' batting average. He has 21 strikeouts and three walks in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Williams, with a 7.61 ERA in his last 10 starts, was skipped through the rotation after the Monday off-day and will pitch on nine days' rest. His last time out, he limited the Indians to two runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse surrendered five earned runs Tuesday on a career-high 13 hits, one of which loomed large. A Felix Pie fly ball that ticked off Norichika Aoki's glove was ruled a double, and Pittsburgh went on to score four runs.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson gave up eight hits and a season-high-tying five walks against the Rays on Tuesday, giving up three runs in five innings while battling a high pitch count all night. He finished the month of August 2-0 with a 2.84 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers decided they had seen enough of Tom Gorzelanny in the starting rotation and returned him to the bullpen in favor of Thornburg, who allowed only one earned run in 18 innings over his first three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hitting his stride following return from Tommy John surgery, Morton has been team's most consistent starter for a month, averaging seven innings with a 1.83 ERA his last five starts. Got Bucs' only win in recent series with Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo worked seven scoreless innings to beat the Pirates on Thursday, and will get a rematch. Since Gallardo debuted in 2007, only the Reds' Johnny Cueto has more wins against the Pirates than Gallardo's 11. Cueto has 13.
away_pitcher_note: Although Cole has gone 2-7 since starting his career with four straight wins, his ERA has hardly varied through 14 starts. His run support has suffered more than his pitching: eight runs in the last six losses. He has nine quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta's sinker should play at hitter-friendly Miller Park, but he has struggled in home games this season to the tune of a 5.12 ERA in 14 starts. On the road, he has a 3.94 ERA in 14 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano, who did not make his first start until Game No. 36, will finally qualify for listing among league leaders by pitching five innings; right now has fourth-best ERA. Coming off seventh scoreless start, against Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin did not get a decision in his last outing, giving up two earned runs over five innings against the Phillies. He was able to shrug off an error by Anthony Rizzo that led to a run. The lefty finished August with an impressive 2.65 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse, who was drafted by the Cubs in '96, has beaten them twice this year and is 5-4 with a 4.77 ERA in 18 starts career against them. Lohse tossed six scoreless innings, allowing five hits and striking out six, at Wrigley Field in July.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta picked up his second win and third quality start in his last outing. He's holding opponents to a .178 batting average against, and has struck out 21 over 28 2/3 innings. He was mad at himself for not throwing enough first-pitch strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Hellweg returned to the Brewers as a September callup and has a chance to prove his first stint in the Majors was a fluke (10.97 ERA in three starts and a relief outing).
