away_pitcher_note: Estrada put together one of his best starts last time out Tuesday, holding the Pirates to one run in six innings while striking out eight and walking two. He has 46 K's in 49 1/3 innings, compared to 14 walks, and he sports an impressive 1.10 WHIP.

home_pitcher_note: As Minor tossed 6 2/3 scoreless innings against the Giants on Tuesday, he impressed with the confidence he had in all of his secondary pitches. He had relied too heavily on his fastball in his previous start.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta has pitched even better in May than he did in April. He's allowed just three earned runs over 21 innings (1.29 ERA) with 14 strikeouts and three walks in three May starts, lowering his ERA to 2.05.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran struggled with location in his last start, a 10-4 loss to San Francisco. In his shortest outing of the season, he left the game after just 41 pitches and told reporters he had trouble finding the grip on the ball.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo has hit a rough patch his last three starts, in which he has a 5.50 ERA. Perhaps a matchup with the Braves will do the trick: he's 5-1 with a 1.79 ERA in eight career starts against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Santana is looking to rebound from his worst start of the season against the Cardinals on Friday. Command was a challenge for the right-hander and the five runs and 10 hits allowed were both season highs.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse improved to 5-1 with seven innings of three-run ball in his last start Friday against the Cubs. He allowed all three runs in the first three innings and cruised the rest of the way.

home_pitcher_note: Harang was a tough-luck loser against the Cardinals on Saturday. He pitched six strong innings and gave up three runs with only two earned. Harang was a victim of four bunt hits that led to a couple of St. Louis runs.
away_pitcher_note: Garza's first-inning struggles continued in his homecoming to Wrigley Field. He surrendered three runs in the opening frame to the Cubs on Saturday, but he retired 18 of the final 20 to finish strong over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough outing against the Dodgers, Koehler turned in a terrific seven-inning performance at San Francisco, where he struck out seven. The right-hander has gone at least seven innings in three of his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada gave up a season-high seven hits in a season-low five innings against the Cubs in his most recent turn. It was his first loss since April 15, and the second time in the past three starts he's given up four runs.

home_pitcher_note: Turner has dropped two straight decisions on the road, and now he seeks his first win of the season. In his first two starts at Marlins Park, he's allowed 11 runs in 10 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta struggled with his fastball command against the Braves on May 19, walking a season-high four batters in defeat. However, Brewers manager Ron Roenicke said it was the best Peralta's changeup has looked.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf will make his first big league start since 2012, and the veteran will face one of his former teams, the Brewers. In two relief appearances with Miami, Wolf has thrown five innings. He also picked up his first MLB save.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson will make his season debut in place of Yovani Gallardo, who sprained his left ankle in his last start. Nelson has a 1.71 ERA across nine starts at Triple-A Nashville this year and posted a 0.90 ERA over 10 innings with Milwaukee last season.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse recorded his ninth quality start in his most recent outing, giving up only one run in eight innings against the Braves. His victory snapped a four-game losing streak for the Brewers, who hadn't won since his previous start.
away_pitcher_note: Tillman is coming off one of the worst starts of his career, allowing six earned runs over an inning-plus against the Pirates. The righty has pitched to an ERA over six in his last half-dozen starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garza allowed four runs on five hits over 6 1/3 innings for a no-decision his last start. He walked three and struck out a season-low one batter. Garza is 9-1 with a 3.03 ERA in 12 starts against the O's, the club he has beaten most in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty took a no-decision on Thursday, going 6 2/3 innings and pitching better than his final line indicated. Chen was charged with five runs allowed on eight hits.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo missed his previous scheduled start while nursing a left ankle sprain he sustained in Atlanta, where he allowed four runs in 3 1/3 innings. He has lost his past three decisions after winning his first two starts. He has never faced the O's.
away_pitcher_note: Norris pitched well again on Friday night, allowing four runs -- all of which came in one inning -- over six innings in a win over the Indians. The righty has been the Orioles' best starter.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada surrendered a career-high four homers in his previous start. They were all solo shots in a win, but they brought him to a Major League-leading 16 dingers allowed. He struck out seven, walked none and scattered six hits in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Left-hander Wood came within five outs of his first shutout in his last start Saturday in San Diego. Over his last two starts, he has allowed four runs on five hits and five walks in 14 1/3 innings. He went 20 batters between hits vs. the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta took the loss Saturday despite allowing just one run over six frames. He worked out of several jams, including a first-and-third situation where he fanned Giancarlo Stanton.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel faded after allowing only two hits in five shutout innings vs. the Padres on Sunday, a "residual effect" of being hit on his pitching hand by a comebacker in his previous start. He gave up three runs on a hit and two walks in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse was one out from getting another win in his last start when the bullpen lost the lead. He pitched seven innings in a start against the Cubs in May, giving up three runs on seven hits and a walk while striking out two in the Brewers' 4-3 win.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija finally picked up his first win of the season in his last start. He struck out 10 and helped himself by hitting a RBI double. He said it was the first time he's had all of his pitches working, and was happy to not walk anyone.

home_pitcher_note: Garza looked strong early in his last start against Baltimore, striking out nine in 6 2/3 innings before allowing three unearned runs in the seventh to lose the lead. He's had three quality starts in his last five outings.
away_pitcher_note: Gibson was excellent Wednesday night against the Rangers. He went six innings and struck out four batters while issuing zero walks. He tends to have a tough time on the road. His away ERA in opposing ballparks is 7.77.

home_pitcher_note: On Wednesday against Baltimore, Gallardo didn't appear bothered by the sprained left ankle that delayed his start by three days. He gave up three earned runs over 6 2/3 innings, picking up his first win in nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Deduno gave up a season-high four runs on nine hits and a walk over 5 1/3 innings against the Rangers on Thursday, and was saddled with a no-decision. The right-hander has yet to go more than six innings in any of his five starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco bounced back to register his first quality start since May 13, as the right-hander surrendered just one run on seven hits and four walks against the Yankees on Friday. It was his first win since April 24.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada on Friday recorded his first quality start in three tries, allowing three runs over six innings in a win against the Cubs. It was not his most efficient outing as he issued four walks, including three leadoff walks.

home_pitcher_note: Correia pitched out of several early jams against the Yankees on Saturday and ended up with a quality start. The right-hander gave up just one run on nine hits and a walk over six innings but was saddled with a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta on Saturday had his worst outing of the year, giving up six earned runs in 5 2/3 innings vs. the Cubs. Four of those runs came in his final inning. Peralta finished May with quality starts in four of six attempts.

home_pitcher_note: Cumpton had one of those stats-skewering outings in his last start, roughed up for 10 earned runs in 3 2/3 innings in L.A. So he has a chance to show his ability to turn the page. Yet to allow a homer in 27 2/3 innings in PNC Park.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse was outstanding against the Cubs on Sunday, tossing a three-hit shutout and using only 93 pitches to do so. He has been the Brewers' most reliable pitcher this season with 10 quality starts in 12 attempts.

home_pitcher_note: The surprisingly consistent righty goes for his third straight win. Volquez has allowed one run or two in seven of his 11 starts. On pace for a better than 2-to-1 strikeouts-to-walks ratio for the first time since 2008, when he whiffed 206.
away_pitcher_note: Garza threw his first scoreless outing of the year Monday, allowing six hits and two walks over 6 1/3 while earning the win against Minnesota. He struck out eight Twins and now has 17 strikeouts over his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Locke is called upon to start against the Brewers after Gerrit Cole was pulled from his upcoming Monday start with shoulder fatigue. Schedule Sunday starter Charlie Morton was then bumped to Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo on Tuesday against Minnesota had his worst start of the season, lasting only five innings and allowing six earned runs on eight hits. In six starts since May 3, Gallardo's ERA has ballooned to 4.08 from 1.91.

home_pitcher_note: With Dillon Gee sidelined indefinitely, Matsuzaka will make another start. To stay in the rotation, he must demonstrate better control than he did in a no-decision last time out, walking five Cubs batters over 4 1/3 innings of four-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: When Estrada gets burned, he often gets burned by the long ball. He's allowed a home run in all but one of his 12 starts this season, and Estrada's 18 home runs allowed leads the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: deGrom delivered a less-than-quality start for the first time last Thursday at Wrigley Field, though some of that was due to imperfect defense behind him. Despite the hiccup, the rookie has opened eyes over his first five big league outings.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta's command issues and high pitch counts in recent starts have been a source of frustration for manager Ron Roenicke. "He works really hard on every single batter, and you can't keep doing that," Roenicke said.

home_pitcher_note: Start after start, Niese continues to deliver the goods. His latest effort was a seven-inning, two-run outing in San Francisco that ended in a no-decision. He has contributed quality starts in nine of his last 11 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Before allowing eight runs in five-plus innings of a loss to the Pirates on Friday, Lohse had allowed three or fewer earned runs in 11 of his 12 starts and surrendered only four runs in the outlier.

home_pitcher_note: After posting a 5.00 ERA in April and 4.65 in May, he has allowed three earned runs in 12 1/3 innings so far in June, posting his first back-to-back victories in a Brewers uniform. But Garza is still grinding through games.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey tossed eight strong innings to earn his seventh win Sunday against the Phillies, allowing one run on six hits while walking three and striking out seven. In 17 career starts against Milwaukee, he is 4-7 with a 5.21 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo dominated the Pirates his last time out -- four hits and one walk over seven shutout innings. In seven home starts this season, the right-handed ace owns a 4.01 ERA and 1.24 WHIP while fanning more than twice as many batters as he's walked.
away_pitcher_note: Latos will be making his season debut after being on the disabled list rehabbing from elbow and knee surgeries. He had four pain-free rehab starts in Louisville and was stretched out to 100 pitches. He will replace Tony Cingrani in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada was effective and efficient at times Tuesday -- a six-inning, six-run effort vs. the Mets -- but was ultimately done in by two homers. He has given up a Major League-high 20 on the season, including at least one in each of his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Leake was roughed up for five runs on nine hits in a loss to the Dodgers on Tuesday, in which he walked one and struck out seven. He is 1-1 with a 4.08 ERA in six career starts against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy has more hits (three) than wins (one) this year. He allowed five runs on eight hits over six innings his last time out against the Astros in Houston. His win came on May 3 in San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta bounced back from an iffy start to throw 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball against the Mets on Wednesday. The right-hander's ERA dipped to 2.90 and his WHIP to 1.23. In six road starts this season, Peralta has finished the seventh inning once.

home_pitcher_note: The D-backs called up Bolsinger on Tuesday to replace the injured Bronson Arroyo in the rotation. Bolsinger had a five-game stint with the D-backs earlier in the season, but he had a 1-2 record and 6.08 ERA before being sent to Triple-A Reno.
away_pitcher_note: For the second time in three starts, Lohse was very good Thursday, limiting the Mets to an unearned run over eight innings. Lohse, whose 1.04 WHIP is the best in Milwaukee's rotation, has pitched into the seventh inning in 10 of 14 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Miley has not won since May 10. The long ball has been a problem for him this year as he has allowed a whopping 16. His last time out, against the Astros, he allowed four runs on seven hits (two homers) in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garza's troubles throwing to bases hadn't hurt him this season before Friday, when his two errors contributed to four unearned runs in seven innings against the Reds. The Brewers mounted a comeback to take him off the hook.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson won his first five starts in the big leagues, but his streak ended against the Dodgers on Friday night. He did not have command of his fastball and lasted just five innings, allowing two runs on four hits and four walks.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo appears to be entering a midseason surge. Over his past two starts, he has allowed one run on 10 hits in 14 innings, with 16 strikeouts. "For our success, [we need] for him to be 'that guy,' " Ryan Braun said.

home_pitcher_note: In two Major League starts since a callup from Triple-A Colorado Springs, against the Braves and the Giants, Bergman has seven strikeouts agaInst two walks, and has pitched six innings each time.
away_pitcher_note: With top Brewers prospect Jimmy Nelson pitching so well at Triple-A Nashville, there's urgency for Estrada to get back on track. He has allowed 23 home runs this season, by far the most in the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: Friedrich will start after the club optioned Juan Nicasio to Triple-A. It will be Friedrich's first Major League appearance since July 28, 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta was away from the team between his past two starts because an undisclosed family matter in the Dominican Republic, but returned with a strong, seven-inning outing in a win over Arizona. He's won three straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Matzek, pitching in front of at least 50 family members and friends, didn't have his slider and gave up 10 hits, but remained composed and held the Dodgers to three runs in a loss at Dodger Stadium in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse has had trouble in five past starts at Coors Field, where he owns a 6.67 ERA and a .306 opponents' average. But it hasn't been the long ball that's hurt him; Lohse has allowed only two homers in 27 Coors Field innings.

home_pitcher_note: Garza has quietly gotten on a roll for the Brewers, with five straight quality starts and a 2.41 ERA in that span. He's been hurt several times by trouble throwing to the bases.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since returning from a stint on the 15-day disabled list because of left shoulder inflammation, Gonzalez surrendered four earned runs on five hits and three walks with six strikeouts over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo has pitched seven innings in each of his last three starts, allowing only two runs on 15 hits with three walks and 20 strikeouts. It's all on the heels of a five-inning, six-run stinker against the Twins on June 3.
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight start his last time out, Zimmermann received zero runs of support from the Nationals. He allowed two earned runs on seven hits over seven innings in a loss to the Braves. His ERA has dropped from 4.07 to 2.95 since May 28.

home_pitcher_note: It wasn't pretty but Estrada earned the win at Coors Field Friday. After being crushed for six runs in the first two innings, Estrada received enough run support to last 5 2/3 innings, striking out seven against 10 hits.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, vs. Atlanta, Strasburg had his worst performance since mid-April. He got tagged for four runs on nine hits over six innings, but received a no-decision thanks to a game-tying homer from Anthony Rendon in the bottom of the ninth.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta stuck to his guns after allowing two early runs, battling the Rox for 7 2/3 innings to set a career-high four-game win streak. Peralta's only other mistake was Corey Dickerson's homer on a day in which he had his ground-ball game going.
away_pitcher_note: Friedrich gave up nine runs, but just four earned, in losing to the Brewers on Saturday in his 2014 debut. Friedrich pitched decently with his fastball inside, although Aramis Ramirez hit one for a home run.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start at one of his "least favorite ballparks," Coors Field, Lohse tried to limit the damage rather than attacking Rockies hitters. He was often behind in the count and was pulled after three earned runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Matzek gave up five runs in 5 1/3 innings of his last start on Sunday, a loss to the Brewers. He had two rough innings, which led Matzek to say he will work between starts on keeping his fastball down.

home_pitcher_note: Garza pitched into jams in the second and third innings Monday against Washington but earned his sixth straight quality start. He lasted seven innings, struck out seven and limited the damage to a three-run home run.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin has shown glimpses of the pitcher who won 14 games last season. But he gave up five runs on four hits in his last start against the Cardinals and has been inconsistent after a shoulder injury delayed his season.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo has been spectacular in his last four starts, allowing three earned runs and 19 hits over 27 innings. He's lowered his ERA from 4.08 to 3.23 in that span of four quality starts, striking out 25 in the process.
away_pitcher_note: After lasting fewer than four innings in each of his two previous starts, De La Rosa threw an encouraging seven innings in a win over St. Louis on Tuesday. However, he still carries a 7.36 June ERA after allowing four earned runs vs. the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Hutchison hasn't enjoyed much success at home this season. On the road, he has a 2.23 ERA, but at home, he has allowed 25 earned runs, 35 hits, eight home runs and 15 walks over 27 2/3 innings. He's also lost three of his past four decisions overall.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada had his best start since May 13 on Wednesday, limiting the Nationals to two hits and two runs over 6 1/3 innings. Although he walked four, Estrada didn't allow a home run for just the second time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Happ is coming off one of his best starts this season. He pitched 7 2/3 scoreless innings vs.the White Sox, striking out a season-high eight and allowing four hits. It was his longest outing since being acquired by Toronto in July 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta has won five straight starts but owns a 4.22 ERA in that span. "He's not locked in," Brewers manager Ron Roenicke said. "He's still making good pitches, but he's struggling to get through the lineup."

home_pitcher_note: Simon used only 80 pitches through seven innings and his sinker nabbed 15 ground-ball outs in another fine start vs. the Giants on Saturday. Simon had to be lifted for a pinch-hitter or he might have continued before the Reds won in extras.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse on Friday delivered his 13th quality start but saw a victory slip away from the bullpen for the fifth time this season. He has allowed three or fewer earned runs in four straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey flirted with notching a third career no-hitter during Sunday's 4-0 win over the Giants. The bid ended on a Buster Posey two-out single in the seventh inning.
away_pitcher_note: Garza likes to remain on a regular five-day schedule but will be working with two extra days of rest for this start because of a pair of Brewers off-days. He has pitched into the seventh inning of four straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Latos and Sam LeCure combined on a one-hitter against the Padres, but the Reds still took a 1-0 loss Monday. Latos regretted a leadoff walk in the fifth to Tommy Medica, who was able to score the lone run without a hit in the inning.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo allowed only three earned runs in 27 innings over four starts before struggling against the Rockies (eight runs, five earned, on a season-high 10 hits). For the first time in weeks, he couldn't command his curveball.

home_pitcher_note: Two more home runs to the Jays pushed Estrada's MLB-leading total to 26 homers surrendered this season, but he counted the outing as a positive in terms of command and execution of his pitches, particularly his changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels had a 1.88 ERA in 10 starts, pitching seven or more innings in each one, before he struggled Wednesday against the Marlins in Miami, where he allowed five hits, three runs and four walks in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: After posting a 2.12 ERA in his first 10 starts, the right-hander has a 5.15 ERA in his last seven starts. "We've got to get him locked in better and making some consistent pitches," Brewers manager Ron Roenicke said.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed six hits, two runs, one walk and struck out four in seven innings in Thursday's 5-4 win over the Marlins. He pitched a clean first inning, too. He has allowed 16 earned runs in 17 first innings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse's command has been a bit off in recent starts, with two of his last three starts lasting only five innings. That matches his shortest outings of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez needed 45 pitches to get through the first inning Friday against the Pirates, setting the tone for his eighth loss of the season. He managed to pitch into the sixth inning, throwing 117 pitches in a losing effort.

home_pitcher_note: Garza is coming off his best Brewers start, a complete-game, two-hit shutout of the Reds on Saturday. No Brewers pitcher had allowed as few hits and struck out as many batters (nine) in a shutout since CC Sabathia in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Buchanan allowed six hits and three runs with a walk and three strikeouts in six innings in a losing effort Saturday against the Pirates. He has pitched six or more innings in five of his nine career big league starts.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough start against Colorado on June 29, Gallardo bounced back with a stellar seven-inning, two-run outing in Cincinnati, in a tough-luck loss. Gallardo has quality starts in five of his last six outings.
away_pitcher_note: Kelly last pitched in the Majors on April 16, when he strained his left hamstring in Milwaukee. He'll return to the Majors after three rehab starts at Triple-A. In his last outing there on July 6, he allowed one run in 4 1/3 innings on 72 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers' top prospect was recalled Thursday, and he makes his second start of the season. He pitched 5 2/3 scoreless innings and gave up five hits and three walks to earn his first career big league victory on May 25.
away_pitcher_note: Despite allowing a baserunner in every inning Monday, Wainwright tossed seven scoreless innings, the ninth such outing this season in which he has gone at least seven without allowing a run. He has quality starts in 15 of 18 outings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta had his worst start of the season Tuesday against the Phillies, lasting only 4 1/3 innings and allowing nine earned runs on eight hits. Part of it was bad luck: The Phillies had four infield hits off the righty.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez, in his fifth start since joining the rotation on June 16, tossed a season-high six innings on Tuesday. He allowed four runs on eight hits, two of which were two-run homers. He has thrown 85 and 88 pitches his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his latest start, vs. the Phillies, Strasburg grinded through 5 2/3 innings, allowing two runs and striking out nine batters. Both runs were scored in the sixth inning, when Marlon Byrd singled to drive home Jimmy Rollins and Chase Utley.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse boasts six victories on the road, but his 3.99 ERA and .252 opponents' batting average in 11 outings outside of Wisconsin are both numbers that could improve.

home_pitcher_note: Roark was forced to move up in the rotation after Gio Gonzalez missed his bullpen on Thursday because of a canceled flight. Roark surrendered one earned run over seven innings in his last start against the Phillies on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Garza has taken no-hitters into the sixth and seventh innings of his last two starts against Cincinnati and Philadelphia. The righty has been very consistent lately, hurling quality starts in eight of his last nine.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez was scheduled to start Saturday but moved back a day when he missed the Nationals' workout on Thursday because of a canceled flight. He threw his bullpen on Friday, instead. The lefty's 22-inning scoreless streak ended July 10 vs. the O's.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo was tagged for five earned runs in 5 2/3 innings in his last outing against St. Louis. After four straight strong starts in mid-June, he's cooled off a bit, allowing 12 runs over his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: After Philadelphia tagged him for nine runs in 4 1/3 innings on July 8, Peralta bounced back with seven shutout innings against the Cardinals on July 13. Prior to that start, he had allowed 8+ hits in five straight.
away_pitcher_note: Latos gave up four runs (three earned) on three hits over five innings against the Pirates on July 11 before leaving with low back spasms. Prior to that, he had allowed four earned runs in 22 innings (1.64 ERA) over his previous three starts.

home_pitcher_note: After earning a promotion to Milwaukee with strong stats in Triple-A, Nelson was unimpressive in his first start after being called up, allowing eight runs on eight hits over 4 1/3 in a loss to the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey allowed three runs on two hits against the Cubs on July 10 before exiting after five-plus innings with a strained right knee. Over his prior two starts, he posted a 0.53 ERA (one earned run in 17 innings pitched).

home_pitcher_note: Despite allowing 10 hits to the Nationals in the second-half opener, Lohse was efficient in seven innings of one-run ball. He became the second pitcher this year to allow one run or less on 10+ hits, joining Cliff Lee.
away_pitcher_note: Leake started his second half with a series-opening loss to the Yanks. He struggled early but remained effective deep through the game, allowing four runs in seven innings. He's thrown over 100 pitches in three straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garza was blooped and bounced out of Saturday's start in Washington after 42 pitches, five runs and one out. The Brewers could bring him back early, but Garza said he'd rather the other four starters stay on schedule.
away_pitcher_note: Gee's first start after the All-Star break was also his first in 10 days, and just his second since returning from a two-month stint on the disabled list with a strained right lat. It was not his best; he gave up four runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: In three July starts, Gallardo has a 5.40 ERA, allowing 11 earned runs over 18 1/3 innings in 19 starts. He was unspectacular in his last outing, against Washington, giving up four runs over six innings in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Quietly, Wheeler is budding into a consistent young pitcher. He has thrown at least six innings and allowed exactly one run in each of his last four starts, compiling a 1.42 ERA over that stretch. He has 21 strikeouts and 10 walks in those outings.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta turned in his second great performance in a row on Monday, allowing one run on three hits over seven innings to the Reds. After being roughed up by the Phillies on July 8, Peralta has allowed one run in 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start back from his second disabled list stint of the season, Niese gave up four runs on 11 hits in Seattle and admitted to being "rusty." He'll try to establish some momentum in Milwaukee, where he made his big league debut in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson showed huge improvement in his second start since entering the rotation, allowing three runs on four hits over six-plus innings. He cruised through six two-hit innings before lapsing in the seventh.
away_pitcher_note: Over his last six starts, deGrom is 4-1 with a 1.59 ERA, 45 strikeouts and 11 walks in 39 2/3 innings. Since June 21, only deGrom and reigning NL Cy Young Award winner Clayton Kershaw has that many strikeouts with an ERA under 4.00.

home_pitcher_note: Odorizzi is coming off a win against his hometown team, the Cardinals, in his first career start in St. Louis. The rookie right-hander, who grew up half an hour away from Busch Stadium, went 5 2/3 innings, allowing two runs and striking out eight.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse was his usual reliable self vs. Cincinnati on Wednesday, giving up one run on four hits over 6 2/3 innings. He's submitted 15 quality starts in 22 attempts this season and has been the anchor of the Milwaukee rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Cobb had perhaps his best start of the season on July 23 vs. the Cardinals, tossing seven scoreless innings and striking out 10. Cobb is 3-0 with a 2.59 ERA in four July starts.
away_pitcher_note: Garza delivered the mother of all bouncebacks against the Mets, allowing only one run and two hits over eight innings, five days after he recorded only one out against the Nats. It snapped a two-start losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: Price is 6-0 in his last six starts, the latest win coming after the Rays rallied for four runs in the seventh inning to beat the Red Sox on Friday. Price, who has said he is pitching the best baseball of his career, went eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo has not won in six starts since his last victory on June 19. He allowed just four hits over 7 2/3 scoreless innings against the Mets. Gallardo struck out eight and did not walk a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright won his third 1-0 decision of the season on Sunday to become the National League's first 13-game winner. He has held an opponent scoreless in 10 of his 21 starts and pitched at least seven innings in 17 of them.
away_pitcher_note: Since allowing nine Phillies runs on July 8, Peralta has been solid, holding opponents to a .174 average and posting a 1.37 ERA over his last three starts. The streak started with seven good innings against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals acquired Masterson from the Indians in a July 30 trade and will throw him right into the rotation as they once again need a fifth starter. Masterson just wrapped up a two-start rehab assignment after dealing with right knee discomfort.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse has had some battles against his former team, evidenced by a 3-5 record and 4.04 ERA against the Cardinals in 10 starts. They've batted .302 against him, tied for fourth highest of any opponent.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey will be making his Cards debut and pitching on seven days' rest. He went 2-2 with a 3.55 ERA in four July starts. This will be his first career start at Busch Stadium. He pitched there in relief during the 2013 Fall Classic.
away_pitcher_note: Garza has rebounded nicely since a nightmare outing at Washington on July 19 in which he surrendered five runs and only recorded one out. In two starts since, he's allowed two runs and only seven hits in 15 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson was supposed to start over the weekend in St. Louis, but he was pushed back because of a blister on his right index finger and will make his first-ever start against the Giants instead.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum needs two victories to reach 100 for his career. He's 3-4 with a 5.44 ERA on the road, compared to 6-3 with a 3.51 ERA at home. Lifetime, Lincecum is 3-1 with a 3.46 ERA at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo extended his scoreless streak to 16 2/3 innings by limiting the red-hot Rays to a walk and four singles over seven innings in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong is coming off the first nine-inning complete game of his career and the second of the season by a Giants pitcher. The only other one was Tim Lincecum's June 25 no-hitter against San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: When he beat the Cardinals on Friday, Peralta tied Clayton Kershaw, Max Scherzer and Adam Wainwright for the Major League lead in victories, at 13. "I've improved in pretty much everything," Peralta said.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy's coming off an outing against the Mets in which he sustained the longest no-hit bid of his 13-year career -- 6 1/3 innings. He's 0-3 in four appearances at Miller Park despite a respectable 3.43 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse is coming off a rare bad outing as he allowed nine runs over four innings to the Cardinals on Saturday. Before that, he had recorded nine straight starts, allowing four or fewer earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: The Dodgers acquired Hernandez earlier this week from the Phillies. He has been sizzling as of late. He's posted a 3-0 record with a 1.88 ERA in his past four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers will make his first Major League start of the season after accumulating a 9-5 record and 2.55 ERA in 17 starts at Triple-A Nashville. Fiers has 25 starts for Milwaukee over the past two seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has lost three of his last four decisions, but he's 25-2 at Miller Park. The Angels ambushed him for four runs in the first inning, but he then allowed one hit in the next six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson was solid for six of his seven innings on Tuesday, allowing only a three-run home run to Pablo Sandoval. The right-hander has three straight quality starts after struggling against St. Louis his first time in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: The first three innings were rough for Kershaw against the Angels, but he rallied with four hitless innings for a no-decision. He's 3-0 lifetime at Miller Park, 4-3 lifetime against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta's streak of quality starts ended vs. the Rockies. He gave up a career-high 13 hits and a season-high nine runs over five innings. Arrieta only threw 78 pitches, but Colorado didn't miss many. At home he's 2-0 with a 1.85 ERA in seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo's 16 2/3-inning scoreless streak vanished quickly Wednesday, as the righty struggled and gave up three first-inning runs against the Giants. He battled command issues and lasted only four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks posted the longest outing of his short big league career in his last start against the Rox, going eight innings and giving up two runs. In his last 28 1/3 innings, he's given up four earned runs for a 1.27 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta set a career high with nine strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings of one-run ball in a win over the Giants, despite scattering seven hits. He's been fantastic over his last five starts, allowing six earned runs over 33 innings for a 1.64 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wada did not get a decision in his last outing, but did post his second quality start. The lefty held the Rays to two runs over six innings, walking one and striking out six, which matches his season high. This will be his first start vs. the Crew.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse saw his pitch count driven up by battling Dodgers batters but still managed a quality start on Friday, rebounding from a disastrous outing in St. Louis. He's racked up 17 quality starts in 23 tries this season.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson posted his first quality start at Wrigley Field since May 17 in his last outing, but it wasn't good enough for a win. The May game also is the last time he faced the Brewers, and he threw seven shutout innings at Wrigley in a 3-0 win.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers gave the Brewers exactly what they were hoping for in his first Major League start of 2014. Filling in for Matt Garza, he lasted eight innings against the Dodgers on Saturday, allowing one run off three hits.

home_pitcher_note: The long ball cost Greinke in his last start as he surrendered two in a game for the first time since April 6. He also surrendered four earned runs, marking only the fourth time he's done that in 24 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson turned in his fourth straight quality start, allowing two runs over six innings to the Dodgers on Sunday. He worked his way out of three consecutive jams with limited damage, stranding seven baserunners.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw played the role of stopper his last time out, halting a two-game slide by limiting Milwaukee to one run in eight innings and finishing 1-for-2 with an RBI, a run scored, a walk and a hit-by-pitch.
away_pitcher_note: The key stat from Gallardo's win over the Cubs on Aug. 11: Zero walks. That was the fifth time in 24 starts that he did not walk a batter, and he's allowed only four earned runs in 35 1/3 innings in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Haren has righted the ship after a disastrous five-start stretch that saw him compile a 10.03 ERA in 23 1/3 innings, giving up only three earned runs and issuing just one walk in his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta had won five consecutive starts and 10 of his previous 11 decisions but was defeated on Tuesday by an old foe. He fell to 0-3 this season against the Cubs, compared with 14-3 against his other opponents.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers moves up in the rotation because the Brewers are skipping Kyle Lohse, but he'll be throwing on regular rest because of Monday's off-day. Fiers is coming off a 14-strikeout, six-inning performance against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Happ entered his last outing with a 1.71 ERA since the All-Star break, but hit a bit of a rough patch vs. the Mariners. The veteran lefty surrendered a costly two-run single to Dustin Ackley in the fifth and allowed five runs in his six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson's recent opponents -- Wainwright, Bailey, deGrom, Lincecum, Kershaw and Greinke -- have produced five Cy Young Awards and five of baseball's last seven no-hitters. Now comes 2012 NL Cy Young Award winner Dickey.
away_pitcher_note: Dickey allowed a two-run homer in the first inning of his last start but that was all it took to take the loss. He didn't allow another run as he completed his second consecutive quality start but suffered from a lack of run support.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo is 12-4 with a 2.57 ERA in 23 starts plus one relief appearance against the Pirates. He's already started four times against them this season, three of which became Brewers wins.
away_pitcher_note: A rematch of an earlier duel, in which on June 8 Locke dropped a 1-0 gem to Gallardo - the first of six quality starts in which he hasn't gotten the win. Locke's control has slipped a bit but still has walked only 19 in 14 starts.

home_pitcher_note: By beating the Dodgers on Sunday, Peralta joined NL Central foes Johnny Cueto and Adam Wainwright with an MLB-best 15 wins. No Brewer has led his league in victories since Pete Vuckovich in strike-shortened 1981.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran sports a 2-to-1 strikeout-to-walk ratio -- something he hasn't had for a full season since 2008. Volquez has a 25-12 vs. NL Central teams over his career, including a 4-1 record in eight starts in Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Fiers labored through 44 pitches in the first two innings before retiring the final 18 batters he faced. He's thrown three stellar starts since entering the rotation in place of the injured Matt Garza.
away_pitcher_note: Worley comes off his poorest start of the season, but already rebounded by blanking Atlanta for five innings after surrendering six first-inning runs. Hurt by the long ball in last two starts after giving up a total of four in first nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Stults will attempt to remain undefeated in August, as he's 3-0 with a 1.46 ERA in four starts this month heading into this start against the Brewers. He has a 3.18 ERA in his last 11 starts, seven on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse skipped his last turn through the rotation due to a sore ankle that was hampering his mechanics, especially in his last three-inning outing. He threw a full bullpen session Friday and said he felt ready to go.

home_pitcher_note: Ross was a hard-luck loser his last time out against the Dodgers. After taking a two-hit shutout into the eighth inning, he allowed a two-run home run in a 2-1 loss. He did establish the club record for most consecutive quality starts (12).
away_pitcher_note: Nelson was not sharp in his last start against Toronto, allowing four runs on nine hits over 5 2/3 innings. It snapped a streak of five straight quality starts, and afterward Nelson acknowledged he needs to mix up pitches better.

home_pitcher_note: Despaigne will continue his fight against regression vs. the Brewers. In his first five starts, he was 2-1 with a 1.31 ERA. In his last six, he's 1-4 with a 5.81 ERA. He's allowed a combined seven runs in the first inning of his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Historically dominant against the Pirates, Gallardo struggled against them on Friday, lasting only five innings while allowing six runs (three earned) on eight hits and three walks. Only 57 of his 99 pitches were strikes.

home_pitcher_note: The last time the Giants won a game Vogelsong started at AT&T Park? Seven home starts ago, back on May 24. That's despite his 3.22 home ERA, which is 1.21 lower than his road ERA. Overall, they've lost each of his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: After 3 2/3 hitless innings Saturday, Peralta's night unraveled against the Pirates as he lasted only five innings, allowing eight runs (seven earned) on seven hits and three walks. He allowed three home runs for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy's August ERA is 2.94, his best month of the season except April (2.87). His WHIP (walks and hits per inning) as a Giant is 1.21 in six starts, an improvement over his 1.43 figure in 20 games with Boston.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers posted a fourth straight stellar start Sunday, allowing only two runs on two Pirates hits over seven innings. In four starts in place of Matt Garza, Fiers has given up 10 hits and four walks in 28 innings, good for a 0.50 WHIP.

home_pitcher_note: An overlooked benefit of Bumgarner's sparkling one-hitter last Tuesday against Colorado was that it gave the bullpen some much-needed rest. With four complete games, he has doubled the career total he had entering the season.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse skipped a start to get treatment for a right ankle injury and returned from an 11-day layoff with some rust (four walks) but better results (six innings, four hits, one run against). He's 8-5 on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Turner threw 66 pitches over 3 2/3 innings in his first start for the Cubs on Wednesday in Cincinnati. The plan is for Chicago to get a look at the right-hander, acquired from the Marlins, in the final month and continue to stretch him out.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson, optioned to Class A in a paper move that opened a spot for relief help, will "return" to make his first career start against the Cubs. He faced them twice in relief last year, working two scoreless innings each time.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta didn't have his command in his last start vs. the Reds, and he threw 96 pitches over four innings, matching his shortest outing of the year. He gave up six runs for the second time this season. The Reds also stole six bases against him.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo was in line to win after working six hard-fought innings against the Padres last week, but a lead escaped Francisco Rodriguez in the ninth inning. He's 9-3 with a 3.00 ERA in 18 career starts against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks finished August 4-0 with a 1.69 ERA in six starts. This will be his second outing vs. the Brewers, who he held to six hits over 7 1/3 scoreless innings on Aug. 12. In his last start, he held the Cardinals to two runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander returns for his first start since Aug. 3, when he strained a left rib-cage muscle in a start at St. Louis. Garza last pitched in a three-inning simulated game, so his pitch count will be limited.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta has turned in two lousy starts in a row, including a six-run, nine-hit outing against the Giants in which he lasted a season-low three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Recovered from a right shoulder stress reaction, Wacha will be making his first start since June 17. He threw 34 pitches in a rehab start on August 31 and will be limited to 50-60 in this outing. Marco Gonzales is expected to back him up.

home_pitcher_note: All five of Fiers' starts this season have met the definition of "quality," including a seven-inning, three-run outing against the Giants on Saturday. He was on the wrong side of Jake Peavy's 7 1/3-inning no-hit bid.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey had a troublesome start to his last outing, but kept the Cubs scoreless over his final four-plus innings to position the Cards for the win. He has allowed two or fewer earned runs in five of his six starts since joining the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has not been particularly sharp since skipping a start with a sprained ankle and was blunt in assessing his last start against the Giants. "I'll just make it simple for you: It was terrible execution," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn had a laborious afternoon on Monday, but he kept the Cards in the game by limiting the Pirates to three runs in six innings. He lasted that deep despite throwing 52 pitches through two innings, and he stranded eight runners.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson will make the 10th start of this particular tenure in the Brewers' rotation, with uncertainty to follow. The team will probably revert back to a five-man rotation, though manager Ron Roenicke has not revealed his plan.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright showed better overall command of his repertoire on Tuesday, though the Pirates hit three of his mistakes out of the park. He's allowed three-plus runs in five straight starts but has also finished at least six innings in each of those.

home_pitcher_note: Pushed from the series against his nemeses, the Cardinals, Gallardo will instead pitch against a Marlins team he has handled to the tune of a 5-0 record and 1.12 ERA in seven career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Penny didn't make it past the third in his last start vs. the Mets Tuesday. In three frames, he gave up four runs on seven hits. When he makes his second straight start Monday, he'll face a team against whom he has a 5.07 ERA in eight career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garza's return from a month-long stint on the DL for a rib-cage strain wasn't great: He surrendered six runs on eight hits in only three innings. But the good news was that he felt healthy.
away_pitcher_note: The Marlins needed Koehler to turn in a long outing, and he did that Wednesday, throwing 103 pitches in seven innings and fanning a career-high 10. A two-run homer put him in line for a loss before Miami picked him up.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching the first game of the Brewers' biggest series of the season to date, Peralta fell into a 2-0 hole against the Cardinals before recording his second out. He's 1-4 in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cosart was dominant through seven innings on Friday, but he ran into some trouble in the eighth and exited after 7 2/3 innings having struck out six. Before allowing one in the fifth, he'd faced 207 consecutive batters without giving up a homer.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers has exceeded expectations since the Brewers promoted him to the rotation in the wake of Matt Garza's oblique injury. All six of his outings have been quality starts, and only once has he surrendered more than two runs.
away_pitcher_note: The fourth inning got away from Eovaldi in his last turn vs the Braves on Saturday. After loading the bases on an intentional walk, he gave up a two-run single to the pitcher. He settled down to make it through 6 1/3 innings, but allowed three runs.

home_pitcher_note: In three starts since taking time off to heal a sprained ankle, Lohse has allowed 13 earned runs, 17 hits and eight walks in 15 2/3 innings. "He's a 'feel' guy, and he's lost his feel right now," catcher Jonathan Lucroy said.
away_pitcher_note: Corcino starts instead of Mat Latos, who has been sidelined with a bone bruise in his right elbow.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo has lost three of four starts since Aug. 16 with one no-decision. In each of those losses, he has not lasted longer than five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Holmberg replaced injured righty Dylan Axelrod two batters into Monday's game vs. the Cardinals and delivered 5 2/3 scoreless innings. While he had to work out of a couple of self-created jams, the club felt Holmberg deserves another look.

home_pitcher_note: Garza has not been particularly sharp in his two starts off a month-long stint on the disabled list. He needed 84 pitches for four innings against the Marlins over the weekend.
away_pitcher_note: Leake tossed six innings, allowing three runs on eight hits while striking out eight in a win over the Cardinals last Tuesday. In three starts against Milwaukee this season, the right-hander is 1-2 with a 4.74 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn was denied his 16th win on Thursday despite allowing one run while pitching his second career complete game. Lynn has allowed two or fewer earned runs in 11 of his last 13 starts and continues to be at his best deep in games.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta turned in a much-needed quality start in his last outing after the Brewers had lost 13 of 14, allowing one run on five hits in 6 2/3 innings in a 4-1 victory over Miami. Prior to that, however, the right-hander had lost three straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright picked up his 18th win on Friday. In his last two starts, Wainwright has given up two runs in 17 innings. Wainwright didn't walk anybody Friday, a sign that his control appears to be back after a shaky August.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers is making his first start since hitting Marlins slugger Giancarlo Stanton with a pitch, resulting in facial fractures. In seven starts since being called up Aug. 9 to fill in for Matt Garza, Fiers is 6-1 with a 1.74 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Miller picked up his 10th win on Saturday, going six innings and giving up one run. Miller has given up just three runs in his last 27 innings, a streak that coincides with his ability to mix in his secondary pitches with his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse appears to have recovered from an ankle injury that cost him one start in mid-August and limited his effectiveness in a couple others. In his last start last Friday against Cincinnati, he allowed two runs on five hits in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Locke has alternated poor and strong starts for a month, and he's on schedule for another good one. He has held the Brewers to a .122 average in two starts this season and is averaging 6 2/3 innings in 10 home starts.
away_pitcher_note: After missing the Cardinals for the second straight series, Gallardo draws a much more favorable matchup. He's 12-5 with a 2.67 ERA in 25 games (24 starts) against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez is 2-1 vs. the Brewers this season and has improved his career record against NL Central teams to 27-12 -- accounting for 42 percent of his total wins. He is 4-0 with a 1.73 ERA over his last eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Garza has gradually worked back to full strength since a month-long stint on the DL. He's worked three innings, four innings and six innings in his three starts so far, and should be back to the 100-pitch mark now.

home_pitcher_note: Worley steps back into his original rotation spot, after moving aside for one turn to make way for Charlie Morton (sports hernia) and make his first start in 11 days. His seven wins are tied for second on the team since mid-June.
away_pitcher_note: Thanks to a resurgent slider, Peralta has authored a turnaround. He had a 4.81 ERA and a .294 opponents' average in August, and has lowered that to a 2.75 ERA and a .243 batting average against in three September starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto needs two victories to reach 20 and is coming off one of his poorer outings of the season at Chicago, where he gave up a season-high five walks along with six earned runs in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers was just fine in his first work since a scary incident involving Marlins star Mike Stanton, taking a no-hitter into the sixth inning and a shutout bid into the seventh against the Cardinals on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: In two starts since joining the rotation, totaling 11 2/3 innings, Corcino has given up four runs and five hits. With four walks last time out vs. the Cubs, he needs to improve command.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse is coming off consecutive quality starts, a good sign he's moved past the ankle injury that compromised his August. In his last start at St. Louis on Thursday, Lohse needed only 88 pitches for 7 1/3 fine innings.

home_pitcher_note: Holmberg has allowed three earned runs over his last 18 2/3 innings as he rebounded from a lousy first impression. In a 2-1 loss on Friday at St. Louis, he made two mistake pitches for back-to-back first-inning homers but turned in a solid start.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo featured his best curveball of the season in his last start Friday and struck out 11 Pirates over seven scoreless innings, his first double-digit performance in more than two years.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson is stepping in for Matt Garza, who was scratched because of shoulder tightness. Nelson is 2-7 with a 4.38 ERA in 11 big league starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Jokisch's first big league start. The lefty has made three relief appearances since he was called up to the Cubs in early September. At Triple-A Iowa, he was 9-10 with a 3.58 ERA in 26 starts, striking out 143 over 158 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off consecutive seven-inning gems, Peralta has a chance to join Yovani Gallardo (2011) and Chris Capuano ('05) as the only Brewers pitchers since 1992 to win at least 17 decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Wada thought he was done after his outing Sept. 18, but the Cubs will give the lefty one more start. Wada beat the Brewers on Aug. 13 at Wrigley, giving up two runs over 6 2/3. The team needs to decide whether to pick up his option for 2015.

home_pitcher_note: Burned by back-to-back Reds home runs in his most recent start, Fiers will get a chance to author a positive finish to a tremendous bounce-back season that thrust him back into the Brewers' future plans.
away_pitcher_note: Rookie Kyle Hendricks was slated to start the season finale but the Cubs decided the right-hander had reached his innings limit for the year, so Turner will get one more start. This will be his sixth start with the Cubs and first since Sept. 21.

away_pitcher_note: In his final spring start, a win against the Rangers, Kendrick built his pitch count to 90. He hopes his developing curveball augments his fastball, cutter and changeup. It's his first opener start.

home_pitcher_note: Tired of landing on the disabled list in four straight seasons, Garza worked with his younger brother over the winter to simplify his delivery. In his 17 quality starts last season, Garza had a 2.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The development of a split-finger changeup makes Lyles a more diverse pitcher than in the past. Lyles hopes results this April are like the first month last year, when he went 3-0 with a 2.70 ERA in six starts.

home_pitcher_note: The 25-year-old Dominican is coming off of a breakthrough season in which he led the team in victories, innings, strikeouts and quality starts, and posted a pair of five-game winning streaks.
away_pitcher_note: Butler was limited to three starts last season because of right shoulder and rotator cuff issues, but he reported to camp stronger and won the job with his overall work in six Spring Training starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers made a last-minute switch to their starting rotation that positioned Fiers to open a series against the division-rival Pirates. Manager Ron Roenicke said he valued Fiers' experience over the younger Jimmy Nelson.
away_pitcher_note: Locke makes the start he earned by prevailing over Vance Worley in a tight spring competition for an open spot in the Pirates' rotation. The lefty pitched two-hit ball for six innings in his only Miller Park start last season.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson finished his first Spring Training as a full-fledged member of the Major League starting rotation with a 6.23 ERA, and that didn't count the 10 runs he surrendered last week in a Minor League game.
away_pitcher_note: The "loser" of the rotation showdown with Jeff Locke got paroled from the bullpen when Charlie Morton went on the disabled list (recovering from labrum surgery). Worley was one of only 30 starters with 110-plus innings and a sub-3.00 ERA in 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse cruised through Spring Training until being roughed up by the Cubs in his final tune-up, and he was roughed up again on Opening Day against the Rockies. Colorado's eight earned runs matched Lohse's career high.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates are touted for having several high-profile pitching prospects, but for now this 25th-round 2010 Draft choice gets the call to step in for Francisco Liriano, who is on paternity leave. Sadler went 11-4 last season in Triple-A.

home_pitcher_note: By virtue of a rainout, Wainwright unexpectedly draws the fourth home opener of his career. He's 1-1 with a 5.51 ERA in the previous three. Wainwright threw six shutout innings in his Opening Night start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies were so on top of Garza's pitches at Miller Park that he worried he was tipping, and switched up the signs. Now he'll face another proficient offense during the Cardinals' home opener.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn opened his season with a quality start, but also a loss, as he was undone by a hit batter and errant pickoff throw. It marked just the second April loss of his career, as his 12 April wins since 2012 are most in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta looked sharp in his first start, allowing just two runs in seven innings in a loss to the Rockies. He was 3-1 with a 2.18 ERA in five starts against the Cardinals last year.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey worked six innings in his season debut April 10, allowing a pair of two-run Joey Votto homers in a 5-4 Cardinals loss. The 36-year-old right-hander ranks among the top 10 active pitchers in wins and strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers allowed five runs in five innings to the Pirates in his first start, giving up a homer and four doubles. He is 2-1 with a 1.30 ERA in six games, four starts, during his career against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Worley struggled in his season debut Saturday, giving up six runs on seven hits and two walks while striking out four in 6 1/3 innings. Worley will get a rematch with the Brewers, looking to get on track and recapture his 2014 form.
away_pitcher_note: This will be a rematch from Saturday in Milwaukee, where Nelson debuted his new curveball and set a career high with nine strikeouts. The trick will be adjusting now that the Pirates have had a look.

home_pitcher_note: Locke was able to get his fastball in on Brewers right-handed hitters in beating them last Friday, and his challenge now will be to respond to their expect adjustments. He's owned Aramis Ramirez (2-for-17).
away_pitcher_note: It's a rematch with Andrew McCutchen, who hit a misplaced slider for a go-ahead, three-run home run to beat Lohse on Sunday at Miller Park. Before that pitch, it appeared Lohse had righted some recent command woes.

home_pitcher_note: Cole kicked off the Pirates' homestand with a win over the Tigers, carrying a 1-hitter into the seventh before leaving with the bases loaded and no outs. Cole has racked up 14 strikeouts and only four walks in 11 innings over his first two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Downright ebullient out of Spring Training, Garza is searching for that good feeling in the regular season. In a win against the Cardinals, he was forced to work almost exclusively with his fastball. The slider remains a project.

home_pitcher_note: Six pitches into his start against the Cardinals, Peralta had surrendered three hits and two runs. The Cardinals were swinging early and often and Peralta was leaving pitches up in the strike zone with similar frequency.
away_pitcher_note: The seven scoreless innings DeSclafani threw vs. the Cubs in a win on Tuesday marked a career-high. He was taken out after 97 pitches by manager Bryan Price, who indicated that he wouldn't be afraid to extend the rookie longer later in the season.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers gave up two runs in 5 2/3 innings and lost Thursday in St. Louis. He lost to the Pirates in his season debut, striking out eight while allowing five runs over five innings. He's permitted 14 hits in 10 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: During a four-inning performance vs. the Cubs on Wednesday, Marquis was not locating his sinker well. It not only was up in the strike zone, but pitches were also drifting back over the plate.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson gave up three runs (two earned) on five hits and struck out three in a rematch with the Pirates on Friday. He'll face the Reds at Miller Park, where he threw seven two-hit innings and struck out nine in his 2015 debut.
away_pitcher_note: In a 6-1 loss at St. Louis Friday, a risky decision backfired on Cueto. He intentionally walked Jon Jay to load the bases for Yadier Molina, who hit an elevated sinker for a three-run double in the seventh for the go-ahead runs.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse's early struggles continued against the Pirates on Saturday, when he allowed six runs on six hits and three walks. Command has been the issue so far for Lohse, who believes he's close to turning his season around.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey acknowledged the "need to sharpen up some things" following a 5-2 loss in St. Louis, where he allowed five runs in 5 2/3 innings. He was done in by a two-out, two-run double by Matt Carpenter in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: Garza emerged from Spring Training excited about his rediscovered slider, but he has struggled in the regular season and has a dissapointing ratio of strikeouts (nine) to walks (nine).
away_pitcher_note: Since winning a rotation job, Martinez has shown himself a more complete pitcher by complementing his fastball with a nice changeup-slider mix and also pulling back on velocity in order to improve command and stamina.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta is facing the Cardinals for the second time after allowing four runs on 10 hits in only five innings at Busch Stadium. His career ERA against the Cards is up to 4.58.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright finished eight innings in his most recent start, becoming the first Cards starter to go that far. He's still not pleased with the crispness of his pitches following a shortened spring, but he's still finding a way to get the results.

away_pitcher_note: Lynn has allowed one earned run in each of his first three starts, even though his last two haven't been especially sharp. Lynn is looking forward to pitching on regular rest after making his last two starts following a week off.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis gave up five runs on nine hits in five innings in his last start, but evened his record at 1-1 thanks to an offense that pounded out 16 runs vs the Brewers. He has allowed 21 hits in 15 innings in his three starts, but also has 21 K's.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has been a bright spot for the Brewers, accounting for two of the team's three quality starts after three full turns through the starting rotation. He's coming off an eight-inning no-decision in a duel with Johnny Cueto.

away_pitcher_note: Lohse had surrendered at least four earned runs and at least six hits in each of his first three starts before turning in a seven-inning gem against the Reds on Thursday. It helped snap an eight-game Brewers losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: Lorenzen will be recalled from Triple-A Louisville to take the rotation spot of Homer Bailey, who's on the DL with a right elbow ligament sprain. The 23-year-old Lorenzen has only two seasons in the Minors but a full selection of pitches.
away_pitcher_note: A six-inning, three-run quality start against the Cardinals marked progress for Garza, who remained frustrated after a third loss in four outings. "It's about time for that progress to kick in to results," he said.

home_pitcher_note: Lester will get a chance to face another NL Central team when he meets the Brewers. The lefty is still looking for his first win with the Cubs, but he was encouraged by his last outing, when he struck out 10 over six innings vs. the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta has given up 32 hits, but walked only six batters, over his first 25 innings. Chicago's Starlin Castro and Anthony Rizzo are a combined 22-for-48 (.458) with seven home runs vs. Peralta.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta struck out six over six innings in his last start against the Reds, retiring the first 11 batters. At Wrigley, he is 1-1 with a 1.98 ERA so far. In his career, he's 2-2 with a 2.59 ERA vs. the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers has almost twice as many hits and walks allowed (36) as innings pitched (18 2/3). Anthony Rizzo of the Cubs was 5-for-6 with a home run and a double off Fiers last season.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel threw eight shutout innings against the Pirates on Monday night. He has walked one and struck out 23 over 25 1/3 innings. The key? Fastball command. And it helps that he and catcher Miguel Montero are on the same page.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson will try to rebound against the Cubs after his ERA rose from 1.35 to 4.03 during a 9-6 loss to the Reds on Monday. Chris Coghlan is 4-for-6 with two doubles and a home run vs. Nelson.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse still hasn't rounded into form, but appears to be getting closer after lasting seven innings in each of his last two starts. He surrendered three home runs to the Reds on Tuesday, but limited the damage to four runs.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw gave up another home run, this time to Buster Posey, but the ace got through seven innings without a walk against the Giants and pitched well enough to deserve a win.

home_pitcher_note: Garza has pitched in 226 regular-season games and spent parts of five seasons with NL teams, yet has never faced the Dodgers. He has faced six players on L.A.'s roster, including Jimmy Rollins (26 at-bats).
away_pitcher_note: He again was the stopper, winning after a Dodgers loss, but Greinke had to battle with runners in scoring position the first four innings and a pitch count that limited him to six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta will make his 40th career start at Miller Park, where he's 18-16 with a 4.04 ERA in 39 starts plus one relief appearance. He's 0-2 there so far this year, after going 10-6 last season.
away_pitcher_note: Wieland is promoted from Triple-A for this start, making him the Dodgers' ninth starter this year. Wieland was 3-0 at Triple-A, and says his arm is finally strong after Tommy John surgery.

home_pitcher_note: After striking out 12 Cubs in six innings last Saturday for his first quality start, Fiers goes from one good matchup on paper to another. He's 3-0 with a 1.08 ERA in two starts and one relief appearance against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Frias earned a second shot at Brandon McCarthy's rotation spot by getting into the sixth inning without allowing a run to the D-backs, enjoying the luxury of a big early lead from his offense.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson has been the Brewers' most consistent starting pitcher despite an extremely unfavorable schedule. This is the third straight occasion on which he's faced the same team in consecutive starts.
away_pitcher_note: This will be a rematch for Hammel, who did not get a decision in his last start vs. the Brewers at home. He gave up three runs over six innings and battled a cracked nail on his right middle finger. He's 5-0 in seven career starts vs. the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: When Lohse is "on," he is quick and efficient. He was not either of those things in his most recent outing against the Dodgers, who pushed Lohse's pitch count to 103 in only five innings. He's worked only one quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Wood is coming off a rough outing against the Cardinals. He gave up six runs on six hits over five-plus innings, including a grand slam to Mark Reynolds. This is his fourth start on the road. He's looking for his first win away from Wrigley.

home_pitcher_note: Garza has been better in his last three outings, meeting the definition of quality start each time. But he has surrendered five home runs in those games and won only one of them.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks did not get a decision in his last outing against the Cardinals, giving up four runs on six hits over five innings. He relies on his command, and has struggled getting a good feel for his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta is coming off his finest outing of the season, a three-run, eight-inning performance against the Dodgers in which he was still hitting 96 mph with ease in the eighth.
away_pitcher_note: After serving his five-game suspension, Samardzija returns to the mound for this series and road-trip opener in Milwaukee. Samardzija helped end a five-game losing streak by allowing two runs over seven innings vs. Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers has struck out 20 batters over 11 innings in his past two starts, including an "immaculate inning" against the Dodgers on Thursday in which he struck out all three batters he faced on just nine pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Sale followed the same path of Jeff Samardzija, by pitching against the Tigers and then beginning his five-game suspension Thursday. Sale is on a streak of two straight non-quality starts for the first time since the 2013 season.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Nelson's third straight start against a team from Chicago, coming off consecutive starts against the Cubs. He set a career high with 11 strikeouts on Friday against the Cubs, but also served up three home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana needed 107 pitches to get through five innings in his last start against the Tigers, allowing two runs and fanning eight. He is 0-2 in his last three starts but has yielded just five earned runs in his last 19 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Can anything stop Colon at age 41? Last week, he beat the Phillies despite giving up four runs over six innings in his worst start of the year. Colon will pitch twice more before his 42nd birthday -- not that age has done anything to slow him yet.
away_pitcher_note: Kyle Lohse hasn't had an ERA like this -- 7.03 after 106-pitch, five-inning, four run slog against the Cubs on Saturday -- since 2010, when he had the right forearm surgery that would revive his career.

home_pitcher_note: DeGrom's fastball location was off last time out at Wrigley Field, and it showed throughout his third loss in four decisions. The Mets see it as nothing more than a rough patch, figuring deGrom will right himself as he did at points last season.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling at the start of the season, Garza has authored four consecutive quality starts. He's 1-0 with a 1.64 ERA in three career starts against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Quite strong over the first five innings of his big league debut Tuesday, Syndergaard caved for three runs in the sixth during a loss to the Cubs. He'll make his Citi Field debut Sunday against the Brewers looking for his first career win.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta is coming off an odd outing in which he threw 46 pitches and didn't allow a ball out of the infield through four innings, then struggled through a 38-pitch fifth. He has thrown four straight quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lobstein's stretch of starts with seven-plus innings ended Wednesday with six runs on seven hits over 2 1/3 innings against the Twins. He'll face a Brewers lineup struggling mightily this season against left-handed pitching.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers retired the first 11 batters in his most recent outing before an error and an infield hit allowed the next two men to reach base. He's produced 49 strikeouts in 35 1/3 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers have 51 hits over 37 1/3 innings against Sanchez, but he hasn't faced them since 2012, before his trade to Detroit. He tossed eight innings of one-run ball with nine strikeouts against the Twins in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson had never surrendered multiple home runs in any of his first 18 Major League starts, but he's allowed a combined five over his last two outings. He's 0-2 with a 7.07 ERA in three starts on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Greene pitched five scoreless innings against the Cardinals on Friday before having to leave early with mild ulnar tendinitis. Greene underwent an MRI on Saturday that came back clean. He has given up one run on his past 13 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse carried a 7.03 ERA into the Brewers' road trip and lowered it to 5.85 with eight outstanding innings against the Mets. By Bill James' "game score," it was one of the eight best outings of Lohse's career.

home_pitcher_note: Though Teheran has proven effective in two of the three starts he's completed since making a commitment to rely on his fastball, his inconsistent command has prevented him from consistently maximizing the value of his slider.
away_pitcher_note: Garza is coming off the worst start of his career, a 10-run, 3 1/3-inning nightmare against the Mets. Nine of those runs came during a 15-batter, 10-run rally in the fourth inning, which Garza departed after only one out.

home_pitcher_note: Alex Wood, who was scheduled to start, was a late scratch because of a stomach virus. Stults has made seven starts, walking only eight batters in 48 1/3 innings. His last appearance, and last start, was on May 13.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta had authored four consecutive quality starts before allowing five earned runs on nine hits in five innings at Citi Field last weekend. He owns a 1.50 ERA in three career starts against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: After coming one out shy of a no-hitter on Sunday, Miller owned a Major League-best 1.33 ERA. He has allowed one run and recorded 20 strikeouts over 25 innings in his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers will face the Braves for the first time in his career, completing the National League circuit (minus Milwaukee, for whom he's played his entire career).

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz endured some growing pains as he flashed some promise and also his youth while allowing a career-high five runs against the Rays on Tuesday. He acknowledged that he needs to prove more consistent with his command.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing five home runs over his previous two starts, Nelson was a ground-ball machine against the Tigers on Tuesday, with no fly balls hit to the outfield over his final five innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: For the first time this season, Lohse is coming off consecutive quality starts. He cruised for eight innings against the Mets on May 15, then practiced damage control against the Tigers on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum's ERA is his lowest after eight starts since he fashioned a 1.76 ERA early in 2010. His strikeouts-per-nine-innings ratio is his lowest ever, reflecting his emphasis on guile rather than pure stuff.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing 10 runs against the Mets on May 21, Garza surrendered just two hits through the first six innings of Thursday's tough-luck loss in Atlanta. He's allowed three runs or less in five of nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner's 5.2 strikeout-to-walk ratio is his best yet. He approaches the end of a month in which he has recorded a 2.95 career ERA, his best for any month except September/October (2.56).

home_pitcher_note: Fiers has had a superb May, allowing two runs or fewer in four of five starts and fanning 35 against 10 walks. This will be his first time with three days' rest.between starts.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong's working on leveling his home vs. road performance. His ERA away from AT&T Park is 7.43, compared to 1.46 at home.

home_pitcher_note: The 6-6, 245-pound right-hander continues to come up big for Milwaukee. He's allowed three runs across his last two outings (for a 1.97 ERA in 13 2/3 innings), and has lasted into the sixth in his past five starts and seven of nine on the year.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has altered between outstanding and so-so starts in his last six games. It seems one inning, or stretch of hitters, often trips him up. Last time out against the Cubs, all four of his runs allowed were in the fifth.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse allowed five runs in 5 1/3 innings -- four of them coming in the sixth -- in his last outing while striking out seven. He's 4-3 with a 4.46 ERA in 13 career starts against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Hellickson seems to be rounding into form after a tough start. His last two outings have been his best this year. He worked a combined 12 2/3 innings and allowed just five runs.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old sinkerballer will come up from Double-A Biloxi to replace an injured Wily Peralta. Wagner has only nine career starts above Class A, but has been outstanding for the last year-and-a-half in the Minors.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson has been the D-backs' most consistent starter this year, but he has received the lowest run support. Over his past five starts, he has a 1.39 ERA but only one win to show for it.
