away_pitcher_note: Fiers did his job on three days' rest last time out, delivering five innings of two-run ball. This time, he will be pitching on regular rest.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Lynn's third start of the season against Milwaukee. He lasted only five innings in the previous two, allowing a combined seven earned runs on 16 hits. Lynn has finished seven innings just twice in 10 starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Cravy will make his Major League debut. He's not overpowering, but owns a 3.71 ERA in seven Minor League seasons and a strikeout-to-walk ratio of nearly three to one. He went eight innings in his most recent Triple-A start.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey has made two scoreless seven-inning starts this year, the first of which came in Milwaukee on April 16. He's gone at least seven innings deep in five of 10 starts this season and has a 1.30 ERA at Busch Stadium in 2015.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has surrendered six home runs over his last five starts, all in home games. On the road, Nelson has a 3.59 ERA in 12 career games.

home_pitcher_note: Gibson dominated in the month of May, going 3-1 with a 1.36 ERA, and has allowed three earned runs or fewer in each of his last nine starts. He'll be making Friday's start on extra rest.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers are puzzled about why Lohse has struggled so mightily this season. "He's not the aggressor right now," manager Craig Counsell said. "It's like he's playing defense the whole game."

home_pitcher_note: The Twins are in need of a starter after playing in a doubleheader on Wednesday in Boston, and they decided to stick with an in-house option. Graham, 25, has posted a 3.10 ERA with 17 strikeouts and seven walks in 20 1/3 innings in relief this year.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing 19 earned runs and 23 hits over his previous three starts, Garza delivered five innings of strong relief in the Brewers' 17-inning win over Arizona on May 31. Could it be the outing that gets him going?

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey took a loss on Tuesday despite holding the Red Sox to one run on six hits in seven innings. The sinkerballer has proven himself to be one of Minnesota's most reliable starters this year.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers' last two starts have been bullpen-savers. He pitched six scoreless innings for a 1-0 win over the Cardinals in his last start, a day after the Brewers blew out their bullpen in a 17-inning game against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Going for a seventh straight win, Burnett takes on a Milwaukee team against which he is 0-4 with the Pirates. He hasn't faced the Brewers since '13, but their current players have accumulated 130 at-bats against him -- with one homer.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing five runs (four earned) in the first inning against the Cardinals on Wednesday, Nelson has surrendered 11 earned runs and 14 hits in that frame in 11 starts. The Brewers will work with Nelson on a fix.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano takes another stab at adjusting his home/road splits, which are totally opposite to what they were in 2013, when he dominated in PNC Park (8-1, 1.47 ERA). This season, he has an ERA of 6.04 at home compared to 1.52 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Jungmann, who is ranked as the club's No. 13 prospect, will be making his Major League debut. He was the Brewers' top Draft pick in 2011 at No. 12 overall. The righty was 2-3 with a 6.37 ERA at Triple-A this season.

home_pitcher_note: Morton will seek a couple of career firsts: He has never begun a season 4-0, and has never won four straight starts in a season. But he'll have to be sharper than in his previous start, when the offense picked him up in a 10-8 decision.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse struggled again in his last outing, surrendering a five-run lead and taking an no-decision. The veteran is now 3-6 with a 6.59 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Matt Garza is just 4-7 on the year with a 5.09 ERA, but those numbers aren't indicative of his most recent performances. The righty said he has been getting back to pitching like himself, which has led to success lately.
away_pitcher_note: Roark started '15 in the bullpen, but injuries in the rotation forced him back into a starting role. Since his first start May 25, he's gone 2-0 with a 3.78 ERA. His last start vs. the Crew saw him throw a career-high 112 pitches over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers gave up two runs in 4 1/3 innings in his last start and he said he felt like he had to battle through every pitch.The righty is 2-6 with a 4.06 ERA on the season.
away_pitcher_note: A Wisconsin native, Zimmermann has stifled the Brewers in his career, holding them to just eight runs over 30 2/3 innings. He's been even better at Miller Park, holding a 1.50 ERA there.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson has been much better at home on the road, posting a 3.38 ERA and better than five strikeouts for every walk at Miller Park. On the road, he has a 4.66 ERA and 1.46 strikeouts per walk.
away_pitcher_note: Ross made his Major League debut last week against the Cubs, taking the loss after a five-inning start. The 22-year-old right-hander is the youngest player on the Nationals' roster and holds a 3.74 career ERA in the Minors.

home_pitcher_note: "I thought he'd respond to the stage, and he did," Brewers manager Craig Counsell said of Jungmann's impressive seven-inning Major League debut in Pittsburgh. This will mark his first start in front of the home fans.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer allowed only one run through the first six innings of his last start before struggling in the seventh vs. the Yankees. He hasn't faced the Brewers since 2009, but holds a 2.77 career ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has lots of experience against the Royals (20 starts plus one relief appearance) but has faced only one Kansas City batter in more than 10 at-bats. Omar Infante is 6-for-32 (.188) against Lohse.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez has only dropped one decision in his last seven starts, recording six or more strikeouts in his last three. He is 5-1 with a 4.88 ERA in nine starts at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: His five innings of scoreless relief in the Brewers' 17-inning win over Arizona seemed to do the trick. Including that outing, Garza is 2-0 with a 1.50 ERA over three appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Rain pushed back Young's scheduled start on Sunday to a more favorable one against Milwaukee. While he is 1-1 in his career against the Brewers, all three games were at Miller Park with just six runs allowed over 21 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton will make his first start of the season following left-hander Jason Vargas being put on the 15-day disabled list. While the Royals have not won any of Blanton's seven relief appearances, he has only allowed three runs over 15 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers' best work has come away from Miller Park, where he is 2-2 with a 2.46 ERA in six starts. Compare that to home, where he is 1-4 with a 5.45 ERA in seven starts with an opponents' batting average 30 points higher.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie would have earned the win in his last start had the Royals' bullpen not allowed two runs against the Rangers. Since his 11-run Yankees outing, Guthrie has looked on track, giving up just three runs and five hits in his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: The inconsistency which has defined Nelson's first full season in the Majors has begun to grate. "It is just unacceptable," Nelson said. "I just have to be more consistent. I have to be better."

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa held the Marlins -- who had pounded other Rockies pitchers -- to one run in seven innings Sunday, and is 4-0 with a 2.56 ERA in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: In what was only his second Major League start, Jungmann pitched five innings, allowed seven hits and two runs while striking out five against the Nationals. He's 1-1 with a 2.25 ERA in his young career.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis has dropped his last two starts, giving up eight runs in 10 innings against the Astros and Cardinals. His ability to handle aggressive teams in early innings is being tested.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander's struggles continue in 2015, as he's allowed 18 home runs in 14 starts. In fact, Lohse has surrendered at least one homer in all but two of his outings.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin was victimized by homer-friendly Minute Maid Park in his last start, a loss at Houston. But in his only home start, he fanned eight and yielded two runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garza's ERA jumped over 5.00 after allowing six runs and 13 hits in 6 2/3 innings during his last start. The right-hander looked to have his season on the right track in two previous successful outings.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers had a 2.97 ERA over seven starts before Wednesday's rough outing in Kansas City, in which his strikeout total (two) spoke volumes about the Royals' knack for fighting off putaway pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Niese credits a mechanical adjustment to his recent improvement, which has manifested itself in three consecutive quality starts. The left-hander's next start comes at Miller Park, the site of his big league debut way back in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson is coming off back-to-back losses. He allowed three runs on 11 hits and two walks with no strikeouts in five innings against the Royals on Thursday. In two career starts against the Mets, Nelson is 0-1 with a 2.25 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: One of the quirkier records in Mets history belongs to Colon, who has recorded a decision in 26 consecutive starts dating back to last season. He'll put that streak on the line at Miller Park, where he is -- go figure -- 2-0 in two career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Jungmann earned his second big league win Friday against the Rockies, allowing four runs on eight hits and one walk with four strikeouts in six innings. This will mark Jungmann's fourth start in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: deGrom is coming off a birthday loss in Atlanta, through no real fault of his performance on the mound. He held the Braves to just two hits and a walk before allowing a pair of runs in the eighth, raising his ERA to just 2.34 this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has allowed 11 runs in 10 innings over two starts against the team with which he began his career, including a six-inning, five-run outing at Target Field on June 5.
away_pitcher_note: May continued his strong June with another solid start on Saturday against the Cubs. He gave up just one run over six innings in a no-decision, and he has a 1.88 ERA in four starts this month.

home_pitcher_note: Garza's rocky season has continued, as he's surrendered 26 hits and 16 runs over his last two starts (12 IP). However, he had one of his best performances on June 6 against the Twins, allowing one run over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gibson has struggled in June after a solid showing in May, and he lasted just five innings against the Cubs on Sunday, giving up two runs on six hits. He has a 5.25 ERA in four June starts after a 1.36 ERA in six May outings.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers managed just 4 1/3 innings in his June 7 start against the Twins, allowing seven hits and two runs. However, he carries a 1.88 ERA in three appearances against Minnesota (two starts).
away_pitcher_note: Milone was solid last time out, giving up two runs over six innings in a win against the White Sox on Monday. He's 2-0 with a 2.52 ERA in four starts since rejoining the rotation in June.

home_pitcher_note: O'Sullivan got hit pretty hard in his last start Tuesday against the Yankees. He not only allowed 10 hits and six runs in 4 1/3 innings, but four of those runs came on four home runs. He hopes for better against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson surrendered just two hits and matched a career high by throwing eight innings in his previous outing. He had allowed 21 total hits in 10 innings over his two previous starts.

home_pitcher_note: Everybody in the world will be watching Hamels until the Phillies trade him, if they trade him before the July 31 non-waiver Trade Deadline. He could help his cause with some stronger performances down the stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Jungmann lowered his ERA to 2.74 last time out, allowing no runs and striking out five in five innings against the Mets. The rookie right-hander is set to make his fifth career start.

home_pitcher_note: Harang will be happy to see that June is over when he next takes the mound. His ERA jumped from 2.02 to 3.56 over his five June starts due in large part to the seven home runs he allowed, compared to four in April and May.
away_pitcher_note: When the Brewers' offense carried Lohse to a win over the Twins, he became the 14th pitcher to log victories against each of the 30 current franchises. Now he'll face a former team for the second straight start.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley rejoins the Phillies' rotation after landing on the disabled list May 16 because of a strained right shoulder. That followed two years worth of recovery following a pair of right elbow surgeries.
away_pitcher_note: With a loss to the Twins on Saturday, Garza fell to 0-3 with a 8.50 ERA in his last three starts and became the second Major Leaguer to reach 10 losses. He's allowed 31 hits over 18 innings in those three games.

home_pitcher_note: Battling rainy conditions, Lorenzen completed 5 2/3 innings vs. the Mets and allowed one earned run and six hits with four walks and four strikeouts. He walked two batters to load the bases in the sixth, while dealing with a slick baseball.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers have more well-known pitchers in their rotation, but Fiers has been the staff's most valuable arm. The Brewers are a respectable 7-9 when he starts, and he leads the staff by a wide margin with 93 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Smith will make his third career start, still looking for his first win. Smith showed improvement in his second start against the Mets on Sunday, giving up three runs (one earned) in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: On one hand, Nelson still hasn't delivered consecutive quality starts this year. On the other hand, he made an in-game adjustment Monday after falling into an early 4-1 hole. "That's important," manager Craig Counsell said.

home_pitcher_note: After winning his previous two outings, Leake was roughed up in his start Monday against the Twins. He gave up seven runs, including six in the fourth, on nine hits in four innings. It tied his shortest start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Jungmann has thrived since a promotion to the Major Leagues, where he can simply worry about getting outs versus earning a promotion. He's allowed two or fewer runs in four of his five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has pitched much better lately than the box scores indicate, good news for a team that may try to trade him later this month. "If you get distracted, you're not doing the things you need to do to win," Lohse said.
away_pitcher_note: Wisler got some quick revenge against the Nationals in his last start, throwing 5 1/3 shutout innings and striking out six batters, thanks largely to a sharp slider. In three starts since being called up, Wisler has posted a 2.60 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cravy will fill in for the injured Matt Garza and make his second career start. He was impressive in his Major League debut June 2 against the Cardinals, pitching seven innings and allowing just one run on four hits.
away_pitcher_note: Banuelos' excellent MLB debut Thursday was cut short due to cramps and dehydration, but before exiting, the lefty showed a plus changeup and struck out seven Nationals hitters through 5 2/3 shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers has put together a string of three straight quality starts. Last time out Fiers held the Reds to 3 hits in seven scoreless innings to pick up the win. It was his first win since June 12.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran is coming off his fifth home win of the season, where he allowed one run in seven innings against the Phillies. He'll try to improve the command of his fastball in his next start, as that has been an issue for him throughout the season.

home_pitcher_note: Bolsinger will look to go deeper into games as he hasn’t lasted longer than 5 1/3 innings in each of his last five starts. After winning his first four home starts, Bolsinger has lost his past two outings at Dodger Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has picked up the win in each of his past three starts, but expressed frustration with not going deeper into games after his last outing against the Reds. He hasn't gotten past the sixth inning in five of his past seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Beachy will be making his first start since 2013 with Atlanta after undergoing Tommy John surgery in March 2014. The 28-year-old owns a 14-11 record with a 3.23 ERA in 46 career starts with the Braves from 2010-13.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie continues to make a case for keeping a rotation spot when the injured Wily Peralta returns, as he's coming off an eight-inning outing where he allowed just one run on four hits vs. the Reds. The righty has a 2.43 ERA in six career starts.

home_pitcher_note: In the last game before the All-Star Break, Anderson will take the mound for his first career start against Milwaukee. Anderson took the loss last time out against the Phillies, which snapped a three-start winning streak.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse surrendered 11 hits in five innings during his previous outing. It was the fourth time this season the veteran right-hander had given up 10 or more hits in a start. He gave up three runs in five innings against the Dodgers on May 4.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers was the Brewers' most valuable starter in the first half, leading the team in WAR (1.0, per FanGraphs' measure), strikeouts per nine innings (8.6) and FIP (3.87). He gets the ball first coming out of the break.
away_pitcher_note: Morton will get the Pirates' second half underway against the Brewers, who saw the best of Morton earlier this season. He scattered three hits and struck out six in 7 1/3 scoreless innings in a win over Milwaukee on June 10.

home_pitcher_note: A loss in Nelson’s final first-half start snapped his three-game win streak, but it might have been his best outing of the year. He didn’t allow a hit until the sixth inning, and lost on three unearned runs in the seventh.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano wasn't named an All-Star, but he's pitched like an ace lately, going 4-2 with a 2.15 ERA in his last 10 starts. Liriano has been better on the road, going 3-2 with a 2.00 ERA in eight starts away from PNC Park.

The lefty, who in the past has flamed out after good starts, is trying something different, with an ERA of 1.59 in his last six starts compared to 5.37 up to that point. Confidence in all of his pitches has played a major role.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers characterized it as a precautionary move when they placed Garza on the disabled list before the All-Star break with right shoulder tendinitis. He’ll return after missing only one start.
away_pitcher_note: Salazar has lasted fewer than five innings in three of his past five starts, posting a 4.20 ERA in that span. The righty was strong in a July 10 win over the A's, allowing one unearned run over 8 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Much of the damage against Lohse during the first half came at Miller Park, where the veteran posted an 8.06 ERA and surrendered 13 home runs in 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson is the first pitcher in the Modern Era to open a career with four straight starts of at least 6 2/3 innings and no more than one run allowed. The rookie held Houston to one run in a win on July 9.

home_pitcher_note: Godley is making his Major League debut after making his last three starts for Double-A Mobile. The right-hander was acquired by the D-backs in December in the Miguel Montero trade and was a reliever the past two years.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers is coming off arguably his best outing of 2015, holding the Pirates to one run on three hits over seven innings. He’s struck out 106 batters in 107 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin has thrown five innings in each of his three starts this season, but has done so with plenty of rest. Friday's outing will be Corbin's first on regular rest.
away_pitcher_note: Opponents better hope they get to Nelson early. The right-hander carries a 9.00 ERA in the first inning this season, but that number plummets to 3.36 after the opening frame.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa won for the first time in five starts on Monday, giving up one run over seven innings against the Marlins. In his only career start against the Brewers, he gave up four runs in five innings in a no-decision on May 29.
away_pitcher_note: Jungmann passed another early-career test in his last outing. He scattered five hits over seven innings against the Pirates, holding them to a single run in his first start facing a team for the second time.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson has completed seven innings twice in his past three starts after doing it zero times in his first 15 outings. He beat the Brewers on May 30, against whom he has a career 3.00 ERA (two runs in six innings).
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander's return from the disabled list was a rousing success, as Garza induced a trio of double plays in six scoreless innings against the Indians. He'd been on the DL with a sore shoulder.

home_pitcher_note: Heston looks to continue what has been a dominant July. The right-hander’s 1.32 ERA this month ranks fifth best in the National League as he’s allowed four runs in 27 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The long ball has burned Lohse. He’s already surrendered more home runs this season (23) in 113 innings as he did last season (22) in 198 1/3 innings. Spacious AT&T Park should be a good place for Lohse to get back on track.

home_pitcher_note: Cain appears to be settling in after returning from the disabled list. In his last outing on July 22, the right-hander fired six innings of one-run ball. He struck out six and walked one in the 7-1 win over San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta will pitch in the Majors for the first time since straining his left oblique during a May 22 start at Atlanta. At the time, Peralta believed he’d miss one start, but he missed two months instead.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy is rounding into form at exactly the right time. After losing his first four starts of the season, the right-hander has won back-to-back outings. He’s pitched into the sixth innings in each start since returning from the DL.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers’ 10-strikeout effort against Arizona was the sixth double-digit strikeout game of his career. He is being scouted heavily ahead of the Trade Deadline, though Brewers GM Doug Melvin says he's not motivated to move Fiers.

home_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old is in his best stretch of the season, winning five of his last six starts with a 2.54 ERA in that span. “I’m not letting the stuff that happened before affect me,” Nelson said in explaining his recent success.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta had trouble with his timing in his last outing against the Phils, and his teammates had difficulty, period, as they were no-hit by Cole Hamels. Arrieta did notch his seventh consecutive quality start and has a 1.37 ERA in that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Jungmann had won three straight starts before losing to the D-backs on Saturday in an outing doomed by a two-run, 33-pitch first inning. He has a 1.59 ERA in three starts at home and will face the Cubs for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: Aside from an injury-shortened outing, Hammel had the shortest start of the season Sunday when he allowed six runs in 3 2/3 innings. He's gone eight games with earning a win, but he has allowed more than two earned runs in two games in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Garza has allowed three runs in 11 2/3 innings since returning from a DL stint, and two of the runs scored when Arizona's Chris Owings knocked a slider in the dirt for a two-run double. "It's coming back," Garza said.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks didn't feel he pitched badly in his last start. He did need 31 pitches to get through the first inning against the Rockies, but went five-plus. He now has six starts in which he left with the lead, but received a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse pitched into the seventh inning of his last start for only the third time since May 15. But he also was burned again by the long ball, making it 18 times in 21 starts that he has surrendered at least one home run.
away_pitcher_note: The Cubs traded for Dan Haren on Friday, but he just started for the Marlins, so Richard will be added to the roster for the series finale. It'll be Richard's fourth start with the Cubs and his first since July 20 against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta showed little rust in his return from a two-month stint on the disabled list, pitching at 96 mph during six-plus innings at San Francisco. It was his first Major League outing since May 22.
away_pitcher_note: Ross gave up a homer in his last start after not allowing one in 16 straight starts, a franchise record. Despite that, he picked up a win over the Mets, pitching through five innings allowing two hits and one run.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson delivered a third straight quality start with seven scoreless innings against the Cubs but took a no-decision after a rare letdown by the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Cashner took a no-decision in his last start, on July 30 against the Mets, pitching through five 1/3 innings while allowing six hits and seven runs (five earned).

home_pitcher_note: The rookie continued his streak of allowing two earned runs or fewer last time out in a tough-luck loss to the Cubs. In fact, opponents haven't scored more than two earned runs against him in nine of his 10 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy was supposed to miss his turn on July 31 for the birth of his child but made the start. He pitched through seven innings, allowing four hits and two runs, and struck out five.

home_pitcher_note: Walks haunted Garza in his last outing against the Cubs. He issued four free passes, including one that preceded a three-run homer from Anthony Rizzo that was the difference in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Despaigne earned a win to start off August. He pitched six innings against the Marlins, allowing five hits and three runs with five strikeouts. Despaigne is 2-3 on the road this season with a 4.88 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cravy, who made his Major League debut vs. the Cardinals on June 2, will start in place of the struggling Kyle Lohse on Friday. Cravy allowed one run on four hits in his first start, but he took a tough-luck loss in a 1-0 defeat to St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn has had mixed results against the Brewers this year. He pitched a season-high 7 2/3 innings against them at Busch Stadium on June 2, holding them scoreless. But he allowed six runs in five innings at Miller Park on April 26.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta got knocked around in his second outing since returning from the disabled list with a strained left oblique. The right-hander allowed six runs on eight hits against the Padres in just 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia lasted just five innings in his last start, largely due to extended counts and the four walks he issued. But he allowed just one run and has yet to give up more than three in any of his nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson scattered three singles and a walk over 6 2/3 innings last time out in his fifth straight quality start. He hasn’t allowed an earned run in 20 2/3 innings spanning over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey will enter this start having made 10 consecutive quality starts. His ERA during that stretch is 1.91. He has limited opponents to three or fewer runs in 19 of 22 starts and two runs or fewer in nine of his last 10.

home_pitcher_note: Haren did not get a decision in his Cubs debut on Wednesday, lasting five innings against the Pirates. Manager Joe Maddon said the problem may have been that the righty was too pumped. This will be his first start at Wrigley since Aug. 20, 2013.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander struck out a career-high eight batters last time out in a win over the Padres. The start marked his eighth consecutive in which he allowed two earned runs or fewer.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel was lifted early in his last start and not happy about it. Will manager Joe Maddon let the right-hander go deeper? Hammel has given up a home run in each of his last three starts. He beat the Brewers on July 31 at Miller Park.
away_pitcher_note: Garza is set to square off with the Cubs, his former team, for the second time this month. The right-hander allowed three runs on four hits in six innings of work while issuing four walks on Aug. 1, taking the loss.

home_pitcher_note: In his past seven starts, Lester has gone no fewer than seven innings and has allowed two or fewer runs in all but one of those outings. Despite only three strikeouts Friday, he has 53 K's in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: It's Cravy’s fourth Major League start, and his second since replacing Kyle Lohse in the rotation. The remainder of his season amounts to an audition for 2016, when Cravy has a shot to crack the Brewers’ starting five.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta has made three starts since a two-month stint on the DL for an oblique strain, and his most recent was also his best. But he owns an 8.82 ERA in three career starts against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Morgan put together one of his best starts for the Phillies on Saturday in San Diego, retiring the first nine batters he faced and allowing two runs in six innings. But consistency has been an issue. Can he keep it up?

home_pitcher_note: Nelson's great outing Sunday was undone by Matt Carpenter's three-run home run in the seventh inning, but the bigger picture is promising. Nelson is 6-1 with a 2.26 ERA over his last nine starts, with 52 strikeouts versus 16 walks.
away_pitcher_note: Williams has mostly struggled this season, but he put together his best start of 2015 on Sunday in San Diego, where he allowed one run in seven innings. That is just two runs allowed in 12 innings over his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie will look to bounce back from his first dud as a big league starter. Jungmann needed 81 pitches to get through 2 2/3 innings against the Cubs, the first time in 12 starts that he did not at least clear the fifth.
away_pitcher_note: Things have not been going very well for Harang. He has an 8.10 ERA in his past nine starts dating to June 4, which includes the eight runs he allowed in just 5 1/3 innings Monday in a loss to Arizona at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Garza is coming off back-to-back starts of seven innings -- the first time the right-hander has accomplished the feat this season. His ERA sits below 5.00 after allowing just two runs last time out, and he has seemingly turned his season around.
away_pitcher_note: Nicolino relies heavily on command, and continues to go through the learning curve. He gave up four runs in 5 2/3 innings in a no-decision against Boston. He's at 131 2/3 innings, counting 115 at Triple-A New Orleans.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers will continue to let their rookie right-hander audition for a role in the starting rotation despite his struggles. The 26-year-old Cravy is 0-4 this season and carries a 5.92 ERA after 24 1/3 Major League innings.
away_pitcher_note: Is the rookie a starter or reliever? The Marlins are still trying to find that out about Conley, who has a 5.00 ERA in his last 18 innings, with nine strikeouts. In two starts, he's posted a 5.59 ERA in 9 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta put together his best start since returning from the disabled list on July 28 last time out against the Phillies. The right-hander blanked Philadelphia over seven innings, scattering six hits.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler has emerged as the most reliable starter on the staff, and his 134 1/3 innings are the most on the team. The right-hander, however, is seeking his first win since July 23. He's dropped four straight decisions.

away_pitcher_note: Nelson is 6-1 with a 2.31 ERA over his last 10 starts. However, the right-hander struggled in his only other outing against the Nats this season, as he was touched up for seven run on 10 hits over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ross hasn't lasted five innings in each of his last two starts, having given up four runs and six hits over four innings in his last outing against the Giants. Ross did well vs. Milwaukee earlier this season, tossing eight strong innings on June 13.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander bounced back from his worst outing as a pro in grand style. Jungmann struck out a career-high nine batters last time out against the Phillies. He said his command of his off-speed pitches was key to the performance.

away_pitcher_note: Garza is the lone veteran remaining in Milwaukee’s starting rotation as they briefly turn to a four-man group. He put together back-to-back seven-inning starts for the first time this season before allowing five runs on eights hits in a loss.

home_pitcher_note: On Thursday, Tomlin held the Yankees to one run over seven innings in his second start back from right shoulder surgery. Through 13 1/3 innings since rejoining the rotation, Tomlin has allowed three runs (all on solo homers).
away_pitcher_note: Three times this season, Peralta has been saddled with a loss after delivering a quality start. Wednesday was the opposite, as he won after allowing six Marlins runs on nine hits in only five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson will make his first start since Aug. 7, when he suffered a strained oblique. He's taking the rotation spot of Carlos Carrasco, who was scheduled to pitch but hit the disabled list Tuesday night with shoulder soreness.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson is 7-1 with a 2.39 ERA over his last 11 starts and has not lost a decision since before the All-Star break. The Brewers are 13-12 in games he starts.

away_pitcher_note: Very much in a groove the past month, Iglesias has allowed one earned run over his past 19 innings, and his 13 strikeouts vs. the D-backs on Sunday were the most by a Reds rookie since Gary Nolan fanned 15 on June 7, 1967, against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Garza authored four straight starts of three or fewer earned runs coming off a stint on the disabled list, but has not allowed five or more earned runs in consecutive outings.
away_pitcher_note: Sampson needs a strong outing after posting an 8.03 ERA over his last three starts, during which opposing hitters batted .404 against him. He threw 100 pitches over four innings with five runs allowed during a no-decision vs. Detroit on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta's velocity was down during a loss at Cleveland, but he insisted he felt 100 percent. That led pitching coach Rick Kranitz to suspect a case of dead arm. The Brewers will carefully monitor Peralta before this start.
away_pitcher_note: Lamb  threw 108 pitches over five innings in a 5-1 loss to the Dodgers on Tuesday. The lefty acknowledged he is still learning the importance of getting ahead of hitters to apply more pressure on them.

home_pitcher_note: After a 14-start stretch in which he posted a 2.98 ERA, Nelson walked a career high eight batters and allowed five runs in 3 1/3 innings in Cleveland on Aug. 26. Nelson is 3-1 with a 1.85 ERA in four starts against the Pirates this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cole notched his 15th win after limiting the Marlins to one run in 7 1/3 innings Thursday. Cole had been stuck at 14 wins since July 26, though that was due to a lack of run support as much as any problems he encountered on the mound.

away_pitcher_note: Locke pitched seven innings of two-run ball to earn a win over the Marlins last Wednesday. He gave up five hits and a walk while striking out three. The quality outing was one of only a few for the lefty in the second half.

home_pitcher_note: Lorenzen had a decent start going Monday vs. the Cubs in his big league return. A rough fifth inning sent him out early but manager Bryan Price was thrilled with how he challenged hitters early and made good pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson walked eight batters on a rainy night in Cleveland on Aug. 26, and zero batters in seven solid innings against the Pirates on Tuesday. The result was his team-best 11th victory.

home_pitcher_note: The maturation process for Nicolino is going as scheduled. Over his last four starts, the rookie has a 1.98 ERA over 27 1/3 innings. Nicolino also has thrown at least six innings in each of those games.
away_pitcher_note: Davies dazzled with a fastball/changeup combo in his first turn through a Major League lineup on Wednesday, but the Pirates gave him trouble the second time through, after Davies tried working in a curveball.

home_pitcher_note: Conley is starting to work deeper into games. The rookie left-hander has worked at least five innings in three straight starts, with an ERA of 3.94 over that span. He struggled to go five two previous starts before that.
away_pitcher_note: Jungmann's ERA after 16 Major League starts is 2.42, a mark which would be significant were the season to end now. In the past 40 seasons, only three rookies have made at least 16 starts and finished with an ERA that low.

home_pitcher_note: Koehler paces the Marlins with 156 2/3 innings after his third straight six-inning start. He was in line for his first win since July 23, but had to settle for a no-decision against the Mets. Since the All-Star break, Koehler is 1-8 (5.26 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: After picking up his first Major League victory with three relief innings following a rain delay on Saturday in Cincinnati, the hard-throwing Pena will make his first Major League start.

home_pitcher_note: After he worked his way back from a flexor strain in his right elbow, Burnett will make his first start since July 30. His only outing vs. the Brewers this year was a strong one: one run over seven innings with six strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta will be well-rested, since his last start was cut short after two innings and 39 pitches by rain. He is trying to author a positive finish after missing two months of this season with a rib cage injury.

home_pitcher_note: Morton pitched well in his last start, holding the Cardinals to two runs (one earned) over six innings. He lost to the Brewers at Miller Park in July but threw 7 1/3 scoreless innings against them at home on June 10.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has done some of his best work against the Pirates, going 4-1 with a 1.72 ERA in five starts. He has a 1.64 ERA in two starts at the spacious PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Locke couldn't overcome a pair of early errors behind him but rebounded well in a loss to the Reds on Monday. While he's struggled on the road, Locke has fared much better at home this season, going 3-4 with a 3.62 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Davies worked quickly and effectively for seven innings in Miami on Labor Day for his first Major League win. Thirteen of his 21 outs came on the ground, and he faced the minimum in six of those innings.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano had his best swing-and-miss stuff on Tuesday in Cincinnati, striking out 10 over six shutout innings. The Bucs have won 12 of his last 13 starts. He's 0-2 with a 4.85 ERA in two starts against Milwaukee this season.
away_pitcher_note: Jungmann's 3 2/3-inning, seven-hit, six-run outing in Miami on Tuesday was his poorest showing in 17 big league starts. He set a career high for earned runs allowed and came within one hit of his high for that category.

home_pitcher_note: Pena allowed two runs on three hits and four walks over five innings in his first Major League start against the Marlins on Wednesday. The rookie righty's second act will come against a tough foe in the first-place Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez has allowed three or more runs in each of his last eight starts and has pitched past the fifth in just three of those games. In his only start against the Brewers this season, Martinez threw seven shutout innings at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta's first four innings against the Pirates on Thursday were among his best of the year, but he received no decision as he permitted two runs over six innings. He has yet to beat the Cardinals in three starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia is coming off his worst start of the year, one in which he allowed a season-most six runs in a season-short 4 1/3 innings. In two starts against the Brewers this season, Garcia has allowed one run over 14 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson said after his last start, a loss to the Pirates on Friday, that he hasn't been happy with his command lately. He'll look to get back on track at Miller Park, where he's 5-3 with a 3.16 ERA in 13 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey has made 17 straight starts of at least six innings, one away from the longest such stretch of his career. He’s also allowed two runs or fewer in 13 of those outings. He could become the team’s first to reach 200 innings in this start.

home_pitcher_note: In each of his two starts against the Pirates, Davies has walked at least three batters and surrendered at least four earned runs. In his other start against the Marlins, he walked no batters and allowed only one run.
away_pitcher_note: Finnegan has 23 relief appearances but this will be his first big league start. Since his July 26 trade to the Reds, he was 0-3 with a 6.28 ERA in eight starts for Triple-A Louisville. He will be in the mix for next season’s rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Jungmann has a 5.61 ERA over his last five starts, but that stretch includes a gem against the Reds in which he pitched six scoreless innings and allowed only three hits.
away_pitcher_note: Smith made three starts for the Reds earlier this season and is back in the rotation. Although known for throwing strikes in the Minors, his big league starts were marred by command issues and high walk totals.

home_pitcher_note: Pena has pitched well, but has had particular trouble with opposing pitchers. In each of his three outings (two starts and a relief stint), Pena's counterpart has delivered a hit, including a pair of doubles.
away_pitcher_note: DeSclafani began his Saturday start vs. the Cards by allowing hits to each of his first three batters and a run. But he shut it down from there and retired 15 in a row. His curveball has become an increasingly valuable item in his toolbox.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel struggled with fastball command in his last outing and was lifted after allowing four runs in 3 2/3 innings against the Pirates. He was embarrassed by his outing, especially the first inning. "I need to start pulling my weight here," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Last season, opponents batted .261 against Peralta. This year, they’re batting .298, and his strikeouts are down from seven per nine innings last season to five this season. He says he's healthy since a two-month DL stint.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta will try for the second time to get his 20th win. He did not get a decision in his last start against the Pirates, despite posting his 17th consecutive quality start. He's 7-5 with a 2.33 ERA in 13 starts at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander will make a spot start in place of Jimmy Nelson, who has been shut down for the season after being struck in the head by a liner last week. Cravy will be looking for his first win.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off his shortest outing of the season, lasting just three innings vs. the Pirates and giving up four runs before he was lifted. The right-hander now has 14 no-decisions in 29 starts. He's 1-0 in two starts vs. the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: In earning his first big league win with seven strong innings in Miami on Sept. 7, Davies didn't walk a batter. But he issued nine total walks in his next two starts, both losses. For a command specialist, that's trouble.

away_pitcher_note: Davies was back on the attack during six scoreless innings against the Cubs on, as manager Craig Counsell said, "a night where he can kind of fall back on and say, ‘My stuff works against the best in the game.'"

home_pitcher_note: The rookie looks to complete an unbeaten May in which he's 1-0 in four starts. Davies also is trying for his first career win at Miller Park, where he's 0-3 in six starts, and his first against the Reds.

away_pitcher_note: A lot could be going better for Simon so far in 2016, as the veteran holds a 10.16 ERA through nine starts and could lose his rotation spot to a younger starter if he doesn’t turn things around.

away_pitcher_note: After a slow start to the season, Leake has pitched well his last four starts, allowing four runs in 28 innings. Though he lost in his start Thursday against the Nats, he threw seven strong innings and allowed only two runs, both on solo homers.

home_pitcher_note: Davies seems to have settled in following a rough start to his season. He picked up his first home win on Friday against the Reds and has now given up two earned runs in four of his last five starts.

away_pitcher_note: Nelson has pitched into the eighth inning in three of his last four starts and delivered four consecutive quality starts, continuing his run as the Brewers' best pitcher this season. Only one of his five wins have come on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson turned in perhaps his best start of the year Monday against the Nationals, tossing seven innings of one-run ball. But he was pulled for a pinch-hitter after only 79 pitches, so he should be fresh for this start.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra has pitched at least six innings in five of six starts since a promotion from Triple-A, including three quality starts. The Brewers won his first five outings before falling to the Cardinals in the last homestand.

away_pitcher_note: After tossing four straight quality starts, Anderson has been hit around. He has allowed nine runs over 10 innings in his last two outings, although he has 10 strikeouts and three walks during that stretch. He has not faced the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta has a 3.50 ERA and a .250 opponents’ average in three starts since returning from a demotion to the Minors and will be facing the Pirates for the first time in 2016. He has a 3.55 ERA in six career starts against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl has pitched well since returning to the Majors, posting three quality starts. On Saturday, he held the Marlins to three runs (two earned) but lost. Oddly, Kuhl didn't record a strikeout or a walk in the six-inning start.

home_pitcher_note: Garza had allowed three or fewer runs in five straight starts before struggling in Seattle, where he lasted only 3 2/3 innings and surrendered six runs (five earned) on nine hits.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong bounced back from a shaky outing in San Francisco with a quality start on Sunday, but lost to the Marlins despite yielding three runs (one earned) in six innings. He is 1-2 with a 2.05 ERA in six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson’s quality start (six innings, two earned runs) against the Rockies on this homestand marked a breakthrough. It snapped a streak of six straight losses in which he didn’t throw a pitch past the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon continued his efficient and impressive rookie season last time out, holding the Astros to two runs on four hits and a walk while striking out a career-high eight over eight innings. His last eight outings have been quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has made two appearances since an Aug. 16 scare in Chicago, where he was drilled in the left thigh by a 107-mph Kris Bryant liner. Anderson pitched two relief frames at Seattle, then started and pitched five innings vs. Colorado on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Nova is coming off a 98-pitch complete game against the Astros on Tuesday, when he allowed one run on six hits and struck out six. He's 3-0 with a 3.20 ERA, 18 strikeouts and one walk in four starts since joining the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Davies lost consecutive starts before getting back on track against the Rockies, against whom he surrendered a Nolan Arenado homer in the first inning but no further runs. He pitched eight scoreless innings in his only career start vs. the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez has only given up two runs on seven hits in 15 innings over his last two starts. He has won both his starts against the Brewers at Miller Park this season, allowing one run on nine hits in 13 total innings.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta lacked the bite on his slider against the Pirates, but managed to get through five innings with only two runs allowed. This is a tough matchup; Peralta is 4-10 with a 5.02 ERA in 15 starts against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright went five innings and allowed seven runs (two earned) in his last start against the Mets. He pitched seven scoreless innings and gave up seven hits the last time he faced the Brewers on July 2.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran deserved a better fate Friday, when a pair of Jonathan Villar errors led to five unearned runs off Garza in the sixth inning of a loss to the Pirates. The miscues extended the frame long enough for Jordy Mercer to hit a grand slam.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver earned his first Major League win in his last start, which was also the longest (six innings) of any of his three outings so far. He has struck out 16 over his first 15 big-league innings but has also allowed three home runs and walked five.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon will face the Brewers for the fourth time this season after a rough outing in Milwaukee on Saturday. The rookie allowed five runs on seven hits in three innings, his first non-quality start since June 24.
away_pitcher_note: After missing nearly the entire month of August with right elbow inflammation that landed him on the DL, Guerra will make his return to the rotation. Guerra has allowed only three runs in 14 2/3 innings against the Pirates this season.

home_pitcher_note: Nova reeled off another quality start Sunday in Milwaukee, holding the Brewers to one run on three hits in six innings. He is 4-0 with a 2.87 ERA, 22 strikeouts and one walk in 31 1/3 innings over five starts for the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Thankfully for Nelson, August will be over when he takes the mound against Pittsburgh. Nelson allowed 30 runs (28 earned) over 28 innings and six starts in August as his ERA jumped from 3.42 to 4.45.

home_pitcher_note: Brault quickly ran up a high pitch count in a loss to the Cubs on Monday, lasting only four innings on 92 pitches while allowing three runs. He held the Brewers to three runs on seven hits in six innings on July 29.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson's last start came against these same Pirates, as he worked five scoreless innings without any problems before giving up two solo homers in the sixth that decided the game.

home_pitcher_note: Davies struck out nine while allowing three runs over 6 1/3 innings in Monday's loss to the Cardinals. Davies did not walk a batter, but he was hurt by homers from Jedd Gyorko and Kolten Wong.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks may miss Wrigley Field. He's 9-1 with a 1.21 ERA at home, best home ERA in MLB. He's also given up three or fewer runs in 18 straight starts since May 22. He lost to the Brewers on May 17 in Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta struck out 10 over seven innings of one-run ball Tuesday vs. the Cardinals. Since being recalled in early August, in five starts, the 27-year-old has a 3.00 ERA with 27 strikeouts in 30 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel got back on track after an abbreviated outing, and gave up one run over six innings against the Pirates. He has thrived at Wrigley Field, winning six straight there with an 0.69 ERA in that stretch. He's 1-1 in Milwaukee this season.

home_pitcher_note: Garza pitched seven innings of one-run ball to beat the Cardinals on Wednesday. Not a strikeout pitcher, Garza has 17 K's in his last two starts. Before that, he had struck out 17 in his previous six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Montgomery will make his fourth start with the Cubs as they stick with a "soft" six-man rotation. Manager Joe Maddon wants the rest of the rotation to conserve energy in the final month, so Montgomery will stay in the mix for now.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia has lost three straight starts, though he is coming off a decent performance against the Reds. Two of his best starts this season have come against Milwaukee. Those included a shutout and eight-inning outing in which he allowed one run.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra was limited to 70 pitches in 3 1/3 scoreless innings at Pittsburgh in his last start because it was his first game off the DL. He should be able to extend to about 90 pitches in this start.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez continues to be the Cardinals’ most consistent starter. He has allowed five runs over his last four starts -- all wins -- and has pitched at least six innings in five straight. He limited the Brewers to one run over six innings last month.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has endured a down season, but he has a respectable 3.75 ERA in a pair of starts against St. Louis despite a modest ratio of strikeouts (six) to walks (six) in 12 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright snapped an eight-start winless streak, though it lasted only five innings due to a high pitch count (93). Still, Wainwright is encouraged by the progress he has made with his mechanics in his last two starts -- both wins for the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson has completed a sixth inning in just one of his last 14 starts, but he and Craig Counsell have been making it work. Anderson has not surrendered more than three earned runs in any of his 11 starts since the start of July.

home_pitcher_note: Though he allowed just 2 runs, Weaver was knocked out of his last start after 4 innings due to an elevated pitch count. The Cards are encouraging him to be more aggressive with his repertoire, which they hope will keep Weaver from nibbling so much.
away_pitcher_note: Davies’ last start was a duel between two of baseball’s best changeups, and Kyle Hendricks and the Cubs won. Davies, though, was beaten by soft contact.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson replaced Anthony DeSclafani, who is being skipped for extra rest, and will make his second big league start of the season. On Aug. 14, Sampson faced the Brewers in long relief and delivered five innings with one run allowed.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta has pitched at least seven innings in back-to-back starts against the Cardinals and Cubs, two of the National League’s top three offenses. He’s pitched his way back into the Brewers’ plans for 2017, Craig Counsell said.

home_pitcher_note: Straily lacked his crisp stuff and battled through five innings in a 4-1 loss to the Pirates. He faced nine men in a three-run first. Jung Ho Kang hit a 0-2 fastball for a two-out, two-run double and Straily regretted the placement of the pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Garza has a 0.98 ERA while holding opponents to a .162 average over his last three starts, and is reinventing himself in the penultimate season of a four-year contract. “I’m finally back full strength and healthy,” he said.

home_pitcher_note: Although prone to giving up homers, Adleman kept the ball in the park and provided a quality start of six innings with two runs on Friday vs. the Pirates. He was often in trouble but found ways to escape jams.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra threw 74 pitches vs. the Cards in his second start off the DL, and would have kept going had Brewers hitters not cobbled together a long inning. Craig Counsell opted to cut Guerra’s outing short rather than stretch him another 10-15 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Montgomery will make his fifth start with the Cubs as they stick with a "soft" six-man rotation. Montgomery did not get a decision in his last outing, against the Brewers, giving up one run on two hits over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers are 2-8 in Nelson’s last 10 starts, including a loss at St. Louis on this trip in which he surrendered four runs on a pair of two-run homers in the same inning. Nelson leads the National League with 14 losses and 78 walks.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey will be happy to be back at Wrigley Field. He's 6-4 with a 2.44 ERA in 14 starts at home, compared with 3-4 with a 4.54 ERA on the road. In his last start, he took the loss against the Astros, although he posted his 19th quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson's last Wrigley Field start was cut short after 11 pitches on Aug. 16 when he was struck in the left thigh by a Kris Bryant liner. That outing came in the middle of a stretch in which Anderson has a 3.30 ERA over his last 13 games, 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta is coming off a win over the Astros in which he gutted out 5 1/3 innings. He wasn't feeling well, but battled through the outing. He'll be pitching on six days' rest, and is 4-0 with a 1.39 ERA in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Davies took a shutout into the 7th inning of his last start in St. Louis but settled for a no-decision. He is riding a wave of four straight quality starts, including a Sept. 5 loss to the Cubs in which he gave up two earned runs in 6 2/3 frames.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Hendricks held the Cardinals without a hit over eight innings, then served up a leadoff home run in the ninth. He still got the win, and now is 8-1 with a 1.33 ERA in 11 second-half starts. He's also 9-1 with a 1.21 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta deserved better in his loss to the Reds on Monday, when he surrendered three runs on a walk followed by a series of ground balls to the wrong spot. He rebounded to retire 15 straight on the way to his sixth quality start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Garza took the loss against the Reds in his last start, but only one of the five runs he allowed was earned. It's a recent trend for Garza. He's given up 12 runs in his past four starts, but only three earned runs for a 1.16 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Brault is still looking for his first big league win. The rookie left-hander went 3 2/3 innings in his last start, allowing five runs (three earned) on nine hits against the Phillies. He's 0-2 with a 3.27 ERA in two prior starts against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson will be starting on five days' rest in what would've been a start for Junior Guerra, who was shut down for the season. Nelson earned a win Thursday against the Cubs in his last start, allowing three runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl won his last start, tossing six innings of two-run ball against the Phillies. He's gone at least six innings in six of his last eight outings. Kuhl allowed two runs on five hits in 6 1/3 innings against the Brewers in August.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson took a no-decision Friday against the Cubs at Wrigley Field in his most recent start, allowing two runs in six innings. Anderson is 2-1 with a 2.33 ERA in four starts against the Pirates this season, including a 3.20 strikeout-to-walk rate.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong hasn't completed five innings in any of his last three starts. He was charged with six runs (four earned) on seven hits in 4 2/3 innings against the Reds his last time out. He beat the Brewers on Aug. 26, allowing two runs in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers are 14-13 when Davies starts, including his win over the Cubs on Saturday at Wrigley Field. He will be facing the Reds for the fourth time and has a 3.57 ERA in the first three matchups.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off being skipped one start, DeSclafani was not sharp in Saturday’s 10-4 loss to the Pirates in Game 1 of a doubleheader. He lasted four innings and allowed six runs (four earned) with six hits and three walks.

home_pitcher_note: This will mark Jungmann’s first start since April 28, when a loss at Wrigley Field prompted a demotion to Triple-A Colorado Springs. Jungmann eventually dropped to Double-A Biloxi before regaining his form and earning a September callup.
away_pitcher_note: Despite four walks, Straily earned his team-leading 18th quality start and 13th win vs. the Bucs. He gave up three runs over six innings with five K's. He’s not afraid to throw strikes or give up homers, especially solo shots, to get contact outs.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta will pitch on six days of rest in his first start since beating the Cubs on Sept. 18 at Wrigley Field. He has a 3.12 ERA in 13 career starts against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: This will likely be Finnegan’s 31st and final start of 2016. The left-hander lasted 2 1/3 innings in his previous start, on Sept. 17 vs. the Pirates. Pitch efficiency and length of outings will be a focus as he heads into next season.

home_pitcher_note: Perez has logged four straight quality starts, compiling a 2.13 ERA over that span. He didn't allow a walk in a no-decision against the Angels on Monday, which was just the third time in his 31 starts this year he did not walk a batter.
away_pitcher_note: Garza pitched for the Rangers during the second half of 2013 before signing a four-year, $50 million contract with Milwaukee that runs through 2017. He hasn’t faced Texas since 2010, when Garza was with Tampa Bay.

home_pitcher_note: Griffin lasted just 1 2/3 innings in his last start while dealing with an upper respiratory infection. He is 3-3 with a 6.32 ERA in his last nine starts. His only career start against the Brewers came on June 4, 2013, when he went seven scoreless.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has a 7.15 ERA in 10 starts since the beginning of August. Opponents have hit .311 with a .907 OPS in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels helped the Rangers clinch the AL West with seven scoreless inning against the A’s on Friday. It was just the second time in his last five starts that he allowed six-or-fewer runs. He has a 3.62 ERA in 13 career starts against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Working with a more effective curveball, Anderson has a 2.30 ERA over his last 11 starts and has surrendered more than two earned runs only once in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis, usually a fast worker, sped his delivery beyond his control and struggled for 4 2/3 innings in a road loss to the Dodgers. But the Rockies have won every one of his road starts since May 30.
away_pitcher_note: A soft-tosser who relies on deception and a quick pace, Suter has not allowed a run in 12 relief appearances since losing his Major League debut as a starter in Seattle on Aug. 19.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies scratched Tyler Anderson and will go with Hoffman instead. Hoffman has given up 27 runs in 22 1/3 innings during five starts but has limited opponents to one run in four innings since being moved to the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers’ Opening Day starter will try to author one more quality in his final outing of a trying 2016 season. Peralta spent much of the year in the Minors after being demoted in early June, but he has a 3.23 ERA in nine starts since coming back.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez beat the Cardinals at home in his first Major League start but struggled on the road while losing to the Giants in his second. Making adjustments that will add finish to his pitches is his challenge.
away_pitcher_note: Cravy will make his 20th appearance, second start, during what has been a successful season. The 27-year-old has a 2.39 ERA and will look for his first big league win against the Rockies.
