home_pitcher_note: Guerra has pitched professionally all over the world, including Spain and Italy, on his way to the Brewers via the waiver wire. At 32, he has finally cracked Major League Opening Day roster.
away_pitcher_note: Gray's 185 strikeouts in 2016 were a club rookie mark. Now his improved curveball accompanies the slider as a put-away pitch. Last Aug. 23, Gray fanned 10 in six innings at Miller Park in a no-decision. It's his first opener.

home_pitcher_note: Davies didn't crack Milwaukee's Opening Day roster last season but emerged to be one of the team's best starters. Working with what manager Craig Counsell calls "elite command" and a plus change-up, Davies led the Brewers last year with 2.8 fWAR.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson fanned 10 and yielded two runs in five innings in his only start at Miller Park last season, but he took the loss. From his debut last June 11, he led rookies in innings (114 1/3) and fielding-independent pitching ERA (3.64).

home_pitcher_note: Peralta was Milwaukee's Opening Day starter in 2016, but pitched poorly and was demoted to the Minor Leagues. It took an injury to bring Peralta back to the big leagues in August, and he capitalized by posting a 2.92 ERA over his final 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Last season, Chatwood returned from missing more than a year because of Tommy John surgery and posted a 1.69 road ERA in 80 innings. He is 2-0 with a 2.08 ERA in two career starts vs. Milwaukee but has never pitched at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson was 5-1 with a 2.56 ERA over his final 12 starts last season, but might have been on the outside of Milwaukee's rotation looking in had Matt Garza not gone down with a groin strain. Anderson is aiming for more consistency this season.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela joins Kyle Freeland as rotation members making their Major League debuts. Senzatela is making the jump from Double-A. In his last 67 Minor League starts, he has a 2.58 ERA and 305 K's in 384 innings pitched.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson will work to throw more strikes after leading the Majors in '16 with 86 walks and 17 hit batters. The Brewers held him until the fifth game of the season because he's fared pretty well against the Cubs, with a 3.68 ERA in 12 games, 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson will make his Cubs debut against the Brewers. The lefty was limited to four games last season following back surgery in March 2016. He's faced the Brewers once in his career, back on July 12, 2015, and did not get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Milone didn't have to wait long for his shot as a starter. After being the odd man out in the competition, he took over in the fourth inning on Opening Day for Junior Guerra, who sustained a right calf strain that will sideline him for six weeks.
away_pitcher_note: Not many teams can have the Major League's ERA leader as their fifth starter, but that's where Hendricks was slotted heading into the season. The right-hander, who compiled a 2.13 ERA in 31 games last year, finished third in the NL Cy Young voting.

home_pitcher_note: Davies couldn't command his off-speed stuff vs. the Rockies, and he will need that curveball and changeup vs. the Cubs. In 5 career starts against Chicago, he has a 4.18 ERA, including six shutout innings on Sept. 23, 2015, when he gave up two hits.
away_pitcher_note: It was only one start, but manager Joe Maddon said Arrieta looked like he did in 2015 (when he won the NL Cy Young Award) in his season opener April 4 against the Cardinals. Arrieta struck out six over six innings and gave up one unearned run.

home_pitcher_note: Happ tossed seven strong innings in his last start, allowing just three earned runs, but he was undone by a bloop and a blast vs. Baltimore. Adam Jones hit the decisive two-run homer, but it also went just 344 feet.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta surged to the finish last season thanks in part to a few extra ticks on his fastball, which he attributed to improved mechanics. His second pitch of 2017 registered 98.8 mph, a good sign he carried those mechanics into this season.

home_pitcher_note: Stroman recorded all but two of his 19 outs via the strikeout or ground ball during his last start vs. the Rays. That should hardly come as a surprise, because he led the AL in ground-ball rate last season.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson didn't have a spot in the rotation until Matt Garza went down with a right groin strain during the final week of Spring Training. But Anderson showed he belonged by delivering the Brewers' first quality start in the team's 4th game.

home_pitcher_note: Fans get to welcome back Arroyo to GABP, where he pitched from 2006-13. His Saturday debut vs. the Cardinals lasted only four innings and he made a few mistakes with his breaking ball, two resulting in home runs from Aledmys Diaz.
away_pitcher_note: Here's a case of a pitcher working on a pitch during spring and actually putting it to use in the season. Nelson threw more than 12 changeups in 6 quality innings vs. the Cubs in his '17 debut and plans to make that pitch a big part of his mix.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman bounced back from a shaky first start to tame the Cardinals last Sunday, yielding four hits in six shutout innings of an 8-0 Reds' win. The 34-year-old veteran, who signed a one-year deal during the offseason, struck out six and walked one.
away_pitcher_note: Milone took the place of injured Opening Day starter Junior Guerra and drew a tough opening assignment vs. the World Series champion Cubs. Maybe he will fare better vs. the Reds, who ranked 12th of 15 NL teams last season with a .680 OPS against LHP.

home_pitcher_note: After a dominant 2017 debut (7 innings, one hit, nine strikeouts, one walk), Finnegan appeared poised to win his second straight Monday when his teammates handed him a 5-0 lead after two innings. But he failed to get past the second inning.
away_pitcher_note: In his only career start at Great American Ball Park, Davies blanked the Reds for seven innings on four hits and no walks last July. He had a 3.97 ERA in four starts against the Reds last season, with 16 strikeouts versus one walk.

home_pitcher_note: Romano will be making his big league debut. The 23-year-old had a 3.13 ERA in six Spring Training games and was one of the final cuts before the team broke camp. He has a 1.38 ERA and 0.92 WHIP in two starts for Triple-A Louisville.
away_pitcher_note: Using Bill James' game score as the measure, 2 of Peralta's 4 best performances came at the Reds' expense -- a shutout in '13 and an 8-inning, no-run start in '14. His 3.11 ERA against the Reds is Peralta's best versus any NL Central opponent.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey held the Dodgers to one run on four hits over six innings but was saddled with a 2-0 loss Wednesday. He got better as the game progressed, retiring 14 of the last 15 batters he faced. Last year, he was 7-4 with a 2.62 ERA at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson seized his opportunity while replacing the injured Matt Garza with a 0.69 ERA in two starts that included seven shutout innings April 12 at Toronto. Anderson is throwing strikes; 59 of his 89 pitches against the Blue Jays were on target.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson wasn't happy with his outing in his last start, but it was good enough to pick up his first win. He held the Dodgers to three hits over five scoreless innings. It was his second career start at Wrigley Field, and first since July 30, 2014.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson led the National League in walks last season, but a tweak in his delivery is cutting down the free passes and paying big dividends. He is 1-0, with a 1.38 ERA with wins over the Cubs and Reds -- and just two walks over 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks will be pitching on four days rest for the first time this season, and being in that groove should help him rediscover his 2016 form. He has a 2.47 career ERA against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Milone (1-0, 7.36) preserved his spot in the rotation with five decent innings in a win Friday at Cincinnati. He did not issue a walk, pleasing manager Craig Counsell. "That's how you keep the damage down," Counsell said.

home_pitcher_note: The good news for Davies is that he's been here before. His ERA after three starts is 8.79, nearly identical to his 8.78 after three starts in 2016 before the righty turned a corner. Davies went 11-4 with a 3.54 ERA in 25 starts the rest of the way.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez had a bizarre outing last Saturday in which he struck out 11 while walking eight. He had particular trouble commanding the sinker. He threw 118 pitches in the outing, so he may be limited in how deep he can go in this one.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta is coming off consecutive quality starts and has yet to surrender more than three earned runs in an outing. It's a continuation of his strong finish to 2016, when he posted a 2.92 ERA over his final 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: It's been a rough start for Adam Wainwright, who has logged just 13 2/3 innings over three starts. He's averaging 20 pitches per inning and has allowed 10 of 15 leadoff hitters to reach. He's allowed 21 hits over his last two starts (8 2/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Anderson is one Brewers pitcher who has had some success against St. Louis. In five starts, he owns a 2.42 ERA spanning 26 innings. Anderson surrendered one run in his first 13 innings this year before a five-inning, three-run start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn threw seven scoreless innings to stop the team’s three-game losing streak in his last start. He continues to be a fastball-first pitcher, but he leaned more heavily on his cutter last time out than usual.

home_pitcher_note: Is this the year Nelson solves St. Louis? He is 0-7 with a 7.34 ERA in nine games, eight starts against the Brewers’ division rival. Cardinals batters have hit Nelson at a .316 clip.
away_pitcher_note: Leake had a 14 1/3-inning scoreless streak snapped last time out, but he continues to pitch brilliantly. With an expanded repertoire of pitches, Leake has allowed just two runs in 21 1/3 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Garza is coming off the disabled list to make this start after missing the start of the season with a right groin strain. He pitched in a pair of Minor League games to tune up and should not be on any limited pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: Garrett struck out 12 batters over seven innings but took a 2-0 loss to the Orioles on Wednesday. The rookie lefty has three fully-formed pitches, but his changeup has made the most progress, and it’s one he’s used exclusively vs. righty hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Davies’ follow-up to a breakthrough 2016 season has been a struggle. In the wake of his most recent start (Thursday vs. the Cardinals), Davies led the National League with 29 hits allowed, and led the Majors with 18 earned runs allowed.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman regretted hanging a curveball to Jonathan Schoop during a no-decision in a 2-1, 10-inning loss to the Orioles. The second-inning Schoop homer was the only blemish in a strong seven-inning performance with four hits and one run.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta started the season 3-0 with a 2.65 ERA before running into trouble with the Cardinals’ Adam Wainwright on Friday. Wainwright touched Peralta for four RBIs on a no-doubter of a two-run home run followed by a two-run single.
away_pitcher_note: Davis will be back from the disabled list after a right forearm bruise from being hit by a pitch. He threw two successful side bullpen sessions and felt good about his sinker and the location of his four-seam fastball during the time away.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers scored enough against Cardinals righty Mike Leake to push Anderson to the top of the NL leaderboard with a 1.13 ERA. Two pitches have made the difference: a curveball he refined last season, and a cutter that has been effective in 2017.
away_pitcher_note: Colon has looked masterful in two outings and provided the reminder he’s 43 years old in his other two outings.  He baffled his former Mets teammates over six innings in his April 5 season debut.

home_pitcher_note: After leading the National League in walks last season, Nelson and the Brewers were encouraged that he issued only three total walks in his first three starts. But he fell into old habits and walked six Cardinals in a loss on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia is still looking for his first win as a Brave, despite allowing two runs in 6 1/3 innings and two runs in six innings in his past two starts (both no-decisions). Garcia has a 2.88 ERA in 21 career appearances against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Garza’s season debut was tough to read because teammates committed three errors behind him. But the veteran right-hander said he was encouraged by the execution of his offspeed stuff, which has become more important as he adapts to age.
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz is coming off two very strong starts, including one run on four hits in seven innings on April 23 in Philadelphia. He has a 1.93 ERA in three career appearances against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha has finished at least six innings in each of his four starts and has yet to allow more than three earned runs in an outing. He’s among the Majors' leaders in lowest exit velocity allowed and has an impressive strikeout-to-walk rate of 3.83.
away_pitcher_note: Davies recorded a win vs. the Cards at home April 20, but he enjoyed his first truly positive start five days later vs. the Reds, working five scoreless innings for a win. It marked the first time this season that Davies did not issue multiple walks.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez is the only Cards starter still winless, but he remains among MLB’s strikeout leaders and showed better command in his previous start. Getting through the first inning unscathed is key for him.
away_pitcher_note: After going 3-0 with a 2.65  ERA in his first three starts, Peralta has surrendered 10 earned runs and 17 hits over nine innings in his last two outings against the Cardinals and Reds. He surrendered four homers in his most recent start.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright pitched into the seventh for the first time this season in a win last week. Inefficiency continues to be an issue, but Wainwright’s past two outings have been steps in the right direction.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson entered his Friday start against the Braves with the National League’s best ERA and finished that night seventh, at 2.10. He worked six innings against the Cardinals last week without allowing an earned run.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl left his last start early after being hit in the right knee by a hard ground ball. He was swollen and sore in the following days but expects to be fine Friday. Kuhl had a 2.19 ERA in 12 1/3 innings over two starts against the Brewers last year.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has performed well historically at PNC Park, where he has a 2.96 ERA in five career starts. The right-hander hasn't completed six frames since he worked seven innings of one-run ball in his last win, at Cincinnati on April 13.

home_pitcher_note: Cole pitched well Monday in Cincinnati but was again not helped by his defense or lineup. Since a five-run outing on Opening Day, Cole has thrown at least six innings in each of five starts while posting a 2.61 ERA and 32 strikeouts in 31 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garza spent the spring working on offspeed stuff, and used it in a win over the Braves. Garza noticed he didn’t have his good, heavy fastball, so he worked off other pitches instead, including his changeup. Notably, he struck out 7 and walked none.

home_pitcher_note: Glasnow took a potentially significant step forward Tuesday in Cincinnati, logging his first MLB win and six-inning start against the Reds. He felt he turned a corner mechanically, and it showed in his aggressive approach on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Davies still has not pitched past the sixth inning this season, but his two most recent outings have been more like it. Davies has limited the Reds and Cardinals to two earned runs in 10 innings over those games.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta was denied in his bid to be the first National Leaguer to log his fifth victory, but that was more about the Cardinals’ Carlos Martinez than about Peralta himself. When Peralta exited in the sixth inning, St. Louis had yet to score a run.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz’s only loss came in his only road start of the season, a 2-0 defeat in Baltimore on April 21. He’s struggled to keep his pitch count down, one reason he hasn’t thrown more than six innings in a game this year.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson will pitch against his 25th different opponent when he draws the Red Sox for the first time. In his three starts at home this season, Anderson has held opponents to a .206 average.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick gave up six runs on eight hits in four innings on Thursday in a loss to the Orioles. It was his first Major League start since 2015 after he spent last season in Triple-A.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson needed only 30 pitches to toss three hitless innings Friday vs. the Pirates, but a 2-hour, 27-minute rain delay ended his start prematurely. The right-hander has now gone four outings without a quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez posted his third straight quality start on Friday night in a no-decision against the Twins. The left-hander has the second-best ERA among Boston starters, and he’s struck out at least a batter per inning in each of his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garza has been a pleasant surprise for the Brewers this season after recording an ERA over 4.50 in each of the past two seasons. His most recent start was his best of the year as he threw seven innings of one-run ball in a no-decision vs. the Bucs.
away_pitcher_note: Harvey will be pitching for the first time since the Mets suspended him three games for violating a team rule. The Mets are as worried about Harvey’s on-field performance as they are his comportment; he is 0-2 with an 11.17 ERA his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Davies will try to build on his success vs. the Mets. The 24-year-old has faced them twice in his career, going 1-0 with a 3.18 ERA while striking out 12 in 11 1/3 innings. Two of the four earned runs he’s allowed against them have come via the HR.
away_pitcher_note: Though Gsellman continues to struggle with consistency in his first full big league season, he showed positive signs in his last start, allowing three runs in five innings. Gsellman will be making his first career appearance against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta seeks his fifth win in his eighth start this season. In his last outing, a no decision against the Red Sox on Tuesday, Peralta gave up four earned runs on five hits over 4 1/3 innings. The righty struck out four of the 20 hitters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: While deGrom continues piling up strikeouts, amassing 51 over his last 30 2/3 innings, he has struggled overall with a 4.70 ERA in those five starts. In five career outings against the Brewers, deGrom is 3-1 with a 2.32 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Perdomo will try for his first victory of the season in his sixth start. He has allowed eight earned runs in his last 23 innings in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson (2-0, 2.97 ERA) fell short of earning his fourth quality start against the Red Sox on Wednesday, allowing two earned runs on nine hits over 4 2/3 innings. In seven starts this season, the right-hander has to yet to reach 100 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Richard held the Rangers to one run in seven innings in his last start. He is 3-3 with a 5.04 ERA in 14 career games, including eight starts, against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson saw his ERA drop under 4.00 after his most recent outing against Boston, when he allowed just one unearned run on four hits and four walks over 6 2/3 innings while fanning eight.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin has won two of his last three starts. He gave up three runs in 6 1/3 innings against the White Sox in his last start. He is 0-1 with a 5.23 ERA in five career games against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Garza (2-0) has made three straight quality starts for the first time since August 2015. The righty is coming off a performance manager Craig Counsell described as "excellent," allowing two earned runs over six innings in a win over the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Cosart has allowed just one earned run combined in two starts this season, but he has yet to eclipse the 70-pitch mark. He has worked 7 2/3 innings as a starter in ’17, allowing seven hits and three walks while striking out four.
away_pitcher_note: Davies earned his fourth win of the season in his latest outing against the Mets, but the righty was bailed out by 11 runs from the Brewers' offense. Davies has yet to reach the sixth inning in any of his eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season, Butler threw six shutout innings against the Cardinals and got the win. This will be his Wrigley Field debut for the Cubs, and 2nd time he's pitched there. On July 29, 2015, he took the loss, with the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Espino will make his MLB debut at Wrigley Field after seven stellar starts for Colorado Springs. The 30-year-old Panama native, who has impressed since being signed to a Minors contract in November, takes over for Wily Peralta, who moves to the 'pen.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta has had a rough May. He's given up 12 earned runs over 15 2/3 innings in three games. In his last start, he made two mistakes, and both ended up as two-run homers by the Cardinals in a 5-0 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson has five consecutive starts without a decision, with the Brewers winning two of those outings. In his  last start, the Padres had four runs and six hits in his 5 1/3 innings. Anderson is 2-0 with a 2.66 ERA in his career vs. the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson missed the Blue Jays when the Brewers made a brief, two-game trip to Toronto in early April, but he will catch them this time. He has been excellent in May, with a 1.15 ERA and a .193 average against in 15 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Biagini allowed Atlanta to score six runs during their first six at-bats in his last outing but settled in to retire the next 12 batters he faced. This will be his fourth start, and his pitch count should be around 90.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran has been a bright spot for a pitching staff that has otherwise underachieved. Garza’s 1.11 WHIP in 29 2/3 innings leads the starting staff and is 25th among Major Leaguers who have thrown that many frames this season.
away_pitcher_note: Stroman has allowed two runs or fewer in seven of his nine starts. He also homered during his last start vs. Atlanta, and he'll have another chance to hit in Milwaukee. His only other appearance vs. the Brewers was a complete-game loss.

home_pitcher_note: After posting an 8.24 ERA in his first four starts, Davies has begun to settle into a groove. He is 4-0 with a 3.38 ERA over his last five outings, including a win in San Diego last week in which he completed six innings for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: Ray bounced back after a couple of poor starts to dominate the Padres. He allowed just two hits over 7 2/3 scoreless innings at Petco Park. Ray walked three and struck out six in the win.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra, who strained his right calf during a third-inning at-bat on Opening Day, returns to action after a seven-week absence. He threw 91 pitches in his second rehab start, so he won’t be on a strict pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: Godley has pitched well since replacing Shelby Miller in the rotation. Last time out he gave up three runs on eight hits over seven innings as he was outdueled by San Diego's Clayton Richard.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson had a 1.12 ERA after his first four starts but has gone backward since then. Including a loss at Wrigley Field in which he surrendered a season-high six earned runs, he owns a 7.30 ERA in his five most recent outings.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has been on a roll. He's won his last four starts and his last five decisions overall. Initially it was his slider he credited for the streak, then his changeup, now he feels he has all his pitches working.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson is still seeking his first win of the season at Miller Park after taking a loss against the Blue Jays in the opener of this homestand. Fourteen of his 16 walks this season have been issued at home.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin battled in his last start and managed to get through six innings against the White Sox. Chicago touched him for eight hits and three runs, but Corbin managed to get the win in a 5-4 Arizona victory.

home_pitcher_note: Gsellman produced his first quality start since April 19 against the Padres on Wednesday, allowing three runs over six innings in his first start since a 10-day stint in the bullpen. The Brewers tagged him for six runs in four innings on May 13.
away_pitcher_note: Garza had a 2.43 ERA and was riding a streak of four quality starts before running into trouble against Toronto in his last start, when he was charged with six earned runs on seven hits in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Pill, who made his Major League debut in relief Saturday in Pittsburgh, will be making his first Major League start. Pill was 1-0 with a 0.00 ERA in two starts for Double-A Binghamton and 3-1 with a 1.96 ERA in seven starts for Triple-A Las Vegas.
away_pitcher_note: Davies has cleared the sixth inning in each of his last two starts after not doing so in his first eight outings of the season. He has been solid in four road starts, going 2-0 with a 3.74 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After his ERA ballooned to 4.07 on May 14, deGrom has been outstanding in his last two starts, yielding one run in 15 1/3 innings. Friday against the Pirates, he threw a season-high 118 pitches in 8 1/3 innings, his longest outing of the year.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander’s second game off the DL will be his first road start this season. Guerra suffered a calf strain after three innings on Opening Day and was sidelined until a start against the D-backs on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Saturday vs. the Pirates, Wheeler pitched six innings, giving up three runs on seven hits with five strikeouts and two walks before leaving with a blister on his right middle finger. He has allowed eight earned runs in his last 27 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: For the second consecutive May, Anderson carried a no-hitter into the eighth inning at Miller Park. He struck out a career-high 11 batters with an invigorated 96.9-mph fastball -- the hardest pitch Anderson has ever thrown, according to Statcast.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson attacked against the D-backs, and the result was one run in seven innings and a season-high 10 strikeouts. His 81.5 percent first-strike rate was the second best of Nelson’s career.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw is coming off a no-decision in his shortest outing of the season, which lasted 4 1/3 innings. Though it was short, he threw 109 pitches, the second most he’s thrown all season. He is 5-4 with a 3.11 ERA in 11 career starts against Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Garza’s first two losses of the season have come consecutively, most recently against the Mets on Monday in New York. In two career starts against the Dodgers, he is 0-1 with three runs allowed over 12 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hill gave up one run in five innings to earn the win in his last start against St. Louis, while throwing a season-high 86 pitches. He is 2-1 with a 3.86 ERA in six games (five starts) in his career against Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Davies, who is 3-3 with a 6.46 ERA in six starts at home this season, allowed two runs over five innings during his last outing in New York against the Mets last Wednesday. This will be Davies’ first start against Los Angeles in 2017.
away_pitcher_note: Maeda, for the second straight start, gave up three first-inning runs, but put up zeros in his final four innings. He also made two throwing errors, his first error since June 30, 2016. He’s 1-0 with a 1.46 ERA in two career starts against Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra has allowed just one run over 10 2/3 innings in two starts since returning from the disabled list. He fired six scoreless innings against the Mets his last time out. This will be his first career start against San Francisco.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija is coming off his shortest outing of the season, a four-inning effort against Washington. His command was otherwise impeccable in May, when he struck out 49 and walked one.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has pitched 14 straight scoreless innings over his last two starts. The right-hander had been 0-1 with a 7.30 ERA over his previous five starts. He is 1-2 with a career 8.55 ERA in four starts against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Cain has struggled in his 13 career starts against the Brewers (5.01 ERA in 102 2/3 innings), but he has only seen their young ballclub twice since 2014. He’s faced current Brewers hitters in just seven at-bats.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson made franchise history in his last start against the Dodgers on Friday, becoming the first Brewers pitcher to make consecutive starts with at least 10 strikeouts while allowing no walks.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off the best start of his career, a complete-game shutout against the Phillies, Blach will face the Brewers for the first time. He’s thrown five consecutive quality starts with a 1.91 ERA in them.

home_pitcher_note: Espino is up from the Minors to pitch in place of an injured Matt Garza. Espino pitched capably over four rainy innings against the Cubs in May and has been solid at Colorado Springs, with a 3.44 ERA in nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto has faced just three other teams as often as he’s opposed the Brewers. His sharp 2.71 ERA in those 20 starts is matched by his 4.91 strikeout-to-walk ratio, his best against any team he’s faced more than three times.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado shifted from the bullpen to the rotation after Taijuan Walker was placed on the DL with a blister. In three starts since, Delgado is 0-1 with a 1.80 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Davies faced the D-backs on May 25, he allowed three earned runs on seven hits over six innings. But in his latest start, a win over the Dodgers on Sunday, the right-hander did not allow a hit for 4 1/3 innings and struck out six.

home_pitcher_note: Godley took a no-decision after a quality start his last time out, May 31 against the Pirates. This will be his seventh start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: The split-finger specialist struggled with command against the Giants, throwing only 52 of 90 pitches for strikeouts. That lower-than-usual strike percentage meant Guerra wasn’t able to consistently get to his splitter, a strikeout pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Ray has won four straight starts and allowed one earned run over that span, in 30 1/3 innings pitched. He tossed seven shutout innings vs. the Brewers on on May 25.
away_pitcher_note: With 7 2/3 more scoreless innings against the Giants on Tuesday, Anderson extended his scoreless streak to 21 2/3 innings over his last three starts. He has 22 strikeouts and five walks in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn had a solid performance in his last start despite going just five innings. He gave up three hits and one run. The Cardinals ended up losing the game to the Reds, 6-4, handing Lynn a no-decision. He is looking for his first win since May 5.
away_pitcher_note: Suter stepped in to start Game 1 of Tuesday's doubleheader after No. 8 prospect Brandon Woodruff was scratched with right hamstring tightness before making his MLB debut.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzales will be making his first Major League start since 2015 after undergoing Tommy John surgery in April 2016. He is 4-2 with a 4.82 ERA in his career with the Cardinals and went 1-3 with a 3.26 ERA in five starts in Triple-A Memphis this year.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has struggled against the Cardinals throughout his career. He is 0-8 with a 7.09 ERA in 10 games, including nine starts, against St. Louis. He is 0-4 with a 7.27 ERA in four games, three starts, at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Leake has had a rough streak as of late, having lost his last three starts and coming off his shortest game this year. In his five innings pitched in the 5-2 loss to the Reds, he gave up 10 hits and two earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Garza is set to make his first start since returning from a DL stint because of a chest contusion that was the result of a collision with a teammate. Garza is 5-5 with a 3.99 ERA in 14 career starts against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Picking up his third win of the season on Friday, Wacha put on a strong performance against the Phillies, allowing two runs on five hits over six innings. The outing was the first time since May 19 he pitched past the fifth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Davies is coming off wins against the D-backs and Dodgers in his previous two starts -- he’s earned wins in five of his last seven starts -- and is 2-0 with a 2.81 ERA in five career starts against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra, who is coming off a loss against the Diamondbacks, will make his sixth start of the season. He is 1-1 with a 3.60 ERA in two career starts against the Padres, both of which came last season.
away_pitcher_note: The Rule 5 draftee will receive another shot in San Diego’s rotation. Diaz lasted two-plus innings in his first career start, losing his command and mechanics in the third after two strong frames. He has a 2.31 ERA in eight appearances since May 9.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has allowed just one run in his last four starts, a span of 27 2/3 innings. In six home starts this season Anderson is 2-0 with a 1.69 ERA in 37 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After two dynamic starts to begin his career, the right-hander struggled in the next two, allowing 14 earned runs and four homers, each with two outs, in eight innings. Manager Andy Green expressed concern with his command after both June starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson has allowed seven runs and 16 hits over his last 11 2/3 innings in two starts against the Giants and Cardinals. He was 2-1 with a 2.28 ERA in five May starts and is 1-0 with a 3.20 ERA through his first three starts in June.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander will pitch with added confidence after earning his first win of the season last time out, holding the Reds to three runs in 6 2/3 innings. He faced Milwaukee on May 15, fanning nine in one of his team-leading seven quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start off the disabled list Wednesday, Garza allowed four runs in five innings against the Cardinals but got the win. He threw seven innings of one-run ball earlier this season vs. the Pirates on May 6.
away_pitcher_note: Cole got back on track against the Rockies on Tuesday, firing seven one-run innings with three strikeouts. It was a good sign for Cole following a four-start, 10.71 ERA stretch. He has a 5.74 career ERA at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Davies allowed two runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Pirates earlier this season. The right-hander has allowed seven runs over his last four outings at Miller Park and has made his last two starts on the road.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates lost for the 10th time in Kuhl’s 13 starts on Wednesday, when he allowed three runs in five innings against the Rockies. Kuhl has not pitched more than five innings since April 18, and his lone win came in his first start.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing four first-inning runs to the Padres in his last outing, Guerra finished with five hitless frames. In his last three starts at Miller Park, Guerra has allowed five earned runs over 16 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Williams gave up three runs in an ugly first Friday, but recovered to retire the last 12 he faced, getting through five frames vs. the Cubs with no further damage. Williams has a 4.06 ERA in his last seven starts, and the Bucs are 5-2 in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Over Anderson's last five outings, totaling 34 2/3 innings, the right-hander has allowed four runs. Three of those came in his last start vs. the Padres when he allowed his first two homers since May 21.
away_pitcher_note: Nova is coming off two straight wins, including a seven-inning start vs. the Cubs on Saturday. In 12 IP vs. the Brewers, all in '16, Nova has fanned 10 and given up two homers, to Jonathan Villar (on the DL) and Chris Carter (now with the Yankees).

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has steadily legitimized his bid to become a frontline starter. His ability to harness his emotions and command his fastball more consistently has enhanced the value of his four-pitch arsenal.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson threw his first career complete-game win over the Padres on Sunday. It was the Brewers' first since 2015. Of this Braves' roster, Brandon Phillips has given Nelson the most trouble in the past, going 9-for-24 with two homers against him.

home_pitcher_note: Minus one inning at Nationals Park, Dickey’s knuckleball has proven to be quite effective over each of his past three starts. He has distanced himself from the walk and homer woes that plagued him earlier this year.
away_pitcher_note: Garza took his first losing decision of June in his last start against the Pirates on Monday. The right-hander allowed four earned runs over 5 1/3 innings, causing his ERA to rise to a season-high 4.42.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran has righted himself as he has thrown his two-seamer more frequently and generated more consistent command. He has allowed three earned runs or less in five of his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Davies was 3-1 with a 4.13 ERA in May, but he hasn't found that same success in June. He allowed a season-high seven runs in his last outing, a loss to the Pirates on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Adleman last faced the Brewers in his season debut on April 16, when he allowed one run in four innings. In his last two starts, he has allowed a combined five runs in 11 innings, while walking eight batters.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra got a no-decision his last time out against the Pirates despite walking five batters. He gave up three runs on seven hits with six strikeouts in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Castillo earned a second start after allowing two runs in five innings in his Major League debut Friday against the Nationals. The 24-year-old is the organization's No. 5 prospect, according to MLBPipeline.com.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson pitched six strong innings in the Brewers’ win over the Pirates. The righty allowed two runs on two hits with seven strikeouts and two walks.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey struggled in his season debut Saturday, allowing eight runs in 1 2/3 innings. The 11-year-veteran has a career 4.31 ERA and will look to get back on track against the Brewers, whom he holds a 4.64 ERA against in 22 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson’s road woes continued in the Brewers’ loss to the Braves. He gave up four runs on six hits with eight strikeouts and three walks in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: It’s a small sample, but Garza has been hurt in his six starts at home by the long ball (seven of the eight he’s allowed this season have come at Miller Park) and walks (11 of 16). He has a 5.11 ERA in eight career starts against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez has hit a rough patch in his last three starts, mostly due to his command. He's walked 14 batters over that span, during which he's posted a 7.90 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Davies became only the 13th pitcher in Brewers history to work seven innings of a game without logging a single strikeout, but he didn’t surrender a run, either. He’s struck out 5.8 batters per nine innings, down from 7.4 per nine innings last year.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler will be recalled from Triple-A New Orleans to make his first Major League start since May 16. He was optioned to the Minors after allowing eight runs in three innings vs. the Astros. Koehler posted a 1.15 ERA in three Triple-A starts.

home_pitcher_note: Home runs have been a problem for Guerra. After serving up four Reds homers on Tuesday, he has allowed more homers this season in 41 2/3 innings (11) than he did in all of last season in 121 2/3 innings (10).
away_pitcher_note: Straily has been lights out since allowing a season-high-tying nine hits to the Pirates on June 10. In three starts, he’s 1-0 with a 1.56 ERA and has struck out 18 over 17 1/3 innings. The right-hander hasn’t faced Milwaukee this season.

home_pitcher_note: Replacing the injured Chase Anderson, Suter will make his first start at Miller Park. He made a spot start at St. Louis on June 13, allowing three runs on five hits over 4 2/3 innings. He threw a perfect eighth in his last outing vs. the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty is coming off of his second consecutive loss after being charged with three earned runs on six hits through five innings, including two home runs, against Toronto. His ERA is up to a season-high 4.54.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson recorded 50 strikeouts in June, tying him with Ben Sheets for the second-most in a month in franchise history. He tied his career high with 11 K's in his last start, an 11-3 win over the Reds on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez is coming off of his best start of the season after pitching eight shutout innings and allowing just two hits and a walk. The righty also struck out a season-high eight batters and lowered his ERA from 7.26 to 6.48.

home_pitcher_note: Garza ended June by receiving a no-decision in the Brewers' 3-2 win over the Marlins on Friday. The right-hander allowed two runs on six hits over five innings in the start and is 2-2 with a 4.71 ERA with 12 walks and 28 strikeouts at Miller Park.
away_pitcher_note: With Chris Tillman on the paternity list, Aquino will be recalled from Triple-A Norfolk to make his second Major League start. He has a 4.46 ERA in 12 starts for Norfolk in 2017 and allowed two runs in six innings in a start this season vs. Boston.

home_pitcher_note: Montgomery was put into the rotation because of an injury to Kyle Hendricks and has been consistent. Joe Maddon says the lefty needs to work on his fastball command, adding, "when it shows up, heads up, because his other stuff is really good."
away_pitcher_note: Davies started off shaky in his last start, allowing four runs in the first three innings. But the right-hander bounced back by tossing three straight 1-2-3 innings, which manager Craig Counsell said were his best innings of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Montgomery continued to mature as a starter in June, going 4-0 with a 2.59 ERA in five starts. However, he wasn't as sharp in his most recent start, allowing three runs in 5 1/3 innings vs. Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra saw his fastball velocity dip to an average of 90 mph in his last start, allowing four runs in four innings of a 10-3 loss to Miami. On a positive note for Guerra, manager Craig Counsell noted improvement in the righty's offspeed pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Named to the AL All-Star team, Severino struggled in his last outing, allowing six runs in 5 1/3 innings and taking the loss against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Filling in for the injured Chase Anderson on Monday, Suter struck out a season-high eight batters and earned his first MLB win as a starter. He became the first lefty to earn a win for the Brewers at Miller Park since Randy Wolf did in July 2012.

home_pitcher_note: Tanaka has strung together three great starts after an uncharacteristically bad stretch before them, leading the Yankees to believe he has worked through his funk. Over his last three outings, he's posted a 2-0 record with a 1.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has struck out eight batters in each of his last four starts, including a 6-2 win over the Orioles on Tuesday. He didn't allow an earned run over seven quality innings and did not walk a batter for the fifth time this year.

home_pitcher_note: Davies finished the first half of the season with three straight winning decisions, including an 11-2 win over the Cubs on July 6. He has a small sample size vs. the Phillies, allowing nine hits in one game last year.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta opens the second half for the Phillies, in part because he has pitched better lately and in part because he remained in Philadelphia to throw over the All-Star break. He has a 3.94 ERA in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last home start on July 4 vs. the Orioles, Nelson allowed one unearned run over seven innings. He is 4-3 with a 2.35 ERA at Miller Park this season.
away_pitcher_note: Nola lately has looked like the guy that made him the Phillies’ first-round pick in the 2014 Draft. He is 4-3 with a 2.61 ERA in his last seven starts before the All-Star break. He has struck out 52 in 48 1/3 innings in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Garza is coming off his first scoreless performance of the season, allowing just five hits over 6 1/3 innings vs. the Orioles on July 5. It was the deepest he's gone in an outing since May 6, and it was his sixth quality start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: This could be one of Hellickson’s final starts before the July 31 non-waiver Trade Deadline. He could be traded before the end of the month. He has a 3.20 ERA in his last four starts, improving his trade value.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl made an emergency, three-inning start Sunday on two days' rest after throwing a career-high seven innings on July 6. After struggling through May, Kuhl has put together a 3.50 ERA in his last seven outings.
away_pitcher_note: Suter will make his fourth start in place of the injured Chase Anderson. He allowed two earned runs over 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision at Yankee Stadium on July 8, and has yet to give up a run to the Bucs over four relief appearances in 2016.

home_pitcher_note: Nova finished his first half strong, holding the Cubs to two runs and striking out six over 6 2/3 innings on July 8 at Wrigley Field. He is seven innings shy of breaking the Pirates’ season-high innings total (127 1/3) set by Jeff Locke in 2016.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra left his last start on July 7 after getting hit by a comebacker and was placed on the 10-day DL with a left shin contusion on July 9. He last faced Pittsburgh on June 21, allowing three earned runs over six innings in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start of the second half, Cole held the Cardinals to two runs on four hits and no walks while striking out four in six innings. He's 3-3 with a 3.16 ERA in nine career starts vs. the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Davies has yet to take a losing decision on the road this season, going 5-0 with a 3.62 ERA in nine starts. He is 1-1 in two starts vs. the Pirates, but he allowed seven earned runs over five innings in a 7-3 loss to them on June 20.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon battled through five innings in Saturday’s loss to the Cardinals, allowing four runs - three with two outs in the fifth. He went 0-2 with a 3.86 ERA against Milwaukee last year and has not faced them this season.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson will face the Pirates for the second time this season after throwing 30 pitches over three perfect innings in a rain-delayed no-decision on May 5. Following that game, he went 6-2 with a 2.39 ERA in 12 starts before the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: Nola is establishing himself as the Phillies’ top starter. He is 3-1 with a 1.78 ERA and a 0.99 WHIP over his last five starts. He also is 4-3 with a 2.65 ERA in eight starts since the beginning of June.
away_pitcher_note: Garza last pitched against the Phillies on Sunday, allowing one earned run on three hits in five innings. After the start, manager Craig Counsell said Garza is improving his efficiency and putting together a nice season "under the radar."

home_pitcher_note: A free agent after the season, Hellickson's time with the Phillies could be winding down ahead of the July 31 non-waiver Trade Deadline. He has a 3.26 ERA in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Suter is coming off his shortest start of the season in place of the injured Chase Anderson. The lefty surrendered two earned runs on seven hits in 4 2/3 innings against the Pirates on Monday. He has never faced the Phillies even as a reliever.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff served up a season-high three homers to the Marlins over six innings in his last start. He allowed five runs in a no-decision. Over his last three outings, the right-hander is 1-0 with a 3.18 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra only gave up three hits in 5 2/3 innings in his last start against the Pirates on Tuesday, but two of those hits were home runs. Guerra has yet to face the Phillies this season.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson’s second stint with the Nationals got off to an excellent start, as he threw seven innings of two-run ball to beat the Angels. He was also efficient, firing 91 pitches. With that outing, he has secured the No. 5 spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Davies produced one of his best starts of the season on Wednesday, allowing one unearned run over seven innings in the Brewers' loss to the Pirates. Manager Craig Counsell said Davies' offspeed stuff was exceptional and encouraging moving forward.

home_pitcher_note: Gio's most recent outing was his worst in two months, as he gave up four runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Angels. Still, Gonzalez enters this start with his lowest career ERA through 20 starts since 2011, when he had a 2.67 ERA for the A’s.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Pirates, Nelson suffered a loss for the first time since June 23, allowing four earned runs in five innings. He threw five shutout innings the last time he faced the Nationals on June 26, 2016.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer allowed back-to-back-to-back homers to begin his last outing against the D-backs, the first time he has surrendered three consecutive homers. He believes there was a lot to learn from that start and is looking to make adjustments.
away_pitcher_note: Blazek gets the call for a spot start after the Brewers placed Matt Garza on the DL with a calf strain. Blazek has 108 relief appearances in the Majors, but this will be his first big league start. He had a 2.89 ERA in 10 Triple-A starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Suter pitched six innings of one-run ball in his fourth start in place of the injured Chase Anderson on Saturday. He struggled the last time he faced the Cubs on April 8, allowing four earned runs on four hits and two walks in one inning of relief.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana has posted a quality start in both of his outings with the Cubs. He admitted to being a little nervous in his first home start but settled down to work six innings. This will be his second career start at Miller Park and first since 2015.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra only tossed four innings in his last start on Sunday, allowing five earned runs in a losing decision to the Phillies. He has yet to face the Cubs this season, but he made two quality starts (1-0) against them in 2016.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks' last outing was his first off the disabled list. He'd been sidelined with soreness in his right hand. Getting back on his five-day routine is key. He's 1-0 vs. the Brewers this season, but he has given up eight earned runs over 11 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Davies is 1-1 against the Cubs and 6-4 with a 6.45 ERA at Miller Park this season. He earned a win in one of his best starts this season at Wrigley Field on July 6, surrendering just two earned runs on five hits with no walks over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA in two starts since the break. He hit four batters in his last start, including three in one inning to load the bases. The best news for the Cubs is that he did not give up a home run (he's given up 25 this year).

home_pitcher_note: Nelson has continued to be a solid force in the Brewers' rotation, making his team-leading 12th quality start in a no-decision vs. the Nationals on Wednesday. He is 0-1 with a 5.73 ERA in two starts against the Cardinals this season.
away_pitcher_note: July has not been kind to Martinez, who has posted a 5.90 ERA over five starts. He allowed five runs in three of those games. In his most recent start, vs. the Rockies, he allowed five runs on seven hits and two walks over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suter is coming off his best start of the season, allowing no runs on four hits over a career-high seven innings against the Cubs on Friday. He is 0-1 with a 3.12 ERA in three games against the Cardinals this season, including one start.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver will make a second spot start in place of Adam Wainwright, who remains on the DL. Weaver was stung by a grand slam in his first start this season, which lasted five innings. He is 0-1 with a 3.00 ERA in two career starts vs. Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Garza will make his first start off the DL after nursing a lower leg strain. He threw a bullpen session Monday with no issues, manager Craig Counsell said. He earned a win against St. Louis on June 14, allowing four earned runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha dominated in his last start, holding the D-backs scoreless through six innings and allowing just three hits. He has now held his opponent scoreless in four of his last six starts and holds a 1.86 ERA over that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Faria has pitched well since being recalled from Triple-A Durham on June 7, recording quality starts in eight of 10 starts. He’s been a strike-throwing machine and is fearless about letting his stuff play.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff was set to make his MLB debut on June 13, but was scratched with hamstring tightness and placed on the DL. Woodruff had a 6.75 ERA in three games since he returned to Triple-A, but threw five shutout innings in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Cobb experienced his worst outing of the season Monday against the Astros when he allowed eight runs on nine hits in three innings en route to his seventh loss of the season. He is 5-3 with a 2.59 ERA in nine starts at Tropicana Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: Davies made a quality start against the Cubs last time out, allowing 3 earned runs over 7 innings in a losing effort. This will be his first career start vs. the Rays. He is 6-0 with a 2.80 ERA in 11 road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Archer’s streak of six consecutive quality starts got snapped Tuesday in Houston when he allowed four runs, two of which came via solo homers. He did pitch six-plus innings, so he has pitched at least six innings in 14 consecutive starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson leads the Brewers with 13 quality starts this season, including a 3-2 win over the Cardinals on Tuesday his last time up. He has yet to face the Rays in his career and is 4-2 with a 4.66 ERA in 10 road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Santana tossed his Major-League-leading fifth complete game in his last outing over the Padres. No other team has more than four complete games on the season. In his career, Santana has a 16-13 record with a 3.80 ERA during Interleague play.
away_pitcher_note: Suter will make his seventh start in place of the injured Chase Anderson. He last started Wednesday vs. St. Louis, allowing a career-high five earned runs over 5 1/3 innings. He has four quality starts this season and has never faced the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Last time out, Mejia was charged with four runs off seven hits over four innings in the loss to Texas. Mejia hasn’t lasted at least six innings since July 8. Over that span, Mejia has allowed eight earned runs across a combined 18 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garza will make his second start since coming off the DL with a calf strain. He cruised through the first four innings of his last start vs. the Cardinals on Thursday, allowing just one run in 5 2/3 innings of an eventual Brewers' 2-1 win.

home_pitcher_note: Woodruff threw 6 1/3 scoreless innings against the Rays on Friday, becoming the fifth Brewer to make a scoreless start in his MLB debut. He loaded the bases in the first two innings but was able to escape the jams and struck out six batters.
away_pitcher_note: Colon recorded his 37th complete game in his last outing, allowing four runs to the Rangers. He earned his first victory as a Twin, marking the 10th organization he has won with. Against Milwaukee, Colon is 4-3 with a 4.89 ERA in 10 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Davies threw seven shutout innings against the Rays on Saturday, allowing just one hit in the sixth inning. He has made four straight starts pitching at least seven innings, allowing just three earned runs over 28 2/3 innings in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Minnesota will recall Enns from Triple-A Rochester to make his Major League debut. The lefty, who was one of two pitchers acquired from the Yankees in the Jaime Garcia trade on July 30, has a 2.38 ERA in eight Triple-A starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off his third start of at least eight inning this season, Nelson looks for his third win vs. the Reds. He owns a 1.93 ERA against them this season, allowing three earned runs over 14 innings, while striking out 16.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey lasted only 3 1/3 innings and allowed a career-high 10 runs on 10 hits during Sunday’s 13-4 loss to the Cardinals. "No command. I just didn't have it,” Bailey said.

home_pitcher_note: Suter's latest four-inning start against the Twins was his shortest of the season. He has not started against the Reds, but he threw an inning of relief against them this season, allowing no hits and striking out two.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman will be activated from the DL to make his first start since right knee inflammation knocked him out of his July 17 game vs. the Nationals after one inning. Feldman’s arm isn’t rusty, but he likely won’t be running and moving 100 percent.

home_pitcher_note: Garza allowed a season-high eight earned runs and four home runs in his last start against the Twins on Tuesday. He is 4-5 with a 4.71 ERA in 15 career starts vs. the Reds, including a four-inning no-decision on April 24.
away_pitcher_note: Barely more than half of Romano’s 91 pitches in a 7-3 loss to the Padres on Tuesday were strikes. He wasn’t able to access his changeup as the club hoped, and he lacked command of his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Davies surrendered six earned runs on a career-high 11 hits in 5 2/3 innings Thursday, snapping his career-best streak of four straight starts with at least seven innings. He is 1-1 with a 4.58 ERA in three starts vs. the Pirates this season.
away_pitcher_note: Nova allowed 10 hits and six runs in a loss against the Tigers on Wednesday. He’s allowed double-digit hits in both starts against the Brewers this year, but he beat them July 18 with six innings of three-run ball and six strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: While he leads the Brewers with 14 quality starts this year, Nelson allowed a career-high nine earned runs on 11 hits and three walks in his last start against the Reds. He is 0-1 with a 4.50 ERA in two starts against the Pirates this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cole threw a season-high eight innings on Thursday to record his seventh straight road win and seventh straight quality start. He has a 2.74 ERA since July began. The Bucs have won all three of his starts against the Brewers in 2017.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez is coming off one of his worst starts of the season, giving up five runs in 4 1/3 innings to the Marlins on Sunday. He’s faced the Brewers once before on the final game last season, allowing two runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garza has not faced the Rockies this season, but he is 2-5 with a 6.10 ERA in seven career starts against them. Garza allowed three earned runs over 5 1/3 innings on Sunday and has not surpassed six innings in five straight starts since July 5.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis makes his second start of the season after an emotional return to the big leagues in which he tossed seven scoreless innings vs. the Braves. The righty played to his strengths Monday, inducing 11 groundouts.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers skipped Woodruff in the rotation on his scheduled start day last Tuesday. The right-hander has made two career MLB starts since being called up on Aug. 4, including 6 1/3 shutout innings in his big league debut at Tampa Bay.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland has pitched better at Coors Field than on the road this season, a rarity for most hurlers. The Denver native’s 3.31 ERA at home is nearly a full run lower than his road ERA of 4.22. Sunday is his 11th home outing.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson will make his first start off the 10-day DL after sustaining a left oblique strain in an at-bat on June 28. He's made two rehab starts with no setbacks since then. He is 3-3 with a 4.92 ERA in 11 career starts against Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: On the heels of his first Major League win, Stratton will make his fourth start of 2017. Against the Nationals, Stratton spun 6 2/3 innings of scoreless ball, striking out 10. It was the fifth time a Giants pitcher had more than 10 K's in a start.
away_pitcher_note: Davies has been much better on the road (2.52 ERA) than at home (5.97), and he offered an interesting explanation. He likes the extra time to collect himself on the road while the Brewers bat in the top of the first inning.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija owns a 4-1 record over his last five starts and has pushed himself on the mound, averaging 110 pitches. Against the Brewers in his career, Samardzija has a 4.48 ERA in 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has surrendered 19 hits over his past two starts, but 17 have been singles. Against the Pirates in his most recent outing, all eight hits off Nelson were singles.

home_pitcher_note: Giants fans gave Moore a standing ovation after his last start when he broke a nine-start winless streak. He allowed one hit over seven innings before surrendering a walk and hit in the eighth. Both runners came around to score.
away_pitcher_note: Garza has a 2.70 ERA in three career starts at AT&T Park, thanks in part to a stellar 17 strikeouts versus three walks. He has not won a road game since June 14 at St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Maeda took a perfect game into the sixth inning of his last start, a duel with Justin Verlander, but allowed four runs and three extra-base hits after that and took the loss in Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson, in his first return from the DL after straining his oblique, spun five innings of one-run ball against the Rockies at Coors Field. Anderson tallied 73 pitches and said he felt more comfortable as the game progressed.

home_pitcher_note: After Alex Wood landed on the disabled list on Tuesday with SC joint inflammation, the Dodgers will insert Stripling into the rotation. The righty, normally used in long relief situations, will make his first start this season.
away_pitcher_note: Davies was a hard-luck loser against the Giants after tossing six innings and allowing two runs while the Brewers’ offense sputtered. Davies dazzled in his one career start at Dodger Stadium last season, posting seven innings of one-run ball.

home_pitcher_note: Darvish comes off the disabled list for this start. He left the rotation with lower back stiffness, but his time on the sidelines was spent working on mechanical issues.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson allowed three runs on seven hits in five innings in his last start against the Giants. The right-hander had success against the Dodgers in a start against them in June, pitching eight scoreless innings in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Garza pitched five innings of one-run ball in his last start against the Giants. He's faced the Cardinals twice this year, going 2-0 with a 4.22 ERA in 10 2/3 innings. Garza has won his last two home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver is expected to make his second straight start in place of Adam Wainwright, who is on the 10-day DL. The rookie dominated in his last outing, holding the Padres scoreless over seven innings. He allowed just three hits and struck out 10.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson allowed two runs on six hits over five innings in his last outing vs. the Dodgers. He's won his last three decisions at Miller Park. In two starts vs. the Cardinals this year, he owns a 3.38 ERA in 10 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez put together a solid outing his last time out, pitching seven innings and allowing two runs (one earned) on seven hits. He has held opponents to three runs or fewer in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Davies’ last three starts have been quality, but the most recent two came on the road, where he has a 2.13 ERA in 84 1/3 innings. In 72 1/3 innings at Miller Park, Davies owns a 5.97 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez is riding a five-game win streak, owning a 0.79 ERA over that stretch with a 25-8 strikeout-to-walk ratio. He will be making his second start against the Brewers this season, giving up two runs over seven innings on July 26.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson is coming off a victory in one of the Brewers’ most important games of the year, a victory at Dodger Stadium that swung the team’s western road trip to a winning one. He held L.A. to four hits in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Roark has turned his season around following the All-Star break, owning a 5-2 record with a 3.31 ERA over 49 innings. In the first half, he went 6-6 with a 5.27 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Woodruff returns for September after the Crew cleared a portion of the schedule that required only four starting pitchers. He hasn’t pitched in a game for more than a week; weather in the southern U.S. forced him to get his work in a simulated game.
away_pitcher_note: The reigning NL Cy Young Award winner has pitched seven innings in each of his last three starts, including his return from a brief trip to the DL on Monday. He beat the Brewers on July 27, giving up one run over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: The quick-working Suter returns from a stint on the 10-day DL with a left rotator cuff strain. He'll be on a limited pitch count, since he threw only 34 pitches in three innings for Class A Wisconsin on Wednesday to complete the comeback from injury.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson has become a reliable starter for the Nationals, with whom he owns a 2.94 ERA in eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey bounced back well from an outing cut short by shoulder soreness, going six innings and allowing two runs on four hits in a 2-0 loss to the Mets on Thursday. Both runs came in the first inning.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Anderson’s fourth start off the DL, and it comes at the scene of his injury. He strained his left oblique at Great American Ball Park on June 28 and spent the next seven weeks on the DL.

home_pitcher_note: After spending most of the season in the bullpen or in Triple-A, Stephenson has made the most of another shot at the rotation, winning his past three starts. He's allowed more than three runs only once in six starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Davies has been a road warrior this season, going 8-1 with a 2.13 ERA in 14 starts. He says he likes the time on the bench while the Brewers bat in the top of the first inning on the road because it calms him.

home_pitcher_note: A high pitch count limited Castillo to only four innings in his last start vs. Pittsburgh, in which he fanned five and allowed two runs. The rookie hasn't won since July 30, but not for lack of results: He has a 2.97 ERA since then.
away_pitcher_note: Garza was briefly bumped from the rotation, but he will return at Great American Ball Park, where he has a 3.83 ERA in eight career starts. Opponents had a 1.007 OPS against him in August.

home_pitcher_note: The Cubs are 9-1 in Lackey's last 10 starts. He took advantage of the wind blowing in at Wrigley in his last outing, throwing seven shutout innings against the Braves. Home has been good to him: He's 3-0 with a 2.48 ERA in his last five outings.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson will be on two days’ extra rest, in part to give him a breather and in part to line up the Brewers’ best starter for the opener of a three-game showdown with the Cubs. He’s eight strikeouts shy of 200.

home_pitcher_note: Filling in for Jake Arrieta, Montgomery, who has pitched mostly out of the bullpen, will be making his fourth straight start. In his three previous outings, he gave up four earned runs in 18 innings, striking out nine and walking two.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson has a 5.74 ERA in four career starts at Wrigley Field, skewed high by a May 21 loss when he surrendered six earned runs in four-plus innings, which included homers leading off three different innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off another solid outing -- 6 2/3 innings, two runs -- against the Pirates on Tuesday. Since returning from a finger injury on July 24, the 2016 Major League ERA leader (2.13) is 2-1 with a 2.36 ERA in nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Davies’ task starts with the reigning National League MVP. Kris Bryant is 9-for-22, including four extra-base hits, in his career matchups vs. Davies, who owns a 5.14 ERA in four starts at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie has made a statement about his status in the Brewers’ future plans with a 1.52 ERA in his first four big league starts. His 1.10 WHIP is impressive for a player just learning the league.
away_pitcher_note: Brault will make just his second start of the season as the Pirates continue to tinker with their rotation. The first lefty to start for the Pirates this year, Brault allowed three runs over five innings vs. the Cubs in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Suter's second start and third outing back from a strained rotator cuff. He's not expected to pitch deep into the game after throwing 43 pitches in a Sept. 3 start and 14 pitches in a Sept. 6 relief outing. So the 'pen will be active.
away_pitcher_note: Cole will get an extra day of rest before facing the Brewers for the fifth time. In four games vs. Milwaukee this season, he is 1-0 with a 2.33 ERA. He is coming off a no-decision after holding the Cubs scoreless through eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers pulled Anderson after five scoreless innings and 67 pitches on Saturday, because they were thumping the Cubs, 14-0, at the time. That put him in play to pitch on three days’ rest in place of injured ace Jimmy Nelson.
away_pitcher_note: After being sent down to Triple-A on June 10, Glasnow was recalled on Sunday and will make his 13th Major League start this year. He posted a 7.45 ERA and 1.91 WHIP over his starts with the Pirates and went 9-2, 1.93 ERA in 15 Minor League starts.

home_pitcher_note: Along with emerging as the Marlins' ace, Urena also has been their most productive starter away from Marlins Park. On the road, he's 9-1 with a 4.09 ERA, compared to 4-5 (3.17 ERA) in Miami. Urena has won four of his last five decisions.
away_pitcher_note: A former first-round Draft pick and Brewers closer, Jeffress will make his first Major League start after 263 appearances in relief. It will be another “bullpen day” for the Brewers, who have won two such games in recent weeks.

home_pitcher_note: Conley has faced the Brewers four times, twice in 2015 and 2016. Three were less than remarkable, racking up 10 earned runs in 12 innings. But the other, in April 2016, produced the best start of his career, 7 2/3 shutout innings with seven K’s.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching as the visiting team’s starter should suit Davies, who is 9-2 with a 2.04 ERA in 16 road starts this season. He’s said he likes the downtime after warming up in the bullpen while his team bats in the top of the first inning on the road.

home_pitcher_note: In his first three big league starts, Peters has 18 strikeouts, second most ever for a Marlin. Sunday marks his first game against a non-National League East opponent. Milwaukee performs at about league average against left-handed pitchers.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie’s last start against the Pirates marked the first time he has allowed more than two runs in a big league game. Woodruff will seek a bounceback in his third straight start at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon gave up six runs over 4 2/3 innings against the Cubs on Sept. 7, his most recent start before an extended period of rest. The Pirates hope that time off gets him back on track after posting a 7.17 ERA in 11 second-half starts.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty is getting closer to a full workload after throwing 50 pitches in his last outing, which was Suter’s second abbreviated start and third appearance since returning from a rotator cuff injury. He should be up to 70-75 pitches for this game.

home_pitcher_note: Williams will make his first start since Sept. 8, when he allowed four runs on four hits and four walks over 4 2/3 innings against the Cardinals. Still, the rookie has posted a 3.64 ERA in 11 second-half starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson gutted through 5 1/3 innings on three days’ rest in his last start on Wednesday, also against the Pirates, without command of his curveball or cutter. He’ll be back on a normal schedule for this game.

home_pitcher_note: Brault is coming off a dominant start in Milwaukee, where he held the Brewers to one hit and a walk while striking out six over six scoreless innings to earn his first MLB win. He’ll face Milwaukee again on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Wilkerson will make his first Major League start after debuting in relief last week against the Marlins with two strikeouts in a scoreless inning. He fired seven hitless innings in his last start -- a playoff outing for Triple-A Colorado Springs.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers stuck with a long-set plan to give Davies a day of extra rest before his most recent start against the Marlins, and as a result, he’ll pitch the opener of a huge four-game series. He has a 3.96 ERA in four 2017 starts against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta, who had to leave his last start on Sept. 4 because of a strained right hamstring, had a bullpen session on Tuesday and pronounced himself ready to go. He could possibly make three more starts in the regular season.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers’ No. 4 prospect will make his first career appearance against the rival Cubs. Woodruff has surrendered three or fewer earned runs in five of six MLB starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is coming off a no-decision against the Cardinals in which he lasted 4 2/3 innings, when he was ejected for arguing a call. He is 1-2 with a 3.79 ERA in three starts against the Brewers this year; the win was at Miller Park on July 3.

home_pitcher_note: After a stint on the DL with a strained rotator cuff, Suter is getting back to full strength. He’s thrown 43, 50 and 64 pitches in three starts since returning, which should push him to the 80-85 range for this start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks is 1-1 with a 4.91 ERA in four starts against the Brewers this season. Since coming back from the disabled list, he's 3-2 with a 2.42 ERA in 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson is 5-0 with a 2.34 ERA in 10 home starts. He will look to replicate his last start against the Cubs, when he surrendered only one hit in five scoreless innings and exited at 67 pitches because the Brewers were leading, 14-0.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana did not get a decision in his last outing, against the Cardinals, giving up three runs over 5 2/3 innings. He's faced the Brewers once this year, on July 28, and took the loss, giving up two runs over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Davies leads off a second straight series for the Brewers after delivering seven quality innings in a no-decision against the Cubs on Thursday. He’s still seeking win No. 18, which would be most for a Brewer since Chris Capuano in 2005.
away_pitcher_note: At 28, this will be McGuire’s first big league start after he made four relief appearances since his first September callup from Double-A. He’s recorded 5 2/3 scoreless innings, and the club wants to see where he might fit for 2018.

home_pitcher_note: After dueling Max Scherzer on Sept. 2, when Woodruff allowed one run in seven innings, the rookie right-hander has pitched capably but not exceptionally. He has surrendered 13 earned runs in 17 innings over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Bailey’s final 2017 start, and the club hopes he can finally put his checkered injury past behind him. He allowed four earned runs and seven hits over four innings vs. the Cardinals on Thursday, but he felt fine physically.

home_pitcher_note: Suter has slowly built his pitch count since a stint on the disabled list for a rotator cuff strain, most recently working 5 1/3 innings against the Cubs on Saturday. He has a 3.31 ERA in his 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Although his last start saw him hang some breaking balls and take a 5-4 loss to Boston on Friday, Romano has all but cemented his status in the 2018 rotation. Another strong start would be a good way to go into the offseason for the right-hander.

home_pitcher_note: Gant stepped into the rotation last week for his first MLB start of the season. He lasted just three innings due to the fact that he wasn’t all that stretched out. This time, he should be cleared to push a little bit deeper if pitching well.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson lost a duel with the Cubs’ Jose Quintana in his final start at home of the regular season. He has a 2.95 ERA in eight career starts vs. St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: This will be the final start of Weaver’s breakout season. He won seven straight starts before being chased after allowing eight runs over three innings in his last start. Weaver is 2-0 with a 3.00 ERA against the Brewers in 2017.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers’ Opening Day starter, Guerra was demoted to the Minors at the end of July and had been pitching out of the bullpen since returning as a September callup. He’ll start what amounts to another bullpen day for the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: The Cards made a late switch to replace Carlos Martinez with Flaherty, who will be making his fifth start this year. Flaherty, who is still seeking his first Major League win, will be making his first career appearance against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: After they were eliminated from postseason contention Saturday, the Brewers decided to call it a season for 17-game winner Zach Davies and start 28-year-old rookie Wilkerson instead. It will be his third big league appearance and second start.
