home_pitcher_note: In his 10th season, Richard has earned his first Opening Day start. It's quite the milestone achievement for the veteran lefty who battled back from two shoulder surgeries, Minors stints with three teams and a long stretch in the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson earned his first Opening Day assignment by becoming a four-pitch threat last season, thanks to a refined curveball and a new cutter. The Brewers need him at his best with ace Jimmy Nelson still recovering from shoulder surgery.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old prospect has dominated everywhere he's pitched. He posted a 1.99 ERA over two Minors seasons before notching a 1.54 ERA this spring. Now, Lucchesi is set for his big league debut, taking the place of the injured Dinelson Lamet.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin was San Diego's Opening Day starter last season, when he went 13-10 with a 3.89 ERA in 32 starts. After signing a two-year deal in the offseason with the Brewers, he will debut against his former team.

home_pitcher_note: It certainly feels like a make-or-beak year for Perdomo, who is entering his third season with the Padres. The righty sinkerballer led the NL in ground-ball rate last season and should get a boost from an improved infield defense.
away_pitcher_note: The quick-working lefty was the ultimate utility pitcher for the Brewers last year, when Suter shuttled between the Minors and Majors four times while posting a 3.42 ERA. He bulked up over the winter to be better the third time through the order.

home_pitcher_note: Davies missed one spring start and two turns through the MLB rotation with a mild left oblique strain in early March, but he rebounded to be ready for Milwaukee's home opener vs. the Cardinals. He'll aim to improve upon last year's 5.82 home ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Mikolas will climb a Major League mound for the first time since he was a Texas Ranger in August 2014. The right-hander pitched the past three seasons for Japan's Yomiuri Giants, going 31-13 with a sterling 2.18 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has a 2.72 ERA in 49 2/3 career innings against the Cardinals. The Brewers made sure to align their rotation so Anderson would catch both St. Louis and the Cubs on Milwaukee?s opening homestand.
away_pitcher_note: Adam Wainwright's hamstring strain gave Flaherty an opportunity in St. Louis' rotation. The righty features electric swing-and-miss stuff, but he struggled to a 6.33 ERA over his first six Major League appearances last year.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Brewers fans first in-person look at Chacin, the right-hander who signed a two-year deal with Milwaukee just before Christmas.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez will take the mound in Milwaukee looking for his first win. The Cardinals ace struggled on Opening Day, when he walked six and allowed five runs over four-plus innings against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Cue the Jurassic Park theme. Suter, known as 'The Raptor' for his unique style of running, takes the mound for home games to music from the 1997 film. It works; he's held opponents to a .683 OPS in 20 appearances at Miller Park.
away_pitcher_note: Lester lasted 3 1/3 innings in his Opening Day start against the Marlins and had trouble finishing his pitches. He served up seven hits and walked three.

home_pitcher_note: No. 3 on MLB Pipeline's list of Brewers prospects, Woodruff made eight MLB starts last year and beat Junior Guerra for the fifth starter spot coming out of camp.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Hendricks' second start of the season. He gave up one run on four hits and three walks over six innings in his opener against the Marlins, while striking out five. He's 4-1 with a 2.31 ERA in eight career starts at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers held Davies for their home opener so he wouldn't miss this series against the Cubs. Davies has a 3.90 ERA in 10 career starts against Chicago, including a 3.66 ERA in five starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: Darvish didn't have good command of his fastball in his Cubs debut against Miami, as he gave up five runs on five hits over 4 1/3 innings. Darvish's only previous start vs. Milwaukee came last Aug. 27, when he gave up three runs over five frames.

home_pitcher_note: By delaying their introduction of a fifth starter to the mix, the Brewers ensured Anderson would appear in this series against their chief division rival. He owns a 3.79 ERA in seven career starts against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana cruised through the first four innings in his last start but allowed five runs in the fifth and took the loss. He did last six innings and gave the bullpen a breather. He threw a three-hit shutout in his previous outing against Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Mikolas impressed on the mound, and at the plate, in his first start after three seasons in Japan, homering and earning a win in Milwaukee. He returns for a rematch with the Brewers against righty Jhoulys Chacin.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin took a loss vs. St. Louis in his last start, allowing six runs (three earned) on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings. He’ll look for a bounce-back performance vs. the Cards, building off the five strikeouts he posted against them Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez fired a gem in his last start, holding these same Brewers without a run in 8 1/3 innings, with 10 Ks.
away_pitcher_note: Suter looks to minimize contact in his next start vs. the Cardinals. He was roughed up for four earned runs on eight hits in five innings in a loss to the Cubs his last time out. The southpaw gave up three earned runs vs. San Diego in his 2018 debut.

home_pitcher_note: Recovered from the hamstring issue that briefly delayed his season, Wainwright looks to rebound from the command and velocity issues that turned his first start into a disappointing one.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first start of the season, Junior Guerra is looking to rebound from a disappointing 2017 season. He earned a 3-1 win for Triple-A Colorado Springs, giving up one run in 5 2/3 innings on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Much improved in his second start, Matz allowed only one run -- none earned -- against the Nationals to more than halve his ERA. He and the Mets feel confidence and conviction are keys for Matz, whose mid-90s fastball can keep hitters uncomfortable.
away_pitcher_note: Seeking his first win in his third start, Davies is looking to rebound after giving up six runs in 5 2/3 innings his last time out against the Cardinals. He is 2-0 in four career starts against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Struggling to keep balls away from the middle of the plate in his second start, Harvey allowed eight hits and four runs in five innings. His next outing will come at Citi Field, where Harvey delivered five shutout innings in his season debut.
away_pitcher_note: A victim of no run support, Anderson took a 3-0 loss against the Cubs his last time out, giving up two runs over six innings. Anderson has given up four homers in his last two starts after giving up 14 all of last year.

home_pitcher_note: By his own standards, Syndergaard has been far from perfect in his first three starts, with 15 hits and four walks in 16 innings. The resulting 3.94 ERA is far from bad, but more than a run higher than Syndergaard’s 2.89 career ERA entering the year.
away_pitcher_note: Control issues plagued Chacin as he walked three batters and gave up three runs in the third inning while getting a no decision in a 5-4 win at St. Louis on Monday. Better fastball control should yield better results.

home_pitcher_note: Suter's most recent start, against the Cardinals, represented a step forward. He recorded a sixth-inning out for the first time and surrendered season lows for runs (one) and baserunners (five).
away_pitcher_note: Castillo is coming off the best of his three starts in 2018 -- six innings, three runs, five hits, no walks and four strikeouts vs. the Phillies. Although he allowed two homers, manager Bryan Price thought it was a "much more polished effort."

home_pitcher_note: Guerra went from 2017 Opening Day starter to beginning the 2018 season at Triple-A, but he earned a call-up April 11 and made the most of it, pitching into the sixth inning of a series-clinching win against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Romano has struggled to close out the 1st inning (18.00 ERA) in his last 2 starts, giving up 3 two-out runs on 5 hits. It’s something he’s trying to tighten up, because he knows he needs to get out of innings when he has the chance.

home_pitcher_note: Davies owns a 3.72 ERA in nine career starts against the Reds. This will be his third straight start at Miller Park to begin the season.
away_pitcher_note: The third time through the order has been trouble for Mahle in his last 2 starts. At Pittsburgh, he gave up 4 runs in the 5th inning of a 5-0 loss. On Friday vs. the Cardinals, it was a 4-run 6th in a 5-3 defeat. The long ball got him in both starts.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson is coming off a solid start, allowing 1 run on 2 hits in 6 1/3 innings in a win over the Mets. He has pitched at least 6 innings in 3 of his 4 starts. Anderson has allowed 6 homers, but 3 were in a 4-inning stint against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Peters bounced back from his roughest big league start -- nine runs in 2 2/3 innings -- with an efficient six innings, two runs in a win against the Pirates. He threw 78 pitches, and went with 25 curveballs, with four swinging strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin has yet to turn in a quality start in four outings. He allowed one run on five hits in four innings in his last start, a no-decision in a 3-2 Brewers loss to the Mets. He has struck out 11 batters and walked 10.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing 8 runs in 8 1/3 innings in his first 2 starts, Richards threw 7 shutout frames in a no-decision against the Pirates on Saturday. He's best when he can get to his changeup. He's throwing 57.6 percent fastballs, 22.6 percent changeups.

home_pitcher_note: Suter’s last two outings have been encouraging. In his most recent start against the Reds, he did not walk a batter for the first time in four games, and the only damage against him came on a pair of run-scoring singles.
away_pitcher_note: Still searching for his first win, Urena has repeatedly given up runs in the early innings. Last year, Urena paced the team with 14 wins. His WHIP is 1.43, compared to 1.27 in 2017, and opponents are batting .284. In '17, they hit .238 off him.

home_pitcher_note: When Guerra throws enough strikes to access his outstanding splitter, he’s tough. But throwing strikes is sometimes a problem for him. Against the Reds his last time out, only nine of 20 pitches in a scoreless first inning were strikes.
away_pitcher_note: The road has been rough on Smith, who has made 2 away starts and has a 13.50 ERA in 5 1/3 innings, after being tagged for 5 runs in 2 1/3 frames on Monday vs. the Yankees. At home, he has a 3.48 ERA with 15 strikeouts in 10 1/3 innings over 2 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy takes the mound in the first game of a two-game set with Milwaukee at Kauffman Stadium. Kennedy had his first rough outing of 2018 last Wednesday in Toronto, giving up eight hits and four earned runs over five innings in a 15-5 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Davies is coming off the finest of his first four starts this season. His biggest test came when the Reds' very first batter, Jesse Winker, doubled and took third on an error, but he never budged from there and threw 6 1/3 scoreless.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel will get the start on Wednesday against the Brewers. Hammel pitched his longest game since 2012 when he went nine innings against Detroit on Friday and gave up two runs in a 10-inning loss.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin takes the mound for the finale of this two-game Interleague set. He worked six scoreless innings against the Marlins on Friday, allowing four hits while striking out five and walking three.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off his first win of the season, in which he went five innings vs. the Rockies, giving up three earned runs. He did not get a decision against the Brewers on April 6, when he gave up four runs on nine hits over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Two mistakes cost Anderson against the Marlins, as former Brewers prospect Lewis Brinson hit a pair of long home runs. They accounted for Miami’s only runs, though, as Anderson worked into the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: Darvish hasn't been able to finish the fifth inning in three of his four starts. In his last outing, he gave up five runs in 4 2/3 innings against the Rockies. He pitched well vs. the Brewers on April 7, giving up one run on two hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Suter has allowed 31 hits over 25 1/3 innings and opponents are hitting .295 against him. He escaped with a no-decision on Saturday against the Marlins despite allowing five runs in five innings. Suter has yet to complete six innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana struck out seven over 5 1/3 innings in his last outing, against the Rockies, and got the win. He beat the Brewers on April 8, throwing six shutout innings. This will be his second start at Wrigley Field this year.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra is coming off a strong outing -- one unearned run over five innings against the Marlins. He has given up just one earned run with 15 strikeouts over 16 innings in three starts since being called up from Triple-A.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood got his first win as a Cub with six-plus innings vs. the Indians, becoming the first Cubs starter of 2018 to pitch into the seventh. While with the Rockies in '17, Chatwood was roughed up to the tune of a 7.71 ERA in two games vs. the Crew.
away_pitcher_note: Davies only surrendered two runs in six innings against the Royals on Tuesday, but he got away with some hard-hit outs. He last faced the Cubs on April 7 and allowed one run in six innings and struck out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Finnegan was given a quick hook after 77 pitches in five innings with three runs allowed (two earned). He overcame a 25-pitch inning, and the lefty felt some mechanical tweaks helped him improve from his first two poor starts.
away_pitcher_note: After a 6.59 ERA and a .970 opponents’ OPS in his first three Brewers starts, Chacin is 2-0 with a 1.72 ERA and a .606 opponents’ OPS in his last three starts. One big difference: A better slider, Chacin’s key pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey threw only 50 pitches in his five innings during Wednesday’s 7-4 loss. He gave up four earned runs, including two homers. The right-hander complained his slider hasn’t been effective, and said it’s been a reason he’s given up long balls.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson missed the Reds when they came to Miller Park in April, but he has a 2.68 ERA in 37 innings spanning seven career starts against them.

home_pitcher_note: Reds coaches have noticed a change in Castillo's arm angle that leaves his fastball flat in the zone rather than having its usual nasty movement. They will try to make changes between starts, but they would prefer to skip him.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers didn’t rehab Miley’s groin injury only to let him go, so they are calling him up to the Majors to take Brent Suter’s spot in the rotation. Miley struck out 11 in six innings in his final rehab start.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra took a hard-luck loss Saturday at Wrigley Field, allowing a run and three hits over six innings. He walked two and fanned six in the Cubs' 3-0 win. Guerra has allowed no more than one run in each of his four starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Kingham earned a second start after turning in one of the best debuts for any pitcher in recent memory. The right-hander took a perfect game into the seventh inning, finishing with one hit allowed and nine strikeouts in a win over the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin rolled through three innings of one-hit ball Monday against the Reds before hitting a rough patch. He went on to allow four runs on five hits in 4 1/3 innings. Chacin is 2-3 lifetime vs. Pittsburgh with a 5.35 ERA in six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon bounced back from consecutive tough outings and recorded a quality start vs. the Nationals his last time out, but was still saddled with a loss. The right-hander owns a 1-3 record with a 3.73 ERA in six starts against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson improved to 3-2 despite struggling with his fastball command in his last start Tuesday in Cincinnati. He walked four batters and allowed four earned runs in in 5 1/3 innings in a Brewers win.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl threw his shortest outing of the season vs. the Nationals in his last start, surrendering four homers in 4 2/3 innings. He’ll look to right the ship against the Brewers. The righty is 2-0 with a 2.42 ERA in five starts vs. Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Miley delivered a quality start and a victory in his Brewers debut as the club finished a three-game sweep of the Reds. He walked three batters, and that’s the number to watch after Miley led the Majors with 93 walks last season.
away_pitcher_note: Armed with a substantial lead on Wednesday, Kluber cruised through seven innings in a win over the Rangers. The righty allowed three solo home runs, ending with six strikeouts and no walks.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra surrendered two earned runs and no home runs in his first four starts, then surrendered five earned runs and a pair of two-run homers to the Pirates on Friday. The issue was fastball command, or lack thereof, he said.
away_pitcher_note: Carrasco labored on Thursday, allowing six runs on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Blue Jays in Game 1 of a doubleheader. The righty has gone 0-1 with a 10.80 ERA over 8 1/3 innings in his past two starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last two starts -- a loss at Miami with little run support and a win against the Mets -- Marquez has held opponents to a .250 batting average, with 14 strikeouts against three walks.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers are 6-2 in Chacin’s starts, including four straight wins, and he’s throwing his slider more effectively of late. Chacin began his MLB career with the Rockies and has a 4.23 ERA in 69 games (62 starts) at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis has gone at least seven innings in four of his last five starts -- a span that has seen him hold opposing hitters to a .197 batting average and go 3-1 with a 1.89 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers will recall the rookie from Triple-A Colorado Springs for what will be his third stint with the big league club this season. He’s already made one start and five relief appearances in 2018.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies are 3-4 in Freeland's starts, but he has pitched better than that statistic. He has 38 strikeouts against 13 walks, and has gone at least seven innings in each of his last three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Suter moves back to the starting rotation after a week-long stint in the bullpen, replacing an injured Wade Miley. Watch out for him at the plate; Suter homered off Corey Kluber in an emergency relief stint on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Gray has been dominant in his last three outings, holding opponents to one run in 20 innings, with 25 strikeouts and three walks. The slider, his signature pitch, is getting better with each start.
away_pitcher_note: The No. 9 Brewers prospect will make his Major League debut after the team placed Chase Anderson on the 10-day DL with an illness. Peralta led the Triple-A Pacific Coast league with 46 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin has faced the Dodgers in his last two starts, so he's probably happy to get a look at some hitters who are less familiar with his stuff. He allowed just two runs over 11 innings in those two starts against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra surrendered two earned runs over four starts in April, but has been knocked around for nine earned runs on 12 hits in a pair of starts in May. He did strike out nine in his last start, a season high for a Brewers pitcher.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke got a no-decision last time out against the Nationals, despite giving up just one run over seven innings. He drove in the D-backs' lone run in the game and stole his sixth career base.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers have won each of Chacin’s last five starts, including an outing against his former club in Colorado on the Crew's current road trip.

home_pitcher_note: Koch has had three tough draws in a row. He faced off against Clayton Kershaw, Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer. Koch has pitched well since being called up from Triple-A to take the injured Taijuan Walker's spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff’s return to the rotation didn’t go well once he started a second turn through the Rockies' batting order at Coors Field. He surrendered as many hits (nine) as he recorded outs before the Brewers tapped the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Gibson lowered his season ERA to 3.43 in his previous outing against the Angels on May 12. He tossed six scoreless innings in that start and held the Angels to three hits and struck out six.
away_pitcher_note: Finally, Suter is on a normal schedule. He threw 82 pitches in emergency relief of Wade Miley on May 8, then threw 82 more pitches a day earlier than scheduled on Saturday after Chase Anderson fell ill.

home_pitcher_note: Romero's Major League career has gotten off to a scorching start. The 23-year-old righty is 2-0 with a 0.54 ERA in three starts as a Twin and has struck out 20 batters in 16 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Can the 21-year-old do it again with all fastballs? Of 98 pitches in Peralta’s 13-strikeout gem against the Rockies on Sunday, 90 were four-seam fastballs with remarkable movement. He allowed only one hit in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Odorizzi took a tough no-decision his last time out against the Mariners on May 14. He held Seattle scoreless over six innings before the Mariners tallied a late run against the Minnesota bullpen to win 1-0.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra didn’t have control of his splitter on Monday against the D-backs, so he pitched predominantly with his fastball and delivered six quality innings to snap a three-star losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson was scratched from a May 12 start at Colorado and placed on the DL with what he later believed was food poisoning, but was better by the next day. He should have no restrictions against his former team.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke threw six innings of one-run baseball and received a no-decision on Tuesday against the Brewers. He struck out five and walked one. Greinke has returned to form recently and hasn’t allowed more than one earned run in a start since April 30.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers had won five straight Chacin starts before losing at Chase Field on May 15 despite his seven-inning effort, which matched Chase Anderson for the Brewers’ longest start this season. He has has a 2.58 ERA over his past seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Last time out, Koch had his first rough outing since replacing Taijuan Walker in the rotation. He allowed eight runs in just 4 1/3 innings. It was his second straight loss, though he deserved a better fate in the previous one against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Suter, the utility man of the staff, has settled into a regular schedule after several emergency-type outings, first a relief stint in place of an injured Wade Miley, then a start on short rest after Chase Anderson fell ill.
away_pitcher_note: Godley's last win was April 27 against the Nats. He allowed three runs his last time out against the Mets, but only one was earned. Godley has scuffled with his command, walking four in two of his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Davies was placed on the 10-day DL on May 3 for a rotator cuff injury and sent on a Class A rehab assignment last week. An impactful pitcher in the Brewers' rotation before the injury, Davies has a 2-3 record with a 4.24 ERA in 2018.
away_pitcher_note: Inconsistency has plagued Matz all season. He’s delivered a quality start just once in eight tries, mostly because he has recorded four outs after the fifth inning in all his starts combined. Matz’s lone win came against the Brewers on April 13.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra got a no-decision in the Brewers' 3-1 loss to Minnesota over the weekend, and Milwaukee has lost four of Guerra's past five starts overall.
away_pitcher_note: Rounding into form, Syndergaard has delivered quality starts in five of his past six outings. His ERA over that stretch is 2.89, with more than four times as many strikeouts as walks, and he has won each of his last two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson returned Monday night after a stint on the DL due to an illness. He pitched six innings of two-run ball against the D-backs on Monday, asserting himself back into the top of the Brewers' rotation.
away_pitcher_note: After skipping a start to work on his craft, Vargas delivered five shutout innings in his return to the rotation against the Marlins, lowering his ERA from 13.86 to 9.87. The Brewers’ superior offense should pose a stiffer test at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin pitched five innings of shutout baseball Tuesday night against the D-backs. Pulled after 86 pitches, Chacin struck out six batters, his second-highest total in 2018.
away_pitcher_note: Wheeler holds a 1.38 ERA against the Marlins this season, but a 6.97 mark against everyone else. He allowed two runs in 6 1/3 innings in his lone start against the Brewers last year, and is 1-0 lifetime with a 1.54 ERA in two starts at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: It appears Suter has benefitted from settling into a regular schedule. He has allowed three earned runs with 12 strikeouts in 11 1/3 innings over his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver has done little to show he’s ready to vacate his rotation spot after a string of rough starts, completing seven innings in each of his past two outings. The righty was the recipient of just three combined runs of support in those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Davies showed some rust Thursday in his return from a stint on the disabled list for a right rotator cuff injury. He surrendered four earned runs on six hits and two walks in four innings against the Mets, striking out only two.
away_pitcher_note: Somewhat quietly, Wacha is enjoying a career year in his age-26 season.  He hasn’t lost since Opening Day and is 5-1 with a 2.88 ERA across 10 starts overall.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra was effective and efficient against the Mets on Friday, logging six quality innings on 72 pitches before manager Craig Counsell opted to tap his bullpen. Guerra has allowed two or fewer runs in seven of nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Cards' No.1 prospect will make his highly anticipated return more than 15 months removed from Tommy John surgery. The 23-year-old put up eye-popping numbers in four rehab starts, striking out 44 of 82 batters he faced in 23rd scoreless frames.

home_pitcher_note: Santiago threw one inning and 13 pitches in relief on Monday against the Indians, but that effort was considered a side day following his Saturday start. Santiago broke an 11-start winless streak in that start against Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson has a respectable 4.42 ERA but has allowed 13 home runs in 55 innings . The right-hander was removed after 3 2/3 innings on Saturday against the Mets after allowing five runs on seven hits and three walks.

home_pitcher_note: In six May starts, the right-hander allowed 15 earned runs on 24 hits and 13 walks in 40 innings pitched. He struck out 30, yielded two home runs and posted a .173 average against and .500 OPS against.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin struggled his last time out against the Mets on Sunday, allowing five earned runs on eight hits over 6 1/3 innings. The five runs allowed was the most he has given up all season and the first time he allowed more than two runs since April 30.

home_pitcher_note: Covey admittedly did not have his best control when finishing with a no-decision in allowing two earned runs over 4 1/3 innings Monday. He also threw only 48 of his 80 pitches for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Suter has become a regular in the Crew's rotation and already has five wins this season. While most of Suter's starts have lasted only five innings, he gives the Brewers a chance to win with a 4.63 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kluber spun six shutout innings against the White Sox on Wednesday, piling up 10 strikeouts with zero walks. The Tribe ace is riding a streak of 112 batters faced with zero walks and has a 0.68 ERA in his past four turns.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra is winless in his past three starts despite allowing just three earned runs in 16 1/3 innings for a 1.65 ERA. He faced the Indians at Milwaukee on May 9, allowing four runs on six hits in five innings. It was his last loss.

home_pitcher_note: Over Carrasco's last two starts, hitters have gone 10-for-18 with five extra-base hits and 10 runs scored against the righty with two outs. He allowed six runs on seven hits in 3 2/3 innings in a loss to the Twins on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson took the loss in his last outing Friday against the White Sox in Chicago, but he left in the sixth inning with the score tied and a runner on first base with two outs. He is 2-2 with a 2.67 ERA on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez has been finding his groove. He has a 2.14 ERA in his past six starts, striking out 45 and walking 13 in 33 2/3 innings. The Phillies need more of that, particularly with the offense struggling the past few weeks.
away_pitcher_note: A five-run outing against the Mets to end the month of May proved a blip for Chacin, who rebounded to pitch 5 2/3 scoreless innings against the White Sox. Including that Mets game, Chacin has a 2.60 ERA over his last 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta posted a 0.90 ERA in May, but allowed five runs in six innings in Sunday’s loss to the Giants. Arrieta had harsh words for his team’s defensive shifts afterward. It will be interesting to see if things change against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Suter has been solid in his six starts away from Miller Park, posting a 3.77 ERA over 31 innings. He's faced the Phillies just once in his career, going six innings in a one-run outing last July.

home_pitcher_note: After suffering two consecutive losses, Eflin bounced back on Tuesday, when he allowed one run over 7 2/3 innings against the Cubs. He is 1-1 with a 3.97 ERA this season in his two starts at home. Sunday will be his first career start vs. the Crew.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff has been up and down between the big leagues and Triple-A this season. He threw two perfect innings of relief in his last MLB outing on May 23 and earned a no-decision after allowing two runs in six innings for the Sky Sox earlier this week.

away_pitcher_note: Quintana struck out a season-high 10 batters over 5 2/3 innings in his last start against Philly, but got a no-decision. He's 4-2 with a 2.62 ERA on the road, and will be making his second start at Miller Park this season. He won there on April 8.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson ended April with a 2.86 ERA, but has seen that number rise to 4.57 with three straight abbreviated outings after a strong return from the DL on May 21. He walked three and allowed three earned runs in 4 1/3 innings vs. Cleveland last week.
away_pitcher_note: The Cubs like what Chatwood is doing even if the numbers don't look too good. He's walked 56 in 58 1/3 innings after seven walks in his last start vs. Philly. It was the 8th time in 12 starts that he'd walked at least five. He beat the Crew in April.

away_pitcher_note: Montgomery has made it no secret he wants to start, and he's doing a good job subbing for Yu Darvish. He is 2-0 in 3 starts, yielding 2 earned runs in 17 2/3 innings. In his last outing vs. the Pirates, he threw a season-high 95 pitches in 6 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suter continues to be a rock in the Brewers' rotation, winning four of his past five starts. His most recent outing came in Philadelphia, where he got the win and held the Phillies to three runs over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta faced Milwaukee in his last outing and had his worst home start with the Phillies, allowing four earned runs on four hits and three walks over 5 1/3 innings. In five career starts at Miller Park, he is 3-0 with a 2.03 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra has no-decisions in four of his past five starts, but he consistently keeps the Brewers in the game. He allowed one run over six innings against the Cubs on Monday night, but didn't get a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin has picked up two consecutive wins. After scattering eight hits in 7 2/3 innings of one-run ball at Wrigley Field, he tied his career high with nine strikeouts vs. the Brewers on Sunday. Eflin has a 3.63 ERA in four road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson hurled his best start since Opening Day on Tuesday night against the Cubs, pitching six shutout innings of one-hit ball. His 107 pitches were a season high for any Brewers pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Nola is pushing for an All-Star nod with eight wins and a 2.27 ERA through 14 starts. He held the Rockies to four hits over 6 2/3 innings in his last outing on Tuesday, striking out 10 batters for the third time this season.

away_pitcher_note: The Brewers are 12-3 behind Chacin, who is 6-0 with a 2.86 ERA over his past dozen starts. Now he has a new weapon, a splitter, which Chacin debuted while working six scoreless innings against the Cubs in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon returns to the mound to face the Brewers after allowing two earned runs over seven innings in his last start against the D-backs. He's produced quality starts in three of his past four outings, allowing 8 earned runs with 23 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta's third career start will come against the Pirates, as the Brewers need a fifth starter. Peralta struck out 13 batters in his Major League debut on Mother's Day in Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Leaning on his breaking balls, Kuhl has seemingly turned a corner lately. He owns a 2.45 ERA over his last five starts, and six of his last eight outings have been quality starts. Kuhl is 3-0 with a 1.91 ERA in six career starts against the Brewers.

away_pitcher_note: The return from the DL hasn't been what Martinez pictured. The Cardinals have lost three straight behind Martinez, who’s walked 18 in 12 2/3 innings. He’s walked at least five in each of his last three appearances.

away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander will take the hill in the second game of three in Milwaukee. Flaherty is coming off throwing five scoreless innings on Sunday against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has surrendered more home runs this season (15) than last season (14) in 64 fewer innings. He surrendered a pair of two-run shots in Sunday’s loss to the Phillies after holding the Cubs scoreless in his previous outing.
away_pitcher_note: After beginning June with three quality starts, Mikolas allowed four earned runs over five innings Monday in a no-decision against the Phillies. He settled down after a first-inning, three-run home run to Odubel Herrera.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin likes pitching at home, wherever home may be. After going 9-2 with a 1.79 ERA in 16 starts at Petco Park for the Padres in 2017, he has a 2.31 ERA in his first six Brewers starts at Miller Park.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver continued his bout of erratic starts on Tuesday, giving up four earned runs on five hits with four walks through five against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta will make his Miller Park debut against the Royals in his second start since rejoining the rotation. The rookie phenom delivered six shutout innings of two-hit ball last Tuesday vs. the Pirates in his first game in the Majors since May 19.
away_pitcher_note: Junis will start the opener of a two-game series against the Brewers at Miller Park. He threw six solid innings on Wednesday against the Rangers, but lacked run support in the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Suter has pitched a season-high seven innings in each of his last two starts, allowing three total runs over that span. In three Interleague outings (two starts) this season, Suter is 2-1 with a 2.93 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Duffy will start the finale of a two-game set against the Brewers. The lefty bounced back from a rocky start against the Astros in his previous outing with six shutout frames against them in a no-decision on Friday in which he allowed just two hits.

home_pitcher_note: DeSclafani starred on the mound and at the plate in his last start, winning his third straight start and becoming the first Reds pitcher since 1959 to hit a grand slam. He is 2-2 with a 4.15 ERA in five career games (four starts) vs. the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra threw five-plus innings of one-run ball last Friday against the Cardinals, lowering his ERA to 2.82. Without a win since May 14, Guerra hasn’t allowed more than three runs in a start since May 9.

away_pitcher_note: Anderson rebounded in his last start and struck out a season-high nine batters in a no-decision to the Cardinals. His issue this season has been the home run ball, already giving up 16 long balls in 2018.

away_pitcher_note: Chacin, who started June red-hot allowing five runs over 24 1/3 innings, surrendered a season-high eight runs and five walks last Sunday in a series-finale loss to the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Harvey was efficient with 84 pitches over 6 2/3 innings in a 5-3 win over the Braves Tuesday. He allowed one earned run and six hits with one walk and two strikeouts. Harvey has won back-to-back starts for the first time since May 2017.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta has 35 strikeouts in his first 22 2/3 big league innings while holding opponents to seven hits in 74 at-bats (.093). In two of his four starts, Peralta has logged double-digit strikeouts while yielding only one hit.

home_pitcher_note: Suter was named Milwaukee’s pitcher of the month for June after holding opposing hitters to a .198 average (21-for-106) and compiling a 3.60 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gibson got through seven innings against the White Sox, but he gave up five runs on a season-high 11 hits to get pegged with a loss. He had a 3.31 ERA in five starts in June.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra has topped 100 pitches in his last two starts, which is rare for a Brewers team that relies heavily on its solid bullpen. He has struck out at least six batters in each of his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Odorizzi ended a string of rough starts with a solid outing against the White Sox, throwing six scoreless innings with eight strikeouts in a no-decision. Odorizzi finished June with a 5.96 ERA in five outings.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin has been Milwaukee's most consistent starter this season, leading the staff with 18 starts and 97 innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: Fried will try to keep the rotation spot he gained when Brandon McCarthy was placed on the DL last week. The left-handed pitching prospect showed his potential as he recorded 11 strikeouts over 6 2/3 scoreless innings on Saturday in St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta makes his third start since rejoining the rotation in late June. He continued an excellent rookie campaign Sunday against the Reds, rebounding after a rocky first to allow three runs over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz will look to solidify his strong All-Star credentials and improve upon the 1.48 ERA he has produced in four career starts against the Brewers. He has an 0.87 ERA over his past nine starts.

away_pitcher_note: Certainly the most surprising asset within Atlanta’s rotation, Sanchez has provided stability while pitching into the sixth inning in four of his past six starts. He has a 2.83 ERA during that span since the start of June.

home_pitcher_note: The Twins couldn’t solve Guerra his last time out when he hurled five shutout innings of two-hit ball. Guerra has allowed more than three runs in a start just once since May 9.
away_pitcher_note: Newcomb was humbled and affected by humid conditions as he issued five walks over a career-short 2 2/3 innings at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday. He has a 2.13 ERA in the 14 starts made against teams other than the Yankees, Red Sox and Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Urena made a strong return from the DL, tossing five shutout innings in a no-decision against the Rays on Wednesday. The right-hander is 2-2 with a 3.67 ERA in his past seven starts. He's still looking for his first win at Marlins Park this year.
away_pitcher_note: A fly-ball pitcher, Anderson has fared pretty well at spacious Marlins Park, with a 3.15 ERA in three starts there. He’s allowed three earned runs over 17 1/3 innings in his last three Brewers starts.

away_pitcher_note: Chacin’s last start was solid, with two runs over seven innings during a sweep-clinching win against the Twins. It was even better in context, considering ace relievers Jeremy Jeffress, Josh Hader and Corey Knebel were unavailable.

home_pitcher_note: Straily has made three straight starts of six innings or more, and he is coming  off a season-high 111 pitches in six innings of a no-decision at Washington. He is 2-1 with a 5.52 ERA in six starts at Marlins Park.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Peralta pitched in the bottom of the first inning, it didn’t go well. His last road start was July 1 in Cincinnati, and Peralta needed a whopping 43 pitches in a three-run opening frame.

home_pitcher_note: Taillon cruised through six innings Saturday at PNC Park before giving up two runs and getting a quick hook from Clint Hurdle, after which Edgar Santana allowed an inherited runner to score. He has a 3.60 ERA in two starts vs. Milwaukee this season.
away_pitcher_note: Miley will return from the 60-day DL to make his first Brewers start since May 8, when he strained his right oblique against the Indians in his second game back from a groin injury.

home_pitcher_note: Kingham bounced back from a rough start in L.A. with a strong outing vs. the Phillies on Sunday, allowing one run on four hits and a walk with five strikeouts in six innings. He beat the Brewers on May 4, when he gave up four runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra has become one of Milwaukee’s most reliable starters, touting a 2.63 ERA in his last 11 starts and one or fewer runs in 10 of his 17 starts this season. He gave up a season-high five runs against the Pirates on May 4.

away_pitcher_note: Anderson had to work hard in his most recent start, against the Marlins, throwing 96 pitches for 14 outs. However, he didn’t allow an earned run and has a 1.23 ERA in his last four starts.

away_pitcher_note: Suter is scheduled to make his return from the 10-day DL to start in Game 2 of Saturday's doubleheader. The left-hander has eight career appearances against the Pirates, posting a 1.80 ERA with 14 strikeouts over 20 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Chacin has pitched a pair of gems against the Pirates this season, allowing a combined two earned runs on nine hits in 12 1/3 innings, but he didn’t earn a win in either case.

away_pitcher_note: Wood wasn’t able to duplicate last year’s All-Star first half, but he figured out a mechanical flaw and is pitching with more confidence than he’s had since last year. He’s pitched well at Miller Park.

away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez carries a 6.51 ERA and .304 opposing BA since the start of June, a stretch in which he has gone winless in eight starts. His sinker may be the culprit: He's going to it more than any other pitch, and hitters are clipping it at .325.

away_pitcher_note: Hellickson's two most recent starts since being activated from the DL were encouraging. He yielded just one run in 11 innings, with nine strikeouts and three walks.

away_pitcher_note: Roark has searched for any way to get out of his recent funk during which he owns a 7.38 ERA since the start of June. He has struggled to last deep into games and has allowed at least four runs in three straight starts.

away_pitcher_note: Spacious AT&T Park should suit Anderson, a fly-ball pitcher who has a 2.66 ERA in his nine starts so far this season away from Miller Park. Compare that to a 4.81 ERA in 11 starts at home.

home_pitcher_note: Still showing the effects of a sprained elbow that sidelined him for 61 games earlier this year, Cueto may have to rely on deception as well as pure stuff, now that his velocity has lessened by about 2-3 mph.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin, a former Rockies and Padres pitcher, has plenty of experience pitching at AT&T Park. He owns a 2.02 ERA in eight career starts there.

home_pitcher_note: Suarez has allowed three runs or fewer while working at least five innings in seven of his last eight starts. His ERA during this stretch is 2.89. At home, he owns a 3.35 ERA in eight starts, compared to 4.66 in nine road outings.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra’s first two innings off the DL were shaky, as he struggled with control and allowed four runs including Adam Eaton’s three-run homer. But Guerra followed with four scoreless frames and got out of the game healthy.

home_pitcher_note: Buehler’s season has been disrupted by a rib injury that led to disabled list stints and a Minor League option. He returned in Philadelphia on Wednesday but didn’t get out of the fifth inning, allowing 5 runs.
away_pitcher_note: Miley, the former D-backs lefty, has seen a lot of the Dodgers over the years. He has a 3.86 ERA in 81 2/3 innings against L.A., including going 3-0 with a 2.41 ERA in six starts at Dodger Stadium.

away_pitcher_note: The right-hander has yielded two or fewer runs in each of his last seven starts, with a 1.93 ERA and a .225 opponents’ average over 37 1/3 innings in that span.

away_pitcher_note: After carrying a no-hitter into the sixth inning on the way to seven strong frames against the Giants on Saturday, Chacin has allowed three earned runs in 18 innings over his last three starts.

away_pitcher_note: In his first outing since the birth of his first child, Marquez held the Athletics to two runs and five hits in 7 2/3 innings, with eight strikeouts and a solid delivery throughout.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies get a second crack at the rookie right-hander, who carried a no-hitter into the sixth inning and struck out 13 at Coors Field in a memorable Major League debut on Mother’s Day earlier this season.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson sailed for the first six innings against the Cardinals in his last start, but an uncharacteristic loss of control in the seventh led to three walks and a no-decision in a Rox loss.

home_pitcher_note: Miley faced the Rockies a lot while with the D-backs, and found some success. He’s 7-2 with a 3.79 ERA in 12 career starts and one relief appearance against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Gray not only has improved his fastball command, but has a sharper slider and learned to use his curve as a weapon while going 2-0 with a 1.66 ERA in his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers' 2018 Opening Day starter has started to revert to the form that led to his breakout '17 campaign, as he has a 2.08 ERA over his last eight starts, spanning 43 1/3 innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: Richard will make his first start in August, after a brutal month of July in which he went 0-3 with a 7.50 ERA in six starts. In his one start against the Brewers this season, on March 29, he tossed seven innings of one-run ball.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin took the loss his last time out, allowing a season-high nine runs over 4 1/3 innings in a 21-5 rout by the Dodgers. Prior to that, he'd been one of the best pitchers in the NL, posting a 4-0 record and a 2.52 ERA in a six-start stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy will make his Major League debut in the middle game of the series. The 24-year-old has impressed with Triple-A El Paso, going 10-0 with a 2.72 ERA in 16 starts.

away_pitcher_note: Erlin earned another assignment, after his superb spot start on Aug. 2. Primarily used as a multi-inning reliever, he held the Cubs to one run on two hits over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman will be making his first start in Atlanta since being acquired from the Orioles. The right-hander commanded his four-seamer and got good results with his splitter as he held the Mets scoreless through the first five innings Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta has logged at least five strikeouts in nine of his first 10 Major League starts and allowed three or fewer hits in eight of the 10. When he limits walks, he’s tough.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran's inability to consistently command his slider has hurt him as he's posted a 5.03 ERA over his past 10 starts. He has issued at least four walks in three of his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Miley has allowed three or fewer earned runs in all seven of his Brewers starts this season, including his seven-scoreless-inning gem in his most recent road start vs. the Dodgers on July 31.

home_pitcher_note: Newcomb will be pitching at SunTrust Park for the first time since coming within a strike of no-hitting the Dodgers on July 29. He got three days of extra rest before limiting the Nationals to one run over six innings on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson’s 3.81 ERA is respectable, but he’s been burned at times by home runs. He’s allowed a National League-high 23 home runs in 125 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana is coming off a frustrating outing vs. the Royals, in which he gave up five runs over 6 1/3 innings and had trouble with his command. He's 2-0 with a 0.95 ERA in four starts vs. the Brewers this year, yielding two runs over 19 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin looks to regain his July form in the opener vs. the Cubs. Chacin was 4-0 with a 2.64 ERA in five July starts, but has allowed 11 earned runs in 10 1/3 innings this month. In his last start vs. the Cubs on June 13, he hurled six shutout frames.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks did not get a decision in his last start against the Nationals, but he did record his team-leading 11th quality start. He has not walked a batter in three straight starts for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra looks to continue his good work vs. the Cubs this season. In two starts, Guerra has fired 12 innings with a 1.50 ERA and 10 strikeouts. For his career, Guerra has a 1.89 ERA in 19 innings vs. the Cubs with 22 strikeouts and a .194 BAA.

home_pitcher_note: The young right-hander is twirling a fine August after a pair of rough stretches in July. Flaherty fanned nine Royals in seven innings in Kansas City on Saturday, allowing three hits and two runs.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander carries an 8.05 ERA in four starts since the All-Star break into his first career appearance against the Cardinals. Twice in his four starts since the break, Peralta has surrendered seven runs.

home_pitcher_note: Even in his least effective outings, the Cardinals' right-handed All-Star keeps the game within striking distance. Mikolas is one of four qualified starters in the Major Leagues to not allow more than four runs in a game this season.
away_pitcher_note: Miley has rewarded the Brewers’ patience while he recovered from groin and oblique injuries. He has allowed two or fewer earned runs in seven of his eight starts, and three earned runs in the other.

home_pitcher_note: The stoic right-hander is coming off one of his more impactful games of the season, going 5 1/3 one-run innings while crushing a two-run homer on Tuesday against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: In pitching Chacin instead of Chase Anderson, the Brewers are betting that Chacin’s recent performance (one or fewer runs in four of his last six starts) will trump his career struggles against the Cards (0-7, 6.90 ERA in nine games, eight starts).

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has allowed five home runs in 14 2/3 innings in three August starts, pushing his NL-leading total to 24 home runs surrendered this season.
away_pitcher_note: In a loss to Cleveland on Monday, Bailey allowed five earned runs and 10 hits with five strikeouts over 5 1/3 innings. Six of those hits came in two-strike counts.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra is coming off an ugly loss to the Cubs in which he didn’t clear the fourth inning, but he has been excellent at Miller Park. The right-hander has a 2.59 ERA in 80 innings at home vs. a 5.76 ERA in nine starts on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Romano lasted only 1 2/3 innings in a loss to the Indians on Tuesday, giving up six runs on seven hits and two walks. He found trouble quickly in a four-run first inning.

home_pitcher_note: The first inning remained a problem for Peralta in his most recent start against the Cardinals, when he allowed two runs to bump his ERA to 9.00 in 12 opening innings this season. The rookie allowed three runs in five innings on July 1 vs. the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Stephenson has room to improve from his first two starts of 2018. He’s issued nine walks over a combined 5 2/3 innings and has had trouble commanding his fastball, especially in the 1 2/3 innings he lasted in Wednesday’s no-decision vs. Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers’ patience with Miley through groin and rib cage injuries has paid off. He has not allowed more than three earned runs in any of his nine starts, and he has allowed two or fewer earned runs in eight of those games.
away_pitcher_note: Musgrove leads the Bucs' rotation in ERA and WHIP. He was dominant in his last outing, fanning seven while allowing one run on five hits over seven innings vs. the Cubs. He earned a no-decision vs. the Crew on July 15 after giving up five runs.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin has rebounded nicely from a 21-5 loss to the Dodgers in his first start of August, going 3-0 with a 1.42 ERA and .191 opponents’ average in three games since. He’s been the Brewers’ steadiest starter.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon has made three starts vs. Milwaukee in 2018, allowing five earned runs with 18 K's and five walks over 16 innings. He earned a no-decision last time out after giving up one earned run while striking out eight over six innings vs. the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Bench coach Pat Murphy pointed out an oddity after Anderson’s last start: In six innings, he never pitched out of the stretch. The only two Reds hits were home runs, the NL-leading 25th and 26th off Anderson this season.
