home_pitcher_note: Ponce de Leon is making his first start of the season, filling in for Michael Wacha who was placed on the injured list with left knee patellar tendinitis. Ponce de Leon is 2-0 with a 3.24 ERA in three starts at Triple-A Memphis.
away_pitcher_note: Davies has returned from a disjointed 2018 season ruined by injuries to be the Brewers' steadiest starter in 2019. Two of his first four starts have been scoreless, and Davies surrendered one and two runs in the others.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright looks to become the fifth pitcher in franchise history to win 150 games and will also try to rebound from a season-low three-plus-inning start. Key to that will be limiting damage against the curve, which was ambushed in his last game.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin was 0-7 lifetime against the Cardinals in his first nine career matchups through last June, but he has won his last three starts against them, including Opening Day this year. He had seven strikeouts in that game.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets activated deGrom from the injured list shortly before first pitch, tabbing their ace after he missed his previous start due to a sore right elbow. In the Mets’ estimation, the arm issue stemmed from a bout of strep throat that altered deGrom's regular throwing routine.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off five scoreless innings in a spot start against the Dodgers on Saturday, Chase Anderson gets another shot against the Mets. Anderson said he was driven by being left off Milwaukee's postseason roster last year and sent to the bullpen to begin 2019.

home_pitcher_note: Among baseball's early-season mysteries is Noah Syndergaard, who hasn't had an ERA above 5.00 this late in a season since his rookie year. He's still striking out more than a batter per inning, but in his last three starts, Syndergaard's ERA is 6.88.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff's 3.89 FIP indicates he's performed better than his 5.81 ERA after five starts would indicate, though the 26-year-old conceded there is plenty of room for improvement. His two best starts this year have been against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Take out Matz's eight-run blowup this month in Philadelphia, and he would be 2-0 with a 1.61 ERA. Matz has worked hard on the mental side of pitching, working with "brain coach" Trevor Moawad to avoid unraveling during starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez will make his 2019 debut in Sunday's series finale against the Mets. He's had success at Citi Field in the past, with a 1.75 ERA in 17 career starts and an 11-2 record.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander remained Milwaukee's only reliable starter after a no-decision against the Cardinals on Tuesday left him with a 1.65 ERA through five starts. Davies has not allowed more than two runs in any of his outings.
away_pitcher_note: Kyle Freeland is set to come off the 10-day injured list (left middle finger blister) to start Monday. Freeland has a 1.50 ERA against the Brewers in two career starts, but has never pitched at Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin will look for his first scoreless outing of the year in his seventh start on Tuesday in Milwaukee. He lasted four innings, allowing four runs, in his last start against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Righty German Marquez, who is set to face Venezuelan countryman Jhoulys Chacin, struggled at points early in his last start. But in the end, he held the Nationals to three runs and fanned seven in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson will be making his third start since returning to the rotation after beginning the season in the bullpen. In two starts this season, Anderson has gone 9 2/3 innings, allowing just two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela's last start, a win at Atlanta, called for maturity. He didn't agree with the plate umpire's strike zone, but modified his pitches and got batters to swing. In three starts, he has an adjusted ERA+ of 130.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta is healthy again after dealing with a minor shoulder/chest injury and ready to rejoin the rotation. His Major League debut came against the Rockies a year ago on Mother's Day, a 13-strikeout gem at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Gray yielded two home runs and lasted 4 2/3 innings in Atlanta on Saturday, but the Rockies came back to win. He gave himself an "F" grade in all categories. Manager Bud Black said he wasn't that bad, but his command could improve.

home_pitcher_note: While fellow young pitchers Corbin Burnes and Freddy Peralta struggle, Woodruff has produced some better outcomes of late, including a five-inning outing against the Mets on Saturday in which he allowed one run on six hits.
away_pitcher_note: Matz was the Mets’ best pitcher in April and it wasn’t particularly close. Take out his eight-run blowup in Philadelphia, and Matz went 3-0 with a 1.84 ERA the rest of the month. He’ll open May against the same Brewers team he beat in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: After choosing the Brewers over the Mets in free agency, Gonzalez's first two Brewers starts happen to be against the Mets. He allowed two runs in five innings in a no-decision at Citi Field in his Brewers debut.
away_pitcher_note: While Wheeler has remained a bit inconsistent, and prone to isolated bad innings, he is 2-1 with a 3.12 ERA in his last four starts. He has struck out more than a batter per inning over that run, with more than three times as many whiffs as walks.

home_pitcher_note: The bright spot of the rotation so far, Davies has a 1.38 ERA that is the second lowest by a Brewers starter through the first six games of a season. Ricky Bones had a 1.12 ERA through his first six games in 1994.
away_pitcher_note: Since receiving a vote of confidence from Mets management, Vargas has posted a 1.93 ERA in three starts, holding opposing batters to a .180 average. The catch? He’s averaging fewer than five innings per start, rarely facing hitters more than twice.

home_pitcher_note: So steady last season, it wasn’t until Chacin worked six scoreless innings against the Rockies earlier on this homestand that he delivered a scoreless start. The Brewers hope it was something to build on for their Opening Day starter.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals have lost six of Scherzer’s seven starts on the season, though their ace leads the Majors with 62 strikeouts compared to just seven walks. He did not face the Brewers in 2018.

home_pitcher_note: Houser was Triple-A San Antonio’s Opening Day starter and made his first Major League start last month in St. Louis, but he’s effectively an “opener” here, pitching as deep into the game as he can before Freddy Peralta likely follows.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg has started to find a groove in his last three starts, pitching to a 1.25 ERA with 29 strikeouts in just 21 2/3 innings. Opposing batters are hitting .162 during that span.

home_pitcher_note: Woodruff is improving after a slow start, coming off back-to-back outings against the Mets in which he allowed one run on six hits in five innings in each start. "Of all our young guys, I think he has as high a ceiling as anybody," Ryan Braun said.
away_pitcher_note: Hellickson is 3-1 with a 4.26 ERA in seven career starts against the Brewers. He is 2-1 in four starts at Miller Park. He held Philadelphia to two runs in 5 1/3 innings in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana has historically been good against the Brewers (6-3, 2.51 ERA in 12 starts), but the lefty gave up eight runs in three innings vs. the Cubs' rival on April 5. Quintana is 4-0 with a 1.93 ERA in his last five outings.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers brought back Gonzalez to provide some stability for a struggling rotation, and so far he is 2-for-2. Gonzalez has cleared at least five innings in each outing, including a seven-strikeout performance against the Mets his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels will take the mound at Wrigley Field, where he has spun a tidy 1.96 ERA in 15 career starts. The left-hander held the Brewers to two runs over six innings on April 6 and has gone 8-3 with a 3.57 ERA vs. Milwaukee (16 starts) in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Davies has baseball’s second-lowest ERA among qualifiers, but it’s also about context. He covered all but four outs of Sunday’s sweep-clinching win over the Mets, a day after the bullpen pitched 12 2/3 innings of an 18-inning marathon the night before.

home_pitcher_note: Lester has been stellar since returning from the IL, allowing just one earned run over 18 innings (three starts) with 19 strikeouts and one walk. The lefty has not faced the Brewers this year, but went 1-1 with a 2.31 ERA in two starts (11 2/3 IP) in '18.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers’ Opening Day starter has had trouble finding consistency this season, but Chacin has a good matchup. He owns a 2.86 ERA in 12 games (11 starts) against the Cubs, including last year’s NL Central tiebreaker.

home_pitcher_note: Nola is coming off a strong outing -- allowing just three hits and one run over six innings in an 11-1 win over the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching five scoreless innings behind an opener last time out, Peralta will start this time as the Brewers recover from a 15-inning game on Saturday against the Cubs. Peralta's trouble typically comes in the first inning.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff protected the Phillies' bullpen by working eight scoreless innings on Wednesday in St. Louis. The right-hander didn't allow a runner to reach second base until the eighth.
away_pitcher_note: Catcher Yasmani Grandal was right when he said Woodruff was close to a breakout. After pitching to a 5.81 ERA through his first five starts, he has limited opponents to three earned runs over 16 innings his last three times out.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta will be looking to bounce back from a 5-1 loss against the Royals when he surrendered three home runs, all on elevated pitches. Prior to that start, he had allowed only four homers all season.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez has been the steady hand the Brewers needed to stabilize their rotation. Through three starts, including a win over the Cubs last time out, Gonzalez has a 1.69 ERA. He says he's just happy to be in a big league uniform again.

home_pitcher_note: Eflin (5-3, 2.47 ERA) is coming off a masterful performance. He threw a four-hit shutout Saturday against Kansas City for his second complete game of the season. Eflin threw first-pitch strikes to 19 of 31 Royals batters.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander has been bucking baseball’s trend toward hard-throwers, allowing two or fewer runs in each of his eight starts. Only five times this season has a Brewers starter worked into at least the seventh inning. Davies has three of them.

home_pitcher_note: Fried exited his May 7 start after getting hit in the left hand with a second-inning comebacker, then allowed a season-high nine hits five days later against the D-backs. He has a 5.89 ERA over his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin looks to continue his solid run, opening the series in Atlanta with a chance to even his record at 4-4. Chacin has pitched to a 1.59 ERA over his past three starts, holding hitters to a .186 average and .555 OPS.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman will be making his first start since serving a five-game suspension levied for throwing behind Jose Urena earlier this month. He has a 6.04 ERA over his past five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson will make his return from the injured list, looking to pick up where he left off when he sustained a finger laceration in late April. Anderson pitched to a 1.86 ERA in his only two starts of the season before being sidelined.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz made some mechancial changes he hopes will halt the struggles he's had in each of his first four starts. His fastball velocity has been down, and his once-reliable slider has been a liability.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff has been stellar in his past four starts, going 4-0 with a 1.23 ERA. He allowed one hit over six scoreless innings against the Phillies on Tuesday, winning his fifth consecutive decision.

home_pitcher_note: Gio Gonzalez has been a stabilizing presence in the rotation since joining the Brewers in late April, going 2-0 with a 1.69 ERA in four starts. The southpaw looks to continue that roll Tuesday against the Reds in his second home start of 2019.
away_pitcher_note: Over five innings vs. the Cubs on  Wednesday, Gray walked none and struck out seven. But he was burned by two-out home runs in the second and fourth innings to account for all three runs allowed. This will be his first experience pitching at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a 2018 season marred by injuries, Davies will take the mound for his 10th start of ‘19 with a Major League-leading 1.54 ERA. He has not allowed more than two earned runs in any of his first nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Castillo has been one of the best in the NL. It continued Thursday in a 4-2 win over the Cubs. He was limited to 5 1/3 innings because of rain but allowed two hits and a walk with six strikeouts. Three of those K's were from his great changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson will be well-rested in his second start off the 10-day injured list after throwing 76 pitches in Atlanta in his return to action last weekend. He's allowed two earned runs in 13 2/3 innings since joining Milwaukee's rotation.
away_pitcher_note: After a stellar first four starts of 2019, Eickhoff has allowed nine runs over his last two starts. The right-hander has a 6.55 ERA in four career starts against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Milwaukee's top starting pitcher a season ago, Chacin has had to grind through outings this year as opponents drive up his pitch count. Still, he's keeping the Brewers in games, with a 2.45 ERA in 22 innings over his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta pitched well against the Cubs, allowing just one run over six strong innings. Prior to that, Arrieta allowed four earned runs in back-to-back starts and took the loss in each outing.

home_pitcher_note: Woodruff is coming off arguably his most impressive start in his career, an eight-inning outing against the Braves in which he threw the firmest fastball of his career at 98.8 mph and was still throwing 96 mph in the eighth.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin has allowed one run or fewer in four of his last five starts. In his previous outing, he allowed one run over six innings and scattered six hits and four walks.

home_pitcher_note: Pineda settled in after a rough first two innings against the Angels as he made his third quality start in a row, allowing three runs in six innings as he retired 12 of the final 14 batters he faced. He has only two walks in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The task of taming the powerful Twins falls first to Gonzalez, who has allowed only one home run this season and hasn't yielded more than three runs in any of his first five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Smeltzer will make his big league debut vs. the Brewers, with Martin Perez pushed back. For Triple-A Rochester, the 23-year-old made four starts for the Red Wings, going 0-1 with a 1.82 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Davies had baseball's second-best ERA before allowing six earned runs in three innings in his first poor start of the season on Wednesday against the Reds at Miller Park. Though he took a no-decision in an eventual Milwaukee win, he'll look to get back on track against a powerful Twins lineup.

home_pitcher_note: Musgrove will take the mound for Pittsburgh seeking his first win in his third career start vs. the Brewers. The right-hander looks to rebound from a rough start vs. the Dodgers in which he allowed six runs on 10 hits over five innings. Musgrove has worked at least six innings in seven of his 11 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson will make his fifth start of the season to begin the series at Pittsburgh. Anderson hasn't completed five innings in any of his past three starts. He allowed three runs in four innings in a no-decision vs. the Phillies in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: RHP Chris Archer looks to get back on track after three poor outings in May, having allowed 13 earned runs over 13 2/3 innings for an 8.56 ERA. Archer has pitched past the fifth inning just twice this year and hasn't done so since April 13 at the Nationals (7 IP).
away_pitcher_note: Chacin has lost his last three starts, surrendering eight earned runs in 16 innings over that span. He allowed four runs in five innings in a loss against Philadelphia last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Kingham will stay in the rotation after an encouraging performance in Cincinnati. The righty worked four scoreless innings, then gave up three runs and didn't get out of the fifth. He gave up seven hits but struck out five and walked just one batter.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff is coming off a dominant outing vs. Philadelphia. He allowed one hit -- a solo homer by Andrew Knapp -- in eight innings and had a season-high 10 strikeouts. Woodruff hasn't allowed more than two runs in any of his past six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles avoided the IL after leaving his last start with left hamstring discomfort, a bit of good news for the Pirates. He'll face his former team, the Brewers, who helped him fine-tune the pitch mix that's led to his early success in Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Davies, who rebounded from his worst start of the year to work six scoreless innings his last time out, earns this start in place of Gio Gonzalez, who's sidelined with a tired arm.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson is 2-0 with a 2.78 ERA in five starts since moving from the bullpen to the rotation and has fared pretty well in his career against the Marlins, logging a 3.57 ERA in seven career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez faced the Brewers once in 2018, giving up five runs in six innings at Miami on July 10. The 23-year-old is coming off a one-run outing against the Giants at home -- where his ERA is 1.84 -- but on the road, his ERA is 8.26. Hitters are batting .152 against his curveball.

home_pitcher_note: This is a nice 30th birthday present for Nelson, who is scheduled to pitch in the Major Leagues for the first time in just shy of 21 months. He spent that time rehabbing from shoulder surgery, but was solid in five games (four starts) at Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: In May, Alcantara had a 3.23 ERA in five starts. He struck out just 19 in 30 2/3 innings in the month, and he walked 16. What's helping Alcantara is he doesn't give up much hard contact as his average exit velocity this year is 84.9 mph (top six percent in MLB).

home_pitcher_note: Peralta's last three outings came in relief, but he was needed back in a starting role after Jhoulys Chacin joined Gio Gonzalez on Milwaukee's injured list. If Peralta clears the first inning, he is typically in good shape.
away_pitcher_note: On April 22, 2018, Smith fanned 10 in Milwaukee. This year, he has a 33.8 percent strikeout rate. Smith has logged 80 strikeouts in 61 innings, and he has a WHIP of 0.97. He's also allowed 10 home runs, matching his total from 2018 (in 77 1/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: After a pair of eight-inning gems against the Phillies and Braves in which he allowed three earned runs in 16 innings, Woodruff was touched-up for six runs on 10 hits in four innings in Pittsburgh in his last start. He draws the Pirates again.
away_pitcher_note: Davis will make his first MLB start since Sept. 20, 2017, as he steps into the rotation in place of righty Nick Kingham. Davis has allowed five runs on eight hits and three walks while striking out eight in 7 2/3 innings over four relief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Davies pitched into the ninth inning for the first time in his career in his most recent start at Pittsburgh, a performance even more impressive considering the team was coming off a 13-inning game the night before that taxed the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles will make his second straight start against the Brewers after primarily using his fastball and curveball in a 4-2 loss at PNC Park on Sunday. Lyles allowed four runs on eight hits and struck out five while throwing 109 pitches in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson had mostly avoided his trouble with the long ball that marred his 2018 season, but that issue returned in his last start against the Marlins. Miami hit three homers against Anderson in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Brault will get another shot to start after working only four innings vs. the Braves on Tuesday night. Brault has more walks (12) than strikeouts (11) in his past 18 1/3 innings, but he's only allowed six runs (five earned) in those four appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock has been terrific in his past six starts -- which coincides with him pitching out of a full windup with the bases empty -- going 3-1 with a 1.32 ERA and a 0.94 WHIP in 34 innings pitched. He's struck out 41 batters and walked 11 in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta couldn't have pitched much better on Thursday. In his first start since May 13, Peralta had his best of the season, tossing six innings while allowing just one run and striking out nine without surrendering a walk.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander was denied his 10th win Thursday in Seattle when the Astros' bullpen blew a late lead. He's 34-7 with a 2.73 ERA in 48 career Interleague starts, including 2-0 with a 1.08 ERA in two starts against Milwaukee. He leads the Majors with 0.74 WHIP.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff earned the win in his most recent outing last Friday, holding the Pirates to three earned runs over 6 innings with one walk and 10 strikeouts. He's among the NL leaders in wins and strikeouts. Milwaukee is 11-2 in games he starts.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz is coming off one of his best starts of the season after tossing five scoreless innings against the Dodgers. He is 0-1 with an 8.00 ERA in two career starts against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Davies earned the win but had one of his shorter outings in his most recent start on June 8 vs. the Pirates. He allowed three runs over five innings, walking one and striking out three. Davies has allowed two earned runs over 11 career innings vs. the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner was charged with a tough-luck loss Sunday despite holding the Dodgers to one run over seven strong innings. He is 7-4 with a 2.63 ERA in 12 career starts against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson will make his second start of the season on Saturday in San Francisco seeking a longer outing than his first. Facing the Marlins on June 5, he yielded four earned runs over three innings. Nelson is 2-2 with a 5.28 ERA in five career starts vs. the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija took the loss in his last start after yielding three runs over 5 1/3 innings against the Dodgers. He is 3-6 with a 4.28 ERA in 26 career appearances (12 starts) against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson will make his eighth start of 2019 when he faces the Giants in the finale on Sunday. The right-hander took a no-decision in his most recent outing June 9 vs. the Pirates after allowing two runs (one earned) on four hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Padres prefer to pitch their starters on five days’ rest, but Lucchesi has been the exception. He starts with four days’ rest Monday, coming off a strong start at San Francisco in which he allowed two earned runs while striking out six over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin, out with a lower back strain since June 2, will come off the IL to start Monday's Brewers opener at San Diego. Chacin has faced the Padres 16 times in his career, including 12 starts, and has a collective 3.52 ERA and 1.21 WHIP against them.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old lefty is slated for his big league debut, and with a beleaguered bullpen, the Padres could use some length. Allen, the team's No. 5 prospect, posted a 5.15 ERA in 13 Triple-A starts. But he's shown improvement lately.
away_pitcher_note: The rising 26-year-old has delivered quality starts in six of his last seven outings, including a duel with Astros ace Justin Verlander last time out in Houston. Woodruff has a 2.95 ERA over his last nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: After a strong start, Strahm has struggled in his last two outings, allowing 13 runs. He also dealt with rib soreness that kept him off the mound for 11 days between those starts. After walking eight through nine starts, he has walked seven in his last three.
away_pitcher_note: Davies won his first seven decisions before taking a loss in San Francisco in his most recent start, when he allowed three runs in five innings. He has a 2.16 ERA in four career starts against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson and manager Craig Counsell insist it wasn't fatigue that led Nelson to abruptly lose the strike zone in the fifth inning of his last start, when he missed the zone with 12 of 13 pitches and sparked a Giants comeback.
away_pitcher_note: Roark threw a season-high 116 pitches over seven innings during Saturday's 4-3 loss to Texas. He retired his final 10 in a row, and said he gained confidence from manager David Bell letting him stay in the game over his final two innings.

home_pitcher_note: After going 2-0 with a 2.78 ERA in his first five 2019 starts, Anderson is 0-1 with a 5.79 ERA in three starts in June. He is throwing the curve a career-low 10.9 percent of the time while allowing a .471 opponents’ batting average on the pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Gray had one of his best starts of 2019 at Miller Park on May 21, allowing five hits in six innings for a 3-0 win. Gray walked four but struck out nine, as he worked his way out of jams.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin came off the injured list Monday and allowed two runs in 4 2/3 innings in a loss at San Diego. He was a bit wild early and threw 102 pitches, but he found the feel of his out pitch and recorded seven strikeouts on sliders.
away_pitcher_note: Castillo's worst start of 2019 happened at Miller Park on May 22. Lasting only 2 2/3 innings during an 11-9 Reds loss where he earned a no-decison, the ace gave up four runs on five hits (including two homers) with three walks.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers’ streak of nine straight wins when Woodruff starts ended Tuesday at San Diego when he allowed four runs in six innings. He had live stuff in that game, however, touching 100 mph and keeping the Padres hitless until the fourth inning.
away_pitcher_note: DeSclafani last faced the Brewers during his first start of the season on April 2 at GABP. He gave up one earned and three hits over five innings with three walks and eight strikeouts. He is 1-3 with a 4.68 ERA in five career games at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Davies is coming off his poorest start of the season, a 2 2/3-inning outing at San Diego in which he was charged with a season-high five runs on a season-high nine hits. He has never faced the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The Mariners' Opening Day starter has gone 3-0 with a 2.33 ERA in his last 3 starts after a rough stretch (0-6, 7.79 ERA) in his previous seven outings. This will be his first time facing Milwaukee since 2017, when he was with the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Houser, who has been thriving as a high-leverage reliever, will start in place of Jimmy Nelson after Nelson was shifted to the bullpen. Houser has a 1.05 ERA in 14 games out of the bullpen this season.
away_pitcher_note: Carasiti struck out the side Sunday vs. the Orioles in his first relief appearance after signing a Minor League deal on June 8. He’ll get his first shot as an opener, to be followed by Wade LeBlanc (2-0, 3.52 ERA in four games following an opener).

home_pitcher_note: Anderson is coming off a poor start against the Reds in which he allowed six earned runs across five innings. He has pitched into the sixth inning once in nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Leake gave up 11 hits and 8 runs (7 earned) in 5 1/3 innings to the Orioles in his last outing, but still managed the win in a 10-9 decision. The veteran right-hander is 4-0 with a 3.82 ERA in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin hasn't cleared the fifth inning in either of his starts since a stint on the injured list for back tightness, continuing a disappointing season. But he's been encouraged by progress with his signature pitch, the slider.
away_pitcher_note: Archer allowed one run over five innings in his most recent outing vs. the Padres on June 22. In four starts in June, Archer has posted a 5.32 ERA, allowing a combined 13 earned runs across 22 innings, though the Bucs have won three of those games.

home_pitcher_note: Woodruff has been the Brewers' best starter, with all three of his double digit strikeout performances within his last six starts, including a career-best 12 in his most recent outing against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles will make his first start since landing on the IL on June 10 with left hamstring tightness when he takes the mound in Milwaukee. The righty had a solid rehab outing for Triple-A Indianapolis, yielding one run on just two hits over 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Davies said he would look within for answers after a loss to the Mariners last time out. In Davies’ last two outings, he has been charged with nine earned runs over 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Brault will look to finish off what has already been a productive June when he takes the mound for the finale in Milwaukee. Brault has compiled a 2.53 ERA over four June starts, allowing seven runs (six earned) across 22 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Mahle's homecoming start in Anaheim on June 25 got off to a tough start with a homer in each of the first two innings, but he settled in after to fire three scoreless frames. This will be his first start of the season against Milwaukee, which he last faced on June 30, 2018, in a 5 2/3-inning, three-run (one-earned) effort.
away_pitcher_note: Houser was dominant in 14 relief appearances but struggled in his first start back in the rotation, blaming nerves for his command issues in a loss to the Mariners in which he allowed three runs on four hits and three walks in two innings.

home_pitcher_note: Roark started out strong against the Angels on Wednesday, firing four scoreless innings before allowing a solo homer in the fifth. That was the only run charged to him in 5 1/3 innings of work. Roark has already faced the Brewers twice in 2019, most recently delivering a one-run, six-inning effort in Milwaukee on June 20.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson is coming off a win over the Mariners in which he pitched into the sixth inning for the second time in his 10 starts. He allowed six runs in five innings the last time he faced the Reds on June 21.

home_pitcher_note: In two starts vs. the Brewers, Gray is 1-0 with a 3.48 ERA. On June 21 at Miller Park, he gave up four earned runs over 4 1/3 innings while throwing 109 pitches. He labored with four walks and saw a lot of foul balls run up his pitch total.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin is winless since April 30, though he came close last time out against the Pirates, when a lead slipped away from the Brewers' bullpen. He allowed one run in five innings that night and continued to see progress with his slider.

away_pitcher_note: Never mind the pitching, Anderson needs a hit. With Brandon Woodruff's single against the D-backs last Saturday, Anderson is the only Brewers starter without a base hit, and his teammates have been letting him know about it.

home_pitcher_note: Castillo ended a seven-game losing streak and got his first victory since April 7 during Friday's 6-4 win over the Cardinals. He found some added velocity with his sinker, averaging 98 mph and topping out at 99.2 mph on his final pitch in the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander came within five outs of a no-hitter last Friday against the D-backs before Nick Ahmed hit a slider below the zone for a single. Peralta's last two starts: 14 1/3 innings, five hits, two runs.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Woodruff did not record a quality start for the first time since Opening Day. He'll look to get back on track in that area versus the Pirates, against whom he owns a 3-2 career record.
away_pitcher_note: De Jong looked great again in the first three innings of his start vs. Miami on Saturday, but he was tagged for five runs across the fourth and fifth innings. With Trevor Cahill injured, the Bucs are giving De Jong -- a Minors signing -- a third turn.

home_pitcher_note: Burnes will put his perfect 3-0 career record against the Pirates on the line in the second game of the series. In 14 career appearances (though only two starts), Burnes has struck out 34 Pittsburgh hitters in 27 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl reduced his swing-and-miss rate from his first start off the IL to his second, and it worked to his advantage. He drew a ton of weak contact from the Marlins on Sunday, resulting in an efficient six-inning outing.

home_pitcher_note: Houser goes against the Pirates at a high point of an inconsistent season. In each of his last three appearances (two starts), Houser has pitched at least five innings and not given up more than a run.
away_pitcher_note: Crowe allowed eight runs in four innings on June 1, and shortly after, he was optioned to Triple-A Indianapolis. He only pitched one inning there before he was called back up to fill Mitch Keller's spot in the Pirates' rotation.

home_pitcher_note: In the middle of a stretch of 16 games without an off-day, manager Craig Counsell said the Brewers would run with a six-man rotation for now. Lauer will fill that sixth spot against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: In a 7-3 win over the Brewers in his previous outing last Wednesday, Gutierrez threw 102 pitches over seven innings and showed he could handle being stretched in his third big league start. He encountered some jams, but maintained his composure and used his fastball to control the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: After his last outing, Anderson said he has to do a better job of doing his part. He'll get that opportunity against the Reds, against whom he owns a 4-3 lifetime record, despite posting a 4.76 ERA over 45 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Castillo had another strong outing in his last start despite a losing result. Over 5 2/3 innings, he allowed one hit but was charged with three runs. At one point, he retired 15 batters in a row. During that stretch, he was keeping the ball down for grounders and strikeouts, with only two balls leaving the infield.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta was pulled after a rain delay on Thursday with six strikeouts over four innings in Cincinnati. It ended a streak of 11 consecutive starts with seven-plus K’s. He'll look to reach that mark again when the Reds visit Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Mahle is on a legitimate roll lately with a 4-0 record and 2.31 ERA over his last four starts. In 23 1/3 innings during that stretch, he's issued only four walks compared to 24 strikeouts, while opponents are batting .167.

home_pitcher_note: Márquez had a 1.89 ERA over his previous six starts before matching a season high with eight earned runs (in five innings) at Cincinnati on Saturday. But many of the hits off him were soft, and a seeing-eye double through a drawn-in infield accounted for the final runs.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff's 1.52 ERA and 0.72 WHIP is the best of the Brewers' three aces. He's coming off seven efficient innings last Friday against the Pirates, in which he threw 98 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela has a 3.83 ERA in 47 home innings this year, as opposed to a 6.94 in 23 1/3 road innings. One difference is he has kept the ball in the park at Coors (two home runs) as opposed to other parks (five).
away_pitcher_note: Burnes is coming off a four-inning outing against the Pirates in which he was charged with four runs (three earned), marking his first outing all season in which he didn't complete at least five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Remember when the going wisdom was curveballs were not good at Coors Field? Well, according to MLB Quality of Pitch, Gomber's knuckle curve ranks in the top four percent in MLB in overall quality.
away_pitcher_note: Since allowing a season-high six runs against the Reds on May 21, Houser has a 1.71 ERA in his last four outings, one of which was an extended relief appearance.

home_pitcher_note: González's simple toughness won him points in his last start. He yielded four runs in the first two innings against the Padres on Tuesday, but four scoreless innings later, the Rockies had a chance to win.
away_pitcher_note: The big inning has been Lauer's undoing in many of his Brewers starts. He surrendered four runs in his first two innings against the Reds his last time out, then rebounded to pitch three scoreless frames.

home_pitcher_note: Kelly faced the Brewers earlier this month at American Family Field and did not factor into the decision. He allowed five runs (four earned) over six innings in that game.
away_pitcher_note: After a pair of rough starts against the D-backs and Reds, Anderson was brilliant over seven scoreless innings against Cincinnati on June 15, yielding just one hit while walking one and fanning nine. He went 4 1/3 innings against Arizona on June 3, giving up three runs on eight hits.

home_pitcher_note: Gallen is making his second start since being activated from the injured list. He has had two stints on the IL this year. In his first start back against the Giants at Oracle Park, Gallen allowed four runs on four hits in 2 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta looks to keep his breakout season rolling, coming off another great start in which he gave up two runs on five hits over seven innings against the Reds on Wednesday, walking none and striking out six. His last start against Arizona was on June 4, when he yielded one run on one hit, walking three and fanning nine over 7 1/3 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Smith will make his fifth start since rejoining the rotation and his sixth start overall. Last time out against the Dodgers he allowed just one hit over six shutout innings. Smith faced the Brewers earlier this month and allowed one run over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff looks to bounce back from a rough start at Colorado, when he gave up five first-inning runs in a 7-3 loss to the Rockies. He'll be making his second start against the D-backs in 2021, having given up two runs on six hits, while walking one and striking out nine on June 5.
